declarations.description:
Content that a row shows and hides in place. One item is a single disclosure; several are a set whose items open by themselves or, with `exclusive`, one at a time. A help page's questions, the sections of a settings screen, the advanced part of a form. Contract: specs/accordion.spec.json. The element has **no shadow root**: its items are the product's own native `
` elements, which stay in the document. They open and close, are focusable, carry the expanded state, keep their closed content in the page (a field in it keeps its value and is sent with its form) and are opened by a link to a fragment and by the browser's find-in-page, before any script runs and without it. ```html
palette Colors Roles, palettes and the six schemes 48 roles

Every color a component reads is a role.

A label that is a heading

…

A disabled item

…

 ``` An item is a `
` whose first child is its ``: the header. The summary's text is the label, or ONE element in its place — a heading of the level the page's outline needs, or a `` around text with inline content; an element with `data-supporting-text` is the line under the label, one with `data-trailing-text` the short value before the chevron, a `.tanrei-icon` the glyph at the start. `open` is the item's own attribute and property and `toggle` its own event (it does not bubble; `event.newState` is `open` or `closed`) — the browser also sends it when the product sets `open`. A disabled item is ``. Everything drawn is `@tanrei/web/accordion.css` — every value a `--tanrei-comp-accordion-*` token — which draws the whole look and every state before and without this script; the element adds the same sheet to the root it is connected to, so it also works inside another component's shadow root. The script adds what a stylesheet cannot: the system's answer to a press (ripple, dim), the arrow keys, `exclusive` (the `name` it writes on its items), the height motion where the browser cannot move a height to `auto` in CSS, the pressed header kept in place while an item above it closes, focus given to the header when its item closes around it, the supporting and trailing text read as the header's description instead of as part of its name, a disabled header refused, an open item drawn and answered as one target — closed by a press on its content, hovered, pressed and focused as a whole, with the pointer cursor over it (ACC-36; without script only the header is a target), and the debug reports. An accordion in an item's content is content like any other, drawn by its own attributes.

members.name: read
members.description:
Reads the items the accordion holds and writes what follows from them: `exclusive` as their `name`, a disabled
header out of the focus order, the supporting and trailing text as the header's description, the separation and
the glyphs where a stylesheet cannot tell. Called when a property changes and when the items or a header's parts
do; it writes only what differs, so it settles.

members.name: readExclusive
members.description:
ACC-12: `exclusive` is the items' `name` — a name of this accordion's own, so an accordion inside an item keeps its
own — which the browser holds to one open item. Given several open, the first in order stays; the others are closed
here, at once. A `name` the product wrote is left as it is.

members.name: closeAtOnce
members.description: Closes an item without the motion of ACC-13: the styles are computed once with their transitions off.

members.name: readHeader
members.description:
A header's parts (ACC-20, ACC-24). A disabled header leaves the focus order. The supporting and the trailing text
are the header's description, in that order, and not part of its name: each is hidden from the name and named by
`aria-describedby`, which reads what it points to even where that is hidden. Each is text of its own direction
(ACC-31): `dir="auto"`, unless the product named one.

members.name: check
members.description: What a debug build says about an accordion it still draws (ACC-3, ACC-24, ACC-32, ACC-35).

members.name: mutated
members.description: What the observer saw: a change of an item's `open` opens or closes it; anything else is read again.

members.name: toggled
members.description:
Items opened or closed — by the user, by the browser for another (`name`), for a search or a fragment, or by the
product. Called before the change is drawn.

members.name: move
members.description:
ACC-13, where the browser cannot move a height to `auto` in CSS: the content's height is measured once, before the
first frame, and the stylesheet moves its box between 0 and that height. An item whose `open` changes again on the
way goes on from where it is: the pose is turned, and the transition reverses by itself. Where the stylesheet
moves the content alone, or the item's clock does not run (reduced motion, a duration of zero), nothing is done.

members.name: settle
members.description: The motion of an item is over, or was never begun: its pose, its measured height and what it made inert are taken off.

members.name: setInert
members.description: The content of a closing item, out of the focus order while it is still drawn (where no style says so).

members.name: keep
members.description:
ACC-14: the header the user acted on stays where it is in the view while an item above it closes. Its place is
read when the change begins and, only while such an item is still closing, once a frame, and the scrolling of what
holds it is moved by what it lost. Nothing is scrolled for any other reason.

members.name: act
members.description: The user acts on a header: where it is in the view is remembered until the task of the act is over (ACC-14).

members.name: pressOf
members.description: The press of one header (the shared primitive), made when it is first pressed.

members.name: answered
members.description:
The press is this script's from here: the stylesheet's own answer to `:active` stands down for a summary that
carries `data-pressed`, so the attribute is written before anything reads a style.

members.name: onContentClick
members.description:
ACC-36: the click that ends a press in an open item's content closes the item, as its header's would — unless it
moved past the slop, is a second click, is modified, ends a text selection in the item, lands where something
else takes it, or is cancelled by a handler of the product's. The click is decided once it has reached every
listener (a task later), so that the product's own handler on the content is heard first.

declarations.description:
Names the current screen at its top edge and holds the way back and the screen's most used actions, flat while the
content is at its top and set apart once content scrolls under it.

Contract: specs/app-bar.spec.json. A layout region: no role of its own, never focusable, no events of its
own. Its items are the product's icon-only `<tanrei-button>`s — the spec's `navigation` kind with `slot="navigation"` and
its `action` kind with `slot="actions"` — which it lays out and never restyles (APB-11). The title is `headline`,
because HTML's global `title` attribute would put a tooltip over the whole bar; it is the screen's heading, of
`heading-level` (1 by default).

Scrolled: the bar connects to a scrolling element and sets `scrolled` from it — the document's scrolling element by
default, the element whose id `scroll-target` names, or nothing with `scroll-target="none"` (then set `scrolled`
yourself). A large bar shrinks one for one with the scroll until only its top row is left (APB-8).

Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-app-bar-*` tokens. The color reaches under `env(safe-area-inset-top)` and
the side insets; the content stays inside them (APB-10).

declarations.description:
Frames a page or an app: places a header, the navigation, the main content, an aside and a footer, decides from the window's width how each of them is shown, and lets a keyboard reach the content in one step. It draws the frame and none of what stands in it. Contract: specs/app-shell.spec.json. The element has **no shadow root**: it is the frame around the product's own regions, which stay in the document and keep their semantics — a `
` is the page's banner and the one `
` its main landmark for a screen reader, a crawler and a page without script alike. ```html Skip to content
…a callout…
menu
…
…
…
…
… ``` A region is a child with a `slot` attribute — the region's name; no shadow root reads it — and the main region is the one `
` without one. They are written in the order a keyboard walks them (APS-22): the skip link, the announcement, the header, the navigation, the aside while `aside-order` is `before`, the main region, the aside while it is `after`, the footer, the navigation bar. The stylesheet places them by name and never reorders focus. Everything laid out is `@tanrei/web/app-shell.css`, before and without this script (APS-24): the window's class is a media condition, a region the class does not show has no box, and the skip link is an anchor to the main region's id. The element adds the same sheet to the root it is connected to, and what a stylesheet cannot say: - **the class**, as the read-only `windowClass`, the `data-window-class` attribute and `windowclasschange` — from two `matchMedia` listeners of the widths the stylesheet was written with; no resize listener and no frame loop. What the frame holds also inherits it as `--tanrei-app-shell-window-class`, from the stylesheet alone; - **the menu button** — the one icon-only `` in the header — which it answers while the navigation has no place in the layout: `navigationOpen` and the `open` of a `` in the navigation region become true, the drawer's `close` makes them false again, and the button says `aria-expanded` and what it controls; - **the scroll offset**: the header's measured height as `--tanrei-app-shell-scroll-offset` on the document's root (the stylesheet sets the root's scroll padding from it), and the navigation bar's as `--tanrei-app-shell-scroll-offset-end`, so a link's target and a focused element rest clear of both. The product's own sticky parts read the same properties; - **a landmark** for a region whose element does not give one (`role="banner"` on a header that is not a `
`, `aria-label` from `aside-label` on an aside without a name), and `tabindex="-1"` on a `
` that lacks it; - the debug reports of APS-4, APS-21 and APS-29. With `scroll="main"` the main region is the scrolling view: name its id in the app bar's `scroll-target`.

`watch()` for a frame that was just connected: in ONE microtask after the script that connected it, for every
frame of that turn — all read, then all told their class — and before any of them is drawn or a frame painted.
Read in its own connection, each frame had the page styled for itself, after the class the one before it had just
written (fifty at once: fifty style passes). A page has one frame; a gallery of them has many.

declarations.name: styles
declarations.default: css` /* AVT-1: inline with the text or the row it is placed in, one unbreakable box that a layout neither stretches nor shrinks: the host has the box's own side on both axes, so a flex or a grid container that stretches what has no size of its own leaves it alone, and where it is aligned stays the container's to say. AVT-8: pointer events are left as they are — there is no listener here, so a press over an avatar inside a link or a Button reaches that element. */ :host { display: inline-block; flex: none; vertical-align: middle; inline-size: var(--_side); block-size: var(--_side); } :host([hidden]) { display: none; } ${forms} ${box} /* AVT-5: the initials are text of their own direction, isolated from the text around the avatar. */ ${productText('.label')} /* AVT-6: the glyph — the product's, or the system's for the shape — in a box of the size's icon size at the centre, in icon.color, the icon set's unselected family and fill, sys.icon.weight, the optical size of the box, no transition. AVT-15: iconGlyph() mirrors the slotted glyph GlyphMirrorController marked; the avatar mirrors nothing. */ ${iconGlyph('.icon', { size: '--_icon', selected: ':not(*)' })} .icon { color: ${t('icon-color')}; } .icon[hidden] { display: none; } /* The slot is the glyph's ink for GlyphDrawnController: an inline block as wide as the name it holds. */ .icon slot, .ink { display: inline-block; vertical-align: top; } .icon ::slotted(svg), .icon ::slotted(img) { display: block; inline-size: var(--tanrei-icon-size); block-size: var(--tanrei-icon-size); } /* Nothing in a glyph's place until the icon set can draw it — never the glyph's name spelled out (AVT-2); the box keeps its size. */ .icon:not([data-drawn]) { visibility: hidden; } /* AVT-3, AVT-4: the picture lies over the whole box, out of the flow, so that neither its arrival nor its failure moves anything; it covers the box with its proportions kept and its centre on the box's centre, and is clipped by the container. Until it has loaded it has its box (a lazy picture is asked for when that box nears the window) and draws nothing — no broken-picture mark, no alternative text, no address. It is never mirrored or tinted, and forced colors leave it alone (AVT-13). */ .image { position: absolute; inset: 0; display: block; inline-size: 100%; block-size: 100%; object-fit: cover; object-position: center; visibility: hidden; forced-color-adjust: none; /* The picture is not a second thing to drag or to press inside a link (AVT-8). */ -webkit-user-drag: none; -webkit-touch-callout: none; } .image.loaded { visibility: visible; } `

declarations.name: groupStyles
declarations.default: css` /* AVT-16: one row that does not wrap, as wide as its boxes less their overlaps and as high as one box, inline with what it stands beside. The direction is inherited, so a right-to-left layout starts the row at the right and each following box lies over the left end of the one before it (AVT-20). */ :host { display: inline-flex; flex: none; vertical-align: middle; /* Its own size on both axes, so a container that stretches what has none leaves it alone. */ inline-size: max-content; block-size: var(--_side); } :host([hidden]) { display: none; } /* AVT-23: a group without members draws nothing and takes no space. Its own rule: a browser without custom states drops only this one, and the empty group is then a row of no size. */ :host(:state(empty)) { display: none; } ${forms} ${unsafeCSS(overlapBlock(DEFAULT_SIZE, ':host'))} ${unsafeCSS(CORE_SIZES.filter((size) => size !== DEFAULT_SIZE).map((size) => overlapBlock(size, `:host([size='${size}'])`)).join('\n'))} /* Every box, the first too, is drawn back by the overlap, and the row starts that far in: the first stands at the row's start edge, and a box later in the document is painted above the one before it. */ .row { display: flex; flex-wrap: nowrap; align-items: center; padding-inline-start: var(--_overlap); } .row[hidden] { display: none; } ${box} /* AVT-17: the overflow box — placed and surrounded as a member is. It takes no input: there is no listener and no state here. */ .overflow { margin-inline-start: calc(-1 * var(--_overlap)); } /* AVT-18: the sign and the number are one left-to-right run, isolated, so the plus sign stays before the digits in a right-to-left layout; digits of equal width where the font has them. */ .count { direction: ltr; unicode-bidi: isolate; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } /* AVT-19: what assistive technology reads for the overflow box, never drawn. It is inside the box, which is positioned and clips, so it widens nothing around the group. */ .spoken { position: absolute; inset-block-start: 0; inset-inline-start: 0; inline-size: 1px; block-size: 1px; overflow: hidden; clip-path: inset(50%); white-space: nowrap; } `

declarations.description:
Stands for a person, or for a team or a project, by a small picture — by initials or a glyph where there is no
picture — in a round or a square box of three sizes. A picture, never a control.

Contract: specs/avatar.spec.json. `<tanrei-avatar label="Ada Lovelace" initials="AL" src="/people/ada.jpg">`. It draws
the first of these it has: the picture, once it has loaded; the initials the product gives (at most two characters as
a reader counts them, as written — the avatar never makes initials from the name); the glyph in its `icon` slot; the
system's own glyph. The box never changes size and nothing changes place when the picture arrives or fails. Every
visual value is a `--tanrei-comp-avatar-*` token; how far its corners ease is the system's amount
(`--tanrei-sys-shape-corner-smoothing`).

Alone, it is an image named by `label` (the name in full — never "Photo of", never the initials). Beside the same
name in visible text, set `decorative` and the name is read once. It takes no input and no focus and emits no event:
an avatar that leads somewhere is inside a link, one that opens something inside a Button, and a dot or a count on it
is a `<tanrei-badge>` around it.

declarations.description:
Several avatars drawn as one row in which each lies a little over the one before it, with a gap around each, and a
last box that counts the members it does not draw: the avatar's group form.

Contract: specs/avatar.spec.json (AVT-16…AVT-23). `<tanrei-avatar-group label="Reviewers" max="4">` around
`<tanrei-avatar>` members. The group gives its `size` and `shape` to every member and makes each one named, whatever
its `decorative` says. `max` is the most boxes drawn, the overflow box included (six members with `max="4"` are three
members and "+3"); `total` is the real count where the product gives fewer members than exist. The members it does not
draw stay in the document as its children and are not drawn or exposed. Anything that is not a `<tanrei-avatar>` is
not a member and is not drawn.

It is a group named by `label`, holding one named image per member it draws and then the overflow's text
(`overflow-label` or the product's words `avatarGroupOverflowLabel`, with `{count}` filled by the number not drawn;
else the drawn count). The overflow box is text, not a control: showing the people it counts is a
link or a Button beside the group.

No `count` is the dot, `count="0"` draws nothing, a count above `max` shows as `999+`. Every visual value is a `--tanrei-comp-badge-*` token. declarations.name: bottomSheetRelease
declarations.description:
BSH-9: where a released drag goes — `close` (below half the lowest height, or a downward fling with no height below
it), else the next height in the direction of a fling, else the nearest. `position` is the sheet's visible height at
the release, `velocity` its vertical speed in px per ms (positive: down).

Shows supplementary content or a short task in a surface that rises from the bottom edge: `standard`, over the lower
part of its parent while the content above stays usable (a layout region), or `modal`, a modal step that dims
and blocks everything else until it is dismissed (a modal overlay).

Contract: specs/bottom-sheet.spec.json. The content is the default slot. The sheet is as tall as its drag handle's row
and its content, up to its `detent`: `partial` takes `container.partial-fraction` of the area, `full` reaches up to
`container.margin-block-start` below its top. The person moves it between the two by dragging (the handle's row, the
content's padding, or the content where it lets the drag through) or with the drag handle, a button while there are
two heights; the element sets `detent` and fires `detentchange`.

Controlled: the sheet never closes itself. While `closedby` is not `none` it fires `close` with a reason — a released
drag below its lowest height and, for a modal sheet, a press on the scrim, Escape or the platform's back — and you set
`open` to false. A product that does not close it sees it settle back.

Modal: a native `<dialog>` in the shadow root opened with `showModal()`: in the top layer over `::backdrop` (the scrim),
docked to the window's bottom edge, everything else inert, the page held from scrolling and focus kept inside. Focus
goes to the slotted element marked `autofocus`, else the sheet (also when it is mounted open), and returns where it was
when it closes. Standard: a `<section>` named by `label`, docked to the bottom of its containing block — the host fills
the nearest positioned ancestor, so give the parent that holds the sheet and the content `position: relative` — with
presses above it reaching the content; opening it moves focus in, closing it gives focus back, and Tab leaves it open.

Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-bottom-sheet-*` tokens. The color reaches under
`env(safe-area-inset-bottom)`; the sheet sits on the on-screen keyboard (`visualViewport`).

The height it rests at while its content is taller than its partial height: `partial` (the default) or `full`. The
element sets it when the person changes the height (and fires `detentchange`); setting it moves the sheet without an
event. Any other value is `partial`, reported (BSH-25).

attributes.name: closedby
attributes.description: The spec's `dismissible`, as HTML's own attribute: `none` ignores a drag below the lowest height, Escape, back and the scrim; any other value is `any`. Reflected.

attributes.name: no-handle
attributes.description: Draws the drag handle. False (the `no-handle` attribute) draws none; the sheet can still be dragged by its content.

attributes.name: handle-label
attributes.description: The drag handle's accessible name ("Resize sheet"), required while it is a button (BSH-11).

attributes.name: flush
attributes.description: Insets the content by `container.padding`. False (the `flush` attribute) lets it reach the edges (a list with its own padding).

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Names the modal dialog, or the standard sheet's region ("Share photo"). Required (BSH-22).

declarations.description:
Shows where a page sits in a hierarchy of pages and leads back up it: the levels above as links, in order from the top, with the page itself last. Contract: specs/breadcrumbs.spec.json. The levels are the product's own children, which stay in the document (BRC-2, BRC-13): an `` for a level with a destination, a `` for one without — the current page, or a level that has no page. Before the element is defined, and with scripting off, the page holds the whole trail as links that work. ```html Home Components Button ``` A level's label is its text. `aria-current="page"` on the last level marks the current page; `data-icon` names a glyph of the system's icon set, drawn before the label; `data-icon-only` draws the glyph alone and keeps the text as the level's name; `data-mirror="always"` or `"never"` is the product's word on mirroring that glyph in a right-to-left layout. `underline` says when the links are underlined (BRC-30); a row of the overflow menu is a menu item and never is. A level's `click` is the anchor's own: cancel it and the browser follows nothing (BRC-22). Everything drawn on a level is `@tanrei/web/breadcrumbs.css` (every value a `--tanrei-comp-breadcrumbs-*` token), which draws the trail before and without this script; the element adds the same sheet to the root it is connected to. The shadow root holds only what the product did not write: a `
` named by `label`, the ordered list with one item for each level, the separators, and the overflow button with its menu. `overflow="collapse"` (the default) keeps the trail on one line: when it is wider than the width it is given, its middle levels go behind the overflow button, beginning next to the first, as many as the width asks for; then the first; and the last label is cut only when the button and it alone do not fit. The button opens a menu of the levels taken out; choosing one is a click on that level's own anchor. The trail is measured when its width, a label, the text size or the direction changes; at rest it runs nothing. `overflow="wrap"` keeps every level and lets the trail run over as many lines as it needs.

members.description:
BRC-12: the width the layout gives, and a line of the trail's text — one observer for every trail of the page, so
that the trails that change size in one frame (all of them, when a page is first laid out) are measured together.

members.name: due
members.description: The trails drawn in this turn, which are measured together after it (`updated`).

members.name: directed
members.description: The level this element gave its text's direction (BRC-28).

members.name: wraps
members.description: BRC-29: an overflow it does not have is collapse.

members.name: mutated
members.description: What the observer saw. The ripple's layer is this package's own: its coming and going is not a change of the levels.

members.name: onFaces
members.description: A face arrived: the labels may be wider or narrower than they were measured.

members.name: readLevels
members.description:
Reads the product's children: every `<a>` and `<span>` is a level. An address that is no destination is taken off
its anchor, which is then text (BRC-3) — as the Link does (LNK-21), so that it is no link to the browser either.

members.name: check
members.description: What a debug build says about a trail it still draws (BRC-1, BRC-4, BRC-7, BRC-10, BRC-29).

members.name: decide
members.description:
Decides which levels are out of the trail, by the width the trail has: every entry is measured at its own width —
a level with its separator, the overflow button with its own — in one task, so the measuring is never painted;
then levels are taken out, in BRC-9's order, only while what is left does not fit. Nothing is written when the
answer is the one already drawn.

`observed`: it was asked for by the observer of sizes. What is decided is drawn at once all the same; only the
width the whole trail needs — which may be the element's own width, in a layout that gives it the width of its
content — is then written in the next frame, because a size changed while sizes are being told is told late and
reported as a loop.

members.name: watch
members.description: Has the one observer of sizes tell this trail of `element`, or no longer.

members.name: decideTogether
members.description:
`decide()` for every trail of `trails`: each is laid out for measuring, then all are read — one style pass and one
layout between them — and only then does each write what it decided. A trail that measured in its own update, and
again in its own report of sizes, had the page laid out for itself each time (fifty trails drawn at once: 251
style passes and 152 layouts).

members.name: take

type.text: { widths: number[]; button: number; room: number }

members.description: The writing half of `decide()`: what follows from the widths that were read.

members.name: keep
members.description: BRC-8: the width the whole trail needs stays the element's own widest size (see `.sizer`).

members.name: moveFocus
members.description:
BRC-12: focus follows what it was on. A level that held keyboard focus and is taken out hands it to the overflow
button; an overflow button that is removed while it holds focus, or while its menu is open, closes the menu and
hands focus to the first level that returned.

members.name: onMenuClose
members.description: The menu asks to be closed — Escape, a press outside, Tab, a level chosen — and returns focus to the button itself.

members.name: onMenuClick
members.description:
BRC-11, BRC-22: a level chosen in the menu is that level's own anchor activated. The row is a link to the level
(the menu's link item, MNU-53), so the address, a new tab and the browser's own menu are there; a plain
activation of it is handed to the product's anchor as one `click` — the event the product listens to and cancels
(a router's link component) — and the browser follows that anchor unless it was cancelled. The row's own click
opens nothing and goes no further than the menu. A modified or a middle click is the browser's, on the row.

members.description: The press is this script's from here: the stylesheet's own answer to `:active` stands down for an anchor that carries `data-pressed`.

declarations.description:
Lays out a few related Buttons in one row or one column, spaced apart or joined into one shape, places the confirming
and the dismissive ones by the orientation, and names them as a group.

Contract: specs/button-group.spec.json. Every value it reads is a `--tanrei-comp-button-group-*` token: the gap of each
variant, the connected corners, the divider and the padding at a joined row's outer ends. Its items are
`<tanrei-button>` children, labelled or icon-only, each drawn from its own tokens, with its own states, events,
semantics and Tab stop (BGR-5). The group takes no focus, handles no key and keeps no selection; a toggle Button in it
stays independent. It draws nothing of its own but the dividers of a connected group.

Order (BGR-13, BGR-14): a child with the `confirming` attribute (OK, Save, Next, Delete) is placed at the end of a row
and at the top of a column; one with `dismissive` (Cancel, Back) at the start of a row and at the bottom of a column;
the others between them, each run in the order given. The children are not moved in your DOM: each is assigned to a
slot of its own, in the placed order, so focus and assistive technology follow that order (BGR-15).

In a connected group the items are joined as `separation` names (BGR-21): under `divider` they touch, with square
corners where they meet, and no item draws its outline or its elevation's ring along a seam; a seam carries a line
only while the two items it joins rest on the same fill (BGR-24) — between a selected toggle and an unselected one the
edge of the fill already marks it — in `connected.divider.color`, or `connected.divider.on-fill.color` between two
emphasis fills (filled Buttons, selected toggles);
under `gap` they stand `connected.gap` apart with `connected.inner-shape` corners. `auto` — the default — takes
`comp.button-group.connected.separation`, which follows the design system's `sys.behavior.separation`. The group
gives its items their corners, minimum size, seams and outer padding through custom properties the items read
(`--tanrei-group-*`): an internal contract between Tanrei elements, not a styling API.
declarations.name: TanreiButtonGroup

cssParts.description: The line on a seam of a connected group under `divider` (decoration: not exposed, takes no press). A seam between two items that rest on different fills carries none (BGR-24).
cssParts.name: divider

slots.description: The items: `<tanrei-button>` elements, with `confirming` or `dismissive` on the ones the group should place. Anything else is still laid out, and reported in debug builds (BGR-10).

members.name: variant
members.description:
`standard` spaces the buttons apart; `connected` joins them into one shape with rounded outer ends, by a divider or
by a narrow gap (`separation`), for a closely related set (Bold, Italic, Underline; Previous, Today, Next).
Anything else is drawn as `standard` (reported in debug builds, BGR-9).

members.name: orientation
members.description:
`horizontal` lays the buttons out in one row; `vertical` stacks them in one column, every button as wide as the
column. The confirming and dismissive buttons change places with it (BGR-13, BGR-14). Anything else is drawn as
`horizontal` (reported in debug builds, BGR-9).

members.name: separation
members.description:
How a connected group is joined. `divider`: the buttons touch, and a line is drawn on each seam. `gap`: they stand a
narrow gap apart, with tighter corners where they face each other. `auto` takes
`comp.button-group.connected.separation`, the design system's answer (divider in the default system). Ignored
while `variant` is `standard`. Anything else is `auto` (reported in debug builds, BGR-9).

members.name: fullWidth
members.description:
The group fills its container's width and its buttons share it equally (in a column, each is the container's
width): the `full-width` attribute. For the actions at the foot of a dialog, a picker or a side sheet.

members.name: label
members.description:
The group's accessible name ("Text style"). When it is set the group is a `role="group"` named by it; when it is
empty the group adds nothing to the accessibility tree, only its items (BGR-6).

members.name: placed
members.description: The children in the placed order (BGR-13, BGR-14): one slot each.

members.name: placement
members.description: BGR-13, BGR-14, BGR-18: the children by run, as a dialog's and a side sheet's actions are read (src/primitives/actions.ts).

members.name: system
members.description: BGR-21: where a browser has no style queries, the separation is read when the group renders — again when the system is switched.

members.description:
BGR-11: a child that comes or goes, or whose `confirming` or `dismissive` changes, is placed again at once. BGR-24:
one whose `selected`, `toggle` or `variant` changes has the lines beside it drawn again at once — in the same
frame: the observer runs before the next one is drawn.

members.name: drawn
members.description: The variant it draws: an unknown one is standard (BGR-9).

members.name: vertical
members.description: Whether it is a column: an unknown orientation is horizontal (BGR-9).

members.name: order
members.description: BGR-13, BGR-14: the three runs in the order of the orientation, each in the order its items were given.

members.name: read
members.description: BGR-11: the children are read into their runs and placed again — when they change, and when the orientation does.

members.name: place
members.description: BGR-1…4, BGR-11: every item is told its place at once.

members.name: restingFill
members.description:
BGR-24: the fill an item rests on, and whether it is an emphasis fill. The color is the one the Button renders its
container from at rest — `comp.button.<variant>.container.color`, and for a toggle the selected or the unselected
part of its variant (BTN-15) — read from the cascade where the item stands and resolved by the probe, so that two
tokens of one color in the active scheme are the same fill and a container that draws no fill is `none`. It is the
resting color whatever state the item is in, and the enabled one while it is disabled: hover, focus, press and
disabling move no line. Anything that is not a Button has no fill the group knows.

members.name: drawSeams
members.description:
BGR-22, BGR-24: what each seam carries. A line only while the two items it joins rest on the same fill; in the
on-fill color while both rest on an emphasis fill. Written on the dividers at once (no render, no animation).

members.name: checkContent
members.description: BGR-10: fewer than two items, or content that is not a Tanrei Button, still renders and is reported.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description:
`standard` spaces the buttons apart; `connected` joins them into one shape with rounded outer ends, by a divider or
by a narrow gap (`separation`), for a closely related set (Bold, Italic, Underline; Previous, Today, Next).
Anything else is drawn as `standard` (reported in debug builds, BGR-9).

declarations.description:
Performs a main action with one press, and offers related actions in a menu from a second, joined button beside it.

Contract: specs/button-with-menu.spec.json. Two native buttons in one row: the leading half (the optional icon and the
label) performs the main action and fires `click`; the trailing half (the chevron) asks to open or close the menu and
fires `toggle`. The menu is a Tanrei Menu in the shadow root, holding the `menu` slot's items, placed below the whole
button with menu with the end edges aligned; focus returns to the trailing half when it closes. It never opens or closes
itself: set `open` from `toggle`, and to false from `close`.

With `hover-open`, a mouse or a pen resting on the trailing half for `hover-delay` ms (unset: the
`comp.button-with-menu.motion.hover-open-delay` token) asks to open it too, through the same `toggle`. A menu open from
hover takes no focus, asks to close (`toggle` with false) once the pointer has been off the trailing half and the menu
for `motion.hover-close-delay`, and closes on Escape wherever focus is; a press or a key on the trailing half keeps it
open and moves focus in, as if that activation had opened it.

The halves are joined as `separation` names (SPB-30): under `divider` they touch, with square corners where they meet
and a line on the seam, and neither half draws its outline or its elevation's ring along the seam; under `gap` they
stand `container.inner-gap` apart with `container.inner-shape` corners. `auto` — the default — takes
`comp.button-with-menu.container.separation`, which follows the design system's `sys.behavior.separation`. They are
never stacked. `trailing-width="narrow"` draws a slim trailing half: the chevron and a small inset on each side, with
no padding added at its round end — as wide as a narrow icon-only Button (SPB-32).

Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-button-with-menu-*` tokens, one set per variant shared by both halves, each
half drawn in its own state: how a state looks is the active design system's decision, not this component's. How a
press is answered and how keyboard focus is drawn are the system's choices of kind (`--tanrei-sys-behavior-*`),
and how far its corners ease is the system's amount (`--tanrei-sys-shape-corner-smoothing`); all
are read from the cascade, so they follow `data-tanrei-system`.
declarations.name: TanreiButtonWithMenu

slots.description: The leading half's icon: a glyph of the system's icon set (its ligature text), or a `.tanrei-icon`, ``. A glyph the icon set flags is mirrored in right-to-left; `data-mirror="auto | always | never"` on the element decides for one use.
slots.name: icon

slots.description: The trailing half's glyph in place of `expand_more` (one glyph of the icon set). Alone, it turns half a turn while open; with `chevron-open` it is the closed form only.
slots.name: chevron

members.name: variant
members.description: Emphasis, as Button's variants of the same names.

members.name: size
members.description: Visual height (small 32 / medium 40 / large 56 in the default system), Button's heights. The hit areas always meet the minimum target.

members.name: separation
members.description:
How the two halves are joined. `divider`: they touch, and a line is drawn on the seam. `gap`: they stand a narrow gap
apart, with tighter corners where they face each other. `auto` takes `comp.button-with-menu.container.separation`,
the design system's answer (divider in the default system). The halves always sit side by side. Anything else is
`auto` (reported in debug builds, SPB-8).

members.name: trailingWidth
members.description:
How wide the trailing half is: `default` holds the chevron in a square of the height (32 / 40 / 56) and adds the
padding of the rounded outer end (36 / 44 / 60 in the default system); `narrow` is the chevron and
`trailing.padding-inline-narrow` on each side of it, with no outer padding (28 / 32 / 32: the width of a narrow
icon-only Button, SPB-32). The hit area meets the minimum target at both: a narrow half reaches it past its end
edge and is not drawn wider. The `trailing-width` attribute. Anything else is `default` (reported in debug
builds, SPB-8).

members.name: label
members.description: The leading half's visible text and accessible name ("Save"). Required.

members.name: menuLabel
members.description: The trailing half's accessible name ("More save options"): say what the menu offers. Required — the chevron alone is not a name.

members.name: open
members.description: Whether the menu is shown. Set it from `toggle`, and to false from `close`: the button with menu only asks.

members.name: disabled
members.description: Prevents interaction with both halves, removes them from the focus order and presents no menu.

members.name: hoverOpen
members.description: Also asks to open the menu when a mouse or a pen rests on the trailing half for `hoverDelay`; never for touch. A press and the keys still open it.

members.name: hoverDelay
members.description: How long, in ms, the pointer rests on the trailing half before the menu opens on hover. Unset (null) takes `comp.button-with-menu.motion.hover-open-delay`.

members.name: iconChildren
members.description: The children in the icon slot.

members.name: chevronChildren
members.description: SPB-21: the children in the chevron slots; each slot draws its first.

members.name: menuChildren
members.description: The children in the menu slot, each forwarded into the menu through a slot of its own.

members.name: turning
members.description: SPB-13, SPB-21: the open form is changing; the trailing half's corners move over the open motion until it is done.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description: Emphasis, as Button's variants of the same names.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: Visual height (small 32 / medium 40 / large 56 in the default system), Button's heights. The hit areas always meet the minimum target.

attributes.name: separation
attributes.description:
How the two halves are joined. `divider`: they touch, and a line is drawn on the seam. `gap`: they stand a narrow gap
apart, with tighter corners where they face each other. `auto` takes `comp.button-with-menu.container.separation`,
the design system's answer (divider in the default system). The halves always sit side by side. Anything else is
`auto` (reported in debug builds, SPB-8).

attributes.name: trailing-width
attributes.description:
How wide the trailing half is: `default` holds the chevron in a square of the height (32 / 40 / 56) and adds the
padding of the rounded outer end (36 / 44 / 60 in the default system); `narrow` is the chevron and
`trailing.padding-inline-narrow` on each side of it, with no outer padding (28 / 32 / 32: the width of a narrow
icon-only Button, SPB-32). The hit area meets the minimum target at both: a narrow half reaches it past its end
edge and is not drawn wider. The `trailing-width` attribute. Anything else is `default` (reported in debug
builds, SPB-8).

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: The leading half's visible text and accessible name ("Save"). Required.

attributes.name: menu-label
attributes.description: The trailing half's accessible name ("More save options"): say what the menu offers. Required — the chevron alone is not a name.

attributes.name: open
attributes.description: Whether the menu is shown. Set it from `toggle`, and to false from `close`: the button with menu only asks.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: Prevents interaction with both halves, removes them from the focus order and presents no menu.

attributes.name: hover-open
attributes.description: Also asks to open the menu when a mouse or a pen rests on the trailing half for `hoverDelay`; never for touch. A press and the keys still open it.

attributes.name: hover-delay
attributes.description: How long, in ms, the pointer rests on the trailing half before the menu opens on hover. Unset (null) takes `comp.button-with-menu.motion.hover-open-delay`.

declarations.description: The values every design system has. A layer may add more; those get their styles on demand.

BTN-12: the widths of an icon-only Button. A closed set: `default` is the height, `wide` a width of its size, and

declarations.name: AXES
declarations.default: [ { name: 'size', core: CORE_SIZES, default: DEFAULT_SIZE, rules: (value, selector) => sizeBlock(value, selector, DEFAULT_SIZE), probe: (value) => `${PREFIX}-container-height-${value}` }, { name: 'variant', core: CORE_VARIANTS, default: DEFAULT_VARIANT, rules: (value, selector) => variantBlock(value, selector, DEFAULT_VARIANT), probe: (value) => `${PREFIX}-${value}-container-color` }, ]
declarations.description:
The open axes (BTN-7): a size or variant a layer added gets its block on demand, built by the same functions
as the core blocks and falling back to the default's tokens; a value the active system lacks is reported in debug builds.

declarations.name: styles
declarations.description:
BTN-22: with a destination the container is an anchor, and it is the same styled part: every rule above that names
the native `button` names the anchor too, at the same weight (src/primitives/link.ts). Rules are written for
`button` alone, here and in what a button group adds (groupItemStyles); the link form follows them.

Lets people take an action, or switch something on and off, with one tap or click — named by a label, an icon, or both. Contract: specs/button.spec.json. Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-button-*` tokens, one set per state and, for a toggle, per selection: how a state looks is the active design system's decision, not this component's. How a press is answered and how keyboard focus is drawn are the system's choices of kind (`--tanrei-sys-behavior-*`), and how far its corners ease is the system's amount (`--tanrei-sys-shape-corner-smoothing`); all are read from the cascade, so they follow `data-tanrei-system`. The icon is the `icon` slot: a glyph of the system's icon set, given as its ligature text (`favorite`) or a `.tanrei-icon`, ``. With a label it sits on the side `icon-position` names; alone it is the button's only content, the button is as wide as it is high, and `label` is its accessible name. In a right-to-left layout a glyph given by name is drawn mirrored when the system's icon set says it shows a direction (`arrow_forward`, `chevron_right`, `send`; never `check`, `search` or `play_arrow`) — in its own box, on the side `icon-position` names (BTN-19). `data-mirror="never"` or `"always"` on the slotted element decides for one use; an `` is never mirrored for you. With `href` it is a link and not a button (BTN-22): the shadow root holds an `` in place of the `

The icon: a glyph of the system's icon set (its ligature text), or a `.tanrei-icon`, ``. A glyph the icon set flags is mirrored in right-to-left; `data-mirror="auto | always | never"` on the element decides for one use.

members.name: formAssociated
members.description: BTN-29: one of its form's controls, for its form owner and for a disabled fieldset (BTN-32).

members.name: variant
members.description:
Emphasis level. Use one filled button per view for the main action; an icon-only text button is the quiet icon
action of a toolbar or a row. Default filled; a Button placed as a dialog's or a side sheet's action without a
`variant` attribute takes the host's (DLG-20, SSH-17), and a side sheet's close button takes
`comp.side-sheet.close-button.variant` (SSH-5).

members.name: size
members.description: Visual height (small 32 / medium 40 / large 56), which is also an icon-only button's width at its default width. The hit area always meets the minimum target.

members.name: width
members.description:
How wide an icon-only button is: `default` as wide as it is high (32 / 40 / 56), `narrow` its glyph and
`comp.button.container.padding-inline-narrow` on each side of it (28 / 32 / 32 in the default system, whose inset
is 4 at every size; it has no narrow width of its own, so it follows its glyph) for a tight row of icon actions,
`wide` (40 / 52 / 72) for the one action of a row that should weigh more. Ignored with a label. The height does
not change, and the hit area meets the minimum target at every width — a narrow button is never drawn wider to
reach it. Anything else is drawn as `default` (reported in debug builds, BTN-21).

members.name: iconPosition
members.description: Which side of the label the icon sits on, in the reading direction. Ignored without a label or an icon.

members.name: toggle
members.description: Makes the button a two-state control: activation switches `selected`, and assistive technology announces it as pressed or not pressed.

members.name: selected
members.description: Whether a toggle is on. Ignored unless `toggle` is true.

members.name: disabled
members.description:
Prevents interaction and removes the button from the focus order. A disabled submit button sends nothing, and
still stops Enter from sending its form where it is the form's default button (BTN-32). A button that is not a
link is disabled as well by a `<fieldset disabled>` around it. A button disabled while it holds focus keeps it
until the next frame, as the platform's own does, and its `disabled` attribute is written then.

members.name: label
members.description:
The accessible name, where it is more than what the button draws. Required for an icon-only button. Beside a drawn
label it is the whole name in place of the drawn text, which stays drawn — for an action repeated in every row
(drawn "Reset", named "Reset: Spacing") — and it must contain the drawn text, so that a person who says what they
see is heard: a debug build reports one that does not, and the name stays what was given (BTN-16).

members.name: type
members.description:
Web only. What a press does to the button's form: `button` nothing (the default), `submit` asks it to submit as
the platform's own submit button does — after `click`, the form's validation, then its `submit` event — and
`reset` asks it to reset (BTN-27, BTN-28). Anything else is `button` and reported; a toggle and a link ignore it
(BTN-33). `formaction` and its siblings are not read.

members.name: name
members.description: Web only. With `value`, the pair sent with the form when this button is the one that submitted it; nothing is sent while it is empty (BTN-31).

members.name: value
members.description: Web only. What is sent under `name` when this button submitted the form.

members.name: href
members.description:
The destination: a URL, a path or a fragment. Not empty, the button is a link and not a button (BTN-22): the link
role, an `<a href>` in the shadow root, activated by Enter and not by Space, drawn exactly as the button it would
otherwise be. Ignored while `toggle` is set; white space is no destination, and a `javascript:` address or one that
cannot be read is refused and reported in debug builds (BTN-26).

members.name: target
members.description:
Where the destination opens: `same` (here) or `new` (a new tab or window, with `noopener`), which a labelled button
marks with the glyph `open_in_new` after its label and says through `targetLabel` (BTN-24). HTML's `_self` and
`_blank` are read as those two; anything else is `same` and reported. Ignored without `href`.

members.name: targetLabel
members.description: What assistive technology reads after the link's name while `target` is `new` ("opens in a new tab"): your words, in your language. Required then; ignored otherwise.

members.name: rel
members.description: Web only: forwarded to the anchor's `rel`; `target="new"` adds `noopener` to it. Ignored without `href`.

members.name: download
members.description: Web only: forwarded to the anchor's `download` (the file name; empty for the address's own). Ignored without `href`.

members.name: drawnDisabled
members.description: Whether the last render drew the button as disabled: compared once the update has reflected `disabled` (BTN-32).

members.name: watchedForm
members.description: The form whose native controls are listened to for this submit button (BTN-30), so it can be let go.

members.name: hasIcon
members.description: Whether the icon slot has content.

members.name: hasLabel
members.description: Whether the default slot has content: without it the button is icon-only (BTN-12).

members.name: axes
members.default: new OpenAxesController(this, { component: 'button', behavior: 'BTN-7', axes: AXES })
members.description:
BTN-7: a size or variant the core does not have was added by a design system: its stylesheet is adopted,
built once per value for the page. Tokens the active system lacks fall back to the default's, and a value the
active system does not have is reported in debug builds (src/primitives/axes.ts).

members.name: mirror
members.description:
BTN-19: the glyph in the icon slot is marked when the icon set mirrors its name in right-to-left, or the product's
`data-mirror` says so (src/primitives/glyph-mirror.ts); `iconGlyph()` draws the mark.

members.name: link
members.default: new LinkController(this, { ids: { refused: 'BTN-26', newContext: 'BTN-24' }, disabled: () => this.disabled, holds: () => (this.toggle ? 'a toggle' : null), })
members.description:
BTN-22 … BTN-26: the link the button is while it has a destination, what its anchor carries, and what a debug
build is told (src/primitives/link.ts). A toggle holds a state and takes none (BTN-26).

members.name: press
members.default: new PressController(this, { container: () => this.container, holdCarrier: () => this.container?.querySelector(this.hasLabel ? '.label' : 'slot[name="icon"]') ?? null, disabled: () => this.isDisabled, keys: () => this.link.pressKeys, })
members.description:
BTN-8 / BTN-9: the pressed state, press-hold and the answer the system chooses (src/primitives/press.ts). BTN-23: a
link is pressed by Enter alone; Space is the browser's.

members.name: container
members.description: The native button, or the anchor of the link form: the one styled part (BTN-22).

members.name: form
members.description:
The form the button belongs to (BTN-29): the nearest form around it, or the one its `form` attribute names by id.
Read-only, as the platform's own button has it; null where there is none.

members.name: isDisabled
members.description:
BTN-32: disabled by its own `disabled`, or — unless it is a link, as no link of the platform is — by a disabled
fieldset around it. The fieldset's part is the platform's word (`:disabled`) less the element's own attribute:
that attribute follows the property one step late — it is still there while the update that unsets it renders —
and a button enabled by its property is enabled by that same update, so that focus can be moved to it at once.

members.name: formAction
members.description: BTN-33: what a press does to the form now — nothing for a toggle, a link, and a type the button does not define.

members.name: formDisabledCallback
members.description: BTN-32: the platform's word changed — a fieldset around the button was disabled or enabled: it is drawn again, at once.

members.name: setAttribute
members.description:
BTN-2: a button disabled while it holds focus is disabled at once — its property, the native button inside, what
it emits, Tab — and lets go of focus as the platform's own button does, at the next frame in every engine: its
`disabled` attribute, which is the platform's word for a form-associated element and takes focus within the call
in one engine, is written when focus has left, a frame later at most (src/primitives/disabled-while-focused.ts).
The property's reflection comes through here as the page's own `setAttribute` does.

members.name: formAssociatedCallback
members.description: BTN-29: the form owner changed — the button moved, or its `form` attribute was written.

members.name: watch
members.description: BTN-30: while it is a submit button of a form, Enter in the platform's own inputs of that form is listened to.

members.name: onFocus
members.description: BTN-10: where style queries are missing, the focus style is read when focus arrives.

members.name: onFormClick
members.description:
BTN-27, BTN-28: after `click` has gone through the page (src/primitives/after-click.ts) and the product has not
cancelled it, a submit button asks its form to submit and a reset button asks it to reset. The form is read then
(BTN-29). Not held for the press-hold time: the pressed state is shown and the work starts at once.

members.name: submit
members.description:
BTN-31: the platform lets only its own buttons be a submitter, so the form is asked through a submit button of the
platform's own that holds this button's name and value and lasts no longer than the dispatch: the validation, the
`submit` event, `event.submitter` and `new FormData(form, event.submitter)` are the platform's. It stands where
this button stands — a child of it in a slot it does not have, drawn nowhere, naming the same form where this
button names one — so the pair is sent at the button's own place among the form's entries, as the platform's own
button's is; and it is gone when the call returns, also when a listener throws.

members.name: click
members.description:
`element.click()` activates the button as a person would — through the native button, so a toggle switches and
fires `change`, and through the anchor, so a link is followed — and does nothing while disabled.

members.name: onClick
members.description:
BTN-14: a toggle switches its own `selected`, then fires `click`, then `change` (src/primitives/after-click.ts): a
`click` listener on the element already sees the new value, and `change` follows once the click has gone through the page.

members.name: reportType
members.description: BTN-33: a type the button does not define, and a type a toggle or a link ignores. Each once.

members.name: drawnText
members.description: The text the default slot draws.

members.name: reportName
members.description:
BTN-16: a name beside a drawn label must contain the drawn text, so that a person who says the word they see is
heard. The report is all the button does about it: `label` stays the whole name.

events.name: change

declarations.name: PROGRESS
declarations.default: '--_tanrei-calendar-progress'
declarations.description:
CAL-29: the ONE progress every look between two months is drawn from, a custom property of `.pages` that the element
writes and no one registers — 0 at the first view the grid holds, 1 at the next (and 2 at a third, while a change
begins during another or a drag may go either way). A drag and a scroll write it in each frame; a button's, a key's
or a wheel's change writes it in each frame of the page motion, by a clock of the element's (calendar.ts, `travel`).
The rows' offset, a day's fade and the mix of a day's two conditions are `calc()`s of it — steps and clamps of it,
which no transition of a real property could follow — so a moment of a button's change and a drag held at that place
are one look, and nothing has a threshold. `.pages` holds it and the rows and the days inherit it.

declarations.description:
Shows one month as a grid of days, in the page or inside a picker, and lets a person choose one date or one range of
dates from it.

Contract: specs/calendar.spec.json. The calendar draws no surface and no padding of its own: it is seven cells wide
(never wider than its container) and the page, or the picker that holds it, gives it its background. It commits each
choice itself — it sets `value` (or `start` and `end`) and then fires `change` — and is not form-associated: the
product's field is. Months move by the previous and next buttons, Page Up / Page Down, and along the axis the design
system names (`comp.calendar.navigation.axis`, vertical by default) by a wheel or trackpad scroll and by a drag of a
finger, a pen or the primary mouse button: the days follow either point for point — a scroll through month after
month, a drag to the neighbouring month — and settle on the neighbour from a quarter of the way on. A wheel that
reports lines or pages moves one month a step.

Dates are ISO 8601 calendar dates ("2026-09-17") without a time or a time zone. Month and weekday names, digits and
the first day of the week come from `Intl` for `locale` — without it, the nearest `lang` attribute, then the browser's
language. Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-calendar-*` tokens; the navigation buttons are
`<tanrei-button variant="text">` elements that keep their own. `focus()` moves focus to the active day (or the
displayed year in the year view).

cssParts.name: view-toggle
