members.name: words
members.description: CAL-35: the product's words, read where the instance gives none (src/primitives/words.ts).

members.name: mode
members.description: `single`: one date, in `value`. `range`: one contiguous span, from `start` to `end` inclusive. Reflected.

members.name: value
members.description: The chosen date in single mode, as an ISO 8601 calendar date ("2026-09-17"); empty when none is chosen.

members.name: start
members.description: The first date of the chosen range in range mode; empty when none is chosen.

members.name: end
members.description: The last date of the chosen range in range mode, never before `start`; empty while only `start` is chosen.

members.name: min
members.description: The earliest date that can be chosen; empty for no limit.

members.name: max
members.description: The latest date that can be chosen; empty for no limit.

members.name: disabledDates
members.description: Dates inside min and max that cannot be chosen (booked, closed). The `disabled-dates` attribute is a space-separated list or a JSON array.

members.name: isDateDisabled
members.description: A rule no list can hold (every weekend): true for an ISO date that cannot be chosen. Read with `disabledDates`. Property only.

members.name: today
members.description: The date drawn as today; empty reads the device's current date in its own time zone (and again at midnight).

members.name: firstDayOfWeek
members.description: The weekday in the first column (`first-day-of-week`); `locale` takes it from the locale.

members.name: locale
members.description: A BCP 47 tag ("en-US", "ja-JP") for names, digits and the first day of the week; empty: the nearest `lang`, then the browser's.

members.name: startView
members.description: Whether the calendar first shows the days of a month or the list of years (`start-view`).

members.name: showAdjacentDays
members.description: Fills the spare cells with the neighbouring months' days, drawn quieter; they can be chosen (`show-adjacent-days`).

members.name: label
members.description: The accessible name of the whole calendar ("Check-in date"); a picker that holds it names it itself.

members.name: startLabel
members.description: Range mode: the description of the start day (`start-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ startLabel })`). Tanrei has none: without them the day has no description.

members.name: endLabel
members.description: Range mode: the description of the end day (`end-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ endLabel })`). Tanrei has none: without them the day has no description.

members.name: previousMonthLabel
members.description: The previous-month button's accessible name (`previous-month-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ previousMonthLabel })`). Tanrei has none: without them the button is drawn and works, and has no name.

members.name: nextMonthLabel
members.description: The next-month button's accessible name (`next-month-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ nextMonthLabel })`). Tanrei has none: without them the button is drawn and works, and has no name.

members.name: yearViewLabel
members.description: The view toggle's description; its name is the month and year it shows (`year-view-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ yearViewLabel })`). Tanrei has none: without them the toggle has no description.

members.name: todayLabel
members.description: Read after the current year. Today's date is `aria-current="date"` on the web, so it is not added to a day (`today-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ todayLabel })`), else the locale's own word for the present day, from the browser.

members.name: month
members.description: The displayed month.

members.name: active
members.description: The day grid's one tab stop (CAL-10).

members.name: activeYear
members.description: The year list's one tab stop (CAL-12).

members.name: announcement
members.description: The polite announcement of a new month (CAL-13).

members.name: deviceDate
members.description: The device's date while `today` is empty, read again at midnight (CAL-24).

members.name: views
members.description:
CAL-29: the views the grid holds, earliest first — the displayed month alone at rest; while a change plays or a drag
lasts, also the months the days move between. The progress counts them: 0 at the first, 1 at the next.

members.name: step

type.text: { jump: number | null; to: number } | null

members.description: The progress to write once the views are rendered: `jump` at once (where the days are now), then `to` over the page motion.

members.name: travel

type.text: { clock: Animation; from: number; to: number; frame: number } | null

members.description:
CAL-14, CAL-29: the progress on its way from one place to another over the page motion. The progress is a custom
property that no one registers — a registered one makes every transition of the page dear —
so it has no transition of its own: `clock` is an
animation with no effect on the grid, running for the page motion's duration on its curve, and each frame writes
the progress where the clock's eased time says it is. A moment of it and a drag held at that place are one look.

members.name: drag
members.description: CAL-30: the press that may become a drag, or the drag.

members.name: focusAfter
members.description: Where focus goes after the next update, and whether it shows its ring (true after a key, false after a press).

members.name: yearsHeld
members.description:
The year list holds its years: while the year view is shown, and until it has faded out after it (CAL-6's
cross-fade). A calendar in its day view holds none of them — two hundred and one buttons, most of what a calendar
would otherwise be made of, and a picker's date view is a calendar.

members.name: ownChoice
members.description: The calendar set its own choice (CAL-17 is about a date the product sets).

members.name: wheel
members.description: CAL-33, CAL-34: the scroll in progress, if any.

members.name: swallowClick
members.description: CAL-30, CAL-31: the click a taken drag's release still produces chooses no day.

members.name: pressedBox
members.description: CAL-20, CAL-21: the press of a day, a year or the view toggle — whichever container `pressedBox` is.

members.name: press
members.default: new PressController(this, { container: () => this.pressedBox, holdCarrier: () => this.renderRoot?.querySelector('.hold') ?? null, disabled: () => !!this.pressedBox?.closest('[aria-disabled="true"]'), })

members.name: scheduleMidnight
members.description: CAL-24: while `today` is empty, the device's date is read again when it changes (at the next local midnight).

members.name: focus
members.description: Moves focus to the active day, or to the displayed year in the year view (CAL-10, CAL-12).

members.name: resolveLocale
members.description: CAL-24: `locale`, else the nearest `lang` (through shadow roots), else the browser's language; English when `Intl` does not know it.

members.name: homeMonth
members.description: CAL-17: the month of value or start, otherwise of today, between min's and max's months.

members.name: activeDayOf
members.description: CAL-10: the chosen date (start) in the month, otherwise today there, otherwise its first available day, otherwise its first.

members.name: dayCondition
members.description: CAL-2: the condition a day is drawn from, by precedence.

members.name: readAxis
members.description: The axis the months move along, read from the cascade now (never cached).

members.name: stepsOf
members.description: CAL-29: how far apart two consecutive views are — the rows between their first rows (four or five) for neighbouring months, six otherwise; one page on the horizontal axis.

members.name: weekRows
members.description: CAL-29: the column of week rows the views hold, in order: a row two views share is there once.

members.name: progressNow
members.description: Where the days are now, as the progress drawn (a moment of a travel included).

members.name: pageMotion
members.description: The page motion, as the day view carries it — it cross-fades over it (CAL-14): its duration in ms and its curve.

members.name: canTravel
members.description: Whether a month change can play: not where motion is reduced, the page motion is none, or the browser has no animation to keep its time.

members.name: travelling
members.description: Whether the progress is on its way somewhere.

members.name: travelAt

type.text: { clock: Animation; from: number; to: number }

members.description: Where a travel's clock says the progress is: its eased time, between where it began and where it goes.

members.name: beginTravel
members.description: CAL-14, CAL-29: sends the progress from `from` to `to` over the page motion, written in each frame; at once where no change can play.

members.name: endTravel
members.description: Stops a travel where it is: whoever stops it writes the progress next.

members.name: pin
members.description: CAL-29: the grid keeps its six rows' height while it holds more (the rows of a month's view are equally tall).

members.name: rest
members.description: The days are at the displayed month's view, and the grid holds that view alone.

members.name: showMonth
members.description:
CAL-14, CAL-29: shows `month`. With the motion, the days travel there from where they are now — the views on screen
stay, the new month's joins them, and the progress goes to it over the page motion — so a change that begins while
another plays carries on without a jump. Without it (CAL-7, CAL-17, reduced motion) the month is shown at once.

members.name: applyStep
members.description: Writes the progress the last render asked for (see `step`), and rests when it has nowhere to travel.

members.name: onTravelEnd
members.description: CAL-14, CAL-31: the travel has ended — the grid holds the displayed month's view alone again.

members.name: turnTo
members.description:
CAL-13: `month` is shown — the active day keeps its number (the last day of a shorter month), the month is announced
once, and focus stays where it was: a focused day that leaves the view hands it to the new active day.

members.name: carryActive
members.description: CAL-13: the active day keeps its number in `month`, and a day that had the focus hands it to the new active day.

members.name: keepPagingFocus
members.description:
CAL-13: a month button that has just shown the first or the last month is disabled under the focus it holds, and a
disabled button holds none: focus stays in the calendar, on the other month button — the one that leads back — or,
where that one is disabled too (the product moved min or max under it), on the active day. It is moved within the
turn that disables the button — once the other button, which this update may have just enabled, has drawn itself
so — before the platform takes focus, so focus is never on nothing and nothing hears it leave.

members.name: pageBy
members.description: CAL-13: the previous or next month, never past min's or max's.

members.name: onToggleView
members.description: CAL-6: the view toggle switches between the day view and the year view.

members.name: chooseYear
members.description: CAL-7: a year is chosen — the day view of the displayed month in that year, focus to its active day; the choice is unchanged.

members.name: onWheel
members.description:
CAL-33: a wheel or trackpad scroll along the axis is the calendar's — also where the days can move no further — and
one across it, or one that zooms, is left to the scrolling ancestor. A scroll reported as a distance is followed; one
reported in lines or pages is a detented wheel's step, and moves one month as a button does.

members.name: followScroll
members.description:
CAL-33, CAL-34: one event of a scroll, `distance` px toward the next month, at `time`. The days move by it, unless
the scroll has ended: it ends when it has slowed below `SCROLL_SLOW` — having been that fast: a scroll that never
was has not slowed, and is followed until it is quiet — and what follows is ignored for as long as it is no faster
(the tail of a momentum scroll). A faster event (by `SCROLL_RESUME`) is a new push, and moves the days again from
where they are.

members.name: onScrollQuiet
members.description: CAL-34: no event for `SCROLL_QUIET` ms — the scroll is over; days it still holds settle.

members.name: beginScroll
members.description:
CAL-33: the days begin to follow a scroll, as a drag takes them without a pointer: the progress is held where the
days are now (a change that is playing carries on from there, CAL-14), and the grid holds the displayed month's view
and its neighbours'.

members.name: moveScroll
members.description:
CAL-33: the days move `travel` rows (or pages) toward the next month — toward the previous one when negative — one
point for each point, in the frame the event arrives. When they reach a neighbouring month's view that month is the
displayed one (CAL-34: shown, not announced), the grid holds its neighbours', and the scroll carries on with what is
left; where there is no further view (min's or max's month) they stop.

members.name: reachView
members.description: CAL-34: the days have reached `month`'s view — it is the displayed month (CAL-13, without the announcement), between its neighbours'.

members.name: settleScroll
members.description:
CAL-34: the scroll has ended. Between two views the days go to the neighbour's from a quarter of the way on, and
otherwise return, over the page motion (at once where motion is reduced, CAL-32); the month is announced once, if it
is not the one displayed when the scroll began.

members.name: dropScroll
members.description:
CAL-14: something else moves the month (a button, a key, a drag): the scroll no longer holds the days, which stay
where it left them for that to carry on from. A month the scroll had reached is announced, as its end would have.

members.name: cancelScroll
members.description: CAL-32: the scroll is cancelled — the days return to the displayed month's view, nothing is announced, and what is left of it is ignored.

members.name: forgetScroll
members.description: The scroll has nothing left to move (the grid is drawn anew, or gone).

members.name: onDragDown
members.description: CAL-30: a press of touch, a pen or the primary button of a mouse on the day grid may become a drag; another mouse button takes none.

members.name: takeDrag
members.description:
CAL-30: past the slop, further along the axis than across it — the drag is the calendar's. The press chooses no day
and the day under it leaves its pressed state; the grid holds the displayed month's view and its neighbours' (never
one past min or max), and from now on the progress is the pointer's — wherever it goes, since the grid captures it.
While it lasts nothing in the calendar is hovered and a fine pointer shows the grabbing cursor (`data-dragging`).

members.name: followDrag
members.description:
CAL-30: the days move by the distance the pointer has travelled along the axis since the press, in the frame it
moves — toward the next month for a drag toward the top (or the start), wherever the pointer goes in either layout
direction (CAL-26) — and stop at the neighbouring month's view.

members.name: onDragUp
members.description:
CAL-31: the release chooses the displayed month or the neighbour the days have moved toward — the neighbour from a
quarter of the way on (as the end of a scroll does, CAL-34), or the one a fling is toward — shows it as any month change (CAL-13) and lets the
days travel there from where they are; a release on the displayed month returns them and announces nothing.

members.name: onDragCancel
members.description: CAL-32: the platform cancels the pointer (a system gesture, a lost capture): the days return.

members.name: onDragKeyDown
members.description: CAL-32: Escape while a drag lasts cancels it, and is spent on it: nothing behind the calendar hears it.

members.name: cancelDrag
members.description: CAL-32: the drag is over without a choice — the days return to the displayed month's view; nothing is announced.

members.name: dropDrag
members.description:
Lets go of the pointer, without moving anything. The progress stays held where the drag left it until the next
step is written (`applyStep`), so that no style read in between starts a travel from somewhere else.

members.name: endDrag
members.description:
CAL-31, CAL-32: the drag ends on the view at `index`. Another month than the displayed one is shown as CAL-13 says;
the days go there from where the pointer left them over the page motion — at once where motion is reduced.

members.name: moveActive
members.description: CAL-11: moves the active day (showing its month) and focus to it, never before min or after max.

members.name: onGridMouseDown
members.description: CAL-15: a press on a neighbouring month's day moves no focus by itself: the day takes it once its month is shown, if focus was in the grid.

members.name: scrollYears
members.description: CAL-7: the displayed year's row is the third in view, or as near to it as the list's ends allow.

members.name: onYearsFaded
members.description: The year list has faded out (its `visibility` is the last to change): the day view holds no year.

members.name: releaseYears
members.description: Lets go of the years once the day view is shown and the list is out of sight (at once where nothing fades).

members.name: revealYear
members.description: CAL-12: the focused year scrolled into view inside the list.

members.name: reportWords
members.description:
CAL-35: a part that needs a word nobody gave — not the instance, not the product's words — is still drawn and
works; it is recorded (`missingWords()`) and, in a debug build, reported once, naming the prop. The view toggle's
description is not one of them: its name and its expanded state already say what it shows.

members.name: renderDay
members.description: The day grid's item: one day, a gridcell with its condition and state (CAL-2, CAL-3, CAL-15, CAL-16, CAL-23).

members.name: renderColumn
members.description:
CAL-29: the day grid on the vertical axis — ONE column of week rows, keyed by their first day, holding the rows of
every view the grid holds: the displayed month's six at rest, and those of the months the days move between while a
change plays or a drag lasts. Each day is drawn between what the views draw for it, by the progress: faded where a
view does not draw it (a row outside its six; an empty cell without showAdjacentDays), mixed between the adjacent
and the unselected condition where it is a neighbouring month's in one view and the month's own in another. What the
displayed month's view does not hold is inert and hidden until that month is the displayed one (CAL-32).

members.name: renderPages
members.description:
CAL-14, CAL-30: the day grid on the horizontal axis — a page a view, side by side in order, travelling together by
the progress. The displayed month's page is the grid's; the others are inert and hidden until theirs is (CAL-32).

members.name: renderYear
members.description: The year list's item: one year, a button with its condition (CAL-2, CAL-7, CAL-23).

members.name: glyphs
members.description:
CAL-5: the arrows follow the axis — up and down, or back and forward. The names never change with the direction:
arrow_back and arrow_forward are flagged by the icon set, so each Button's icon helper mirrors its glyph in
right-to-left (BTN-19), and previous still points to the start edge.

events.name: change
events.description: The person chose a day that changes the choice. `value`, `start` and `end` are already the new ones (end empty after a start alone); `detail` holds them too.

attributes.name: mode
attributes.description: `single`: one date, in `value`. `range`: one contiguous span, from `start` to `end` inclusive. Reflected.

attributes.name: value
attributes.description: The chosen date in single mode, as an ISO 8601 calendar date ("2026-09-17"); empty when none is chosen.

attributes.name: start
attributes.description: The first date of the chosen range in range mode; empty when none is chosen.

attributes.name: end
attributes.description: The last date of the chosen range in range mode, never before `start`; empty while only `start` is chosen.

attributes.name: min
attributes.description: The earliest date that can be chosen; empty for no limit.

attributes.name: max
attributes.description: The latest date that can be chosen; empty for no limit.

attributes.name: disabled-dates
attributes.description: Dates inside min and max that cannot be chosen (booked, closed). The `disabled-dates` attribute is a space-separated list or a JSON array.

attributes.name: today
attributes.description: The date drawn as today; empty reads the device's current date in its own time zone (and again at midnight).

attributes.name: first-day-of-week
attributes.description: The weekday in the first column (`first-day-of-week`); `locale` takes it from the locale.

attributes.name: locale
attributes.description: A BCP 47 tag ("en-US", "ja-JP") for names, digits and the first day of the week; empty: the nearest `lang`, then the browser's.

attributes.name: start-view
attributes.description: Whether the calendar first shows the days of a month or the list of years (`start-view`).

attributes.name: show-adjacent-days
attributes.description: Fills the spare cells with the neighbouring months' days, drawn quieter; they can be chosen (`show-adjacent-days`).

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: The accessible name of the whole calendar ("Check-in date"); a picker that holds it names it itself.

attributes.name: start-label
attributes.description: Range mode: the description of the start day (`start-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ startLabel })`). Tanrei has none: without them the day has no description.

attributes.name: end-label
attributes.description: Range mode: the description of the end day (`end-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ endLabel })`). Tanrei has none: without them the day has no description.

attributes.name: previous-month-label
attributes.description: The previous-month button's accessible name (`previous-month-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ previousMonthLabel })`). Tanrei has none: without them the button is drawn and works, and has no name.

attributes.name: next-month-label
attributes.description: The next-month button's accessible name (`next-month-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ nextMonthLabel })`). Tanrei has none: without them the button is drawn and works, and has no name.

attributes.name: year-view-label
attributes.description: The view toggle's description; its name is the month and year it shows (`year-view-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ yearViewLabel })`). Tanrei has none: without them the toggle has no description.

attributes.name: today-label
attributes.description: Read after the current year. Today's date is `aria-current="date"` on the web, so it is not added to a day (`today-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ todayLabel })`), else the locale's own word for the present day, from the browser.

declarations.name: CORE_VARIANTS
declarations.default: ['tonal', 'outlined']
declarations.description: The values every design system has. A layer may add more; those get their styles on demand.

declarations.name: CORE_SIZES
declarations.default: ['medium', 'large']

declarations.name: STATUSES
declarations.default: ['info', 'warning', 'error', 'success']
declarations.description: The statuses besides `default`: a closed set (CLO-30), each a prefix before the callout's parts (CLO-3).

declarations.name: AXES
declarations.default: [ { name: 'size', core: CORE_SIZES, default: DEFAULT_SIZE, rules: (value, selector) => sizeBlock(value, selector, DEFAULT_SIZE), probe: (value) => `${PREFIX}-body-typescale-${value}-font` }, { name: 'variant', core: CORE_VARIANTS, default: DEFAULT_VARIANT, rules: (value, selector) => variantBlock(value, selector, DEFAULT_VARIANT), probe: (value) => `${PREFIX}-container-color-${value}` }, ]
declarations.description:
The open axes (CLO-30): a size or variant a layer added gets its block on demand, built by the same
functions as the core blocks and falling back to the default's tokens; a value the active system lacks is reported in
debug builds. A variant a layer adds has no edge: only `outlined` draws one (CLO-4).

declarations.description:
A notice that is part of the content and stays there, as a quiet fill or an outline, in a status's colors with its glyph.
A note, a caution, the reason for something or a summary of what is wrong, in the flow of the page, with an optional
title, actions and a close button.

Contract: specs/callout.spec.json. `<tanrei-callout status="warning">…</tanrei-callout>`: the body is the element's
own content (text, or the product's blocks — long-form blocks in a `<div class="tanrei-prose" data-measure="false">`),
the title is the `headline` attribute or the `title` slot, a glyph of the icon set goes in the `icon` slot, and the
product's Buttons or links in the `actions` slot. Every visual value is a `--tanrei-comp-callout-*` token, one set per
variant and status; how far its corners ease is the system's amount (`--tanrei-sys-shape-corner-smoothing`).

It is a note (`role="note"`), read where it stands and never announced. With `live` it is a live region instead: it
is announced once when it is shown after the page was presented and when its title, body or status changes — politely
(`role="status"`), or assertively for warning and error (`role="alert"`). It never takes focus.

A status is never told by color alone: a status form draws the status's glyph, and the title says it or
`statusLabel` adds it in words for assistive technology ("Warning, …") without drawing it.

`title` is the `headline` property and attribute, because HTML's global `title` would show a tooltip over the block.
`open` defaults to true; `open="false"` is how markup starts a callout closed.

cssParts.description: The block: its fill, its edge in the outlined look, its corners and paddings.
cssParts.name: container

cssParts.description: The box the glyph is drawn in (hidden from assistive technology).
cssParts.name: icon

cssParts.description: The title.
cssParts.name: title

cssParts.description: The body.
cssParts.name: body

cssParts.description: The row of actions.
cssParts.name: actions

cssParts.description: The close button.
cssParts.name: close

slots.description: The body: text, or the product's own blocks (paragraphs, lists, a table, a code block, any component). Text placed directly takes the callout's text style and color; long-form blocks go in a `<div class="tanrei-prose" data-measure="false">` (with `data-size="large"` in a large callout).

A glyph of the system's icon set (its ligature text, in an element), drawn in place of the status glyph, or as the glyph of a callout without a status. A glyph the icon set flags is mirrored in right-to-left; `data-mirror="auto | always | never"` on the element decides for one use.
slots.name: icon

slots.description: The product's own title content in place of `headline`: text with inline content, or a heading of the level the page's outline needs. It is drawn in the title's style; its role and its level are not changed.
slots.name: title

slots.description: The product's own Buttons or links, one or two, laid out in a row below the text.
slots.name: actions

members.name: words
members.description: The product's words, read where the instance gives none (src/primitives/words.ts).

members.name: headline
members.description: A few words above the body that name the notice ("Not published yet"): the spec's `title`. Plain text, never a heading. Empty draws the body alone; the `title` slot takes its place.

members.name: status
members.description: What the notice is: default (a neutral aside, no glyph unless the product gives one), info, warning, error or success, each in its colors with its glyph. A live callout is announced assertively for warning and error.

members.name: statusLabel
members.description: The status in words ("Warning"), read by assistive technology before the title and the body and not drawn. For a callout whose title does not itself say the status. Ignored while `status` is default.

members.name: variant
members.description: How much the callout weighs: tonal is a quiet fill; outlined has no fill and one hairline, for a tinted surface or many callouts close together.

members.name: size
members.description: The size of the text: medium sets it in the interface's text style, large in the style for long reading. Paddings, the glyph and the close button are the same at both.

members.name: live
members.description: Whether the callout is announced: false is a note, read where it stands; true is a live region, announced once when it is shown after the page was presented and when its content changes. It changes nothing that is drawn.

members.name: closable
members.description: Draws a close button, for a notice the person may put away.

members.name: closeLabel
members.description: The close button's accessible name, in the product's language ("Close"). Required while `closable` is set.

members.name: open
members.description: Whether the callout is shown. The close button sets it to false. The attribute: absent is true, `open="false"` is false.

members.name: hasIcon
members.description: Whether the icon slot has content.

members.name: hasTitle
members.description: Whether the title slot has content.

members.name: hasBody
members.description: Whether the default slot has content: an element, or text that is not white space.

members.name: hasActions
members.description: Whether the actions slot has content.

members.name: placed
members.description: CLO-23: the actions that were told their place.

members.name: axes
members.default: new OpenAxesController(this, { component: 'callout', behavior: 'CLO-30', axes: AXES })
members.description: CLO-30: sizes and variants a design system adds, and a value the active system does not have (src/primitives/axes.ts).

members.name: mirror
members.description:
CLO-27: the glyph in the icon slot is marked when the icon set mirrors its name in right-to-left, or the product's
`data-mirror` says so; the callout's own glyphs go through the same rule, which marks none of them under the
default icon set. `iconGlyph()` draws the mark. The callout mirrors nothing itself.

members.name: glyphs
members.description: CLO-29: each glyph box carries `data-drawn` while the icon set can draw its ligature; until then it draws nothing.

members.name: press
members.default: new PressController(this, { container: () => this.renderRoot?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.close') ?? null, holdCarrier: () => this.renderRoot.querySelector('.close .hold'), disabled: () => false, })
members.description: CLO-17, CLO-18: the close button's pressed state.

members.name: internals
members.description: CLO-31: the custom state the styles read to take an empty callout out of the layout.

members.name: cameFrom
members.description: CLO-12: the element that had focus before focus entered the callout.

members.name: upgraded
members.description:
CLO-21: whether this callout was already in the document when its element was made — written in the page's markup
and upgraded — which is being drawn with the page's first presentation.

members.name: announceFirst
members.description: CLO-21: whether its first render is announced: it was added by the product after the page was presented.

members.name: presented
members.description: Whether it has been drawn once: what changes after that is a change.

members.name: content$
members.description: CLO-21: hears the title and the body change while it is live.

members.name: form
members.description: CLO-30: a status this spec does not have is `default`.

members.name: assertive
members.description: CLO-21: warning and error are announced assertively, as a snackbar's.

members.name: empty
members.description: CLO-31: neither a title nor a body — a glyph, actions or a close button alone are not a notice.

members.name: slottedTitle
members.description: The element in the title slot, if any.

members.name: scan
members.description: What the light DOM holds for each slot, read from the children: they are there before a slot says so.

members.name: place
members.description: CLO-23: every action is told its place, and one that is an action no more is told it has none.

members.name: holds
members.description: Whether `node` is in the callout: its own content or its shadow root.

members.name: onFocusIn
members.description: CLO-12: where focus was before it entered the callout.

members.name: onClose
members.description:
CLO-11: the close button, by pointer, touch, Enter or Space (the native button's click): `open` becomes false,
focus goes back where it was before it entered the callout (CLO-12), and `dismiss` says the person closed it — once.

members.name: onFocus
members.description: CLO-19: where style queries are missing, the focus style is read when focus arrives.

members.name: announce
members.description:
CLO-21: announced once — through the live region of its politeness, a frame after both were emptied, so that a text
equal to the last one is announced again. Nothing is announced while it is not live, not open or empty. The two
regions carry `aria-live` and no role: the role is the host's, and a note must not hold an empty alert.

members.name: onContent
members.description: CLO-21: a change of the title or the body while it is shown; what changes inside a glyph or an action is not one.

events.description: The person closed the callout with its close button. Fired once, after `open` became false; never when the product sets `open`.
events.name: dismiss

attributes.name: headline
attributes.description: A few words above the body that name the notice ("Not published yet"): the spec's `title`. Plain text, never a heading. Empty draws the body alone; the `title` slot takes its place.

attributes.name: status
attributes.description: What the notice is: default (a neutral aside, no glyph unless the product gives one), info, warning, error or success, each in its colors with its glyph. A live callout is announced assertively for warning and error.

attributes.name: status-label
attributes.description: The status in words ("Warning"), read by assistive technology before the title and the body and not drawn. For a callout whose title does not itself say the status. Ignored while `status` is default.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description: How much the callout weighs: tonal is a quiet fill; outlined has no fill and one hairline, for a tinted surface or many callouts close together.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: The size of the text: medium sets it in the interface's text style, large in the style for long reading. Paddings, the glyph and the close button are the same at both.

attributes.name: live
attributes.description: Whether the callout is announced: false is a note, read where it stands; true is a live region, announced once when it is shown after the page was presented and when its content changes. It changes nothing that is drawn.

attributes.name: closable
attributes.description: Draws a close button, for a notice the person may put away.

attributes.name: close-label
attributes.description: The close button's accessible name, in the product's language ("Close"). Required while `closable` is set.

attributes.name: open
attributes.description: Whether the callout is shown. The close button sets it to false. The attribute: absent is true, `open="false"` is false.

declarations.description:
Sets a group of related content apart from its background, and can be one action that opens what it shows.

Contract: specs/card.spec.json. Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-card-*` tokens, one set per variant and
state: how a state looks is the active design system's decision, not this component's. How a press is answered and
how keyboard focus is drawn are the system's choices of kind (`--tanrei-sys-behavior-*`), and how far its
corners ease is the system's amount (`--tanrei-sys-shape-corner-smoothing`), read from the cascade.

The content is the default slot: any layout. The card insets it by `comp.card.container.padding` (not with `flush`),
clips it to its corners and hands it the variant's content color as the inherited `color`. With `interactive` the
whole card is one action with the button role — its content must then hold nothing interactive (reported in debug
builds) — and it can be `disabled`, which dims it as a whole. Without `interactive` it has no role (a named group
with `label`) and leaves its content's semantics alone.

With `href` the whole card is one link — a link card (CRD-19), whether `interactive` is set or not: the
shadow root holds an `<a href>` around the slot in place of the element with the button role, drawn as an interactive
card is. Enter activates it and Space does not; `click` fires first and cancelling it cancels the navigation.
`target="new"` opens a new tab, safely (`noopener`), and reads `target-label` as the link's description; the card
draws no mark, because its content is yours — put the icon set's `open_in_new` in it. Its content must hold nothing
interactive, as an interactive card's.
declarations.name: TanreiCard

cssParts.description: The card's shape: its color, elevation, corners and, when interactive or a link, every state and the button or link semantics.
cssParts.name: container

cssParts.description: The box that insets the content and clips it to the corners.
cssParts.name: content

cssParts.description: The outlined variant's edge, drawn above the content.
cssParts.name: outline

slots.description: The content: any layout of media, text and — only when the card is neither interactive nor a link — actions.

members.name: variant
members.description: How the card separates from its background: by depth (elevated), by tone (filled) or by an edge (outlined). Pick by the background.

members.name: interactive
members.description: Makes the whole card one pressable action with the button role (it emits click). Its content must then hold nothing interactive.

members.name: disabled
members.description: Prevents interaction and removes an interactive card or a link card from the focus order. Ignored for a card that is neither.

members.name: inset
members.description:
Insets the content by the card's padding. False (the `flush` attribute) lets content reach the card's edges — a
photo on top — and that content pads its own text (`--tanrei-comp-card-container-padding`).

members.name: label
members.description: The accessible name: of the action or the link when interactive or a link card (normally its heading's text), of a named group otherwise.

members.name: href
members.description:
The destination: a URL, a path or a fragment. Not empty, the whole card is one link (CRD-19) whether `interactive`
is set or not: the link role, one tab stop, an `<a href>` around the content, activated by Enter and not by Space.
White space is no destination, and a `javascript:` address or one that cannot be read is refused and reported in
debug builds (CRD-23).

members.name: target
members.description:
Where the destination opens: `same` (here) or `new` (a new tab or window, with `noopener`), which the card says
through `targetLabel`; it draws no mark (CRD-21). HTML's `_self` and `_blank` are read as those two; anything else is
`same` and reported. Ignored without `href`.

members.name: targetLabel
members.description: What assistive technology reads after the link's name while `target` is `new` ("opens in a new tab"): your words, in your language. Required then; ignored otherwise.

members.name: rel
members.description: Web only: forwarded to the anchor's `rel`; `target="new"` adds `noopener` to it. Ignored without `href`.

members.name: download
members.description: Web only: forwarded to the anchor's `download` (the file name; empty for the address's own). Ignored without `href`.

members.name: axes
members.default: new OpenAxesController(this, { component: 'card', behavior: 'CRD-7', axes: AXES })
members.description: CRD-7: variants a design system adds, and a value the active system does not have (src/primitives/axes.ts).

members.name: link
members.default: new LinkController(this, { ids: { refused: 'CRD-23', newContext: 'CRD-21' }, disabled: () => this.disabled })
members.description:
CRD-19 … CRD-23: the link the card is while it has a destination, what its anchor carries, and what a debug build
is told (src/primitives/link.ts).

members.name: press
members.default: new PressController(this, { container: () => this.container, holdCarrier: () => this.renderRoot.querySelector('.clip'), disabled: () => !this.active, keys: () => this.link.pressKeys, })
members.description:
CRD-8 / CRD-9: the pressed state, press-hold and the answer the system chooses (src/primitives/press.ts). CRD-20: a
link card is pressed by Enter alone; Space is the browser's.

members.name: spaceDown
members.description: Space activates on key-up, as a native button does, and only when the key went down on the card.

members.name: pressable
members.description: Whether the card is one pressable thing: an action (`interactive`) or a link (CRD-19).

members.name: active
members.description: Whether the card is an action or a link that can be taken now.

members.name: click
members.description: `element.click()` activates an interactive card as a person would, and follows a link card; otherwise it does nothing (CRD-2, CRD-11).

members.name: onFocus
members.description: CRD-10: where style queries are missing, the focus style is read when focus arrives.

members.name: onKeyDown
members.description: CRD-1: Enter activates on key-down and Space on key-up, as a native button does.

members.name: inspectContent
members.description: CRD-15: an interactive card's or a link card's content holds nothing interactive; a debug build names what it found, on every slot change.

events.description: An interactive card or a link card was activated by pointer, touch, keyboard or assistive technology. A link card fires it before the browser follows the address; `preventDefault()` cancels the navigation.

members.name: inner
members.description: W, the inner width.

members.name: fluid
members.description: Whether the row is laid out with fluid widths: `fluidWidth`, unless the row is too narrow for side slots (CRL-9).

members.name: fluidSet
members.description: `fluidWidth` as set (CRL-17, CRL-18 read the prop, not the fallback).

members.name: scaled
members.description: CRL-26: whether the others are scaled, and the least scale.

members.name: loop
members.description: Whether loop is in effect: set, and two or more items (CRL-27).

members.name: hero
members.description: H, the hero slot's width, and the width every item's content is laid out at (CRL-9, CRL-15).

members.name: heroStart
members.description: h, where the hero slot starts (CRL-11).

members.name: oneSlot
members.description: CRL-9: fluid widths whose cap is less than the greatest small width — laid out as fixed widths, H being W.

members.name: side
members.description: CRL-10: the widths of the slots on a side where items follow the hero, going outward (empty for fixed widths).

members.name: after
members.description: The slots after the hero, slot 0 first and the edge slot (no width, CRL-12) last (fluid widths).

members.name: before
members.description: The slots before the hero, slot 0 first and the edge slot (no width) last (fluid widths).

members.name: other
members.description: With fixed widths, the width of every slot but the hero's: H, or H × min-scale while the others are scaled (CRL-13, CRL-26).

members.name: resting
members.description: The resting positions in order, while loop is not in effect (CRL-12, CRL-13).

members.name: turns
members.description: While loop is in effect: how many turns the track is long, and the first position of the middle one.

members.name: step
members.description: How far the row scrolls for one position: the hero slot plus the gap (CRL-12).

members.name: maxPosition
members.description: The greatest p: the end of the range, or the end of a looping track.

members.name: range
members.description: The scroll range in px: the track is the carousel's width plus this.

members.name: restingCount
members.description: D, the number of resting positions (CRL-12): N while loop is in effect.

members.name: toSlot
members.description:
CRL-17, CRL-18: whether the resting item is the item at slot 0 and focus brings an item there — fluid widths, a
centred hero or a row that snaps; otherwise (fixed widths at the start, free scroll) the first item wholly in view.

members.name: position
members.description: The scroll position p for a scroll offset: within the range, and whole when it is within a hair of it.

members.name: offset
members.description: The scroll offset of a position.

members.name: logical
members.description: p as the ring sees it while loop is in effect (0 up to N), else p itself.

members.name: slotPosition
members.description:
CRL-12, CRL-27: item `index`'s slot position s at `position`: i − p, or, while loop is in effect, the one value that
differs from it by a whole number of turns and lies above −N / 2 and at most N / 2 (centred) or above −1 and at
most N − 1 (at the start).

members.name: slot
members.description: Slot `k`'s box in a fluid row, k from the edge slot before the hero to the edge slot after it.

members.name: fixedSlot
members.description:
Slot `k`'s box in a row of fixed widths (CRL-13, CRL-26): the hero slot H wide at h, every other slot `other` wide —
H, or H × min-scale while the others are scaled — each g beyond the drawn edge of the one before it going outward,
without end.

members.name: scale
members.description: CRL-26: the scale of an item at slot position `s`: 1 at the hero slot, min-scale a whole slot away and beyond.

members.name: item
members.description:
Item `index` at `position` (CRL-12, CRL-13, CRL-26): its start and width are the linear interpolation between those
of the two slots around its slot position. With fluid widths an item at or beyond an edge slot is not drawn: its box
is the edge slot's, of no width. With fixed widths the slots go on beyond the carousel's edges, where the items are
clipped.

members.name: restingIndex
members.description: CRL-17: the resting item — the item at slot 0, or the first item wholly in view (fixed widths at the start, free).

members.name: revealPosition
members.description:
CRL-18: the position that brings item `index` into place — slot 0, or where the range ends first the resting
position nearest it, the shorter way round while loop is in effect; or, for fixed widths at the start with free
scroll, wholly between the inner edges with the least scroll.

members.name: shorter
members.description: The shortest signed distance around the ring equal to `delta` modulo N.

members.name: settlePosition
members.description:
CRL-14: where a row that snaps comes to rest from `position`: the next resting position in the direction of a fling
(`direction` 1 toward the end, −1 toward the start), or else the nearest one.

members.name: indicatorPosition
members.description:
CRL-29: the indicator's position q for `position` — between resting positions j and j + 1 it runs linearly from j
to j + 1; while loop is in effect it is p less a whole number of turns, from 0 up to N.

members.name: dotDistance
members.description: CRL-29: how far q is from dot j, around the ring while loop is in effect.

members.name: nearestResting
members.description: CRL-31: the index of the resting position nearest `position` (a dot's index), 0 up to D − 1.

members.name: restingPosition
members.description:
The position of resting position `j` (a dot): the resting position itself, or, while loop is in effect, the whole
position of that ring value nearest `from` (the shorter way round).

members.name: stepResting
members.description:
CRL-30, CRL-32: the resting position one step from `position`'s nearest (`direction` 1 or −1): beyond the ends it
wraps while `wrap` is true — forward round the ring while loop is in effect, else to the other end — and otherwise
stays at the end.

members.name: recentre
members.description:
CRL-27: while loop is in effect, the same place on the ring in the middle turn of the track, when `position` has
come within a turn of either end; otherwise `position` itself. Moving by whole turns draws nothing new.

declarations.default: css` /* CRL-8, CRL-12, CRL-40: the carousel places the item — the drawn container's start and width along the row (after any scale: the gap to its neighbours is between these edges), as tall as the row. */ :host { position: absolute; inset-block: 0; inset-inline-start: var(--_x, 0px); inline-size: var(--_w, 0px); display: block; box-sizing: border-box; } /* CRL-26: the container is as wide as the item's box — the carousel already gave that box the scaled slot's width, so nothing shrinks inside it and the gap stays (CRL-40) — and as tall as the row times the item's scale (1 unless the carousel scales the others), centred on the row's height; the ring inside it keeps its own width, and the hit area follows it. */ .container { box-sizing: border-box; position: absolute; inset: 0; margin-block: auto; block-size: calc(100% * var(--_scale, 1)); /* Its own stacking context: the content, the state layer, the ripple and the ring stack inside it. */ isolation: isolate; display: block; cursor: pointer; outline: none; -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent; /* CRL-16: the resting fill under the content, in every state; the content's inherited color. */ background: ${t('item-container-color')}; color: ${t('item-content-color')}; ${unsafeCSS(cornerRadius(`${PREFIX}-container-shape`))} /* At rest there is no state layer: nothing is drawn over the content. */ --_layer: ${t('item-state-layer-color')}; --_layer-opacity: 0; /* CRL-6: the ripple is the pressed state layer. */ --_ripple: ${t('item-pressed-state-layer-color')}; /* CRL-22: a change of the colors and the opacity is animated. */ transition-property: color, opacity; transition-duration: ${t('motion-state-duration')}; transition-timing-function: ${t('motion-state-easing')}; } /* CRL-15: the content is clipped to the container's corners (concentric with it) and laid out at the hero's width and the row's height; declarations.description: The carousel: `<tanrei-carousel>` — the row, and the controls row below it.

One item of a carousel — the spec's item kind `item`: the product's content in a rounded box, one action
named by its label. A child of `<tanrei-carousel>`, which places it, sizes it and says which item is the Tab stop.

The host is a `listitem` with its position among the items; inside it one element has the button role, named by
`label` — the content is not read (CRL-19). The content is the default slot: an image, a poster, anything that is not
interactive (CRL-20). The item lays it out at the hero's width and the carousel's height, aligned as the carousel
says, clips it to its corners and hands it `comp.carousel.item.content.color` as the inherited `color` (CRL-15,
CRL-16). Give an image `inline-size: 100%; block-size: 100%; object-fit: cover`.

declarations.description:
Lets people browse a row of visual items that scrolls sideways around one item in focus — the hero, in the centre (the
default) or at the start, the others narrower (fluid widths) or smaller (scaleOthers) as they move away, every two
neighbours one gap apart at every scroll position (CRL-40) — each item opening what it shows. A featured row may loop, show its position in dots and advance by itself, with a control to stop it.

Contract: specs/carousel.spec.json. The items are `<tanrei-carousel-item>` children, in order. The carousel is a native
horizontal scroller — wheel, trackpad, touch and pen scroll it as the platform does — whose track is as long as the
scroll range; it places every item from the scroll offset (CRL-12), and settles at a resting position when a scroll
ends while `snap` is true (CRL-14). The items are one Tab stop; the arrow keys, Home and End move between items and
bring the focused one into place (CRL-17, CRL-18). Below the items, a controls row holds the page indicator (one
slider, CRL-29 – CRL-31) and the playback control (CRL-35). Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-carousel-*`
tokens.

members.name: heroAlignment
members.description: Where the item in focus sits: `center` (the middle of the row, items on both sides) or `start` (the inner start edge). An unknown value is drawn as `center` and reported (CRL-24). Reflected.

members.name: itemWidth
members.description:
The width the hero is laid out at, in CSS px (the `item-width` attribute); null takes
`comp.carousel.container.large-width`. With fixed widths every item is this wide (at most the inner width); with
fluid widths the hero is kept between a floor and a cap (CRL-9). Not a positive number: treated as null and
reported (CRL-24).

members.name: fluidWidth
members.description: Whether item widths change fluidly (CRL-10). False (the `fixed-width` attribute) makes every item the hero's width.

members.name: contentAlignment
members.description: With fluid widths, where a narrowed item's content is anchored: `center` or `toward-hero` (CRL-15). An unknown value is `center`, reported (CRL-24). Reflected.

members.name: scaleOthers
members.description: Draws the items other than the hero smaller, down to `comp.carousel.container.min-scale`, following the scroll (CRL-26).

members.name: snap
members.description: Whether the row settles at a resting position when a scroll ends (CRL-14). False (the `free-scroll` attribute) lets it rest wherever it ends.

members.name: loop
members.description: Whether the row is endless (CRL-27). Takes effect only with two or more items.

members.name: indicator
members.description: Draws the dots below the items: one per resting position, the current one stretched (CRL-29).

members.name: autoplay
members.description: Advances the row by itself, one resting position every `autoplayInterval` (CRL-32); it holds while hovered, focused within, pressed or hidden, and never runs where motion is reduced.

members.name: autoplayInterval
members.description: How long the row rests before autoplay moves on, in ms (the `autoplay-interval` attribute); null takes `comp.carousel.autoplay.interval`. Not a positive number: null, reported (CRL-24).

members.name: paused
members.description: Whether autoplay is paused, by the person (the playback control, which fires `pausedchange`) or by the product (which fires nothing). Reflected.

members.name: playbackControl
members.description: Draws the playback control while autoplay is on (CRL-35). False (the `no-playback-control` attribute) hides it: keep it wherever you can (WCAG 2.2.2).

members.name: autoplayProgress
members.description: Fills the current dot to show the time until autoplay moves on (CRL-36). Needs `indicator`.

members.name: playLabel
members.description: The playback control's accessible name while autoplay is paused ("Play the slideshow"). Required while it can be drawn.

members.name: pauseLabel
members.description: The playback control's accessible name while autoplay is playing ("Pause the slideshow"). Required while it can be drawn.

members.name: label
members.description: Names the carousel's list and its indicator for assistive technology ("Recently played"). Required.

members.name: restingCount
members.description: D, the number of resting positions of the last arrangement.

members.name: indicatorFits
members.description: CRL-29: whether the indicator's container fits beside the playback control's target.

members.name: current
members.description: CRL-31: the resting position nearest the indicator's position, from 0.

members.name: reducedMotion
members.description: CRL-34: `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, followed as it changes.

members.name: glyphReady
members.description: CRL-38: whether the icon set can draw the playback glyphs.

members.name: resize$
members.description:
Watches the row — the box the arrangement measures (CRL-8) — not the host: the host is also as tall as its controls
row, which an arrangement may add or take away (CRL-29), and an observer told of a change its own callback made
does not come to rest within the frame.

members.description:
CRL-23: the row follows the direction it inherits, and a change of it while the page runs: the scroll offset and
where each item's content sits were written physically for the old direction, so the row is arranged again — the
resting item kept where it was, without motion.

members.name: geometry
members.description: The arrangement of the last layout, the items it placed and the scroll offset they were placed at.

members.name: zoom
members.description: The zoom of the row's ancestors, read when the row is arranged: a device pixel is the window's ratio times it (CRL-40).

members.name: written
members.description: The offset the carousel last wrote itself: a scroll event that reports it is the carousel's own.

members.name: remembered
members.description: CRL-17: the item that last had keyboard focus in the carousel, or the one a dot's move brought (CRL-30).

members.name: pinned
members.description: CRL-32: the Tab stop an advance keeps, until the person moves the row.

members.name: scrolling
members.description: The scroll the carousel is animating, where it goes, and whether it is an advance.

members.name: moving

them), for the velocity of its release.

members.name: fling

members.name: indicatorPointer
members.description: CRL-30: the indicator is being pressed by this pointer, and the dot it last moved the row to.

members.name: elapsed

members.name: runningSince

members.name: timedInterval

members.name: progressAnimation

members.name: progressDot

members.name: hovering

members.name: progressDrawn
