members.name: readOffset
members.description: The scroll offset along the reading direction (a right-to-left row scrolls to negative `scrollLeft`).

members.name: readZoom
members.description:
What a `zoom` in CSS on an ancestor makes of one of the row's own pixels (CRL-40): the browser says it where it
can, and where it cannot the row's box, measured in the window's pixels and in its own, tells it. 1 with no zoom.

members.name: metrics
members.description: The tokens the arrangement reads, in px (and the least scale, a number), through the probes' real properties.

members.name: arrange
members.description:
CRL-8 – CRL-13, CRL-21, CRL-27: arranges the slots for the carousel's width, its axes and its items, and keeps the
resting item where it was, as far as the new range allows, without motion.

members.name: setOffset
members.description: Scrolls to `offset` at once and places the items there.

members.name: place
members.description:
CRL-12, CRL-13, CRL-15, CRL-26, CRL-29, CRL-40: every item and every dot for `offset` — all from the one scroll
position, in one pass.

CRL-40: a browser paints a box's edges on whole device pixels, so two gaps of the same length in CSS px can be
painted a device pixel apart (10 and 9 for a gap of 8 at a pixel ratio of 1.25, measured). So each drawn item's
start is rounded to a device pixel, and its end is the next item's rounded start less the gap, itself rounded: the
rounding falls on a width, never on a gap.

members.name: paintDots
members.description: CRL-29, CRL-36: each dot's stretch and fill for the position `p`; the value of the slider.

members.name: syncTabStop
members.description: CRL-17, CRL-32: one Tab stop — the item that last had keyboard focus, the one an advance kept, or else the resting item.

members.name: onScroll
members.description: CRL-14: the row scrolled: the items follow; a scroll that is not the carousel's own is the person's move.

members.name: onScrollEnd
members.description: CRL-14: a scroll ended (a drag released, a wheel or trackpad gesture over): the row settles while snap is true.

members.name: onTouchMove
members.description: CRL-14: the finger moved.

members.name: sample
members.description: Where the finger of `event` is along the row, at the event's own time.

members.name: onTouchEnd
members.description:
CRL-14: the finger left the row: a release faster than FLING_VELOCITY is a fling, in its direction. The velocity is
the finger's over its moves in the last VELOCITY_WINDOW before the release, timed by the events' own time stamps, so
a busy main thread (or a frame that came late) does not slow a fling down.

members.name: hold
members.description: Holds the row still — no momentum, no pan — while a fling's settle runs (CRL-14); the scroll offset stays settable.

members.name: onWheel
members.description: A wheel or a trackpad takes over from a running settle; Shift with a vertical wheel scrolls the row (CRL-14).

members.name: takeOver
members.description:
The person takes over from a motion the carousel runs (a wheel, a mouse press): it stops where it is, and, unless a
scroll follows, the row comes to rest — settling first while snap is true — once no scroll has come for a moment.

members.name: settle
members.description: CRL-14: while snap is true, the row comes to rest at a resting position — the next one in the direction of a fling, or the nearest.

members.name: atRest
members.description:
The row came to rest. CRL-27: a looping row moves by whole turns back to the middle of its track (which draws nothing
new). CRL-33: the clock starts again from zero after the row moved — and only then: an engine reports the end of the
carousel's own scroll (`scrollend`) when it next updates its rendering, which may be long after the row came to rest,
and a row that has been at rest since keeps the time it has counted (CRL-32).

members.name: motion
members.description:
The motion of a settle, a scroll into place and a dot's move (CRL-14, CRL-18, CRL-30), or of an advance (CRL-32):
the tokens through real properties, 0 where reduced.

members.name: scrollRowTo

parameters.name: { from = this.offset, claim = true, kind = 'scroll' as Motion }

members.description:
Scrolls from `from` to `to` over the motion's duration and easing, or at once where motion is reduced. It starts in
the next frame. With `claim`, that first frame replaces whatever scrolled the row since the call (the browser's own
jump to a focused element, the momentum after a fling); without it, a scroll that came before the first frame wins,
as one that comes during the motion does. The easing's progress is read from an effect without a target, so the
scroll follows the token's curve.

members.name: moveTo
members.description: Moves the row to `position` over the scroll motion, as the person asked (a key, a dot): the Tab stop follows (CRL-30).

members.name: itemOf
members.description: The item an event came from.

members.name: onPointerDown
members.description: A mouse or a pen takes over from a running motion (a touch does in onTouchStart). CRL-33: a press holds autoplay.

members.name: onPointerEnter
members.description: CRL-33: the hover hold; leaving ends a hold that playing lifted.

members.name: onFocusIn
members.description:
CRL-17: the focused item becomes the Tab stop. CRL-18: keyboard or assistive-technology focus — focus the browser
shows, `:focus-visible`, which a pointer's never is — brings it into place over the scroll motion. CRL-33: focus
within holds autoplay, however it came there.

members.name: reveal
members.description: CRL-18: slot 0 (or as near as the range allows, the shorter way round), or wholly in view with the least scroll.

members.name: onKeyDown
members.description: CRL-17: Right / Left Arrow (mirrored in right-to-left) to the next and previous item, wrapping while loop is in effect; Home and End.

members.name: indicatorPress
members.default: new PressController(this, { container: () => this.renderRoot?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.indicator') ?? null, holdCarrier: () => this.renderRoot?.querySelector('.indicator .hold') ?? null, disabled: () => false, keys: [], })
members.description: CRL-5 / CRL-6: the indicator's pressed state, by pointer or touch only, lasting as long as the press.

members.name: playbackPress
members.default: new PressController(this, { container: () => this.renderRoot?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.playback') ?? null, holdCarrier: () => this.renderRoot?.querySelector('.playback .hold') ?? null, disabled: () => false, })
members.description: CRL-5 / CRL-6: the playback control's pressed state.

members.name: dotAt
members.description: CRL-30: the dot nearest a point along the indicator.

members.name: toDot
members.description: CRL-30: moves the row to dot `j`'s resting position, unless it is already going there.

members.name: onIndicatorKeyDown
members.description: CRL-30: Right / Left Arrow to the next and previous resting position (wrapping while loop is in effect), Home and End; mirrored in right-to-left.

members.name: interval
members.description: How long the row rests before it advances, in ms: `autoplayInterval`, or comp.carousel.autoplay.interval through a real property.

members.name: held
members.description: CRL-33: whether a hold is in effect.

members.name: clockRuns
members.description: CRL-32, CRL-34: whether the clock runs now.

members.name: passed
members.description: The time of the interval that has passed, in ms.

members.name: syncClock
members.description: Starts or stops the clock as the conditions of CRL-32 – CRL-34 say; a stop keeps the time that has passed.

members.name: onTimeUp
members.description: CRL-32: the interval has passed with the row at rest: on to the next resting position, or from the last back to the first.

members.name: drawProgress
members.description:
CRL-36: the current dot's fill, as the part of the interval that has passed. One animation of the interval's length
draws it — the fill's scale along the row, from nothing at its start edge to the whole dot, at an even pace — and the
browser runs it: script writes only when the clock starts or stops (a hold, a pause, the row moving, a new
interval), putting the animation at the time the clock has counted and letting it run or holding it there.

members.name: onPlaybackClick
members.description: CRL-35: the person pauses or plays; on play the time starts from zero and the hover and focus holds in effect are lifted (CRL-33).

members.name: onMotionChange
members.description: CRL-34: reduced motion stops autoplay; when it stops being reduced, autoplay starts again with the time from zero.

members.name: onVisibilityChange
members.description: CRL-33: a hidden document holds autoplay.

members.name: checkGlyphs
members.description:
CRL-38: the playback glyphs are drawn only once the icon set can draw them — before that the glyph's box stays and
shows nothing, never the glyph's name as text. A face that never loads leaves the box empty.

members.name: reportOnce
members.description: CRL-20, CRL-24: what a debug build reports, each once per value.

events.description: The person paused or played autoplay with the playback control; `detail.paused` is the new value. Not fired when `paused` is set, nor for a hold.
events.name: pausedchange

attributes.name: hero-alignment
attributes.description: Where the item in focus sits: `center` (the middle of the row, items on both sides) or `start` (the inner start edge). An unknown value is drawn as `center` and reported (CRL-24). Reflected.

attributes.name: item-width
attributes.description:
The width the hero is laid out at, in CSS px (the `item-width` attribute); null takes
`comp.carousel.container.large-width`. With fixed widths every item is this wide (at most the inner width); with
fluid widths the hero is kept between a floor and a cap (CRL-9). Not a positive number: treated as null and
reported (CRL-24).

attributes.name: fixed-width
attributes.description: Whether item widths change fluidly (CRL-10). False (the `fixed-width` attribute) makes every item the hero's width.

attributes.name: content-alignment
attributes.description: With fluid widths, where a narrowed item's content is anchored: `center` or `toward-hero` (CRL-15). An unknown value is `center`, reported (CRL-24). Reflected.

attributes.name: scale-others
attributes.description: Draws the items other than the hero smaller, down to `comp.carousel.container.min-scale`, following the scroll (CRL-26).

attributes.name: free-scroll
attributes.description: Whether the row settles at a resting position when a scroll ends (CRL-14). False (the `free-scroll` attribute) lets it rest wherever it ends.

attributes.name: loop
attributes.description: Whether the row is endless (CRL-27). Takes effect only with two or more items.

attributes.name: indicator
attributes.description: Draws the dots below the items: one per resting position, the current one stretched (CRL-29).

attributes.name: autoplay
attributes.description: Advances the row by itself, one resting position every `autoplayInterval` (CRL-32); it holds while hovered, focused within, pressed or hidden, and never runs where motion is reduced.

attributes.name: autoplay-interval
attributes.description: How long the row rests before autoplay moves on, in ms (the `autoplay-interval` attribute); null takes `comp.carousel.autoplay.interval`. Not a positive number: null, reported (CRL-24).

attributes.name: paused
attributes.description: Whether autoplay is paused, by the person (the playback control, which fires `pausedchange`) or by the product (which fires nothing). Reflected.

attributes.name: no-playback-control
attributes.description: Draws the playback control while autoplay is on (CRL-35). False (the `no-playback-control` attribute) hides it: keep it wherever you can (WCAG 2.2.2).

attributes.name: autoplay-progress
attributes.description: Fills the current dot to show the time until autoplay moves on (CRL-36). Needs `indicator`.

attributes.name: play-label
attributes.description: The playback control's accessible name while autoplay is paused ("Play the slideshow"). Required while it can be drawn.

attributes.name: pause-label
attributes.description: The playback control's accessible name while autoplay is playing ("Pause the slideshow"). Required while it can be drawn.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Names the carousel's list and its indicator for assistive technology ("Recently played"). Required.

declarations.name: measured
declarations.description:
What depends on one line of the typing area's text (CCM-2, CCM-3, CCM-41), for a line of `line` (a CSS length):
the capsule's corners and its glow, which follow the one-line height, and the least height of each group of
Buttons, which is the typing area's with one line — so that a Button is centred on a single line and, as lines
grow, stays at the bottom edge at the distance it had. The stylesheet has it for a line of no height, which is
`container.height` alone; the element writes it again, as a rule of its own, once it has read the member's line.

declarations.name: styles
declarations.default: css` :host { min-inline-size: 0; } /* ── The capsule (CCM-1, CCM-41) ── one container behind everything it holds: as wide as its layout gives it, as tall as what it holds and never less than container.height; filled and lifted by its condition; its edge drawn inside its box (.outline), so that no state moves what it holds. It is the box of the text (CCM-5): the pointer over its own ground is a text pointer, and it answers no press. */ .capsule { box-sizing: border-box; position: relative; display: flex; flex-direction: column; justify-content: center; min-inline-size: 0; min-block-size: ${t('container-height')}; padding-block: ${t('container-padding-block')}; background-color: ${t('standard-container-color')}; box-shadow: ${t('standard-container-elevation')}; cursor: text; transition: background-color ${unsafeCSS(MOTION)}, box-shadow ${unsafeCSS(MOTION)}, opacity ${unsafeCSS(MOTION)}; } .outline { position: absolute; inset: 0; box-sizing: border-box; border: ${t('outline-width')} solid ${t('standard-outline-color')}; border-radius: inherit; corner-shape: inherit; pointer-events: none; transition: border-color ${unsafeCSS(MOTION)}, border-width ${unsafeCSS(MOTION)}; } /* CCM-27, CCM-42: each state paints from that state's tokens of the capsule's condition. Every rule has the resting rule's specificity, so their order is the precedence: hovered, then focused — the typing area's focus, which the element says (data-focused) — then receiving (CCM-23), then disabled over all; the error condition recolors each. */ ${unsafeCSS(state('[data-error]', 'error', ''))} @media (hover: hover) { ${unsafeCSS(state(':hover', 'standard', 'hovered'))} ${unsafeCSS(state('[data-error]:hover', 'error', 'hovered'))} } ${unsafeCSS(state('[data-focused]', 'standard', 'focused'))} ${unsafeCSS(state('[data-error][data-focused]', 'error', 'focused'))} /* CCM-23: receiving — the capsule's own fill and edge, at its own shape and inside its own box: nothing moves. */ .capsule:where([data-receiving]) { background-color: ${t('receiving-container-color')}; } .capsule:where([data-receiving]) > .outline { border-color: ${t('receiving-outline-color')}; border-width: ${t('receiving-outline-width')}; } ${unsafeCSS(state('[data-disabled]', 'standard', 'disabled'))} ${unsafeCSS(state('[data-error][data-disabled]', 'error', 'disabled'))} .capsule:where([data-disabled]) { cursor: default; } /* CCM-41: the corners — one radius at every height — the glow of CCM-42 around them, and the groups' least height. */ ${unsafeCSS(measured('0px'))} /* ── The strip (CCM-43) ── the attachments at the top of the capsule, from the start edge, strip.gap apart: a tile at its own size beside its neighbours, aligned to the top of its line; a row across a whole line. A full line wraps; nothing scrolls sideways, and no item is cut, shrunk or hidden. Only a File item is drawn in it. */ .strip { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: ${t('strip-gap')}; min-inline-size: 0; padding-block-start: ${t('strip-padding-block-start')}; padding-inline: ${t('container-padding-inline')}; margin-block-end: ${t('strip-offset')}; } .strip[hidden] { display: none; } .strip > tanrei-file-item, .strip ::slotted(tanrei-file-item) { flex: 1 0 100%; min-inline-size: 0; max-inline-size: 100%; cursor: default; } .strip > tanrei-file-item[form='tile'], .strip ::slotted(tanrei-file-item[form='tile']) { flex: none; } .strip ::slotted(:not(tanrei-file-item)) { display: none; } /* ── The line being written (CCM-2, CCM-3) ── the typing area takes the room the others leave, with input.padding-block above its first line and below its last. Inline it stands between its two groups; stacked, before the send button alone. Everything beside it stays at the bottom edge of the line as the text grows. */ .line { display: flex; align-items: flex-end; min-inline-size: 0; padding-inline: ${t('container-padding-inline')} ${t('container-padding-inline-with-button')}; } .line[data-start] { padding-inline-start: ${t('container-padding-inline-with-button')}; } .typing { flex: 1 1 0; min-inline-size: 0; padding-block: ${t('input-padding-block')}; } /* A group of Buttons, and the counter among them: centred on one line, actions.gap apart. */ .group { display: flex; flex: none; align-items: center; gap: ${t('actions-gap')}; max-inline-size: 100%; cursor: default; } /* container.gap between a group and the typing area; the send button is the last of the group after it. */ .line > .start { margin-inline-end: ${t('container-gap')}; } .line > .end, .line > .typing + .send { margin-inline-start: ${t('container-gap')}; } .line > .end + .send { margin-inline-start: ${t('actions-gap')}; } /* ── The row beneath (CCM-3) ── stacked: everything but the send button, container.row-gap below the line. The attach button and the leading actions from its start, wrapping onto further lines where the row is too short; the counter and the trailing actions together at the end of the last line. Nothing is cut, shrunk or hidden. */ .row { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: ${t('actions-gap')}; min-inline-size: 0; margin-block-start: ${t('container-row-gap')}; padding-inline: ${t('container-padding-inline-with-button')}; cursor: default; } .row > .end { flex-wrap: wrap; justify-content: flex-end; margin-inline-start: auto; } /* CCM-7, CCM-8: a Button keeps the size, the variant and the width the product gave it; none shrinks. */ .group > tanrei-file-picker, .row > tanrei-file-picker, ::slotted([slot='leading']), ::slotted([slot='trailing']), ::slotted([slot='send']), ::slotted([slot='stop']), ::slotted([slot='attach']) { flex: none; } /* ── The counter (CCM-19) ── on one line, as text of its own direction, in digits of equal width. */ .counter { flex: none; font: ${t('counter-typescale-font')}; letter-spacing: ${t('counter-typescale-letter-spacing')}; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: ${t('counter-color')}; white-space: nowrap; unicode-bidi: isolate; transition: color ${unsafeCSS(MOTION)}; } .counter[data-over] { color: ${t('counter-error-color')}; } /* CCM-4: the width under which it is laid out stacked, as a length the element reads; it is drawn nowhere, takes no room and — inside a box that clips — widens nothing. */ .measures { position: absolute; inset: 0; overflow: hidden; visibility: hidden; pointer-events: none; } .probe { position: absolute; inset-block-start: 0; inset-inline-start: 0; inline-size: ${t('layout-inline-min-width')}; block-size: 0; } /* CCM-30: the one live region is drawn nowhere and still read. */ .announce {${unsafeCSS(unseen)} } /* CCM-35: where motion is reduced a change of state is made at once. */ @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .capsule, .outline, .counter { transition: none; } } /* CCM-33: with a person's own colors the capsule stands on the platform's background with an edge in its text color at rest and in error; in its highlight at the focused width while the typing area has focus, and at twice the receiving width while it is receiving; in its disabled text color while disabled. The counter is text. */ @media (forced-colors: active) { .capsule, .capsule:where([data-error], :hover, [data-focused], [data-receiving], [data-disabled]) { background-color: Canvas; box-shadow: none; } .capsule > .outline, .capsule:where([data-error], :hover) > .outline { border-color: CanvasText; border-width: ${t('outline-width')}; } .capsule:where([data-focused]) > .outline { border-color: Highlight; border-width: ${t('focused-outline-width')}; } .capsule:where([data-receiving]) > .outline { border-color: Highlight; border-width: calc(2 * ${t('receiving-outline-width')}); } .capsule:where([data-disabled]) > .outline { border-color: GrayText; border-width: ${t('outline-width')}; } .counter, .counter[data-over] { color: CanvasText; } } `

declarations.description: Lets a person write a message and send it, in one capsule that holds everything. Built from an Embedded text input (``) — the typing, which grows with what is written — a File picker (``) and File items (``) — the attachments, as a strip at the top of the capsule — and Buttons (``): the send button, the stop button in its place, the attach button, and the product's own in its slots. It adds what ties them: the capsule, which is its own part and shows the typing area's focus on its edge; whether what it holds can be sent, and why not; the files it keeps; the counter; one live region; and the form's value. **It never sends**: `send` hands the text and the attachments to the product. Contract: specs/chat-composer.spec.json. ```html alternate_email ``` `layout="inline"` (the default) puts every action on the line being written; `layout="stacked"` keeps the send button on that line and puts everything else in a row beneath it, inside the capsule. A capsule narrower than `comp.chat-composer.layout.inline-min-width` is laid out stacked whatever `layout` says; a stacked composer with nothing for the row beneath is drawn as an inline one. Tab moves through it in the order it is drawn. Enter sends and Shift+Enter begins a new line; with `send-key="modifier"` Enter begins a new line. Ctrl+Enter and Command+Enter send under both. An input method's Enter never sends, and neither does the return key of an on-screen keyboard: both are the embedded text input's to tell. A request by the keyboard while the message cannot be sent emits `sendblocked` with the reasons, unless there is simply nothing to send. `attachments="own"`: the composer keeps the files a person attaches — chosen, dropped on the capsule or pasted — and draws a File item for each (`attachment-form`: a tile with its picture for an image, a row for anything else); a refused file is a failed row with the product's sentence for its reason. `files` reads the kept files, `addFiles(files)` hands files over and answers with the refused, `clear()` empties the text and the files. `attachments="given"`: the File items are `` children the product adds on `select` and removes on an item's `remove`, each with its status and progress; nothing can be sent while one is uploading, or has failed and can be tried again. Form-associated: it submits the text under `name` and, while `attachments` is `own`, each kept file under `files-name`; after `send` — unless that was cancelled — it asks its form to submit, and then does not empty itself. members.name: formAssociated
members.description: CCM-36: the one control the form meets. Its members stand in its shadow root, or are the product's own children, and take no part in a form.

members.name: value
members.description: The text. Setting it shows it and fires nothing. The `value` attribute is what a form reset returns to.

members.name: label
members.description: The accessible name. Required: the input draws no label and asks no Field for one, so this is the only name it has. Never drawn.

members.name: placeholder
members.description: A hint drawn while the value is empty. Never the name. A multi-line input is as tall as the placeholder's lines, within `min-rows` and `max-rows`.

members.name: layout
members.description: Where the actions stand in the capsule. `inline` (the default, and every value it does not know): on the line being written — the attach button and the leading actions before the typing area, the counter, the trailing actions and the send button after it. `stacked`: the typing area and the send button on one line, and everything else in a row beneath them, inside the capsule. A capsule too narrow for inline is laid out stacked whatever this says; the number of lines never changes the layout.

members.name: minRows
members.description: The fewest lines a multi-line input is tall (`min-rows`). Anything below 1 is 1.

members.name: maxRows
members.description: The most lines the typing area grows to before it scrolls inside itself (`max-rows`). Given to the embedded text input as its `maxRows`, with a default of the chat composer's own: six lines. 0 sets no limit.

members.name: maxLength
members.description: The most user-perceived characters a message may hold (`max-length`); 0 is no limit. It refuses no edit and shortens no paste: text beyond it stays, is marked, and stops sending until the person has cut it.

members.name: counter
members.description: Draws the number of characters, and `maxLength` where one is set, before the trailing actions.

members.name: sendKey
members.description: What Enter does on a hardware keyboard (`send-key`). `enter` (the default, and every value it does not know): Enter sends and Shift+Enter begins a new line. `modifier`: Enter begins a new line and Ctrl+Enter or Command+Enter sends. Ctrl+Enter and Command+Enter send under both.

members.name: attachments
members.description: Whether files can be attached, and who holds them. `none` (the default, and every value it does not know): text alone. `own`: the chat composer keeps the files a person attached and draws a File item for each, and `send` carries them. `given`: the product gives the File items as children and the chat composer lays them out and keeps no file.

members.name: attachmentForm
members.description: The form of the File items the chat composer draws itself, while `attachments` is `own` (`attachment-form`). `auto` (the default, and every value it does not know): a tile with its picture for an image, a row for every other file. `tile`: every file a tile. `row`: every file a row, and no picture. A refused file is a row under every value.

members.name: multiple
members.description: Whether more than one file can be attached. Given to the file picker as its `multiple`; the default is true (`multiple="false"` says false).

members.name: accept
members.description: The kinds of file that are taken: extensions with their dot (".pdf") and media types ("image/png", a family as "image/*"). The attribute is a comma-separated list, as a native file input's. Empty takes every kind.

members.name: maxSize
members.description: The largest size of one file, in bytes (`max-size`). Null sets no limit. Judged from the size the browser reports; the file is not read.

members.name: maxFiles
members.description: The most files one choice or one drop may bring, while `multiple` is set (`max-files`). Null sets no limit; zero refuses every file — the room a full list has left. Nothing is counted across choices.

members.name: sending
members.description: What was sent is on its way, or its answer is still arriving: the product's to set and to clear. While it is set nothing more can be sent; the typing area stays open.

members.name: stoppable
members.description: While `sending` is set, puts a stop button in the send button's place, which asks the product to stop what is under way (`stop`). Ignored while `sending` is not set.

members.name: blocked
members.description: The product's own reason that nothing can be sent now. The send button is disabled and the send key sends nothing; the product says why in its own words.

members.name: keepAfterSend
members.description: Keeps the text and the attachments after `send` (`keep-after-send`), for a product that clears them itself (`clear()`) once it knows the message arrived.

members.name: disabled
members.description: Nothing can be written, attached, removed or sent: every member and every Button in a slot is disabled. Inside a Field, disable the Field.

members.name: error
members.description: Draws the capsule in its error condition and exposes the typing area as invalid. A Field sets it with its own error. It does not stop sending by itself: `blocked` does.

members.name: sendLabel
members.description: The accessible name of the send button the chat composer brings (`send-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ sendLabel })`). Tanrei has none: without them the button is drawn and works, and has no name.

members.name: stopLabel
members.description: The accessible name of the stop button the chat composer brings (`stop-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ stopLabel })`).

members.name: attachLabel
members.description: The accessible name of the attach button the chat composer brings (`attach-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ attachLabel })`).

members.name: removeLabel
members.description: The accessible name of the remove action (`remove-label`): your sentence with the place `{name}`, which the file item fills with the file's name ("Remove {name}"). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ removeLabel })`).

members.name: retryLabel
members.description: The accessible name of the retry action (`retry-label`), with the place `{name}` filled by the file's name ("Retry {name}"). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ retryLabel })`).

members.name: typeErrorText
members.description: While `attachments` is `own`: the sentence on the File item of a file refused for its kind (`type-error-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ fileTypeErrorText })`).

members.name: sizeErrorText
members.description: While `attachments` is `own`: the sentence on the File item of a file refused for its size (`size-error-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ fileSizeErrorText })`).

members.name: countErrorText
members.description: While `attachments` is `own`: the sentence on the File item of a file refused because no more can be added (`count-error-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ fileCountErrorText })`).

members.name: announcement
members.description: A message assistive technology hears through the one live region when the product sets or changes it. Not drawn.

members.name: name
members.description: Web only: the name the text is submitted under.

members.name: typing
members.description: CCM-42: the typing area has focus.

members.name: receiving
members.description: CCM-23: files are dragged over the capsule.

members.name: narrow
members.description: CCM-4: the capsule is narrower than `layout.inline-min-width`.

members.name: count
members.description: CCM-43: how many File items the product gave.

members.name: formDisabled
members.description: Set by an ancestor `<fieldset disabled>`, or by the element's own attribute (`formDisabledCallback`).

members.name: hostNameSentence
members.description:
W8: the sentence a debug build names when the host is given an ARIA name. The host has no role: its name is the
frame's `label`. Empty: nothing is reported.

members.name: words
members.description: CCM-31: the product's words, read where the instance gives none (src/primitives/words.ts).

members.name: system
members.description: CCM-6: the variant of the send button it brings is a choice the active design system makes; a system switch draws it again.

members.name: field
members.description: CCM-28: what a field around the chat composer gives it (src/primitives/field.ts): the name while it has no `label` of its own, the description, the invalid and the disabled state. The chat composer is the field's one control.

members.name: provider
members.default: new FieldProviderController(this, { controls: () => (this.picker ? [this.picker] : []), state: (): FieldState => ({ label: '', description: '', invalid: false, required: false, requiredText: '', disabled: this.isDisabled }), plain: () => null, })
members.description:
CCM-28: the file picker inside asks as every control does, and the chat composer answers it in a field's place —
`disabled` alone — so that its question does not reach a field around the chat composer as a second control.

members.name: given
members.description: W5: the value last set on the element, while the typing area has not taken it.

members.name: kept
members.description: CCM-22: the files it keeps while `attachments` is `own`, in order — handles, never read (CCM-40).

members.name: refused
members.description: CCM-22: the files the last arrival refused, in the order they were refused. Not kept.

members.name: arriving
members.description: What the file picker's two events of one arrival said, until the arrival is over.

members.name: said
members.description: CCM-9: what it last said of whether it can be sent; undefined until it was first drawn.

members.name: known
members.description: CCM-30: what each File item last said; one not in it is new.

members.name: presented
members.description: CCM-30: the chat composer has been presented: a File item that comes now was added.

members.name: own
members.description: CCM-30: the product's own sentence, set or changed in this turn; what the arrivals of this turn say.

members.name: hush
members.description: CCM-38: the next message says no File item: the ones that are there came by a change of `attachments`.

members.name: held
members.description: CCM-25: the File item focus is on, as the last `focusin` said, and the items as they stood.

members.name: drags
members.description: CCM-23: the drags that entered and have not left.

members.name: sendHeld
members.description: CCM-17: focus was on the button in the send button's place when the update began.

members.name: startHeld
members.description: CCM-4: focus was on a Button the layout is about to draw again.

members.name: line
members.description: CCM-41: one line of the typing area's text, as its native element computes it, and the rule that is written from it.

members.name: lent
members.description: What the product's own Buttons in the slots were given, to take back (CCM-10, CCM-26).

members.name: children$
members.description: CCM-43, CCM-25, CCM-3: a child that comes or goes — a File item, a Button in a slot — is drawn at once.

members.name: input
members.description: CCM-5: its one embedded text input, once rendered.

members.name: picker
members.description: CCM-7: its one file picker, while `attachments` is not none.

members.name: control
members.description: W7: focus is the typing area's (CCM-5).

members.name: isDisabled
members.description: Disabled by its own `disabled`, by a field around it, or by its form (CCM-26, CCM-28, CCM-36).

members.name: isError
members.description: CCM-18, CCM-27, CCM-28: the capsule is in its error condition, and the typing area is invalid — by `error`, by a field's, or over the limit.

members.name: attaches
members.description: CCM-38: who holds the files; a value it does not know is none.

members.name: groupName
members.description: CCM-29: the group's name, and the typing area's — its own label, else the field's.

members.name: lengthLimit
members.description: CCM-18: the limit, where one is set.

members.name: over
members.description: CCM-18: the count is over the limit.

members.name: counts
members.description: CCM-19: the counter is drawn.

members.name: counterText
members.description: CCM-19: what the counter shows — the count, then a slash and the limit where one is set.

members.name: slotted
members.description: The elements the product placed in a named slot.

members.name: givenItems
members.description: CCM-21, CCM-43: the File items the product gave, in the order it gave them — and none unless `attachments` is `given`.

members.name: itemChildren
members.description: The `tanrei-file-item` children the product wrote, whatever `attachments` says.

members.name: ownItems
members.description: The File items it drew itself, in the order they are drawn.

members.name: attachShown
members.description: CCM-7: the attach button is drawn.

members.name: rowHolds
members.description: CCM-3: the row beneath would hold something — the attach button, a Button in either slot, or the counter.

members.name: stacked
members.description: CCM-3, CCM-4: it is laid out stacked — by `layout`, or because the capsule is too narrow for inline — and has something for the row beneath.

members.name: enterKey
members.description: CCM-12: what the embedded text input's Enter does; a value of `sendKey` it does not know is enter.

members.name: mostRows
members.description: CCM-5: the most lines of the typing area — 0, or a number of at least its fewest.

members.name: description
members.description: CCM-19, CCM-28: the typing area's description — what the counter shows first, and the field's shown text last.

members.name: room
members.description: CCM-22: the room `maxFiles` leaves, which is what the file picker is given while the chat composer keeps the files.

members.name: reasons
members.description: CCM-9: each reason what it holds cannot be sent, by name; none while it can.

members.name: sendable
members.description: Whether what it holds can be sent now, read-only: what the last `sendablechange` said.

members.name: tellSendable
members.description: CCM-9: the answer or the reasons changed — said once, and never when it is first drawn.

members.name: requestSend
members.description:
CCM-11: a request to send — by the send button (`key` false) or by the keyboard. While it can be sent: `send`,
once, with the text exactly as it stands and the attachments in the order of the strip; then, in a form, the
form's submission (CCM-36), and outside one the emptying (CCM-15); then focus in the typing area (CCM-16). While
it cannot: nothing — but `sendblocked` for a request by the keyboard that a reason other than empty holds back (CCM-14).

members.name: empty
members.description: CCM-15: empties itself — the text, every file it keeps and every File item it drew. Emits nothing.

members.name: clear
members.description:
CCM-15: empties the chat composer as it empties itself after `send` — the text, every file it keeps and every File
item it drew — for a product that set `keep-after-send` and now knows the message arrived. Emits nothing and
announces nothing. The product's own File items (`attachments="given"`) are the product's to remove.

members.name: onStop
members.description: CCM-17: the stop button asks the product to stop, and changes nothing itself.

members.name: onInput
members.description: The person changed the text: the event leaves as it is (W5); the counter, the limit and what can be sent follow.

members.name: onAction
members.description: CCM-12: the embedded text input's action is a request to send. The event itself does not leave the element.

members.name: stop
members.description: W5: the embedded text input's `change` and `rowschange` are not events of the chat composer.

members.name: onTypingFocus
members.description: CCM-42: the capsule's edge is the focus indication of the typing area, however its focus was given.

members.name: onPaste
members.description:
CCM-24: a paste into the typing area that holds files and no plain text is an arrival, and inserts nothing; one
that holds text is the typing area's.

members.name: onGround
members.description:
CCM-5: a press on the capsule's own ground — its padding, the room beside a short text, the gaps of the strip — is
passed on to the typing area, which takes focus with the caret at the nearest point of its text (ETI-12). A press
on a Button, a File item or the counter is not. The press's default is prevented, so that focus is not taken away
again; the capsule shows no pressed state.

members.name: onPickerSelect
members.description: The file picker's `select` and `reject` are answered here and do not leave the element as they are.

members.name: onArrival
members.description: The browser's picker closed with a choice: one arrival, told once. CCM-25: with a file kept or handed over, focus goes to the typing area.

members.name: take
members.description: CCM-23, CCM-24: files that came another way — dropped, pasted — are judged by the file picker as a choice is (FPK-31).

members.name: judge
members.description: The file picker that judges by what the chat composer says now — its own, or, before it was first drawn, one that is nowhere and judges by the same props.

members.name: arrive
members.description:
One arrival, judged. CCM-21: while `attachments` is `given` nothing is kept — `select`, then `reject`, and the
product gives back a File item for each file it keeps. CCM-22: while it is `own` the File items of what an earlier
arrival refused leave; a file that passed and that it already keeps is passed over; with `multiple` the rest is
kept after the others, each one beyond the room `maxFiles` leaves refused for the count, and without it a file
that passed takes the place of the one kept. Then, for what a person did (`person`): `select`, `reject`,
`attachmentschange`, each once and only where it applies. Answers whether a file was kept or handed over.

members.name: emitAttachments
members.description: CCM-22: the files it keeps changed by what a person did.

members.name: sentence
members.description: CCM-22, CCM-31: the product's sentence for a reason — the instance's prop, else the product's words, else nothing.

members.name: files
members.description:
CCM-22: the files it keeps while `attachments` is `own`, in order, as the browser's own `File` handles: a new array
on each read. Never a refused file. Empty while `attachments` is `given` or `none`.

members.name: addFiles
members.description:
CCM-22: hands files over, as a product does whose own action in a slot makes a file — a photograph, a recording.
They are judged by its file picker (FPK-31) and are then an arrival: kept or refused, drawn and announced as a
choice is, with no event. Answers with the refused files and their reasons. While `attachments` is not `own` it
does nothing and is reported.

members.name: drops
members.description: A drag that holds a file, while files can be attached.

members.name: gift
members.description: CCM-20, CCM-26, CCM-29: what every File item it holds is given, through the internal channel: the names of its two actions, whether it is disabled, and that it is an item of the strip's list.

members.name: redraw
members.description:
Changes the files it keeps and draws their File items at once, so that what is emitted afterwards is emitted with
the strip as it will be. CCM-25: where an item that leaves held focus, focus goes to the remove action of the item
that followed it, or of the one before where none follows, or to the typing area where none is left.

members.name: removeOwn
members.description: CCM-22: the remove action of a File item it drew removes the item, at once; a kept file is let go and `attachmentschange` is emitted. The item's own `remove` does not leave the element: it is an event of the product's items.

members.name: readItems
members.description: The product's File items were added to, removed from, or changed: drawn at once, said once.

members.name: afterLeave
members.description:
CCM-25: a File item the product gave left while focus was on one of its actions, and focus is now nowhere: it goes
to the remove action of the item that followed, or of the one before where none follows, or to the typing area
where no item is left. Where the product has already put focus somewhere, nothing is done.

members.name: changed
members.description: CCM-30: something that may be said changed in this turn; everything of one turn is one message.

members.name: say
members.description:
CCM-30: the one message of a turn, in the product's words alone — its own sentence where it set one; while
`attachments` is `own`, what arrived; while it is `given`, each File item that was added after the chat composer
was first presented, finished or failed: its name, then its status text or its error text. Nothing of progress, and
nothing of the chat composer's own making.

members.name: form
members.description: The form it belongs to, if any.

members.name: formResetCallback
members.description: CCM-36: a reset empties it, and emits nothing.

members.name: formStateRestoreCallback
members.description: CCM-40: the text is restored with the page; it begins with no file.

members.name: syncForm
members.description: CCM-36: the text under its name and, while it keeps its own files, each of them under the name given for its files — nothing while disabled. The text is what a restored page gives back.

members.name: adopt
members.description:
CCM-37: the platform's own text area and submit button that the product wrote as children are the form until the
element is defined. Now the text area's text is the value while its own is empty, and each is taken out of what
is drawn, focused, read and submitted.

members.name: measure
members.description:
CCM-41: one line of the typing area's text — the member's computed line height, never its token — from which the
capsule's corners and the least height of its groups are written, as a rule of the element's own. CCM-4: whether
the capsule is narrower than `layout.inline-min-width`, by its own width.

members.name: lend
members.description:
CCM-10, CCM-26: the product's own Buttons in the slots are disabled as their own `disabled` does — every one while
the chat composer is disabled, and the one in the send slot while nothing can be sent — and each gets back what it
had; one the product disabled itself is never enabled.

members.name: keepFocus
members.description:
CCM-17: the button in the send button's place changed while it had focus — focus stays on the button now there, or
goes to the typing area where that one is disabled. CCM-4: an attach button the layout drew again keeps its focus.

members.name: check
members.description: What a debug build is told about the content, once it has all been written: the chat composer still renders.

members.name: ownItem
members.description:
CCM-22, CCM-44: a File item it draws itself. A kept file is a pending File item given the file's handle — a tile
with its picture and no drawn name for an image (auto, tile), a tile for any file (tile), a row otherwise; a
refused one a failed row with the product's sentence, given no handle and never retryable. Neither is pressable.

members.name: attachPart
members.description: CCM-7: its file picker around its trigger — the product's own Button in the attach slot, or the one it brings.

members.name: sendPart
members.description: CCM-6, CCM-17: the send button — or, while a stoppable sending is under way, the stop button in its place: the product's own in its slot, or the one it brings.

members.name: passing
members.description: W9: the names of the slots it has passed on, and the watch on its own children for them.

members.name: members
members.description: The members it has rendered: the custom elements of its own shadow tree.

members.name: focus
members.description: W7, item 2: focus is the control's.

members.name: blur
members.description: W7, item 2: what has focus inside the control loses it (an engine does not take it from inside a host it blurs).

members.name: pass
members.description:
W9: a slot of a member, passed on — `${this.pass('label-icon')}` among that member's children. Rendered only while
the element has a child for it: a member that draws room for a filled slot would take a passing slot that is
always there for content.

members.name: getUpdateComplete
members.description: The element has updated when its members have: what it gave them, they have taken.

members.name: focusWhenReady
members.description: The control has rendered what takes focus only after its own first update.

events.name: sendablechange
events.description: Whether what the chat composer holds can be sent changed, or the reasons it cannot did: `detail.sendable`, and `detail.reasons` by name — `disabled`, `sending`, `blocked`, `empty`, `length`, `uploading`, `failed`. Bubbles. Never when it is first drawn.

events.name: sendblocked
events.description: The person asked to send by the keyboard while it could not be sent for a reason other than being empty or disabled; `detail.reasons` says why. Bubbles.

events.name: send
events.description: The person sent what the chat composer holds, by the send button or the keyboard, while it could be sent. `detail.value` is the text exactly as written; `detail.attachments` the kept `File`s (`own`) or the values of the File items that have not failed (`given`), in the order of the strip. Bubbles; cancelable — a cancelled one keeps the content and asks no form to submit.

events.name: select
events.description: Files were chosen in the picker, dropped on the capsule or pasted, and passed. Once per arrival; `detail.files` is a `File[]` — while `attachments` is `own`, the files newly kept. Bubbles.

events.name: reject
events.description: Files of one arrival were refused. Once, after `select` where both happen; `detail.files` is `{ file, reason }[]`, the reason `type`, `size` or `count`. Bubbles.

events.name: attachmentschange
events.description: While `attachments` is `own`: the kept files changed by what a person did — an arrival that kept a file, or a kept file removed by its File item. `detail.files` is the `File[]` now kept. Bubbles. Never for `addFiles()`, `clear()`, the emptying after `send` or a reset.

The person changed the text: the typing area's own `input` event, which leaves the element as it is. Read the new text from `event.target.value`. Never when `value` is set, and not when the chat composer empties itself after `send`.
events.name: input

events.description: The person activated the stop button while `sending` and `stoppable` were set. The product stops what is under way and sets `sending`. Bubbles.
events.name: stop

attributes.name: files-name
attributes.description: Web only: the name each kept file is submitted under, while `attachments` is `own` and the chat composer stands in a form. Without it no file is submitted.
The id of the form the chat composer belongs to, where it stands outside it: the platform's own attribute. The `form` property is read-only and returns the form element.
attributes.name: form
value
attributes.description: The text. Setting it shows it and fires nothing. The `value` attribute is what a form reset returns to.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: The accessible name. Required: the input draws no label and asks no Field for one, so this is the only name it has. Never drawn.

attributes.name: placeholder
attributes.description: A hint drawn while the value is empty. Never the name. A multi-line input is as tall as the placeholder's lines, within `min-rows` and `max-rows`.

attributes.name: layout
attributes.description: Where the actions stand in the capsule. `inline` (the default, and every value it does not know): on the line being written — the attach button and the leading actions before the typing area, the counter, the trailing actions and the send button after it. `stacked`: the typing area and the send button on one line, and everything else in a row beneath them, inside the capsule. A capsule too narrow for inline is laid out stacked whatever this says; the number of lines never changes the layout.

attributes.name: min-rows
attributes.description: The fewest lines a multi-line input is tall (`min-rows`). Anything below 1 is 1.

attributes.name: max-rows
attributes.description: The most lines the typing area grows to before it scrolls inside itself (`max-rows`). Given to the embedded text input as its `maxRows`, with a default of the chat composer's own: six lines. 0 sets no limit.

attributes.name: max-length
attributes.description: The most user-perceived characters a message may hold (`max-length`); 0 is no limit. It refuses no edit and shortens no paste: text beyond it stays, is marked, and stops sending until the person has cut it.

attributes.name: counter
attributes.description: Draws the number of characters, and `maxLength` where one is set, before the trailing actions.

attributes.name: send-key
attributes.description: What Enter does on a hardware keyboard (`send-key`). `enter` (the default, and every value it does not know): Enter sends and Shift+Enter begins a new line. `modifier`: Enter begins a new line and Ctrl+Enter or Command+Enter sends. Ctrl+Enter and Command+Enter send under both.

attributes.name: attachments
attributes.description: Whether files can be attached, and who holds them. `none` (the default, and every value it does not know): text alone. `own`: the chat composer keeps the files a person attached and draws a File item for each, and `send` carries them. `given`: the product gives the File items as children and the chat composer lays them out and keeps no file.

attributes.name: attachment-form
attributes.description: The form of the File items the chat composer draws itself, while `attachments` is `own` (`attachment-form`). `auto` (the default, and every value it does not know): a tile with its picture for an image, a row for every other file. `tile`: every file a tile. `row`: every file a row, and no picture. A refused file is a row under every value.

attributes.name: multiple
attributes.description: Whether more than one file can be attached. Given to the file picker as its `multiple`; the default is true (`multiple="false"` says false).

attributes.name: accept
attributes.description: The kinds of file that are taken: extensions with their dot (".pdf") and media types ("image/png", a family as "image/*"). The attribute is a comma-separated list, as a native file input's. Empty takes every kind.

attributes.name: max-size
attributes.description: The largest size of one file, in bytes (`max-size`). Null sets no limit. Judged from the size the browser reports; the file is not read.

attributes.name: max-files
attributes.description: The most files one choice or one drop may bring, while `multiple` is set (`max-files`). Null sets no limit; zero refuses every file — the room a full list has left. Nothing is counted across choices.

attributes.name: sending
attributes.description: What was sent is on its way, or its answer is still arriving: the product's to set and to clear. While it is set nothing more can be sent; the typing area stays open.

attributes.name: stoppable
attributes.description: While `sending` is set, puts a stop button in the send button's place, which asks the product to stop what is under way (`stop`). Ignored while `sending` is not set.

attributes.name: blocked
attributes.description: The product's own reason that nothing can be sent now. The send button is disabled and the send key sends nothing; the product says why in its own words.

attributes.name: keep-after-send
attributes.description: Keeps the text and the attachments after `send` (`keep-after-send`), for a product that clears them itself (`clear()`) once it knows the message arrived.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: Nothing can be written, attached, removed or sent: every member and every Button in a slot is disabled. Inside a Field, disable the Field.

attributes.name: error
attributes.description: Draws the capsule in its error condition and exposes the typing area as invalid. A Field sets it with its own error. It does not stop sending by itself: `blocked` does.

attributes.name: send-label
attributes.description: The accessible name of the send button the chat composer brings (`send-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ sendLabel })`). Tanrei has none: without them the button is drawn and works, and has no name.

attributes.name: stop-label
attributes.description: The accessible name of the stop button the chat composer brings (`stop-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ stopLabel })`).

attributes.name: attach-label
attributes.description: The accessible name of the attach button the chat composer brings (`attach-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ attachLabel })`).

attributes.name: remove-label

declarations.description:
Asks one question that may have several answers among a few choices shown all at once. Built from a field group
(`<tanrei-field-group>`) and checkboxes (`<tanrei-checkbox>`): the field group's label, requirement, description and
one error around the product's own checkboxes, whose checked values the group holds as one list under one name, and —
where `select-all-label` is given — one more checkbox before the first that checks them all.

Contract: specs/checkbox-group.spec.json. `<tanrei-checkbox-group name="notify" label="Notify me by"><tanrei-checkbox
value="email" label="Email" checked></tanrei-checkbox>…</tanrei-checkbox-group>`: the checkboxes are the element's
children and stay in the product's light DOM; each stands for its `value`.

Composed (`src/primitives/composed.ts`): its shadow root holds the field group's own element around the
select-all checkbox and a slot, so it draws nothing of its own and has no token — every
`--tanrei-comp-field-group-*` and `--tanrei-comp-checkbox-*` value reaches the members by inheritance, and one
instance is set apart by setting such a property on this element. Each of the eleven props of the frame is the
field group's, set on it unchanged. One level down, the same by hand: `<tanrei-field-group label="Notify me by">
<tanrei-checkbox name="notify" value="email" label="Email" checked></tanrei-checkbox>…</tanrei-field-group>` — for
checkboxes that each need a name of their own, a set that holds something else, or another rule for "all".

`value` is a property only: an array of the checked values, in the order of the checkboxes, followed by the entries
no checkbox stands for, which are kept; it is copied in and out. The first value is written as `checked` on the
children; once the product has set `value`, `value` decides. A person's switch — of one checkbox, or of the select-all
checkbox — sets `value` and fires `input` and one `change`; the checkboxes fire nothing of their own.

Form-associated: it submits one entry per value under `name` — what checkboxes of one name submit — and its
checkboxes submit nothing; a checkbox disabled by itself keeps its entry; a disabled group submits nothing. It
returns to its first value when the form is reset, is restored on navigation, follows `<fieldset disabled>`, and
reports `valueMissing` while `requirement="required"` and the list is empty, with `error-text`, else the required
text, else `label` as its message. It never sets `error` itself.

The element is not focusable itself and has no role: every checkbox is a stop of its own, `focus()` goes to the first
enabled one, and the group, its name and its description are the field group's (`label`, never `aria-label`).

declarations.default: css` ${unsafeCSS(Object.entries(CONDITIONS).map(([condition, selector]) => conditionBlock(PREFIX, condition, PARTS, selector)).join('\n'))} /* CHK-15: the control, then the label at its inline end, comp.checkbox.label.gap away, wrapping. */ ${selectionLabel(PREFIX, `var(--tanrei-comp-checkbox-container-size)`)} /* CHK-21: the label is text of its own direction — its first strong character's — isolated from what is around it; the layout direction still puts it at the control's inline end and aligns the lines it wraps to. */ ${productText('.label', { align: 'start' })} /* CHK-12: the round container, comp.checkbox.container.size across, with the box centered in it. */ .control { display: grid; place-items: center; inline-size: var(--tanrei-comp-checkbox-container-size); block-size: var(--tanrei-comp-checkbox-container-size); } .container, .box { grid-area: 1 / 1; } .container { position: relative; /* Its own stacking context, so the ripple sits above the container color. */ isolation: isolate; inline-size: 100%; block-size: 100%; ${unsafeCSS(selectionContainerShape)} background: var(--_c); transition-property: background-color, border-radius; transition-duration: var(--tanrei-comp-checkbox-motion-state-duration); transition-timing-function: var(--tanrei-comp-checkbox-motion-state-easing); } /* CHK-12: the box, its outline inside its edge, and its fill inside the outline — never under it. */ .box { position: relative; /* CHK-22: the group the outline and the fill are added in — nothing outside the box takes part in the sum. */ isolation: isolate; box-sizing: border-box; inline-size: var(--tanrei-comp-checkbox-box-size); block-size: var(--tanrei-comp-checkbox-box-size); padding: var(--tanrei-comp-checkbox-outline-width); ${unsafeCSS(cornerRadius(`--tanrei-comp-checkbox-box-shape`))} pointer-events: none; transition: border-radius ${unsafeCSS(state)}; } /* CHK-22: the outline and the fill are ONE shape. They are two layers of the same box with the same padding of outline.width, each painted over the whole box and cut by a mask along the same edge, the box's content box: the outline (::before) is everything BUT the content box, the fill (.fill) is the content box. On a pixel that edge crosses, the outline covers a share and the fill exactly the rest, and the fill is ADDED to the outline (plus-lighter, inside the box's isolated group) instead of composited over it: the two shares sum to the whole — for opaque and translucent colors alike, with nothing behind the box showing between them and neither painted over the other (CHK-12), at any zoom or position. What this replaces — an inset shadow over a content-box background, two paints antialiased apart — let up to a quarter of the background through that edge. Both are cut by a mask of two layers, and by nothing else, because that is the one way all three engines cut the two from the same rasterized edge (measured in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit at device pixel ratios 1 to 3, on and off the pixel grid): a fill clipped by background-clip overlaps the masked outline in Chromium, which snaps a background to the pixel grid and not a mask; a fill behind a mask of one layer leaves a seam in Firefox. */ .box::before, .fill { position: absolute; /* Under the marks. */ z-index: -1; inset: 0; box-sizing: border-box; padding: inherit; border-radius: inherit; corner-shape: inherit; /* CHK-5, CHK-13: the state motion when a state recolors the box, the selection motion when the condition does. */ transition: background-color var(--_recolor-duration) var(--_recolor-easing); } /* A mask is alpha, not a color: #000 is "all of it", transparent "none of it". A mask of one layer is a clip in Firefox, rasterized on its own. */ .box::before { content: ''; background: var(--_o); mask: linear-gradient(#000 0 0) content-box exclude, linear-gradient(#000 0 0) no-clip; } .fill { background: var(--_b); mask: linear-gradient(#000 0 0) content-box exclude, linear-gradient(transparent 0 0) no-clip; mix-blend-mode: plus-lighter; } /* CHK-12: the mark is the icon set's check (selected) or remove (indeterminate), a glyph box of comp.checkbox.mark.size centered on the box and not clipped by it, in the selected family and fill at comp.checkbox.mark.weight (the mark's own weight, not sys.icon.weight: it changes the stroke, never the glyph box); the font clamps the optical size to its range (src/styles/icons.ts). Both glyphs are always laid out, so either can fade in or out. */ ${iconGlyph('.mark', { size: '--tanrei-comp-checkbox-mark-size', weight: '--tanrei-comp-checkbox-mark-weight', selected: ':host', duration: '--tanrei-comp-checkbox-motion-selection-duration', easing: '--tanrei-comp-checkbox-motion-selection-easing', })} .mark { position: absolute; declarations.description:
Lets people turn one independent choice on or off, show a parent choice that is only partly on, and mark a required
choice left unmade.

Contract: specs/checkbox.spec.json. Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-checkbox-*` tokens, one set per
condition (unselected, selected, indeterminate and their `error-` forms) and state: how a state looks is the active
design system's decision. How a press is answered and how keyboard focus is drawn are the system's choices of kind
(`--tanrei-sys-behavior-*`), read from the cascade.

Form-associated: with a `name` it submits `value` (default "on") while checked, resets to its `checked` attribute,
honours `required` and a disabled `<fieldset>`, as a native checkbox does. It switches its own `checked` (and clears
`indeterminate`) before it fires `input` and `change`. The semantics are a native checkbox in the shadow root, named
by `label`; a click on the visible label toggles it.

Inside a `<tanrei-checkbox-group>` (CHK-23) it is a choice of that set: its `checked` is the group's — whether the
group's list holds its `value` —, it submits nothing itself whatever `name` it carries, `required` is not read, and
it fires no `input` and no `change`: the group fires one `change` with the list. A checkbox that carries no `value`
has none there (the "on" a bare checkbox submits is not read). Taken out of the group it is as it is anywhere.

declarations.description:
Collects a list of short texts — e-mail addresses, telephone numbers, keywords — typed one after another in one
field. Built from a Field (`<tanrei-field>`), the Text input it frames (`<tanrei-text-input>`) and one Chip
(`<tanrei-chip>`) for each entry, standing in the Text input's box before the typing part: each text the product's
check accepts becomes a chip that can be removed or taken back, and the list is the field's one value.

Contract: specs/chip-field.spec.json. `<tanrei-chip-field name="to" label="Recipients" type="email"
remove-label="Remove {entry}"></tanrei-chip-field>`, with `field.separators = [',', ';', ' ']` (or the attribute
`separators='[",", ";", " "]'`).

Composed (`src/primitives/composed.ts`): its shadow root holds the members' own elements, so it draws
nothing of its own and has no token — every `--tanrei-comp-field-*`, `--tanrei-comp-input-box-*`,
`--tanrei-comp-text-input-*` and `--tanrei-comp-chip-*` value reaches the members by inheritance, and one chip field is set apart by setting such a
property on this element. One level down, the same picture by hand: `<tanrei-field label="Recipients">
<tanrei-text-input type="email"><tanrei-chip slot="entries" kind="input" size="small" label="ada@example.com"
remove-label="Remove ada@example.com"></tanrei-chip></tanrei-text-input></tanrei-field>`. What the chip field adds
to that: making entries, the keys among them, the one Tab stop, the announcements, and the list as one form value.

**An entry is made** of the typed text by Enter, by a separator the product lists (`separators`; none by default),
by focus leaving the field, and from pasted text that holds a separator or a line break. Each candidate is trimmed,
refused where the list holds the same text (`duplicate`) or is full (`maxEntries`: `limit`), and otherwise asked of
the product with `check`: `event.preventDefault()` refuses it (`invalid`), and `event.detail.reason = '…'` gives the
words. The chip field knows no grammar: what an e-mail address is, is the product's check. A refused text stays in
the typing part, and while it does the field is in error with the words of the refusal — `error` and `errorText`
themselves do not change.

**Keys.** The typing part is the one Tab stop. Backspace, or the arrow that points to the line's start, at the start
of the text moves focus to the last entry; there the arrows, Home and End move among the entries, Backspace and
Delete remove the one that has focus, Enter and Space take it back into the typing part to be changed, Escape and
Tab return to the typing part.

`value` is an array of strings (assign a new array to change it); the `value` attribute is read once, as a JSON
array. `inputValue` is the text being typed. Form-associated: it submits one value per entry under `name` — none
while the list is empty, never the typed text —, resets to the list it was first given, is restored on navigation,
follows a disabled `<fieldset>`, and reports a missing value while `requirement` is `required` and the list is empty.

The element is not focusable itself and has no role: `focus()` goes to the typing part, and its name is `label`.

members.name: value

chip field writes it as the person makes, removes and takes back entries, and fires `change`. What the product
sets is shown as given and is not checked — assign a new array — and fires nothing; an entry that is empty or only
white space is left out. The `value` attribute is read once, as a JSON array of strings, and is what a form reset
returns to.

members.name: inputValue
members.description:
The text in the field; for date, time and date-time, the ISO 8601 form of what its segments give (2026-09-27, 14:30,
2026-09-27T14:30), or empty while a segment is empty or the value is not available. Setting it shows it and fires
nothing. The `value` attribute is what a form reset returns to.

members.name: separators
members.description:
The texts that end an entry when they are typed or found in what is pasted, as the product names them for what
its entries are: `[',', ';', ' ']` for e-mail addresses, `[',']` for keywords that may hold a space. The
attribute is read as a JSON array. Empty, the default: Enter and a line break alone make an entry — a name such as
"Lovelace, Ada" must not be cut in two by a default. A line break always ends an entry.

members.name: maxEntries
members.description: The most entries the list may hold (`max-entries`); 0 is no limit. An entry that would exceed it is refused with the reason `limit`; the typing part stays usable. It never cuts a list the product sets.

members.name: variant
members.description:
Stacked is a filled box that shows focus and error with a line inside its edge, under the label its Field draws
above it; filled and outlined float the label inside the box, marked by a tinted box and a bottom line, or by a
border. Use one style
per form. A design system may leave some out (the default system ships stacked only) or add values.

members.name: size
members.description: Minimum height of a single-line field's container (48 / 56 in the default system). The hit area always meets the minimum target.

members.name: type
members.description:
What the value is: chooses the keyboard, autocorrection, obscured entry and semantics. `code` is text written for
a machine rather than for a reader — a snippet of configuration, a pattern, an identifier, a query, a key: a
left-to-right run in the code face that the browser does not correct, capitalise, check for spelling or complete,
on one line or, with `multiline`, on many. `date`, `time` and `date-time` are entered segment by segment in the
locale's numeric form. The value is always a string.

members.name: placeholder
members.description:
A hint shown while the value is empty and the label is not in the input line (above, floated or hidden). Never a
replacement for `label`. In a code field it is an example of the code and is drawn as code; a hint in words
belongs in its Field's `supportingText`. Ignored by a date, time or date-time field, whose empty segments each show their own.

members.name: autocomplete

its entries are: `[',', ';', ' ']` for e-mail addresses, `[',']` for keywords that may hold a space. The
attribute is read as a JSON array. Empty, the default: Enter and a line break alone make an entry — a name such as
"Lovelace, Ada" must not be cut in two by a default. A line break always ends an entry.

attributes.name: max-entries
attributes.description: The most entries the list may hold (`max-entries`); 0 is no limit. An entry that would exceed it is refused with the reason `limit`; the typing part stays usable. It never cuts a list the product sets.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description:
Stacked is a filled box that shows focus and error with a line inside its edge, under the label its Field draws
above it; filled and outlined float the label inside the box, marked by a tinted box and a bottom line, or by a
border. Use one style
per form. A design system may leave some out (the default system ships stacked only) or add values.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: Minimum height of a single-line field's container (48 / 56 in the default system). The hit area always meets the minimum target.

attributes.name: type
attributes.description:
What the value is: chooses the keyboard, autocorrection, obscured entry and semantics. `code` is text written for
a machine rather than for a reader — a snippet of configuration, a pattern, an identifier, a query, a key: a
left-to-right run in the code face that the browser does not correct, capitalise, check for spelling or complete,
on one line or, with `multiline`, on many. `date`, `time` and `date-time` are entered segment by segment in the
locale's numeric form. The value is always a string.

attributes.name: placeholder
attributes.description:
A hint shown while the value is empty and the label is not in the input line (above, floated or hidden). Never a
replacement for `label`. In a code field it is an example of the code and is drawn as code; a hint in words
belongs in its Field's `supportingText`. Ignored by a date, time or date-time field, whose empty segments each show their own.

attributes.name: readonly
attributes.description: The value can be focused, selected and copied, but not changed (the `readonly` attribute).

attributes.name: autocomplete
attributes.description: The autofill hint, as an HTML autofill field name (email, current-password, one-time-code…). A code field left without one asks the browser to offer no remembered entry.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Names the control, visibly and to assistive technology. Required, unless the control names itself (a checkbox or a switch with its own label): then leave it empty and the field adds only help and an error.

attributes.name: label-hidden
attributes.description: Does not draw the label, which stays the accessible name (`label-hidden`). For a control whose visible label is elsewhere.

attributes.name: supporting-text
attributes.description: Help shown below the control and given to assistive technology as the control's description (`supporting-text`). While the field is in error it gives way to `errorText`, unless the design system keeps both (`--tanrei-comp-field-error-text-placement: append`).

attributes.name: error-text
attributes.description: Shown while `error` is true, in `supportingText`'s place (below it, which stays, where the design system says `append`): what is wrong with this answer and how to put it right, in words (`error-text`).

attributes.name: error
attributes.description: Puts the field in the error condition: the error text is drawn, the control is exposed as invalid and, where it has an error condition of its own, drawn in it. The field never sets this itself.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: Disables the control and draws the frame as disabled. Disable a framed control here, not on the control, so that its label follows.

attributes.name: requirement
attributes.description: What the form asks of the control: `required` exposes it as required and draws the required mark; `optional` draws the optional tag; `none` says and draws nothing. It never validates.

attributes.name: required-mark
attributes.description: How this control shows that it is required (`required-mark`): `tag` is a small filled tag with `requiredText`, `asterisk` is "*" after the label, `none` draws nothing and keeps the semantics; `auto` takes the design system's answer (`--tanrei-comp-field-requirement-mark`, which follows `--tanrei-sys-behavior-requirement-mark`).

attributes.name: required-text
attributes.description: The text of the required tag (`required-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ requiredText })`). Tanrei has none: without them the asterisk is drawn in the tag's place and the required state is kept.

attributes.name: optional-text
attributes.description: The text of the optional tag, also part of the description (`optional-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ optionalText })`). Tanrei has none: without them no tag is drawn and nothing is said.

attributes.name: invalid-text
attributes.description: The error text shown while an entry was refused by the product's check and the check gave no reason of its own (`invalid-text`). This field's own: it reads no word of the product's. Empty, `errorText` is shown.

attributes.name: duplicate-text
attributes.description: The error text shown while an entry was refused because the list already holds the same text (`duplicate-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ duplicateEntryText })`); with neither, `errorText` is shown.

attributes.name: limit-text
attributes.description: The error text shown while an entry was refused because the list holds `maxEntries` already (`limit-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ entryLimitText })`); with neither, `errorText` is shown.

attributes.name: remove-label
attributes.description: The accessible name of each entry's remove action (`remove-label`): the whole name in your language, with the place `{entry}` that the chip field fills with that entry's text. This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ entryRemoveLabel })`); with neither the action is drawn, works and has no name.

attributes.name: added-text
attributes.description: The sentence assistive technology is told when one entry is made (`added-text`), with the place `{entry}`: this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ entryAddedText })`); with neither nothing is said.

attributes.name: added-count-text
attributes.description: The sentence assistive technology is told when several entries are made at once (`added-count-text`), with the place `{count}`: this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ entriesAddedText })`); with neither, `addedText` is said for the last of them.

attributes.name: removed-text
attributes.description: The sentence assistive technology is told when an entry is removed (`removed-text`), with the place `{entry}`: this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ entryRemovedText })`); with neither nothing is said.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Web only: the name each entry is submitted under.

declarations.default: ['outlined', 'elevated']
declarations.description: The values every design system has. A layer may add more; those get their styles on demand.
