declarations.description:
Shows a compact choice, a suggested action or an item the user entered as a small labelled control.

Contract: specs/chip.spec.json. Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-chip-*` tokens, one set per variant, look
(plain, or `selected.` for a filter chip that is on) and state, and the `remove.` parts of an input chip's remove
action in its own states: how a state looks is the active design system's decision, not this component's. How a
press is answered and how keyboard focus is drawn are the system's choices of kind (`--tanrei-sys-behavior-*`),
and how far its corners ease is the system's amount (`--tanrei-sys-shape-corner-smoothing`).

`kind` decides what the chip does and its parts; `variant` only how it looks. An action chip is a button. A filter chip
is a button with a pressed state: activation switches `selected` and fires `change`, and when on it shows a check in
its leading position. An input chip has a remove action, a second button named by `removeLabel`, pressed by pointer,
touch or assistive technology and not a Tab stop: an input chip is one stop, and Backspace or Delete on it removes it,
which the chip tells assistive technology with `aria-keyshortcuts`. Both fire `remove` — the chip never removes itself
(the page does, and moves focus). By default the remove action reads as destructive (`destructiveRemove`; the attribute
`no-destructive-remove` turns it off): it looks the same at rest and takes the error color while it is hovered,
focused or pressed — a color only, never a change of name, glyph or size. The label is the visible text and the
accessible name; the icon (the `icon` slot) and the avatar (the `avatar` slot, input chips only) are decorative.

An action chip with `href` is a link and not a button (CHP-33): the shadow root holds an `<a href>` in place
of the `<button>`, drawn from the same tokens in every state. Enter activates it and Space does not; `click` fires
first and cancelling it cancels the navigation. `target="new"` opens a new tab, safely (`noopener`), draws the icon
set's `open_in_new` at the chip's inline end and reads `target-label` as the link's description. A filter chip and an
input chip take no destination.

cssParts.description: The check a filter chip that is on shows in the leading position (hidden from assistive technology).

cssParts.description: The box that clips the avatar to comp.chip.avatar.shape.
cssParts.name: avatar

cssParts.description: The label text.
cssParts.name: label

cssParts.description: An input chip's remove action: the native button on its round container, with its own states (the cancel glyph, filled).

slots.description: The leading icon: a glyph of the system's icon set (its ligature text), or an ``. A glyph the icon set flags is mirrored in right-to-left; `data-mirror="auto | always | never"` on the element decides for one use.
slots.name: icon

slots.description: The leading image of an input chip (an ``), in place of the icon. Ignored for other kinds.

members.name: kind
members.description: What the chip does: action (a button), filter (on or off) or input (an entered item the user can remove). Kind decides the role and the parts, not the look.

members.name: variant
members.description: Look: outlined sits flat on a plain surface; elevated is raised for chips over media or a busy background.

members.name: size
members.description: Visual height (small 24 / medium 32 in the default system). The hit area always meets the minimum target.

members.name: selected
members.description: Whether a filter chip is on. Ignored unless `kind` is filter.

members.name: disabled
members.description: Prevents interaction and removes the chip, and its remove action, from the focus order.

members.name: label
members.description: The visible text and the accessible name.

members.name: removeLabel
members.description: The accessible name of an input chip's remove action; it should name the item ("Remove Ada Lovelace"). Required when `kind` is input.

members.name: destructiveRemove
members.description:
Whether an input chip's remove action reads as destructive: the same at rest, the error color while hovered,
keyboard-focused or pressed. Set `no-destructive-remove` where removing loses nothing (a filter the user can add
back in one step). Color only: the name, glyph, size and behaviour are the same either way. Ignored unless `kind` is input.

members.name: removable
members.description:
Whether an input chip draws its remove action. Set `not-removable` for an entry that cannot be taken away now (a
read-only field's): no remove action is drawn, so none stands there doing nothing, none is a stop, Backspace and
Delete ask for nothing, and the chip is padded as one without a remove action (CHP-38). Ignored unless `kind` is input.

members.name: href
members.description:
The destination of an action chip: a URL, a path or a fragment. Not empty, the chip is a link and not a button
(CHP-33): the link role, an `<a href>` in the shadow root, activated by Enter and not by Space, drawn exactly as the
action chip it would otherwise be. Ignored unless `kind` is action; white space is no destination, and a
`javascript:` address or one that cannot be read is refused and reported in debug builds (CHP-37).

members.name: target
members.description:
Where the destination opens: `same` (here) or `new` (a new tab or window, with `noopener`), which the chip marks
with the glyph `open_in_new` after its label and says through `targetLabel` (CHP-35). HTML's `_self` and `_blank`
are read as those two; anything else is `same` and reported. Ignored without `href`.

members.name: targetLabel
members.description: What assistive technology reads after the link's name while `target` is `new` ("opens in a new tab"): your words, in your language. Required then; ignored otherwise.

members.name: rel
members.description: Web only: forwarded to the anchor's `rel`; `target="new"` adds `noopener` to it. Ignored without `href`.

members.name: download
members.description: Web only: forwarded to the anchor's `download` (the file name; empty for the address's own). Ignored without `href`.

members.name: hasIcon
members.description: Whether the icon slot has content.

members.name: hasAvatar
members.description: Whether the avatar slot has content.

members.name: axes
members.default: new OpenAxesController(this, { component: 'chip', behavior: 'CHP-7', axes: AXES })
members.description: CHP-7: sizes and variants a design system adds, and a value the active system does not have (src/primitives/axes.ts).

members.name: mirror
members.description:
CHP-30: the glyph in the icon slot is marked when the icon set mirrors its name in right-to-left, or the product's
`data-mirror` says so (src/primitives/glyph-mirror.ts); `iconGlyph()` draws the mark. The check and the remove glyph
the chip draws itself are not named to the controller: they are never mirrored. CHP-35: the mark of a link that
opens a new context is named — the icon set mirrors `open_in_new`.

members.name: link
members.default: new LinkController(this, { ids: { refused: 'CHP-37', newContext: 'CHP-35' }, disabled: () => this.disabled, holds: () => (this.effectiveKind === 'action' ? null : this.effectiveKind === 'filter' ? 'a filter chip' : 'an input chip'), })
members.description:
CHP-33 … CHP-37: the link an action chip is while it has a destination, what its anchor carries, and what a debug
build is told (src/primitives/link.ts). A filter chip holds a state and an input chip a second action:
neither takes one (CHP-37).

members.name: press
members.default: new PressController(this, { container: () => this.container, holdCarrier: () => this.renderRoot.querySelector('.label'), disabled: () => this.disabled, keys: () => this.link.pressKeys, })
members.description:
CHP-8 / CHP-9: the chip's pressed state, press-hold and the answer the system chooses (src/primitives/press.ts).
CHP-34: a link chip is pressed by Enter alone; Space is the browser's.

members.name: removePress
members.default: new PressController(this, { container: () => this.removeButton, holdCarrier: () => this.renderRoot.querySelector('.remove .hold'), disabled: () => this.disabled || !this.removes, origin: selectionRippleOrigin(() => this.removeButton), })
members.description:
CHP-20: the remove action's own press, within its round container; a press in its hit area outside the round
container grows the ripple from the container's center (src/primitives/selection.ts).

members.name: container
members.description: The chip's native button, or the anchor of its link form: the one styled part (CHP-33).

members.name: effectiveKind
members.description: A kind the chip does not know is drawn and behaves as an action chip.

members.name: removes
members.description: CHP-18, CHP-38: an input chip has its remove action unless it is not removable.

members.name: on
members.description: CHP-11: selected counts only on a filter chip.

members.name: click
members.description: `element.click()` activates the chip as a person would — through its native button, or its anchor, so a link is followed — and does nothing while disabled.

members.name: onFocus
members.description: CHP-10: where style queries are missing, the focus style is read when focus arrives.

members.name: onClick
members.description:
CHP-11: a filter chip switches its own `selected`, then fires `click`, then `change` — the order and timing of a
native checkbox's: the state has already switched when `click` listeners run, and `change` follows once the click
has finished its way through the page. Its last stop is the window, so `change` is fired from a listener added
there for this click; a listener that stops the click on its way still gets its `change`, in the next task.

members.name: onKeyDown
members.description: CHP-19: Backspace or Delete on a focused input chip asks for its removal, once per press.

members.name: onRemoveClick
members.description:
CHP-18: the remove action fires `remove`, never `click`: its native click stops at the remove button, inside the
shadow root, so it never reaches the element's listeners.

members.name: requestRemove
members.description: CHP-22: the chip asks; the page removes it and moves focus.

events.name: change
events.description: A filter chip was activated; fired after its `click`, as a native checkbox does. `detail.selected` (and the element's `selected`) is the new value.

events.name: remove
events.description: The user asked to remove an input chip, with its remove action or with Backspace or Delete. The chip stays until the page removes it.

The chip itself was activated by pointer, touch, keyboard or assistive technology. Never fired by the remove action. A link chip fires it before the browser follows the address; `preventDefault()` cancels the navigation.
events.name: click

attributes.name: kind
attributes.description: What the chip does: action (a button), filter (on or off) or input (an entered item the user can remove). Kind decides the role and the parts, not the look.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description: Look: outlined sits flat on a plain surface; elevated is raised for chips over media or a busy background.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: Visual height (small 24 / medium 32 in the default system). The hit area always meets the minimum target.

attributes.name: selected
attributes.description: Whether a filter chip is on. Ignored unless `kind` is filter.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: Prevents interaction and removes the chip, and its remove action, from the focus order.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: The visible text and the accessible name.

attributes.name: remove-label
attributes.description: The accessible name of an input chip's remove action; it should name the item ("Remove Ada Lovelace"). Required when `kind` is input.

attributes.name: no-destructive-remove
attributes.description:
Whether an input chip's remove action reads as destructive: the same at rest, the error color while hovered,
keyboard-focused or pressed. Set `no-destructive-remove` where removing loses nothing (a filter the user can add
back in one step). Color only: the name, glyph, size and behaviour are the same either way. Ignored unless `kind` is input.

attributes.name: not-removable
attributes.description:
Whether an input chip draws its remove action. Set `not-removable` for an entry that cannot be taken away now (a
read-only field's): no remove action is drawn, so none stands there doing nothing, none is a stop, Backspace and
Delete ask for nothing, and the chip is padded as one without a remove action (CHP-38). Ignored unless `kind` is input.

attributes.name: href
attributes.description:
The destination of an action chip: a URL, a path or a fragment. Not empty, the chip is a link and not a button
(CHP-33): the link role, an `<a href>` in the shadow root, activated by Enter and not by Space, drawn exactly as the
action chip it would otherwise be. Ignored unless `kind` is action; white space is no destination, and a
`javascript:` address or one that cannot be read is refused and reported in debug builds (CHP-37).

attributes.name: target
attributes.description:
Where the destination opens: `same` (here) or `new` (a new tab or window, with `noopener`), which the chip marks
with the glyph `open_in_new` after its label and says through `targetLabel` (CHP-35). HTML's `_self` and `_blank`
are read as those two; anything else is `same` and reported. Ignored without `href`.

attributes.name: target-label
attributes.description: What assistive technology reads after the link's name while `target` is `new` ("opens in a new tab"): your words, in your language. Required then; ignored otherwise.

attributes.name: rel
attributes.description: Web only: forwarded to the anchor's `rel`; `target="new"` adds `noopener` to it. Ignored without `href`.

attributes.name: download
attributes.description: Web only: forwarded to the anchor's `download` (the file name; empty for the address's own). Ignored without `href`.

declarations.name: CODE_BLOCK_BEFORE_CSS
declarations.description: The stylesheet text of a block that is not upgraded, in the components' layer: `code.css` alone carries it, first.

declarations.name: CORE_VARIANTS
declarations.default: ['filled', 'outlined']
declarations.description: The values every design system has. A layer may add more; those get their styles on demand.

declarations.name: CORE_SIZES
declarations.default: ['small', 'medium']

declarations.name: DEFAULT_VARIANT
declarations.default: 'filled'

declarations.name: DEFAULT_SIZE
declarations.default: 'medium'

declarations.name: sizeBlock
declarations.description:
The members of the size axis (COD-2, COD-3): the code's text style, taken whole, and the two paddings. The weight is
named apart, because a syntax role adds its emphasis to it (COD-18).

declarations.name: variantBlock
declarations.description:
A look (COD-1): the container's fill, and the ground — the opaque color the gutter and the copy button's patch stand
on while code scrolls under them (COD-10, COD-13). A filled look's ground is its fill. The outlined look has none of
its own (its fill is transparent): it is read on whatever it is placed on, which a stylesheet cannot know, so the
ground is `--tanrei-code-block-ground` where the product names it and the surface color otherwise.

declarations.name: layoutBlock
declarations.description:
What the element's shadow styles change by its props, at the values of a block with no header and no copy button:
the padding above the first line (COD-3; COD-8 puts the header's own there) and the padding before and after the
lines (COD-10 widens the one at the copy button's side).

declarations.name: SYNTAX_ROLES
declarations.default: ['comment', 'keyword', 'string', 'constant', 'function', 'type', 'tag', 'property', 'punctuation']
declarations.description:
The syntax roles a run may name (COD-18), besides `plain`: the values of the token axis `comp.code-block.syntax`,
as every design system has them. Data, not selectors: each is drawn by ONE rule from the two tokens that carry its
name — `syntax.color.<role>` and `syntax.emphasis.<role>`, a step of weight added to the code's own. The list is
held to the generated tokens twice: the build refuses to write `code.css` while it differs from the roles
`src/generated/tokens.css` names (scripts/build.js), and a role a layer ADDS to the axis gets the same
rule from `roleRule` — in the build of a product's own stylesheet, and in the element when it first meets a run of
that role whose tokens the cascade has.

declarations.name: CODE_BLOCK_DRAWN
declarations.default: '--_code-block-light'
declarations.description:
A name these rules set on the block: a root whose cascade gives it draws the block's lines already, and the element
does not add the rules to it again (src/primitives/sheets.ts). No shadow style of the element sets it.

declarations.name: layered
declarations.description: Rules in the components' layer, as a stylesheet's text.

declarations.name: CODE_BLOCK_CSS
declarations.description: The stylesheet text: the rules in the components' layer, as `code.css` carries them and the element adopts them.

declarations.name: BARE_BLOCK_CSS
declarations.description:
A bare `pre` — rendered Markdown that the product did not wrap in the element: the filled look at the medium size
with the code's text, scrolling in its own box (COD-1 to COD-4, PRS-15). Declarations only: the build writes them
under prose's own `pre` (scripts/build.js).

declarations.name: firstLine
declarations.description: COD-25: a start line below 1 or not whole is 1.

declarations.name: furnish
declarations.description:
What stands beside each line. `texts` are the lines' texts in order, with or without their line breaks: only whether
a line is empty is read from them (COD-17). `true` for the props is a block that has none of them.

declarations.name: AXES
declarations.default: [ { name: 'size', core: CORE_SIZES, default: DEFAULT_SIZE, rules: (value, selector) => sizeBlock(value, selector, DEFAULT_SIZE), probe: (value) => `${PREFIX}-container-padding-block-${value}` }, { name: 'variant', core: CORE_VARIANTS, default: DEFAULT_VARIANT, rules: (value, selector) => variantBlock(value, selector, DEFAULT_VARIANT), probe: (value) => `${PREFIX}-${value}-container-color` }, ]
declarations.description:
The open axes (COD-25): a size or variant a layer added gets its block on demand, built by the same
functions as the core blocks and falling back to the default's tokens; a value the active system lacks is reported in
debug builds. A variant a layer adds has no edge: only `outlined` draws one (COD-1).

declarations.name: styles
declarations.default: css` /* COD-1: a block as wide as its layout gives it and never wider, with no space outside itself. */ :host { display: block; min-inline-size: 0; max-inline-size: 100%; } :host([hidden]) { display: none; } /* COD-25: a block with no code draws nothing and takes no space. Its own rule: a browser without custom states drops only this one, and the empty block is then an empty box. */ :host(:state(empty)) { display: none; } ${unsafeCSS(sizeBlock(DEFAULT_SIZE, ':host'))} ${unsafeCSS(CORE_SIZES.filter((size) => size !== DEFAULT_SIZE).map((size) => sizeBlock(size, `:host([size='${size}'])`)).join('\n'))} ${unsafeCSS(variantBlock(DEFAULT_VARIANT, ':host'))} ${unsafeCSS(CORE_VARIANTS.filter((variant) => variant !== DEFAULT_VARIANT).map((variant) => variantBlock(variant, `:host([variant='${variant}'])`)).join('\n'))} ${unsafeCSS(layoutBlock(':host'))} /* COD-1: the container — the look's fill, container.shape corners through the shared corner rule, no elevation. It clips nothing: the body rounds its own corners, so the copy button's hit area can reach past the edge (CPY-1). The code's text style is set here so that a line of it (1lh) is a length the body and the copy button's patch can use. */ .container { position: relative; display: flex; flex-direction: column; box-sizing: border-box; ${unsafeCSS(cornerRadius(`${PREFIX}-container-shape`))} background: var(--_code-block-container); font: var(--_code-block-font); letter-spacing: var(--_code-block-tracking); } /* COD-9: at least as tall as the copy button and its inset above and below. */ .container.copy { min-block-size: calc(${BUTTON} + ${T('copy-button-inset')} * 2); } /* COD-1: the outlined look's edge, inside the container's size and following its corners — drawn over what the block holds, so a band, the gutter and the copy button's patch never cover it, and nothing moves for it. */ :host([variant='outlined']) .container::after { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 0; border: ${T('outline-width')} solid ${T('outline-color')}; border-radius: inherit; pointer-events: none; } ${shape} /* COD-8: the header — the top of the same container, with no fill and no line: a row that begins copy-button.inset from the top edge, as tall as the copy button where there is one and as one line of the title's text style otherwise, its items centred and header.gap apart; the title begins at the inline padding of COD-3, and the copy button stands copy-button.inset from the end edge (COD-9). */ .header { display: flex; flex: none; align-items: center; gap: ${T('header-gap')}; box-sizing: border-box; padding-block-start: ${T('copy-button-inset')}; padding-inline: var(--_code-block-pad-inline); } .container.copy .header { padding-inline-end: ${T('copy-button-inset')}; } /* The title: one line, cut with an ellipsis at the end of its own direction (the element gives it dir="auto"). */ .title { flex: 0 1 auto; min-inline-size: 0; overflow: hidden; font: ${T('title-typescale-font')}; letter-spacing: ${T('title-typescale-letter-spacing')}; color: ${T('title-color')}; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; } ${productText('.title')} /* The title's box is as wide as its text, so the layout places it — at the start — whatever its own direction is; what is left of the row is between it and the items at the end. */ .space { flex: 1 1 0; } /* The language: at the end, before the copy button, never cut. */ .language { flex: none; font: ${T('language-typescale-font')}; letter-spacing: ${T('language-typescale-letter-spacing')}; color: ${T('language-color')}; white-space: nowrap; } .header > tanrei-copy-button { flex: none; } /* COD-9, COD-10: without a header the copy button stands over the top end corner of the body, copy-button.inset from the top and the end edge, on a patch of the block's ground: whole lines high (a line is never half covered), no taller than the block, with the container's corners at that end. It does not scroll with the code. */ .corner { position: absolute; inset-block-start: 0; inset-inline-end: 0; z-index: 1; box-sizing: border-box; block-size: calc(var(--_code-block-pad-block) + round(up, ${BUTTON} + ${T('copy-button-inset')} - var(--_code-block-pad-block), 1lh)); max-block-size: 100%; padding-block-start: ${T('copy-button-inset')}; padding-inline-end: ${T('copy-button-inset')}; border-start-end-radius: calc(var(--tanrei-corner-radius) * var(--_corner-scale)); border-end-end-radius: calc(var(--tanrei-corner-radius) * var(--_corner-scale)); corner-shape: inherit; background: var(--_code-block-ground); } /* Wrapped, every row ends before the button's column (COD-10): no code passes under it, and it needs no patch. */ :host([wrap]) .corner { background: none; } /* COD-20: in a right-to-left layout the button is at the left, over the gutter where the lines have one. The gutter stays in view there, on the block's ground (COD-13), so no code passes under the button and it needs no patch — which would cover the bar and the start of the band of the lines beside it (COD-15). */ :host(:dir(rtl)) .container.gutter .corner { background: none; } /* COD-4, COD-6: the body holds the lines and scrolls inside the container — sideways when a line does not fit, up and down past maxLines lines — and never scrolls the page sideways. Left to right in every layout (COD-20): the element writes dir="ltr" on it. Its corners are the container's, so what scrolls is cut where the container ends. */ .body { position: relative; flex: 1 1 auto; box-sizing: border-box; min-inline-size: 0; overflow: auto; ${unsafeCSS(cornerRadius(`${PREFIX}-container-shape`))} outline: none; } .container.has-header .body { /* COD-8: the code begins header.padding-block-end below the header's row, in place of the block padding. */ --_code-block-pad-top: ${T('header-padding-block-end')}; border-start-start-radius: 0; border-start-end-radius: 0; } /* COD-10: without a header the padding at the copy button's side is widened by the button and its inset, so a line's end can be scrolled clear of it and a wrapped row ends before its column. declarations.description:
Shows lines of code to read, compare and copy: in the code face, on a quiet fill or inside one hairline, scrolling inside itself or wrapping, with an optional header, line numbers, marked lines, a prompt and a copy button; given the code and its language it highlights the code by itself, in the system's syntax colors. Contract: specs/code-block.spec.json. The code stays in the document, as an ordinary `
`:

    
      
const sizes = ['small', 'medium', 'large'];

    

so it is there without script — for a reader whose script failed, for crawlers, for find-in-page — and the element
draws the frame around it. `@tanrei/web/code.css` draws a block that is not upgraded yet where the element will: its
fill, corners, paddings and face, the header's row with the title and the language label, the room of the copy
button, and — for lines written where the page was made — what stands beside them; nothing moves when the element
is defined. A block built by script sets `code` instead, and the element writes the `
`.

**It highlights by itself** (COD-19). Three sources of color, in this order: runs the document gives —
`` in the ``, or a `` written by `highlightToHtml` where
the page was made — are drawn as they are and never read again (COD-29); otherwise, while `highlight` is true and
`language` names a language the highlighter knows, the block imports `@tanrei/web/highlight` and colors the code
(COD-27); otherwise the code is plain. The code is drawn at once, plain; its colors arrive in one frame and move
nothing (COD-28). A role is one of `comment`, `keyword`, `string`, `constant`, `function`, `type`, `tag`, `property`,
`punctuation` — or one a design system added — colored from `--tanrei-comp-code-block-syntax-color-*` and weighted
from `…-syntax-emphasis-*`. `language` is not drawn: the header's words are `language-label`.

**Lines.** The element gives each line a box of its own — `` holding `` — by
moving the code's nodes and splitting text and runs at line breaks, without adding or removing a character of the
code; `[data-line]` children a highlighter already wrote are used as they are, and lines that `highlightToHtml`
wrote with the block's props are left untouched. Numbers, signs and the prompt are
drawn, not text: never selected, copied or read. A marked line's label (`highlighted-label`, `added-label`,
`removed-label`) is the one thing it adds for assistive technology, before the line.

The body is one focus stop, with the block's name, only while it can scroll; it is left to right in every layout,
and the frame mirrors. The outlined look is read on whatever it is placed on: where that is not the surface color,
name it in `--tanrei-code-block-ground`, which the gutter and the copy button's patch stand on while code scrolls
under them.
declarations.name: TanreiCodeBlock

cssProperties.description: The color the outlined look is placed on, where it is not `sys.color.surface`: what the gutter and the copy button's patch are filled with.
cssProperties.name: --tanrei-code-block-ground

cssParts.description: The block: its fill, its corners, and the edge of the outlined look.
cssParts.name: container

cssParts.description: The row that holds the title, the language and the copy button.
cssParts.name: header

cssParts.description: The title.
cssParts.name: title

cssParts.description: The language label (`language-label`).
cssParts.name: language

cssParts.description: The copy button (a `<tanrei-copy-button>`).
cssParts.name: copy-button

cssParts.description: The part that holds the lines and scrolls.
cssParts.name: body

slots.description: The code: one `<pre><code>`. Runs are `<span data-syntax="…">` inside the `<code>`.

members.name: words
members.description: The product's words, read where the instance gives none (src/primitives/words.ts).

members.name: code
members.description:
The code as plain text, lines separated by line breaks, for a block built by script: the element writes the
`<pre><code>` itself. Leave it empty when the `<pre><code>` is in the document. Ignored where the code holds runs.

members.name: variant
members.description: filled: a quiet fill, for code on a page. outlined: no fill inside one hairline, for code inside a container that is already filled.

members.name: size
members.description: medium sets the code in the code role, for a page and a panel; small in the small code role with less padding, for dense interfaces.

members.name: title
members.description:
A file name or a few words that say what the code is. Drawn in the header and used as the block's accessible name.
The attribute is read and removed from the element, so the browser does not also draw its own `title` tooltip over
the block.

members.name: language
members.description:
The language the code is written in, as an identifier ("tsx", "css", "swift", "sh"), read without regard to case.
It is what the block highlights by (COD-19, COD-27); it is not drawn. Empty, "text", "plain" and "plaintext" mean
code that has no syntax; a language the highlighter does not know is drawn plain. The block never guesses one.

members.name: languageLabel
members.description: The language in your words ("TypeScript", "Shell"), drawn in the header. A label only: the block does not highlight by it.

members.name: highlight
members.description:
True: the block highlights the code by itself where it can (COD-19). False — the attribute `highlight="false"` —
it never does, whatever `language` says; runs the document gives are still drawn in their colors.

members.name: label
members.description: The block's accessible name where it has no title. Not drawn. A block that can scroll needs a title or a label.

members.name: wrap
members.description: False: a line is never broken, and lines that do not fit scroll sideways inside the block. True: a line that does not fit continues on the next row.

members.name: lineNumbers
members.description: Draws each line's number in a gutter at the left of the code.

members.name: startLine
members.description: The number of the first line: an excerpt of a file keeps the file's numbers. A whole number of 1 or more.

members.name: highlightedLines
members.description: The lines the text around the block talks about, by number, as numbers and ranges separated by commas ("3, 7-9"), counted from `startLine`.

members.name: addedLines
members.description: The lines a change adds, written as `highlightedLines` is.

members.name: removedLines
members.description: The lines a change takes away, written as `highlightedLines` is. They are drawn, and left out of what the copy button copies.

members.name: highlightedLabel
members.description: What assistive technology reads before a highlighted line ("Highlighted"). Required while `highlightedLines` names a line.

members.name: addedLabel
members.description: What assistive technology reads before an added line ("Added"). Required while `addedLines` names a line.

members.name: removedLabel
members.description: What assistive technology reads before a removed line ("Removed"). Required while `removedLines` names a line.

members.name: prompt
members.description: A prompt ("$", ">") drawn before every line that is not empty. It is not part of the code: not selected, not copied, not read.

members.name: maxLines
members.description: The most lines shown at once; more than that scroll up and down inside the block. Null shows every line.

members.name: copy
members.description: Draws a copy button that copies the code.

members.name: copyLabel
members.description: The copy button's accessible name ("Copy"). Required while `copy` is true.

members.name: copiedLabel
members.description: What the copy button announces when the code has been copied ("Copied"). Required while `copy` is true.

members.name: copyFailedLabel
members.description: What the copy button announces when the platform refuses the copy ("Could not copy"). Required while `copy` is true.

members.name: empty
members.description: COD-25: there is no code.

members.name: scrollable
members.description: COD-7: the body can scroll, sideways or up and down.

members.name: copyText
members.description: COD-11: what the copy button copies — the lines without the removed ones, joined by line breaks.

members.name: lineCount
members.description: How many lines the code has (COD-6).

members.name: gutter
members.description: Whether the lines have a gutter (COD-13): it stays in view at the left, over the room of a corner button there (COD-20).

members.name: axes
members.default: new OpenAxesController(this, { component: 'code-block', behavior: 'COD-25', axes: AXES })
members.description: COD-25: sizes and variants a design system adds, and a value the active system does not have (src/primitives/axes.ts).

members.name: internals

members.name: highlighter
members.description:
The highlighter of every code block, where it is not Tanrei's own (COD-27: "replace the highlighter whole").
Undefined — the default: `@tanrei/web/highlight`, imported the first time a block needs it; `setHighlighter` and
`registerLanguage` of that module change what it answers. A function: it is asked instead, and that module is never
loaded — for a product that has a highlighter it trusts and wants none of Tanrei's. Null: no block highlights by
itself. Runs the document gives are drawn whatever this is (COD-29).

members.name: colored

members.name: drawn

members.name: asked
members.description: What the highlighter was last asked — the language and the texts — and the way to cancel that question.

members.name: questioned
members.description: Whether the highlighter was asked since the block was last put in the document: its first colors wait for a later task (COD-28), later ones do not (COD-30).

members.name: made
members.description: The lines this element made (as against `[data-line]` children a highlighter wrote).

members.name: written
members.description: The text `code` last wrote into the document.

members.name: mutations
members.description: COD-22: the code, its runs or its lines changed in the document.

members.name: observedPre

members.description: The `<code>` that holds the code: the `pre`'s own, made around the `pre`'s content where the product wrote none.

members.name: given
members.description: COD-29: the document gives the runs — the `<code>` says it was highlighted, or holds a run this element did not write.

members.name: checkRoles
members.description:
COD-19: a role the active design system does not have is drawn plain (no rule matches it) and reported. A role a
design system added to the axis has its two tokens in the cascade: it gets its rule, once.

members.name: maxLength
members.description: COD-31: `comp.code-block.syntax.max-length`, as the cascade gives it to this block; no limit where it is not a number.

members.description:
COD-28, COD-30: draws runs — in one pass, replacing the children of each line whose runs are not the ones drawn and
touching no other line. Only colors and weights change (COD-18), so nothing moves; a selection in a line that is
written again is put back where it was, by its characters.

members.description: COD-32: the code stays plain, everything else the block does is untouched, and what failed is said once.

members.description:
COD-19, COD-27 to COD-33: colors the code by itself where it may. `readings` are the texts the code holds — one,
or two where a line is added or removed (COD-33) — each with the boxes of its lines' code. The first colors of a
block are owed to a later task (COD-28); a block that has its colors and whose code changes is read again in the
task of the change, where its highlighter answers at once, so the new code is drawn with its colors (COD-30).

members.name: writeCode
members.description:
Writes `code` as the text of the `<code>`. Where the lines are this element's own, the lines at the start that
are the same are left as they are — code that grows at its end keeps the lines it had, and their colors (COD-30).

members.name: firstLine
members.description: COD-25: a start line below 1 or not whole is 1.

members.name: cap
members.description: COD-25: a line cap below 1 is none.

members.name: lineBoxes
members.description:
The lines of the code as boxes (the spec's web note): `[data-line]` children of the `<code>`, each holding its code
in a `[data-line-code]`. Lines a highlighter wrote are kept; everything else is moved into lines made here, text
nodes and runs split at line breaks. No character is added or removed.

members.name: sync
members.description:
COD-22: reads the code from the document and draws what the props say on its lines — numbers, signs, the prompt,
the marks and their labels — at once, without a motion and without announcing anything.

members.description: The body and the product's `pre` are watched for their sizes (COD-7): the observer answers at once for each.

COD-12: a copied selection holds the selected characters of the code alone, with the code's own line breaks —

attributes.name: code
attributes.description:
The code as plain text, lines separated by line breaks, for a block built by script: the element writes the
`<pre><code>` itself. Leave it empty when the `<pre><code>` is in the document. Ignored where the code holds runs.

attributes.description: filled: a quiet fill, for code on a page. outlined: no fill inside one hairline, for code inside a container that is already filled.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: medium sets the code in the code role, for a page and a panel; small in the small code role with less padding, for dense interfaces.

attributes.name: title
attributes.description:
A file name or a few words that say what the code is. Drawn in the header and used as the block's accessible name.
The attribute is read and removed from the element, so the browser does not also draw its own `title` tooltip over
the block.

attributes.name: language
attributes.description:
The language the code is written in, as an identifier ("tsx", "css", "swift", "sh"), read without regard to case.
It is what the block highlights by (COD-19, COD-27); it is not drawn. Empty, "text", "plain" and "plaintext" mean

attributes.description: The language in your words ("TypeScript", "Shell"), drawn in the header. A label only: the block does not highlight by it.

attributes.name: highlight
attributes.description:
True: the block highlights the code by itself where it can (COD-19). False — the attribute `highlight="false"` —
it never does, whatever `language` says; runs the document gives are still drawn in their colors.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: The block's accessible name where it has no title. Not drawn. A block that can scroll needs a title or a label.

attributes.name: wrap
attributes.description: False: a line is never broken, and lines that do not fit scroll sideways inside the block. True: a line that does not fit continues on the next row.

attributes.name: start-line
attributes.description: The number of the first line: an excerpt of a file keeps the file's numbers. A whole number of 1 or more.

attributes.name: highlighted-lines
attributes.description: The lines the text around the block talks about, by number, as numbers and ranges separated by commas ("3, 7-9"), counted from `startLine`.

attributes.name: added-lines
attributes.description: The lines a change adds, written as `highlightedLines` is.

attributes.name: removed-lines
attributes.description: The lines a change takes away, written as `highlightedLines` is. They are drawn, and left out of what the copy button copies.

attributes.name: removed-label

attributes.name: prompt
attributes.description: A prompt ("$", ">") drawn before every line that is not empty. It is not part of the code: not selected, not copied, not read.

attributes.description: The copy button's accessible name ("Copy"). Required while `copy` is true.

declarations.description:
Lets people set one color as one complete field of a form. Built from a Field (`<tanrei-field>`) and the Color
input (`<tanrei-color-input>`) it frames: the box — a sample of the value, the value as text, a button that asks
for a picker — under the Field's label, or, in the filled and the outlined look, with the label floating in it,
with the Field's help and its error, tied together for assistive technology and taking part in a form as one
control. It looks and measures like a text field.

Contract: specs/color-field.spec.json. `<tanrei-color-field name="brand" label="Brand color" value="#0f766e"
supporting-text="Six hexadecimal digits, like #0f766e." invalid-text="Enter six hexadecimal digits, like #0f766e."
picker picker-label="Choose color"></tanrei-color-field>`.

Composed (`src/primitives/composed.ts`): its shadow root holds the two members' own elements and nothing
else, so it draws nothing of its own and has no token — every `--tanrei-comp-field-*`,
`--tanrei-comp-input-box-*` and `--tanrei-comp-color-input-*` value reaches the members by inheritance, and one color field is set apart by setting
such a property on this element. Each property is its member's, set on that member unchanged: `label`,
`label-hidden`, `supporting-text`, `error-text`, `error`, `disabled`, `requirement`, `required-mark`,
`required-text` and `optional-text` are the Field's; `variant`, `size`, `value`, `invalid-text`, `picker` and
`picker-label` the color input's. One level down, the same by hand: `<tanrei-field label="Brand color"
supporting-text="Six hexadecimal digits, like #0f766e."><tanrei-color-input name="brand" value="#0f766e"
invalid-text="Enter six hexadecimal digits, like #0f766e." picker picker-label="Choose color"></tanrei-color-input>
</tanrei-field>` — and the box alone, where a row or a column names the color, is `<tanrei-color-input>` with a
`label` of its own.

It is a block as wide as its place, and its box fills it (CLF-43): give it a narrower place for a narrower box.

`value` is at every moment the color input's — a number sign and six lowercase hexadecimal digits, or empty: a
value set as `0F766E` is read back as `#0f766e`, and one that is not a color as empty, with no event. The four
events are that input's own, with this element as their target: `event.target.value` is the new value in every
listener, and `pickerrequest` stays cancelable. It dispatches none itself.

Form-associated: it submits the value under `name` — nothing while disabled —, resets to its `value` attribute, is
restored on navigation, follows a disabled `<fieldset>`, and reports what its color input reports: a missing value
while `requirement` is `required` and it is empty, and a bad input while a committed text is not a color. Enter in
the input presses the default button of this element's form.

The element is not focusable itself and has no role: `focus()` goes to the input — never to the picker button —,
and its name is `label` (with `label-hidden` where it is not drawn), never `aria-label`. It has two focus stops,
its input's: the input, then the picker button while it is shown. A press on the label row, on the box, on the
swatch or on a floating label focuses the input; a press on the help, the error text or the gap between a row and
the box does nothing.

members.name: formAssociated
members.description: CLF-44: the one control the form meets. Its members stand in its shadow root, outside every form.

members.name: label
members.description: Names the control, visibly and to assistive technology. Required, unless the control names itself (a checkbox or a switch with its own label): then leave it empty and the field adds only help and an error.

members.name: labelHidden
members.description: Does not draw the label, which stays the accessible name (`label-hidden`). For a control whose visible label is elsewhere.

members.name: supportingText
members.description: Help shown below the control and given to assistive technology as the control's description (`supporting-text`). While the field is in error it gives way to `errorText`, unless the design system keeps both (`--tanrei-comp-field-error-text-placement: append`).

members.name: errorText
members.description: Shown while `error` is true, in `supportingText`'s place (below it, which stays, where the design system says `append`): what is wrong with this answer and how to put it right, in words (`error-text`).

members.name: error
members.description: Puts the field in the error condition: the error text is drawn, the control is exposed as invalid and, where it has an error condition of its own, drawn in it. The field never sets this itself.

members.name: disabled
members.description: Disables the control and draws the frame as disabled. Disable a framed control here, not on the control, so that its label follows.

members.name: requirement
members.description: What the form asks of the control: `required` exposes it as required and draws the required mark; `optional` draws the optional tag; `none` says and draws nothing. It never validates.

members.name: requiredMark
members.description: How this control shows that it is required (`required-mark`): `tag` is a small filled tag with `requiredText`, `asterisk` is "*" after the label, `none` draws nothing and keeps the semantics; `auto` takes the design system's answer (`--tanrei-comp-field-requirement-mark`, which follows `--tanrei-sys-behavior-requirement-mark`).

members.name: requiredText
members.description: The text of the required tag (`required-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ requiredText })`). Tanrei has none: without them the asterisk is drawn in the tag's place and the required state is kept.

members.name: optionalText
members.description: The text of the optional tag, also part of the description (`optional-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ optionalText })`). Tanrei has none: without them no tag is drawn and nothing is said.

members.name: variant
members.description: The look, as the text inputs beside it: `stacked` is a filled box that draws no label — the label of the Field that frames it stands above it; `filled` and `outlined` float the label inside the box. Use one style per form. A value the color input does not know by name is laid out as stacked. Reflected.

members.name: size
members.description: The container's minimum height: `medium` or `large` (48 / 56 in the default system), the text input's two sizes. The hit area always meets the minimum target. Reflected.

members.name: value
members.description: The color the input holds: a number sign and six hexadecimal digits in lowercase (`#0f766e`), an opaque sRGB color; or empty for no color. It is never a half-typed text: while the input holds something that is not a color, `value` is empty. A text set in capitals or without its number sign is held in the value's own form; one that is not a color is treated as empty. The `value` attribute is also the value a form reset returns to.

members.name: invalidText
members.description: The words for an input committed with a text that is not a color (`invalid-text`), in the product's language: given to the Field that frames the input, which shows them as its error text. While it is empty that Field shows its own `errorText`. Where no Field frames the input they are its description while the error lasts.

members.name: picker
members.description: Shows the picker button. Activated, it fires `pickerrequest` and, unless that was cancelled, presents the browser's own color picker. Reflected.

members.name: pickerLabel
members.description: The accessible name of the picker button, in the product's language (`picker-label`). Required while `picker` is set.

members.name: hostNameSentence
members.description:
W8: the sentence a debug build names when the host is given an ARIA name. The host has no role: its name is the
frame's `label`. Empty: nothing is reported.

members.name: valueMember
members.description: W5: the member that holds the value, once rendered.

members.name: formResetCallback
members.description:
CLF-44: a form's reset reaches the color input. The value is the one this element was first given — its `value`
attribute (W6, item 4) — and with it go the text as typed and an entry error, as they do when the input stands in
the form by hand: a value that is what the input already holds would otherwise leave the text as the person typed
it (CLI-21). The input takes it the way it takes a restored value, and its value is then this element's.

members.name: select
members.description: Selects the text in the input, as the color input's `select()` does.

members.name: name
members.description: Web only: the name the value is submitted under.

members.name: formDisabled
members.description: W6, item 6: a disabled `<fieldset>` around the element, or its own `disabled` attribute, as the platform says it.

members.name: control
members.description: W7: the member focus goes to, once rendered.

members.name: given
members.description: W5: the value last set on the element, while the member has not taken it.

members.name: memberValue
members.description: W5: what `value` returns — `initial` is the member's own default, for an element that has not rendered and was given nothing.

members.name: giveValue
members.description: W5: what `value` is set with. The member takes it at the element's next render; what the member holds already changes nothing.

members.name: firstValue
members.description: W6, item 4: the value a form's reset returns to — the `value` attribute, where the first value is written.

members.name: form
members.description: The form it belongs to, if any.

members.name: validity
members.description: The element's validity: its value member's (W6, item 3).

members.name: repeat
members.description: W6, items 2 and 3: the same value and state, the same flags and message, and the member's own anchor.

members.name: memberUpdated

each of the member's updates, which is when a member speaks. An element whose spec names a member's prop it fills
itself from state the value member holds (a text field: its Field's count text, from its input's count) sets it

members.name: passing

declarations.description:
The box in which people set one color: a text value they can read, type and paste, a sample of it beside the text, a
button that asks for a picker and — in the looks that float one — its label inside the box. It looks and measures
like a text input. It has no label row, no help and no error text of its own: put it in a `<tanrei-field>`, which
names it, describes it and marks it — or use `<tanrei-color-field>`, which is the two together.

Contract: specs/color-input.spec.json. Every visual value is a token: the box is drawn from
`--tanrei-comp-input-box-*`, the one set every input box is drawn from (CLI-45) — the swatch has the box's icon
size — and the swatch's shape and hairline from `--tanrei-comp-color-input-*`; the swatch's fill is the value itself; the picker
button is a `<tanrei-button>`, drawn from Button's own tokens.

```html
<!-- A row of a list of colors that names each: the box alone, named by its own label. -->
<tanrei-color-input label="Primary, tone 40" value="#0f766e" picker picker-label="Choose the color of Primary, tone 40"></tanrei-color-input>

<tanrei-field label="Brand color" supporting-text="Six hexadecimal digits, like #0f766e.">
  <tanrei-color-input name="brand" value="#0f766e" invalid-text="Enter six hexadecimal digits, like #0f766e."></tanrei-color-input>
</tanrei-field>
```

`value` is a number sign and six hexadecimal digits in lowercase (`#0f766e`) — an opaque sRGB color — or the empty
string for no color, and never anything else. The text is the person's: nothing typed is refused, replaced or
reformatted. It is read on every edit — six hexadecimal digits in either case, with or without the number sign, the
white space around them left out — and `value` is the color it reads as, or empty. `input` fires when that changes
`value`. When focus leaves or Enter is pressed the input commits: a color is rewritten in the value's own form and
`change` fires if the value differs from the one last committed; a text that is not a color is kept, marked as an
error and reported with `entryerror` — and to the Field that frames it, which shows `invalidText` (FLD-28).

With `picker`, a button at the end asks for a picker: it fires a cancelable `pickerrequest` and, unless that was
cancelled, presents the browser's own color picker. A pick is an edit by the person. The input draws no picker
surface of its own: a product that has one cancels the request, presents it and sets `value`.

Inside a `<tanrei-field>` it takes the Field's name, description and states — required, invalid, disabled — through
the connection every framed control uses (`src/primitives/field.ts`), and says what only it knows: that it draws the
label itself while its look floats one, how far its value's text is inset — past the swatch — and its own refusal
of a text that is not a color, with its words (CLI-43). Bare, `label` names it, and a filled or outlined input
draws that label floating.

It is a block as wide as its place, and exactly as tall as its box (CLI-44). It is a form-associated element: it
takes `name`, submits its value, resets to the `value` attribute, is restored on navigation, follows
`<fieldset disabled>` and reports `valueMissing` while its Field says it is required and `value` is empty, and
`badInput` while an entry error lasts.

It has no words of its own: `invalidText`, `pickerLabel` and `label` are the product's, in the product's language.

members.name: variant
members.description: The look, as the text inputs beside it: `stacked` is a filled box that draws no label — the label of the Field that frames it stands above it; `filled` and `outlined` float the label inside the box. Use one style per form. A value the color input does not know by name is laid out as stacked. Reflected.

members.name: size
members.description: The container's minimum height: `medium` or `large` (48 / 56 in the default system), the text input's two sizes. The hit area always meets the minimum target. Reflected.

members.name: value
members.description: The color the input holds: a number sign and six hexadecimal digits in lowercase (`#0f766e`), an opaque sRGB color; or empty for no color. It is never a half-typed text: while the input holds something that is not a color, `value` is empty. A text set in capitals or without its number sign is held in the value's own form; one that is not a color is treated as empty. The `value` attribute is also the value a form reset returns to.

members.name: held
members.description: The value the element holds: what the product set, or the person's last edit or pick as the element took it.

members.name: nativeInput
members.description: The native text element, once drawn, and what it held when the element last wrote to it or took from it.

members.name: pickSeen
members.description: What the browser's color input held when the element last wrote to it or took a pick from it.

members.name: name
members.description: The name the value is submitted under in a form. Reflected.

members.name: label
members.description: Names the input for assistive technology where no Field frames it; a filled or outlined input also draws it, as the label that floats in its box. Inside a Field leave it empty: the Field's label names the input, and is what floats.

members.name: labelHidden
members.description: Does not draw the floating label of a filled or outlined input, which stays the accessible name (`label-hidden`). Inside a Field, hide the label on the Field. A stacked input draws no label, so this changes nothing there.

members.name: error
members.description: Draws the input in its error condition and exposes it as invalid. A Field sets it from its own error; set it here only where no Field frames the input. What a color means is the product's to validate; the input never sets this itself, and enters an error of its own only while the text it was left with is not a color.

members.name: disabled
members.description: Prevents focus, editing, the picker button and form submission. Inside a Field, disable the Field, so that its label follows.

members.name: invalidText
members.description: The words for an input committed with a text that is not a color (`invalid-text`), in the product's language: given to the Field that frames the input, which shows them as its error text. While it is empty that Field shows its own `errorText`. Where no Field frames the input they are its description while the error lasts.

members.name: picker
members.description: Shows the picker button. Activated, it fires `pickerrequest` and, unless that was cancelled, presents the browser's own color picker. Reflected.

members.name: pickerLabel
members.description: The accessible name of the picker button, in the product's language (`picker-label`). Required while `picker` is set.

members.name: text
members.description: The text in the input: the person's while they edit, the value in its own form otherwise (CLI-17, CLI-19).

members.name: entryError
members.description: CLI-20: the input was committed with a text that is not a color, and holds it still.

members.name: focused
members.description: CLI-22: the input has focus, however it was gained. The picker button's focus is its own.

members.name: formDisabled
members.description: Set by the platform (the element's `formDisabledCallback`): an ancestor `<fieldset disabled>`, or its own `disabled` attribute.

members.name: says
members.description: What it tells its form, said where an element composed around it hears it (src/primitives/form-says.ts).

members.name: ownValue
members.description: The value the color input made or took from the product last: another `value` is the product's (CLI-21).

members.name: base
members.description: CLI-19: the value last committed — when the product set it, or at the last `change`.

members.name: edited
members.description: CLI-19: the person changed the text since it was last committed or written.

members.name: awaited
members.description: CLI-21: the product set a value while an input method was composing: its text is written when the composition ends, and is not the person's.

members.name: picking
members.description: CLI-29: the browser's picker was presented and no sign of its closing has been seen yet.

members.name: frameChanged
members.description: The Field's answer changed since the last update: the floating label may have other lines (CLI-15).

members.name: axes
members.default: new OpenAxesController(this, { component: 'color-input', behavior: 'CLI-41', axes: AXES })
members.description: CLI-41: sizes and variants a design system adds, and a value the active system does not have (src/primitives/axes.ts).

members.name: frame
members.default: new FieldControlController(this, { errorCondition: true, named: () => !!this.label.trim(), says: () => this.saysToField, changed: () => (this.frameChanged = true), })
members.description:
CLI-43: the input's side of the exchange with the Field that frames it (src/primitives/field.ts). It takes the
Field's name, description and states, whether the label is hidden and whether an asterisk follows it; and it says
what only it knows — that it draws the label, how far its value's text is inset, its own refusal of an entry. It
has an error condition of its own (CLI-9). No Field: it is drawn as a bare input.

members.name: native
members.default: new NativeTextController({ input: () => this.input, value: () => this.text, // What an input method is composing is not read (CLI-17): the text follows the element and nothing is said. A // value the product set meanwhile is the text that waits for the composition's end (CLI-21). setValue: (text) => { if (text === this.text || this.awaited) return; this.text = text; this.edited = true; }, })
members.description: CLI-17, CLI-21: the text and the native element kept in step without breaking an input method (src/primitives/native-text.ts).

members.name: floating

members.name: glyphs

members.name: inert_
members.description: CLI-31: disabled by its own `disabled`, a fieldset's, or the Field's or the field group's around it.

members.name: layout
members.description: How the variant is laid out: filled and outlined by name, every other value as stacked (CLI-41).

members.name: name_
members.description: CLI-11: the accessible name — its own label, else the label of the Field that frames it.

members.name: required_
members.description: CLI-11: its Field says it is required. It has no requirement of its own.

members.name: inError
members.description: CLI-9: in error — its own `error`, its Field's, or an entry error while it lasts.

members.name: labelled
members.description: CLI-15: the label floats in the box — a filled or an outlined input with a name, unless its own `labelHidden` or its Field's says to draw none.

members.name: refusalText
members.description: CLI-20: the words of an entry error while it lasts — `invalidText`; empty where the product gave none.

members.name: saysToField
members.description:
CLI-43: what the input says to the Field that frames it. That it draws the label while its look floats one — its
name, or nothing while the label is hidden; the Field draws no label row either way. How far the value's text
stands from its start edge — past the padding beside the swatch, the swatch and the gap — and the text padding it
keeps at its end edge, with or without the picker button, as lengths of the box's tokens (`INSET`, in the styles).
And an entry error, with its words. No count: a color has one length.

members.name: described
members.description:

them and gives them back as its own description, FLD-28), and then the description its Field gives.

members.name: pickerSize
members.description: CLI-27: the Button size with the input's size name, or Button's default for a size Button does not have.

members.name: form
members.description: The form it belongs to, if any.

members.name: validity
members.description: The native constraint validity: `valueMissing` while its Field says the color input is required and `value` is empty, `badInput` while it holds a committed text that is not a color.

members.name: focus
members.description: Moves focus to the input — never to the picker button.

members.name: select
members.description: Selects the text in the input.

members.name: formDisabledCallback
members.description:
The platform's word on whether the element is disabled: by a `<fieldset disabled>` around it, and by its own
`disabled` attribute too. Lit writes that attribute in the middle of an update, where a change of state would not
be drawn: it is taken once that update is over, so an input whose `disabled` was unset is drawn enabled again.

members.name: syncForm
members.description:
The form's view: the value — a color in its own form, or the empty string — left out while disabled (CLI-31); a
missing value while its Field says it is required (CLI-11), and a bad input while an entry error lasts (CLI-20).
Said when the color input is drawn, and at once when its value changes: a listener of `input` or `change`, and the
form Enter submits, already see the new value. The message of an entry error is `invalidText`, else what its Field
shows for it, else the browser's own words; of a missing value, the browser's own words. Said through `FormSays`,
so that an element composed around the input repeats it (src/primitives/form-says.ts).

members.name: took
members.description: CLI-21: the product gave a value: it is shown in the input and the swatch, an entry error ends, and nothing is said.

members.name: keep
members.description: The color input makes `value` the value itself, and the form sees it at once.

members.name: said
members.description:
CLI-17, CLI-29: `input`, once, when an edit or a pick changed the value; `value` is already the new one. The event
is the browser's own, of the native element the person edited or picked in, where that event leaves the shadow
root by itself — it is composed and bubbles, and outside its target is this element. It is then left to pass, and
nothing is dispatched in its place: a second event would be heard twice by a capturing listener on an ancestor.
Where it would not leave — a pick taken as the picker closes, from its `change` — the element dispatches one.

members.name: changed
members.description: CLI-19, CLI-29: `change`, once, while the value differs from the one last committed. `value` is already the new one.

members.name: typed
members.description:
CLI-17, CLI-18, CLI-20: the person changed the text. Nothing is rewritten: the text is theirs. The whole text is
read, and `value` becomes the color it reads as, or empty. An entry error ends with the edit. Returns whether the
edit changed `value`: `input` is heard for such an edit, and for no other.

members.name: commit
members.description:
CLI-19, CLI-20: commits the text. A color is rewritten in the value's own form — the number sign added, the digits
in lowercase, the white space gone; a text of white space alone is no color and is cleared; a text that is not
empty and not a color is kept as typed and enters the entry error (`entryerror`, with `invalidText`). Then
`change`, once, while the value differs from the one last committed. A text the person did not change since the
last commit commits nothing. A commit also reads three digits (#fff) as the six they stand for (#ffffff): the
value becomes that color, `input` says so, and then `change`.

members.name: onKeyDown
members.description:
CLI-19: the action key commits and, inside a form, then asks for its submission, as a native input does — its own
form, or the form of the element composed around it (src/primitives/default-button.ts, `formOf`). While an input
method composes, every key is its own (CLI-17).

members.name: onBlur
members.description: CLI-19: the input lost focus: the text is committed.

members.name: onPickerClick
members.description:
CLI-28: the picker button asks for a picker — `pickerrequest`, once, with the value — and then, unless the product
cancelled the request, presents the browser's own color picker showing the value, or black while the input holds
none, inside the same user activation. Where the browser has none to present, nothing is presented, nothing
changes and no focus moves.

members.name: onPick
members.description:
CLI-29: a pick in the browser's picker is an edit by the person: the color is written into the input in the value's
own form, the swatch drawn in it, an entry error ended, and `input` fired when it changed the value — for every
pick the browser reports, a drag across the picker included.

members.name: onPickerChange
members.description: CLI-29: the browser's picker closed: its `change`, or — where a browser gives none — the page's next focus.

members.name: onPageFocus
members.description:
Where a browser gives no sign that its picker closed (nothing was picked, or it tells no one), the next focus of
the page counts as one: the window's, when a picker that is a window of its own goes, or any element's.

members.name: pickerClosed
members.description:
CLI-29: when the picker closes, `change` once while the value differs from the one last committed, and focus on
the picker button, as a popover returns focus to its opener. Focus is never taken from where the person has put it
since: the button takes it only while nothing else in the page has it, or what has it is this input's own native
picker.

members.name: onContainerPress
members.description:
CLI-24: a press on the container's padding, on the swatch or on a floating label moves focus to the input and does
nothing else. A press in the input places the caret; the picker button keeps its own press. CLI-25: while the
picker button is shown a press on the swatch is the picker button's instead (`onSwatchClick`), and moves no focus.

members.name: onSwatchClick
members.description:
CLI-25: while the picker button is shown, a press on the swatch — by pointer or touch — does what a press on the
picker button does (CLI-28), as a label passes its press to its control: the swatch takes no focus and draws no
answer of its own, and the keyboard's way stays the picker button.

members.name: reports
members.description: What a debug build tells the developer; the color input still renders.

events.name: input
events.description: The person changed the value: an edit of the text made it a color, another color or no color, or a color was picked in the browser's picker. `value` is already the new one. Composed and bubbling. Never fired when the product sets `value`, nor for an edit that leaves `value` as it was.

events.name: change
events.description: The person committed a changed value: focus left the input, Enter was pressed, or the browser's picker closed. `value` is already the new one. Composed and bubbling. Never fired when the product sets `value`.

events.name: entryerror
events.description: The person committed a text that is not empty and is not a color. `detail.text` is the text as typed, `detail.message` is `invalidText` — empty where the product gave none. Composed and bubbling.

The person activated the picker button. `detail.value` is the value. Cancelable: `preventDefault()` keeps the input from presenting the browser's picker; the product then presents its own surface and sets `value`. Composed and bubbling.
events.name: pickerrequest

attributes.description: The id of the form the color input belongs to, where it stands outside it: the platform's own attribute, which then wins over a form around it. The `form` property is read-only and returns the form element.
attributes.name: form
variant
attributes.description: The look, as the text inputs beside it: `stacked` is a filled box that draws no label — the label of the Field that frames it stands above it; `filled` and `outlined` float the label inside the box. Use one style per form. A value the color input does not know by name is laid out as stacked. Reflected.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: The container's minimum height: `medium` or `large` (48 / 56 in the default system), the text input's two sizes. The hit area always meets the minimum target. Reflected.

attributes.name: value
attributes.description: The color the input holds: a number sign and six hexadecimal digits in lowercase (`#0f766e`), an opaque sRGB color; or empty for no color. It is never a half-typed text: while the input holds something that is not a color, `value` is empty. A text set in capitals or without its number sign is held in the value's own form; one that is not a color is treated as empty. The `value` attribute is also the value a form reset returns to.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: The name the value is submitted under in a form. Reflected.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Names the input for assistive technology where no Field frames it; a filled or outlined input also draws it, as the label that floats in its box. Inside a Field leave it empty: the Field's label names the input, and is what floats.

attributes.name: label-hidden
attributes.description: Does not draw the floating label of a filled or outlined input, which stays the accessible name (`label-hidden`). Inside a Field, hide the label on the Field. A stacked input draws no label, so this changes nothing there.

attributes.name: error
attributes.description: Draws the input in its error condition and exposes it as invalid. A Field sets it from its own error; set it here only where no Field frames the input. What a color means is the product's to validate; the input never sets this itself, and enters an error of its own only while the text it was left with is not a color.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: Prevents focus, editing, the picker button and form submission. Inside a Field, disable the Field, so that its label follows.

attributes.name: invalid-text
attributes.description: The words for an input committed with a text that is not a color (`invalid-text`), in the product's language: given to the Field that frames the input, which shows them as its error text. While it is empty that Field shows its own `errorText`. Where no Field frames the input they are its description while the error lasts.

attributes.name: picker
attributes.description: Shows the picker button. Activated, it fires `pickerrequest` and, unless that was cancelled, presents the browser's own color picker. Reflected.

attributes.name: picker-label
attributes.description: The accessible name of the picker button, in the product's language (`picker-label`). Required while `picker` is set.

declarations.name: read
declarations.description:
CLF-18: reads a text. The white space before and after it is left out; what remains is a color when it is exactly
six hexadecimal digits in either case, with or without one number sign before them, and the color is those digits in
lowercase after a number sign. Nothing at all is `empty`; every other text — fewer or more digits, a three-digit
form, an alpha, a name, a functional notation, any other character — is `invalid`.

It is the one rule: what is typed, what is pasted and what the product sets are all read by it.

declarations.name: readCommitted
declarations.description:
CLI-19: reads a text as a commit does. The rule of `read()`, and besides it the three-digit form CSS has (#fff, fff):
the color whose six digits are each of the three written twice (#ffffff). Only a commit reads it: while the person
types, three digits are on their way to six and read as no color (CLI-18), so the swatch does not flash a color
that was never meant.

declarations.name: valueOf
declarations.description: CLF-17: the value a text makes — the color it reads as, or the empty string while it reads as no color.

declarations.name: isValue
declarations.description: CLF-16: `value` is in the value's own form — a color, or the empty string.

declarations.name: sameColor
declarations.description:
CLF-16: two values are the same color exactly when they are the same string, because the value has one form. (A text
in capitals or without its number sign is the same color as its lowercase form: compare what `valueOf()` gives.)

declarations.name: given
channels

type.text: [red: number, green: number, blue: number] | null

declarations.description: The three channels of a value, 0 to 255 each; null for no color.

declarations.name: fromChannels
declarations.description: A value from three channels: each is rounded and held within 0 and 255.

declarations.name: PICKER_START
declarations.description: CLF-28: the color the platform's picker shows while the field holds none: the picker's own starting color, black.

declarations.name: picked
declarations.description:
CLF-29: a pick of the platform's picker, as the value holds it. The platform reports an opaque sRGB color as a number
sign and six digits (it has converted a pick with an alpha, or one outside sRGB, already); the field reads it by its
own rule, so capitals are taken too. A report it cannot read is no pick: null, and nothing changes.

Lets people find one value by typing, as one complete field of a form. Built from a Field (`<tanrei-field>`) and
the Combobox (`<tanrei-combobox>`) it frames: the box with its list of options under the Field's label — or, in the
filled and the outlined look, with the label floating in it — with the Field's requirement mark, its help and its
error, tied together for assistive technology and taking part in a form as one control.

Contract: specs/combobox-field.spec.json.

```html
<tanrei-combobox-field name="city" label="City" requirement="required" supporting-text="Where the order is sent." value="tokyo">
  <tanrei-option value="kyoto">Kyoto</tanrei-option>
  <tanrei-option value="tokyo">Tokyo</tanrei-option>
</tanrei-combobox-field>
```

Composed (`src/primitives/composed.ts`): its shadow root holds the two members' own elements and nothing
else, so it draws nothing of its own and has no token — every `--tanrei-comp-field-*`,
`--tanrei-comp-input-box-*` and `--tanrei-comp-combobox-*` value reaches the members by inheritance, and one combobox field is set apart by setting
such a property on this element. Each property is its member's, set on that member unchanged: `label`,
`label-hidden`, `supporting-text`, `error-text`, `error`, `disabled`, `requirement`, `required-mark`,
`required-text` and `optional-text` are the Field's, every other one the combobox's. One level down, the same by
hand: `<tanrei-field label="City" requirement="required" supporting-text="Where the order is sent."><tanrei-combobox
name="city" value="tokyo"><tanrei-option value="kyoto">Kyoto</tanrei-option>…</tanrei-combobox></tanrei-field>` — and
the box alone, where a label stands elsewhere, is `<tanrei-combobox>` with a `label` of its own.

**The options are this element's own children** — `<tanrei-option>`, optionally in `<tanrei-option-group>` — and
they stay there: nothing moves, copies or reads them here. They reach the combobox through a slot, and the combobox
reads them as its own, again whenever one is added, removed or changed (CBF-2).

It is a block as wide as its place, and its box fills it (CBF-1): give it a narrower place for a narrower box.

`value`, `inputValue` and `open` are at every moment the combobox's (CBF-3): this element keeps no copy, so each is
the new one in every listener and where the combobox writes it with no event (a text given up on leaving). The four
events are the combobox's own, with this element as their target; `toggle` does not bubble. It dispatches none
itself.

Form-associated: it submits the committed value under `name` — never the text of an edit, and nothing while
disabled —, resets to its `value` attribute, is restored on navigation, follows a disabled `<fieldset>`, and reports
a missing value while `requirement` is `required` and the value is empty. Enter with no option active presses the
default button of this element's form.

The element is not focusable itself and has no role: `focus()` goes to the input, and its name is `label` (with
`label-hidden` where it is not drawn), never `aria-label`. A press on the label row or on the box focuses the input;
a press on the label row while the list is open is a press outside the combobox, and closes the list; a press on
the help or the error text does nothing.
