members.name: formAssociated
members.description: CBF-4: the one control the form meets. Its members stand in its shadow root, outside every form.

members.name: label
members.description: Names the control, visibly and to assistive technology. Required, unless the control names itself (a checkbox or a switch with its own label): then leave it empty and the field adds only help and an error.

members.name: labelHidden
members.description: Does not draw the label, which stays the accessible name (`label-hidden`). For a control whose visible label is elsewhere.

members.name: supportingText
members.description: Help shown below the control and given to assistive technology as the control's description (`supporting-text`). While the field is in error it gives way to `errorText`, unless the design system keeps both (`--tanrei-comp-field-error-text-placement: append`).

members.name: errorText
members.description: Shown while `error` is true, in `supportingText`'s place (below it, which stays, where the design system says `append`): what is wrong with this answer and how to put it right, in words (`error-text`).

members.name: error
members.description: Puts the field in the error condition: the error text is drawn, the control is exposed as invalid and, where it has an error condition of its own, drawn in it. The field never sets this itself.

members.name: disabled
members.description: Disables the control and draws the frame as disabled. Disable a framed control here, not on the control, so that its label follows.

members.name: requirement
members.description: What the form asks of the control: `required` exposes it as required and draws the required mark; `optional` draws the optional tag; `none` says and draws nothing. It never validates.

members.name: requiredMark
members.description: How this control shows that it is required (`required-mark`): `tag` is a small filled tag with `requiredText`, `asterisk` is "*" after the label, `none` draws nothing and keeps the semantics; `auto` takes the design system's answer (`--tanrei-comp-field-requirement-mark`, which follows `--tanrei-sys-behavior-requirement-mark`).

members.name: requiredText
members.description: The text of the required tag (`required-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ requiredText })`). Tanrei has none: without them the asterisk is drawn in the tag's place and the required state is kept.

members.name: optionalText
members.description: The text of the optional tag, also part of the description (`optional-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ optionalText })`). Tanrei has none: without them no tag is drawn and nothing is said.

members.name: variant
members.description: The look, as the text inputs beside it: `stacked` is a filled box that draws no label — the label above it is the row of the Field that frames it; `filled` and `outlined` float the label inside the box. Use one style per form. A value the combobox does not know by name is laid out as stacked. Reflected.

members.name: size
members.description: The container's minimum height: `medium` or `large` (48 / 56 in the default system), the text input's two sizes. The hit area always meets the minimum target. Reflected.

members.name: value
members.description: The committed choice: the chosen option's value, or, with `allowCustomValue`, a text the person typed that names no option. Empty while nothing is chosen. The `value` attribute is the value a form reset returns to.

members.name: inputValue
members.description: The text in the input (`input-value`). The combobox writes it as the person types and when a value is chosen or restored; the product may set it, and reads it from `input` to load options.

members.name: placeholder
members.description: A hint shown while the input is empty and the label is not in the input line. Never a replacement for `label`.

members.name: readOnly
members.description: The value is shown, can be focused, selected and copied, and is submitted, but cannot be changed: the list does not open and neither the chevron nor the clear button is drawn. The attribute is `readonly`.

members.name: open
members.description: Whether the list is shown. The combobox opens and closes itself and emits `toggle`; the product may also set it (to open on focus, for one). Ignored while the combobox is disabled or read-only or has nothing to show. Reflected.

members.name: allowCustomValue
members.description: False: the value is always one of the options, and a text that names none is given up when the person leaves. True: the options are suggestions, and a text that names none becomes the value as typed (`allow-custom-value`). Reflected.

members.name: filter
members.description: Who decides which options answer the text. `contains`: the combobox shows the options whose label contains what was typed, ignoring case, width and marks, and marks the match. `none`: it shows every option it is given and the product filters, on `input`. Reflected.

members.name: noChevron
members.description: Draws no chevron (`no-chevron`: the spec's `chevron`, inverted, because a boolean attribute cannot default to true): for a field whose suggestions exist only for what was typed. The list then opens by typing and by the arrow keys alone. Reflected.

members.name: clearable
members.description: Draws a clear button while the text is not empty, for a combobox whose value may be none. Without it, emptying the text and leaving the field clears the value. Reflected.

members.name: clearLabel
members.description: The clear button's accessible name, in the product's language (`clear-label`). Required while `clearable` is true.

members.name: status
members.description: What the product's source of options is doing: `idle`, `loading` (the status row shows a loading indicator and the list is marked busy) or `error` (the status row shows `statusText` as an error, announced at once). Reflected.

members.name: statusText
members.description: The status row's text, in the product's language (`status-text`), announced when it changes: a count, that loading failed, or, while loading, the loading indicator's name.

members.name: emptyText
members.description: Shown in the list while the text names nothing the combobox can show, `allowCustomValue` is false and no status is set (`empty-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ emptyText })`). Tanrei has none: without them no such row is drawn.

members.name: separation
members.description: How a group of options is told from what is next to it: `divider`, `gap`, or `auto` for the design system's answer (`--tanrei-comp-combobox-separation`).

members.name: hostNameSentence
members.description:
W8: the sentence a debug build names when the host is given an ARIA name. The host has no role: its name is the
frame's `label`. Empty: nothing is reported.

members.name: asked
members.description: CBF-3: what the product set on the element and the combobox has not been given yet.

members.name: valueMember
members.description: W5: the member that holds the value, once rendered.

members.name: select
members.description: Selects the text in the input, as the combobox's `select()` does.

members.name: memberUpdated
members.description:
CBF-3: `open` is reflected on the host as it is on the combobox. The combobox opens and closes its list itself, so
the host's attribute follows what the combobox holds after each of its updates — which is when it tells its form,
and so this element (`ComposedControl.memberUpdated`).

members.name: name
members.description: Web only: the name the value is submitted under.

members.name: formDisabled
members.description: W6, item 6: a disabled `<fieldset>` around the element, or its own `disabled` attribute, as the platform says it.

members.name: control
members.description: W7: the member focus goes to, once rendered.

members.name: given
members.description: W5: the value last set on the element, while the member has not taken it.

members.name: memberValue
members.description: W5: what `value` returns — `initial` is the member's own default, for an element that has not rendered and was given nothing.

members.name: giveValue
members.description: W5: what `value` is set with. The member takes it at the element's next render; what the member holds already changes nothing.

members.name: firstValue
members.description: W6, item 4: the value a form's reset returns to — the `value` attribute, where the first value is written.

members.name: form
members.description: The form it belongs to, if any.

members.name: validity
members.description: The element's validity: its value member's (W6, item 3).

members.name: repeat
members.description: W6, items 2 and 3: the same value and state, the same flags and message, and the member's own anchor.

members.name: passing
members.description: W9: the names of the slots it has passed on, and the watch on its own children for them.

members.name: members
members.description: The members it has rendered: the custom elements of its own shadow tree.

members.name: focus
members.description: W7, item 2: focus is the control's.

members.name: blur
members.description: W7, item 2: what has focus inside the control loses it (an engine does not take it from inside a host it blurs).

members.name: pass
members.description:
W9: a slot of a member, passed on — `${this.pass('label-icon')}` among that member's children. Rendered only while
the element has a child for it: a member that draws room for a filled slot would take a passing slot that is
always there for content.

members.name: getUpdateComplete
members.description: The element has updated when its members have: what it gave them, they have taken.

members.name: focusWhenReady
members.description: The control has rendered what takes focus only after its own first update.

events.description: The person changed the text: the native, composed `input` of the text element as they type, delete, paste or an input method commits; one more when the clear button empties the text and when Escape restores it. `inputValue` is already the new text. Never fired when the product sets `inputValue` or `value`, or when a choice writes its label. The product's cue to load options.
events.name: input

events.description: The committed value changed by the person: an option was chosen, a custom text was committed, or the value was cleared; `value` is already the new one. `detail.value` and `detail.inputValue`. Composed and bubbling. Never fired when the product sets `value`, when the chosen option is chosen again, or while the person only types or moves through the list.
events.name: change

events.description: The list was opened or closed by the person, or closed by having nothing left to show; `open` is already the new one. `detail.open`, and for a close `detail.reason`: `select`, `commit`, `escape`, `outside`, `press`, `tab`, `focus-out`, `anchor-hidden` or `empty`. After a choice it follows `change`. Composed and not bubbling, as the platform's own `toggle`: heard on the element, and on an element composed around it, and by no ancestor. Never fired when the product sets `open`.
events.name: toggle

events.description: The person pressed Enter with no option active and the text was committed; after any `change` it caused. Cancelable: unless it is cancelled, the form the combobox stands in is then asked to submit.

attributes.description: Disables the control and draws the frame as disabled. Disable a framed control here, not on the control, so that its label follows.

attributes.name: requirement
attributes.description: What the form asks of the control: `required` exposes it as required and draws the required mark; `optional` draws the optional tag; `none` says and draws nothing. It never validates.

attributes.name: required-mark
attributes.description: How this control shows that it is required (`required-mark`): `tag` is a small filled tag with `requiredText`, `asterisk` is "*" after the label, `none` draws nothing and keeps the semantics; `auto` takes the design system's answer (`--tanrei-comp-field-requirement-mark`, which follows `--tanrei-sys-behavior-requirement-mark`).

attributes.name: required-text
attributes.description: The text of the required tag (`required-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ requiredText })`). Tanrei has none: without them the asterisk is drawn in the tag's place and the required state is kept.

attributes.name: optional-text
attributes.description: The text of the optional tag, also part of the description (`optional-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ optionalText })`). Tanrei has none: without them no tag is drawn and nothing is said.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description: The look, as the text inputs beside it: `stacked` is a filled box that draws no label — the label above it is the row of the Field that frames it; `filled` and `outlined` float the label inside the box. Use one style per form. A value the combobox does not know by name is laid out as stacked. Reflected.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: The container's minimum height: `medium` or `large` (48 / 56 in the default system), the text input's two sizes. The hit area always meets the minimum target. Reflected.

attributes.name: value
attributes.description: The committed choice: the chosen option's value, or, with `allowCustomValue`, a text the person typed that names no option. Empty while nothing is chosen. The `value` attribute is the value a form reset returns to.

attributes.name: input-value
attributes.description: The text in the input (`input-value`). The combobox writes it as the person types and when a value is chosen or restored; the product may set it, and reads it from `input` to load options.

attributes.name: placeholder
attributes.description: A hint shown while the input is empty and the label is not in the input line. Never a replacement for `label`.

attributes.name: readonly
attributes.description: The value is shown, can be focused, selected and copied, and is submitted, but cannot be changed: the list does not open and neither the chevron nor the clear button is drawn. The attribute is `readonly`.

attributes.name: open
attributes.description: Whether the list is shown. The combobox opens and closes itself and emits `toggle`; the product may also set it (to open on focus, for one). Ignored while the combobox is disabled or read-only or has nothing to show. Reflected.

attributes.name: allow-custom-value
attributes.description: False: the value is always one of the options, and a text that names none is given up when the person leaves. True: the options are suggestions, and a text that names none becomes the value as typed (`allow-custom-value`). Reflected.

attributes.name: filter
attributes.description: Who decides which options answer the text. `contains`: the combobox shows the options whose label contains what was typed, ignoring case, width and marks, and marks the match. `none`: it shows every option it is given and the product filters, on `input`. Reflected.

attributes.name: no-chevron
attributes.description: Draws no chevron (`no-chevron`: the spec's `chevron`, inverted, because a boolean attribute cannot default to true): for a field whose suggestions exist only for what was typed. The list then opens by typing and by the arrow keys alone. Reflected.

attributes.name: clearable
attributes.description: Draws a clear button while the text is not empty, for a combobox whose value may be none. Without it, emptying the text and leaving the field clears the value. Reflected.

attributes.name: clear-label
attributes.description: The clear button's accessible name, in the product's language (`clear-label`). Required while `clearable` is true.

attributes.name: status
attributes.description: What the product's source of options is doing: `idle`, `loading` (the status row shows a loading indicator and the list is marked busy) or `error` (the status row shows `statusText` as an error, announced at once). Reflected.

attributes.name: status-text
attributes.description: The status row's text, in the product's language (`status-text`), announced when it changes: a count, that loading failed, or, while loading, the loading indicator's name.

attributes.name: empty-text
attributes.description: Shown in the list while the text names nothing the combobox can show, `allowCustomValue` is false and no status is set (`empty-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ emptyText })`). Tanrei has none: without them no such row is drawn.

attributes.name: separation
attributes.description: How a group of options is told from what is next to it: `divider`, `gap`, or `auto` for the design system's answer (`--tanrei-comp-combobox-separation`).

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Web only: the name the value is submitted under.

declarations.default: ['stacked', 'filled', 'outlined']
declarations.description: The values every design system has. A layer may add more; those get their styles on demand.

declarations.default: ['small', 'medium', 'large']

CMB-61, FLD-26: how far the combobox's input text stands from its own start edge, and the padding it keeps at its
end edge, as lengths — the sums the box itself is laid out by (`--_text-start`, `--_end` below), written from the
size's tokens so that the Field that is told them resolves them where it stands: custom properties are inherited.
Beside a leading glyph the text starts after the glyph's padding, the glyph and its gap; the clear button or the

declarations.description:
Lets people find one value by typing: a box that looks and measures like a text input, with a list of options that
narrows as they type and that they choose from, or, where the product allows it, a value of their own. The bare
control: it has no label row and no message of its own.

Contract: specs/combobox.spec.json. The options are `<tanrei-option>` children, optionally in
`<tanrei-option-group>` elements (the pair a select holds too); the combobox reads them — and reads them again when
they change — and renders the rows itself. A `<slot>` among its children stands for the elements assigned to it, so
that an element composed around it passes its own children on as the options. Every visual value is a token: the box is
drawn from `--tanrei-comp-input-box-*`, the one set every input box is drawn from (CMB-63), and the list and the
status row from `--tanrei-comp-combobox-*` — the list's hold the menu's values and the status row's the search's, in
every shipped design system.

```html
<tanrei-field label="City">
  <tanrei-combobox name="city" value="tokyo">
    <tanrei-option value="kyoto">Kyoto</tanrei-option>
    <tanrei-option value="tokyo">Tokyo</tanrei-option>
  </tanrei-combobox>
</tanrei-field>
```

In a form it is framed: by a Field, as above, or as `<tanrei-combobox-field>`, which is that pair as one element.
The Field gives it its name, its description and its required, invalid and disabled states, and draws the label
row, the requirement mark, the help and the error; the combobox says back that it draws the label itself where its
look floats one (`filled`, `outlined`), where its input text starts and ends, and that it is drawn focused for as
long as its list is open (`src/primitives/field.ts`). Bare — a filter in a toolbar, a cell of a table — it is named
by its own `label`, which a stacked combobox does not draw.

It holds two things: `value`, the committed choice, and `inputValue`, the text in the input. Typing changes the text,
opens the list and filters it (`filter="contains"`; with `filter="none"` the product filters, on `input`); a press on
an option or Enter on the active one chooses; leaving the box resolves the text — a typed label chooses its
option, any other text is kept as the value (`allow-custom-value`) or given up. The value changes only by a choice,
a commit or the clear button.

It is a block as wide as its place, with no width of its own. It is a form-associated element: it takes `name`,
submits `value` (never an uncommitted text), resets to the `value` attribute, is restored on navigation, follows
`<fieldset disabled>` and reports `valueMissing` while the Field that frames it says it is required and `value` is
empty. It never validates beyond that, and is never required by itself.

The pattern is the editable combobox with a list box: focus stays in the input while the list is open and one
option at most is the active one (`aria-activedescendant`). While an input method composes, every key is its own.

members.name: nativeSeen
members.description: What the native element held when the element last wrote to it or took from it; undefined until it has.

members.name: name
members.description: The name the value is submitted under in a form. Reflected.

members.name: label
members.description: The combobox's own accessible name, for a combobox no Field frames or one whose visible label is elsewhere; a filled or an outlined combobox draws it floating. Inside a Field leave it empty: the Field's label names the combobox, and its own would win.

members.name: labelHidden
members.description: Does not draw the floating label of a filled or an outlined combobox, which stays the accessible name (`label-hidden`). Inside a Field, hide the label on the Field.

members.name: placeholder
members.description: A hint shown while the input is empty and the label is not in the input line. Never a replacement for `label`.

members.name: error
members.description: Puts the combobox in the error condition: its box is drawn from its error parts and it is exposed as invalid. Inside a Field, set `error` on the Field, which also shows the words. The combobox never sets this itself.

members.name: disabled
members.description: Disables the combobox: it takes no focus, cannot be edited, does not open and is left out of form submission. Inside a Field, disable the Field, so that its label follows.

members.name: readOnly
members.description: The value is shown, can be focused, selected and copied, and is submitted, but cannot be changed: the list does not open and neither the chevron nor the clear button is drawn. The attribute is `readonly`.

members.name: open
members.description: Whether the list is shown. The combobox opens and closes itself and emits `toggle`; the product may also set it (to open on focus, for one). Ignored while the combobox is disabled or read-only or has nothing to show. Reflected.

members.name: allowCustomValue
members.description: False: the value is always one of the options, and a text that names none is given up when the person leaves. True: the options are suggestions, and a text that names none becomes the value as typed (`allow-custom-value`). Reflected.

members.name: filter
members.description: Who decides which options answer the text. `contains`: the combobox shows the options whose label contains what was typed, ignoring case, width and marks, and marks the match. `none`: it shows every option it is given and the product filters, on `input`. Reflected.

members.name: noChevron
members.description: Draws no chevron (`no-chevron`: the spec's `chevron`, inverted, because a boolean attribute cannot default to true): for a field whose suggestions exist only for what was typed. The list then opens by typing and by the arrow keys alone. Reflected.

members.name: clearable
members.description: Draws a clear button while the text is not empty, for a combobox whose value may be none. Without it, emptying the text and leaving the field clears the value. Reflected.

members.name: clearLabel
members.description: The clear button's accessible name, in the product's language (`clear-label`). Required while `clearable` is true.

members.name: status
members.description: What the product's source of options is doing: `idle`, `loading` (the status row shows a loading indicator and the list is marked busy) or `error` (the status row shows `statusText` as an error, announced at once). Reflected.

members.name: statusText
members.description: The status row's text, in the product's language (`status-text`), announced when it changes: a count, that loading failed, or, while loading, the loading indicator's name.

members.name: emptyText
members.description: Shown in the list while the text names nothing the combobox can show, `allowCustomValue` is false and no status is set (`empty-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ emptyText })`). Tanrei has none: without them no such row is drawn.

members.name: separation
members.description: How a group of options is told from what is next to it: `divider`, `gap`, or `auto` for the design system's answer (`--tanrei-comp-combobox-separation`).

members.name: inline
members.description: For tests and fixtures: draws the open list in place below the field — inside its positioned ancestor, which stands for the window — not in the top layer; it then answers no dismissal.

members.name: hasLeading
members.description: Whether the leading-icon slot has content.

members.name: focused
members.description: CMB-15: the input has focus, however it was gained.

members.name: formDisabled
members.description: Set by an ancestor `<fieldset disabled>` (the element's `formDisabledCallback`).

members.name: says
members.description: What it tells its form, said where an element composed around it hears it (src/primitives/form-says.ts).

members.name: presented
members.description: Whether the list is presented: open, usable, and beside a container in the page.

members.name: ownText
members.description: The text the combobox itself wrote or took from the person last: another `inputValue` is the product's.

members.name: ownValue
members.description: The value the combobox committed or took from the product last: another `value` is the product's.

members.name: editing
members.description: The person is editing: the text was changed since the last commit (CMB-17).

members.name: query
members.description: CMB-25: the text the list is filtered by; null shows every option (a list opened by an arrow key or the chevron).

members.name: composedText
members.description: The text was last taken during a composition: its end makes the first match active (CMB-26).

members.name: tabbing
members.description: The key that is moving focus now is Tab: a list it closes says so (CMB-29).

members.name: axes
members.default: new OpenAxesController(this, { component: 'combobox', behavior: 'CMB-56', axes: AXES })
members.description: CMB-56: sizes and variants a design system adds, and a value the active system does not have (src/primitives/axes.ts).

members.name: system
members.description: CMB-44: where style queries are missing the system's separation is read by script, again when the system is switched.

members.name: frame
members.default: new FieldControlController(this, { errorCondition: true, named: () => !!this.label.trim(), says: () => this.saysToField, changed: () => (this.frameChanged = true), })
members.description:
CMB-61: the combobox's side of the exchange with the Field that frames it (src/primitives/field.ts). It takes the
Field's name, description and states, whether the label is hidden and whether an asterisk follows it; and it says
what only it knows — that it draws the label, how far its input text is inset, and that it is drawn focused while
its list is open. It has an error condition of its own (CMB-10). No Field: it is drawn as a bare combobox.

members.name: frameChanged
members.description: The Field's answer changed since the last update: the floating label may have other lines (CMB-8).

members.name: options$
members.description: CMB-31: the options, read from the children and read again when they change (src/primitives/option-list.ts).

members.name: list
members.default: new OptionListController(this, { model: () => this.shown, chosen: () => this.chosen, choose: (option) => this.choose(option), // CMB-26: an active option that is no longer shown gives way to what typing would have found. replacement: (options) => (this.native.composing ? null : this.found(options)), })
members.description: CMB-24, CMB-26, CMB-27, CMB-40, CMB-41: the active option, the keys that move it, the press and the choice.

members.name: anchored
members.description: CMB-22, CMB-23, CMB-58: where the list is — the anchored surface a popover is drawn on, as wide as the container.

members.name: dismiss
members.default: new DismissController(this, { related: () => [this], request: (reason: DismissReason) => this.closeList(reason), })
members.description: CMB-30: Escape pressed elsewhere, a press outside and focus arriving elsewhere (src/primitives/dismiss.ts).

members.name: native
members.default: new NativeTextController({ input: () => this.input, value: () => this.text, setValue: (text) => this.took(text, this.native.composing), })
members.description: CMB-16: the text and the native element kept in step without breaking an input method (src/primitives/native-text.ts).

members.name: floating
members.description: CMB-8: a floating label that does not fit on one line is given the room its lines take.

members.name: mirror
members.description: CMB-54: the glyphs of the two slots, the chosen option's own and the options' are marked when the icon set mirrors them.

members.name: glyphs
members.description: A glyph the combobox draws by name is drawn once the icon set can draw it; until then nothing stands in its place.

members.name: inert_
members.description: Disabled by its own `disabled`, a fieldset's, or the Field's or the field group's that frames it (CMB-46).

members.name: layout
members.description: How the variant is laid out: filled and outlined by name, every other value as stacked (CMB-56).

members.name: filterNow
members.description: CMB-56: a filter the combobox does not define is contains, a status idle.

members.name: chosen
members.description: CMB-17, CMB-57: the chosen option — the first, in order and across groups, whose value equals `value`; never one whose value is empty.

members.name: committedText
members.description: CMB-17: the text of the committed value: the chosen option's label; a value that names no option itself where a custom value is allowed, and nothing otherwise.

members.name: foldedLabel
members.description: An option's label as it is compared, folded once for as long as the options stay.

members.name: needle
members.description: The folded text the combobox filters by now; empty while it shows every option.

members.name: shown
members.description: CMB-25: the options shown now, in their order: every one, or, while the combobox filters, those whose label contains the text.

members.name: words
members.description: CMB-60: the product's words, read where the instance gives none (src/primitives/words.ts).

members.name: name_
members.description: CMB-12: the accessible name — its own label, else the label of the Field that frames it.

members.name: inError
members.description: CMB-10: in the error condition — its own `error`, or its Field's (FLD-8).

members.name: labelled
members.description: CMB-8: the label floats in the box — a filled or an outlined combobox with a name, unless its own `labelHidden` or its Field's says to draw none.

members.name: asterisked
members.description: CMB-7: an asterisk follows the floating label — the Field's answer (FLD-25); never outside a Field.

members.name: leading
members.description: CMB-18: the glyph at the start of the container — the slot's, or else the chosen option's own while the person is not editing.

members.name: chevronShown
members.description: CMB-19: the chevron is drawn.

members.name: clearShown
members.description: CMB-20: the clear button is drawn.

members.name: saysToField
members.description:
CMB-61: what the combobox says to the Field that frames it. That it draws the label while its look floats one — its
name, or nothing while the label is hidden; the Field draws no label row either way. How far its input text
stands from its start edge and the padding it keeps at its end edge, as lengths of the box's tokens (`INSET`, in the
styles). And that it is drawn focused for as long as its list is open, whether or not it has focus (CMB-15).

members.name: statusShown
members.description: CMB-32: the status row has something of the product's to show.

members.name: emptyAsked
members.description: CMB-32: nothing matched, and nothing of the product's stands in the status row's place: the empty text is asked for.

members.name: emptyWords
members.description: CMB-32, CMB-60: what says that nothing matched — the instance's emptyText, else the product's words, else nothing.

members.name: emptyShown
members.description: CMB-32: nothing matched, and the combobox says so in the status row's place.

members.name: something
members.description: CMB-21, CMB-57: there is something to show: an option after filtering, a status row or the empty text.

members.name: usable
members.description: CMB-21, CMB-46, CMB-47, CMB-57: whether the list can be shown at all.

members.name: found
members.description: CMB-26: the option typing makes active: the first shown that is not disabled, or none where Enter keeps the text.

members.name: named
members.description: CMB-29: the first option that is not disabled whose whole label is `text`, compared as the filter compares and ignoring the spaces around it.

members.name: form
members.description: The form it belongs to, if any.

members.name: validity
members.description: The native constraint validity: `valueMissing` while its Field says the combobox is required and its value is empty.

members.name: focus
members.description: Moves focus to the input: the combobox's one stop in the focus order (the clear button, while shown, is the next).

members.name: select
members.description: Selects the text in the input.

members.name: write
members.description: The combobox writes the text itself: no `input` is fired, and the element shows it at once (never into a composition).

members.name: show
members.description: CMB-16, CMB-31: the text is shown in the native element — never into a composition — and what the element then holds is what was seen of it.

members.name: settle
members.description: The person is no longer editing: the text is the committed value's, and the list shows every option again.

members.name: took
members.description:
CMB-16, CMB-21, CMB-25, CMB-26: the person changed the text. The native `input` is the combobox's event — it is
composed and leaves the shadow root by itself. The list is filtered by the text, opened where there is something to
show, and the first match becomes the active option — none where a custom value is allowed or an input method is
composing, so that Enter keeps what was typed.

members.name: commit
members.description: CMB-27, CMB-28, CMB-29: `value` is committed with the text that stands for it; `change` once while it differs.

members.name: toggled
members.description:
CMB-21, CMB-30: `toggle` — composed, so that it leaves the shadow root of an element composed around the combobox
with that element as its target, and not bubbling, as the platform's own `toggle`: no ancestor hears it.

members.name: resolve
members.description:
CMB-29: resolves the text. An empty text makes the value empty; the whole label of an option that is not disabled
chooses the first such option; any other text becomes the value where a custom value is allowed. Returns false
where the text names nothing and no custom value is allowed: the caller keeps it (Enter) or gives it up (leaving).

members.name: restore
members.description: CMB-29, CMB-30: the text of the committed value is written back. Returns whether the text changed.

members.name: openList
members.description:
CMB-21: the person opens the list. Opened by an arrow key or the chevron it shows every option and the chosen one
is active (CMB-26); opened by typing it is filtered and `active` is. `open` is true before `toggle` is fired; the
list is presented by the render that follows.

members.name: closeList
members.description: CMB-30: the list closes, for `reason`. `open` is false, and the list no longer takes input, before `toggle` is fired.

members.name: choose
members.description: CMB-27: the person confirmed `option`. `value` is the new one before `change`; the list then closes, so `toggle` follows.

members.name: present
members.description: CMB-22, CMB-24: into the overlay layer beside the container. Focus stays where it is.

members.name: withdraw
members.description: CMB-30, CMB-45: out of it, fading; closed or closing it takes no pointer input.

members.name: enter
members.description:
CMB-27, CMB-28: Enter. With an option active it chooses it and does nothing else. With none it commits the text —
and where the text names nothing and no custom value is allowed, keeps it and keeps or opens the list — then fires
`action` after any `change` it caused, and asks the form to submit unless `action` was cancelled.

members.name: onFieldKeyDown
members.description: The clear button's Tab leaves the combobox too.

members.name: onFocusOut
members.description:
CMB-29: focus leaves the combobox — the input and, while it is shown, the clear button. The text is resolved, or
given up where it names nothing; the active option is not chosen; an open list closes with the reason tab or
focus-out. Focus that leaves the window has gone nowhere: nothing is resolved until it goes elsewhere in the page.

members.name: onContainerPress
members.description:
CMB-14: a press on the container's padding or on a decorative glyph moves focus to the input and does nothing
else. A press in the input places the caret; the clear button and the chevron answer their own click, and focus
stays where it is (the clear button is reached by Tab).

members.name: onChevron
members.description: CMB-19: a press on the chevron opens the list while it is closed and closes it while it is open; focus is the input's.

members.name: onClear
members.description:
CMB-20: the clear button empties the text and the value: `input` once with the empty text, `change` once while the
value was not empty, focus to the input, and the list left as it is — showing every option while open.

members.name: reports
members.description: What a debug build tells the developer; the combobox still renders.

members.name: labelText
members.description: CMB-38: an option's label with the first run that matched the text in a `<mark>`: one text, drawn heavier there.

members.name: renderStatus
members.description:
CMB-32, CMB-33: the status row, after the last option. Its two live regions exist from the moment the list opens —
the polite one holds statusText, or the empty text, while idle; the assertive one statusText while the source
failed; while loading both are empty, so nothing is announced, and the loading indicator, named by statusText,
stands in the text's place.

events.name: change
events.description: The committed value changed by the person: an option was chosen, a custom text was committed, or the value was cleared; `value` is already the new one. `detail.value` and `detail.inputValue`. Composed and bubbling. Never fired when the product sets `value`, when the chosen option is chosen again, or while the person only types or moves through the list.

events.name: toggle
events.description: The list was opened or closed by the person, or closed by having nothing left to show; `open` is already the new one. `detail.open`, and for a close `detail.reason`: `select`, `commit`, `escape`, `outside`, `press`, `tab`, `focus-out`, `anchor-hidden` or `empty`. After a choice it follows `change`. Composed and not bubbling, as the platform's own `toggle`: heard on the element, and on an element composed around it, and by no ancestor. Never fired when the product sets `open`.

events.name: input
events.description: The person changed the text: the native, composed `input` of the text element as they type, delete, paste or an input method commits; one more when the clear button empties the text and when Escape restores it. `inputValue` is already the new text. Never fired when the product sets `inputValue` or `value`, or when a choice writes its label. The product's cue to load options.
The person pressed Enter with no option active and the text was committed; after any `change` it caused. Cancelable: unless it is cancelled, the form the combobox stands in is then asked to submit.

declarations.name: styles
declarations.default: css` /* A Button's place in a row: inline, on the baseline of the text beside it. */ :host { display: inline-flex; position: relative; vertical-align: middle; } :host([hidden]) { display: none; } /* CPY-7, CPY-11: the three glyphs are drawn in one box — the Button's icon box, which this fills. While the icon set cannot draw a glyph yet (its font is loading) its name would be spelled in a text face: nothing is drawn in its place until it can (data-drawn, src/primitives/glyph.ts), and the box is kept. */ .glyph { display: inline-block; inline-size: 100%; block-size: 100%; } .ink { display: inline-block; } .glyph:not([data-drawn]) { visibility: hidden; } /* CPY-7: the label's box is as wide as the widest of the three texts at all times — they share one cell, the two that are not shown hidden from sight and from assistive technology — and the shown text is at its start. */ .labels { display: inline-grid; justify-items: start; } .labels > span { grid-area: 1 / 1; } .labels > span:not(.shown) { visibility: hidden; } /* CPY-5: the announcements — read, never drawn. */ .live { position: absolute; overflow: hidden; inline-size: 1px; block-size: 1px; clip-path: inset(50%); white-space: nowrap; } /* CPY-3: comp.copy-button.confirmation.duration is an expression; it is computed through a real property of this inert box and read from there (a duration token is never parsed). */ .time { display: none; transition-property: none; transition-duration: var(--tanrei-comp-copy-button-confirmation-duration); } `

declarations.description:
Copies a given text to the clipboard with one press and confirms it — its glyph becomes a check for a moment and
assistive technology is told — or says that it could not. It is drawn by Button and never moves the layout.

Contract: specs/copy-button.spec.json.

declarations.name: TanreiCopyButton

cssParts.description: The Button it is drawn by (a `<tanrei-button>`; its own parts are `container`, `icon` and `label`).
cssParts.name: button

members.name: words
members.description: The product's words, read where the instance gives none (src/primitives/words.ts).

members.name: text
members.description: The text to copy, exactly as it will be pasted. Plain text only.

members.name: label
members.description: What the button does, in your language ("Copy", "Copy link"): the accessible name of the icon-only form and the visible text of the labelled one. Required.

members.name: copiedLabel
members.description: What is announced, and shown in the labelled form, when the text has been copied ("Copied"). Required.

members.name: failedLabel
members.description: What is announced, and shown in the labelled form, when the browser refuses the copy ("Could not copy"). Required.

members.name: iconOnly
members.description: True draws the glyph alone, named by `label`. False (`icon-only="false"`) draws the glyph and the label as text.

members.name: variant
members.description:
The Button variant it is drawn as — `filled`, `tonal`, `elevated`, `outlined` or `text`. The default, text, is the
quiet icon action beside what it copies; a copy that is a view's main action takes another.

members.name: size
members.description: The Button size it is drawn at: `small` (32), `medium` (40) or `large` (56).

members.name: disabled
members.description: Prevents the copy; the button is drawn and exposed as a disabled Button.

members.name: form
members.description: The form it shows now (CPY-3, CPY-4).

members.name: pending
members.description: CPY-2: the browser has been asked and has not answered; a second activation is ignored until it does.

members.name: timer
members.description: CPY-3: the return to rest.

members.name: drawn
members.default: new GlyphDrawnController( this, () => { const glyph = this.renderRoot?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.glyph'); return glyph ? [glyph] : []; }, { firstInFrame: true }, )
members.description:
CPY-11: while the icon set cannot draw a glyph, nothing is drawn in its place (src/primitives/glyph.ts): the glyph
is marked `data-drawn` once its ink is a ligature's and not its name spelled out. A page draws one copy button for
every code block it shows: the first decision is the frame's (`firstInFrame`), one pass for them all.

members.name: click
members.description: `element.click()` activates the button as a person would: through the Button, and not at all while disabled.

members.name: duration
members.description: comp.copy-button.confirmation.duration in milliseconds, as the cascade gives it now.

members.name: rest
members.description: Back to rest, at once and without a word (CPY-5: nothing is announced on the return).

members.name: answer
members.description: CPY-3, CPY-4, CPY-8: the browser's answer — the form, its event, its announcement, and the time counted from now.

members.name: onClick
members.description: CPY-2: an activation — by pointer, touch, Enter, Space or assistive technology, all of which click the Button.

members.name: drawnValue
members.description: CPY-17: the Button value that is drawn — the prop's where the active design system's Button has it, else the copy button's own default.

events.description: The browser confirmed that the text is on the clipboard; `detail.text` is the text.
events.name: copied

events.description: The browser refused the copy or has no clipboard to write to; `detail.reason` is its reason, where it gave one.
events.name: copyfailed

attributes.name: text
attributes.description: The text to copy, exactly as it will be pasted. Plain text only.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: What the button does, in your language ("Copy", "Copy link"): the accessible name of the icon-only form and the visible text of the labelled one. Required.

attributes.name: copied-label
attributes.description: What is announced, and shown in the labelled form, when the text has been copied ("Copied"). Required.

attributes.name: failed-label
attributes.description: What is announced, and shown in the labelled form, when the browser refuses the copy ("Could not copy"). Required.

attributes.name: icon-only
attributes.description: True draws the glyph alone, named by `label`. False (`icon-only="false"`) draws the glyph and the label as text.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description:
The Button variant it is drawn as — `filled`, `tonal`, `elevated`, `outlined` or `text`. The default, text, is the
quiet icon action beside what it copies; a copy that is a view's main action takes another.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: The Button size it is drawn at: `small` (32), `medium` (40) or `large` (56).

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: Prevents the copy; the button is drawn and exposed as a disabled Button.

} .divider { background: CanvasText; } .selector, .range-field { border: ${t('divider-width')} solid CanvasText; } .selector.selected, .range-field.selected, .wheel.typing > .ground { border: ${t('divider-width')} solid Highlight; } .wheels[data-span='joined'] > .band, .wheels[data-span='each'] .wheel > .ground { border-block: ${t('divider-width')} solid Highlight; } .dial { border: ${t('divider-width')} solid CanvasText; } .handle, .track, .center { background: Highlight; } .copy .number { color: HighlightText; } } `

declarations.description:
Lets a person choose a date, a time, or a date and time — or a span of any of them — from a Calendar and time wheels
or a clock dial, in a dialog or in a surface that drops down from a field.

Contract: specs/date-time-picker.spec.json. `modal` (the default) is a native `<dialog>` in the shadow root opened with
`showModal()` — `::backdrop` is the scrim, everything else is inert, focus is trapped — with a start-aligned title row,
the pending value (in a mode with a date) and Cancel and OK; the choice is pending until OK. `docked` is a manual
popover in the top layer, placed below the element whose id is `anchor` with the menu's placement (flipped above when
there is more room there, shifted to stay in the viewport, following the anchor); it is not modal: Tab and focus
leaving close it, and a docked picker that sets a date only commits by choosing it. Both move focus in when they open
and give it back when they close.

The picker never closes itself: it fires `close` with a reason and you set `open` to false. When one activation
commits a choice, the element takes the new `value` (or `start` and `end`) and fires `change` before `close`.

Values are the strings of `<input type=date>`, `type=time` and `type=datetime-local`: "2026-09-17", "19:30",
"2026-09-17T19:30" — no seconds, no time zone. The date is a `<tanrei-calendar>`; the time is set on two wheels (spin
buttons that also take a typed number: press a wheel's chosen value, or type a digit) or on a clock dial with an hour
and a minute selector, chosen by two icon-only `<tanrei-tabs variant="secondary">` at the end of the title row while
the design system offers both (`comp.date-time-picker.time.entry-modes`) — the keyboard glyph for the wheels, the
clock face for the dial, `wheelsLabel` and `dialLabel` their accessible names. They are the picker's only tabs. The
period of a 12-hour time (AM, PM) is a part of the time, after the minute or — where the locale writes it first —
before the hour: a third wheel of two rows in the wheels mode, and in the dial mode a narrow selector that shows the
pending period and changes to the other when pressed; either is a spin button of two values named `periodLabel`, and
neither is ever drawn as selected. The two ends of a range that has a time are two range fields joined by an en dash
("9:00 AM – 5:30 PM") across the whole time section, with no word for start or end; the one the wheels or the dial set
is drawn as selected, and pressing the other sets it. Names, digits, forms, the separator and the preferred clock come from `Intl` for `locale`
(without it, the nearest `lang`, then the browser's language). Every visual value comes from
`--tanrei-comp-date-time-picker-*` tokens; the calendar, the tabs and the Buttons keep their own. The `inline`
attribute, for tests and documentation, draws the open surface in place without the overlay's behaviour.

members.name: words
