members.name: reportWords
members.description:
DTM-48: a word that is drawn or exposed now and that nobody gave — not the instance, not the product's words, not
the platform — is recorded (`missingWords()`) and, in a debug build, reported once, naming the prop. The part is
still drawn and still works. `label` is the instance's alone, and reported for this picker.

members.name: open
members.description: Whether the picker is shown. Open it from your field or button; set it to false when the picker fires `close`.

members.name: presentation
members.description: `modal`: a dialog over a scrim, committed by OK. `docked`: a surface below `anchor`.

members.name: mode
members.description: `date`, `time` or `date-time`: what is chosen.

members.name: range
members.description: Chooses a span (`start` … `end`) instead of one `value`: of dates, of times (the end may fall on the next day) or of both.

members.name: value
members.description: The chosen value without a range: "2026-09-17" (date), "19:30" (time, 24-hour), "2026-09-17T19:30" (date-time); empty when none.

members.name: start
members.description: The first value of the chosen span when `range` is true, in the mode's form; empty when none.

members.name: end
members.description: The last value of the chosen span when `range` is true, in the mode's form; empty while only `start` is chosen.

members.name: min
members.description: The earliest date that can be chosen (it bounds the calendar only); empty for no limit.

members.name: max
members.description: The latest date that can be chosen; empty for no limit.

members.name: disabledDates
members.description: Dates that cannot be chosen, passed to the calendar. The `disabled-dates` attribute is a space-separated list or a JSON array.

members.name: isDateDisabled
members.description: A rule no list can hold (every weekend): true for an ISO date that cannot be chosen. Passed to the calendar. Property only.

members.name: today
members.description: The date the calendar draws as today; empty uses the device's current date.

members.name: firstDayOfWeek
members.description: The weekday in the calendar's first column (`first-day-of-week`).

members.name: locale
members.description: A BCP 47 tag ("en-US", "ja-JP") for names, digits, forms, the separator and the clock; empty: the nearest `lang`, then the browser's.

members.name: startView
members.description: Whether the calendar opens on the days of a month or on the list of years (`start-view`).

members.name: showAdjacentDays
members.description: Whether the calendar shows the neighbouring months' days in its spare cells (`show-adjacent-days`).

members.name: hourCycle
members.description: `h12` (1–12 with a period), `h23` (00–23) or `locale` (the locale's clock). Values are 24-hour in every cycle (`hour-cycle`).

members.name: minuteStep
members.description: The minutes a person can choose: every minute (1), or every 5, 10, 15 or 30 (`minute-step`).

members.name: entryMode
members.description: How the time is set when the picker opens (`entry-mode`): `wheels` or `dial`. Not HTML's `inputmode`.

members.name: unit
members.description: Dial mode: the unit the dial shows, and the selector that takes focus, when the picker opens.

members.name: layout
members.description: `vertical`, `horizontal`, or `auto`: horizontal only when the window is too short for vertical and wide enough.

members.name: label
members.description: Names the picker: its surface's accessible name and the start of its title row — what is being chosen ("Check-in", "Meeting time"). Required, and this instance's alone: the product's words hold none. Empty, the title row draws no words and keeps its height, and the surface has no name.

members.name: dateLabel
members.description: What the header shows for a date not chosen yet: a single value's, and either end's of a range (`date-label`). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ dateLabel })`); Tanrei has none: without them nothing is drawn there, and the place keeps its height.

members.name: startLabel
members.description: Range: the accessible name of the start's range field and the calendar's start day's description; never drawn (`start-label`). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ startLabel })`); Tanrei has none: without them the field and the day say nothing of it.

members.name: endLabel
members.description: Range: the accessible name of the end's range field and the calendar's end day's description; never drawn (`end-label`). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ endLabel })`); Tanrei has none: without them the field and the day say nothing of it.

members.name: confirmLabel
members.description: OK's label (`confirm-label`). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ confirmLabel })`); Tanrei has none: without them an icon-only Button with the check glyph, unnamed.

members.name: cancelLabel
members.description: Cancel's label (`cancel-label`). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ cancelLabel })`); Tanrei has none: without them an icon-only Button with the close glyph, unnamed.

members.name: previousMonthLabel
members.description: Passed to the calendar (`previous-month-label`). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ previousMonthLabel })`); Tanrei has none: without them the button is drawn and works, unnamed.

members.name: nextMonthLabel
members.description: Passed to the calendar (`next-month-label`). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ nextMonthLabel })`); Tanrei has none: without them the button is drawn and works, unnamed.

members.name: yearViewLabel
members.description: Passed to the calendar (`year-view-label`). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ yearViewLabel })`); Tanrei has none: without them the view toggle has no description.

members.name: todayLabel
members.description: Passed to the calendar (`today-label`). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ todayLabel })`); Tanrei has none: without them the locale's own word for the present day, from the browser.

members.name: hourLabel
members.description: The accessible name of the hour wheel and the hour selector (`hour-label`). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ hourLabel })`); Tanrei has none: without them the locale's own name for the hour, from the browser.

members.name: minuteLabel
members.description: The accessible name of the minute wheel and the minute selector (`minute-label`). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ minuteLabel })`); Tanrei has none: without them the locale's own name for the minute, from the browser.

members.name: wheelsLabel
members.description: The accessible name of the entry-mode tab that shows the wheels, which draws the keyboard glyph alone (`wheels-label`). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ wheelsLabel })`); Tanrei has none: without them the tab is drawn and works, unnamed.

members.name: dialLabel
members.description: The accessible name of the entry-mode tab that shows the dial, which draws the schedule glyph alone (`dial-label`). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ dialLabel })`); Tanrei has none: without them the tab is drawn and works, unnamed.

members.name: entryModeLabel
members.description: The accessible name of the row of entry-mode tabs (`entry-mode-label`). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ entryModeLabel })`); Tanrei has none: without them the row of tabs has no name.

members.name: periodLabel
members.description: The accessible name of the period — the period wheel or the period selector, a spin button (`period-label`). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ periodLabel })`); Tanrei has none: without them the locale's own name for the day period, from the browser.

members.name: rangeLabel
members.description: The accessible name of the range display, the group of the two range fields (`range-label`). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ rangeLabel })`); Tanrei has none: without them the group has no name.

members.name: nextDayLabel
members.description: Mode time with a range: added after the end's time, in its range field and its accessible name, while it falls on the next day (`next-day-label`). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ nextDayLabel })`); Tanrei has none: without them "+1" in the locale's digits.

members.name: rangeErrorText
members.description: Mode date-time with a range: the error line while the end is before the start (`range-error-text`). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ rangeErrorText })`); Tanrei has none: without them the line draws no words and keeps its height; OK is still disabled.

members.name: anchor
members.description: Docked: the id of the element the surface is placed against (as the menu's `anchor`), in the picker's own document or shadow root.

members.name: opener
members.description: Docked: the id of the element that opens the picker, when it is not the anchor (a text field's picker button). It gets `aria-haspopup`, `aria-controls` and `aria-expanded`.

members.name: inline
members.description: For tests and documentation: draws the open surface in place (DTM-1's verify), without the overlay's behaviour.

members.name: pending
members.default: { value: EMPTY, start: EMPTY, end: EMPTY }
members.description: The choice shown, from opening to OK (DTM-6).

members.name: editing
members.description: Which end the time section sets (DTM-15): `value` without a range.

members.name: entry
members.description: The entry mode shown (DTM-13).

members.name: shownUnit
members.description: The unit the dial shows (DTM-21).

members.name: angle
members.description: DTM-26: the handle's angle, kept continuous so that a change turns it along the shorter arc.

members.name: instant
members.description: DTM-25: the handle moves without animation (a drag, or the picker just opened).

members.name: stacked
members.description: DTM-34: the actions are a column.

members.name: wheelFrame
members.description: DTM-19: a count that renders the wheels again while they follow a pointer.

members.name: typed
members.description: DTM-43, DTM-44: the typed entry in progress — the wheel or the selector it is on, and the digits read so far.

members.name: armed
members.description:
DTM-44: the wheel that an hour's finished entry moved on to. Its input takes text — so that an on-screen keyboard
stays up — though no entry has begun on it: the next digit begins one.

members.name: ringed
members.description:
DTM-20, DTM-47: the wheel — or the period, wheel or selector — whose focus is keyboard focus, and so shows its ring.
An input's own `:focus-visible` cannot tell, and whether a key pressed after a pointer press makes a focused element
match it is each browser's own guess: the picker keeps the answer itself, so every engine draws the same.

members.name: ringedEnd
members.description:
DTM-28: the range field whose focus is keyboard focus, kept by the picker for the same reason: after a press and
then Space or Enter one engine draws no ring on a button it still reads as focused by the pointer.

members.name: openedWith
members.description: The choice the picker opened with, in the mode's form (DTM-6).

members.name: returnTo
members.description: DTM-4: where focus was when it opened.

members.name: errorShown
members.description: DTM-33: the error line was shown at the last update (it is announced when it appears).

members.name: wheelPress
members.description: DTM-20: a press on a wheel is about to focus its input (no ring), or the next focus was asked to show one or not.

members.name: escapeSpent
members.description: DTM-45: the Escape that ended a typed entry closes nothing: when the key was pressed.

members.name: keyboard
members.description: DTM-45: how much of the window the on-screen keyboard covered at the last look.

members.name: wheels
members.default: { hour: { at: 0, shift: 0, pointer: null, startY: 0, moved: false, samples: [], settling: 0, scrolling: 0 }, minute: { at: 0, shift: 0, pointer: null, startY: 0, moved: false, samples: [], settling: 0, scrolling: 0 }, }

members.name: periodWheel
members.default: { at: 0, shift: 0, pointer: null, startY: 0, moved: false, samples: [], settling: 0, scrolling: 0 }
members.description: DTM-46: the period wheel — its rows' position is 0 before noon and 1 after, and never past either.

members.name: presses
members.description: DTM-29, DTM-30: each selector is pressed on its own (data-pressed, press-hold, the ripple).

members.name: periodPress
members.description: DTM-14: and the period selector, which answers a press as an unselected selector does.

members.name: rangePresses
members.description: DTM-29, DTM-30: and each range field.

members.name: resolveLocale
members.description: DTM-38: `locale`, else the nearest `lang` (through shadow roots), else the browser's language; English when `Intl` does not know it.

members.name: parseMoment
members.description: DTM-8, DTM-40: a value in the mode's form as a moment, or null (reported) when it is not one.

members.name: momentText
members.description: DTM-8: a moment in the mode's form; `""` while a part the mode needs is missing.

members.name: pendingUntilOk
members.description: DTM-6, DTM-7: whether the choice is pending until OK (every picker but a docked one for a date only).

members.name: offered
members.description: DTM-13: the entry modes the design system offers, read from the cascade now.

members.name: shownEntry
members.description: The entry mode shown: the one chosen, or the only one offered (DTM-13).

members.name: time
members.description: The pending time of the end the time section sets.

members.name: confirmable
members.description: DTM-6: OK is enabled while the pending choice is complete and a date-time range's end is not before its start.

members.name: rangeError
members.description: DTM-33: a date-time range whose pending end is before its start.

members.name: nextDay
members.description: DTM-33: a time range's end at or before its start falls on the next day.

members.name: commit
members.description: DTM-6, DTM-7: the pending choice becomes the element's — `change` if it differs — then `close` with the reason.

members.name: requestClose
members.description: DTM-5: asks the product to close the picker, once, with the reason.

members.name: selectEnd
members.description:
DTM-42: the range field of `end` becomes the selected one — the wheels, the time display, the period and the
dial show and set that end's pending time (moving to it, DTM-26). A typed entry ends first; no pending time changes
and nothing is emitted. Selecting the selected one changes nothing.

members.name: rangeHandlers
members.description: DTM-42: a press, Enter or Space on a range field selects it (a native button's click); focus alone does not.

members.name: hourValues
members.description: The hours of the clock in use, as drawn: 1–12, or 0–23.

members.name: indexOf
members.description: The index in its list of the pending value of `unit`.

members.name: withIndex
members.description: The time with `unit` set to the list's entry at `index` (the period kept: DTM-19, DTM-20).

members.name: keyTime
members.description: DTM-20, DTM-22: the keys of a wheel or a selector. Returns the new time, or null for a key that is not theirs.

members.name: valueText
members.description: DTM-20, DTM-22: a spin button's value as drawn, the hour with the period's name in the 12-hour clock ("7 AM").

members.name: syncWheels
members.description: Brings each wheel's rows to its pending value, along the shorter way, unless a pointer or a settle is moving it.

members.name: alignWheel
members.description: A wheel's rows at its pending value now, along the shorter way — also while a pointer holds it: what a drag or a scroll that ended a typed entry goes on from (DTM-45).

members.name: spin
members.description: A wheel's control: the input on its middle row (DTM-20, DTM-43).

members.name: rowMetrics
members.description: The height of a row in px (row.height, at least the target: DTM-32), and the settle's duration in ms (DTM-19).

members.name: settle
members.description: DTM-19: the rows settle `rows` rows on (a drag's end, a fling, a press on a row) and the value is taken once they have.

members.name: onWheelMouseDown
members.description: A press on a row of a wheel keeps the focus on the wheel's input: the rows take none, and the page gets none.

members.name: onWheelScroll
members.description: DTM-19: a scroll moves the rows; when it stops, the nearest row settles.

members.name: onWheelKeyDown
members.description:
DTM-20: the keys of a wheel; the rows move over the wheel motion. DTM-43 … DTM-45: a digit begins or goes on with
a typed entry, and while one lasts the keys that move the wheel end it first, keeping what it read.

members.name: onSpinFocus
members.description:
DTM-20: a wheel shows its ring for focus from the keyboard only. Its control is a text input, which matches
`:focus-visible` however it was focused, so the wheel says itself: no ring after a press on it, the ring it was
asked for when the picker moved the focus, and the ring otherwise (Tab).

members.name: ringKeyed
members.description:
DTM-20: a wheel that has just been worked by the keyboard — a digit, a key that moves it, a key that ends its entry,
text from an on-screen keyboard — holds keyboard focus from then on, however focus first reached it: the wheel that
has focus now shows its ring. So the minute wheel shows where focus is once the hour's entry has moved on to it
(DTM-44), and a wheel whose entry has ended still does, where a press on it had shown none.

members.name: onSpinBlur
members.description: DTM-45: focus leaving a wheel ends its typed entry, keeping what it read.

members.name: onSpinInput
members.description:
DTM-44: text that reaches a wheel's input without a key the picker read — an on-screen keyboard's digits, a paste —
is read as its characters typed in order. The input itself shows only what the entry holds.

members.name: typedText
members.description: The digits read so far as they are shown: in the locale's digits, as the values around them are (DTM-44).

members.name: digitOf
members.description: The digit a typed character is, ASCII or the locale's (DTM-44); null for any other character.

members.name: isValue
members.description: Whether `value` is a value of `unit`: an hour of the clock in use, or a minute (DTM-44).

members.name: canJoin
members.description: Whether a second digit could join `first` (DTM-44): not after 2–9 for the 12-hour hour, 3–9 for the 24-hour one, 6–9 for the minute.

members.name: beginEntry
members.description:
DTM-43: a typed entry begins on `unit`. In the wheels mode the wheel takes focus and its input takes text, so that
an on-screen keyboard comes up for it (`raise`: within the press that began it, where a platform asks for that).

members.name: endEntry
members.description:
DTM-45: the typed entry ends. Kept, what it read becomes the pending value where it is a value of the unit — a
minute rounded down to minuteStep (DTM-8), an hour of the 12-hour clock in the pending period — and the wheel's rows
or the dial's handle move to it; nothing typed, or no value (0 alone for the 12-hour hour), keeps the value it had.

members.name: moveOn
members.description:
DTM-44: the hour's entry has ended by its digits or by a separator: focus moves to the minute — the minute wheel,
whose input takes text from now on (the next digit begins its entry), or the minute selector.

members.name: readTyped
members.description: DTM-44: reads `text` as typed on `unit`, character by character, each on the unit the one before left the entry at.

members.name: readChar
members.description: DTM-44: one typed character on `unit`. Returns the unit the next character is read on.

members.name: entryKey
members.description:
DTM-43 … DTM-45: a key on a wheel or a selector, as a typed entry reads it. A digit begins an entry or goes on with
it. While one lasts: Backspace removes the last digit; Enter ends it, keeping what it read, and presses nothing;
Escape ends it with the value it had and closes nothing; the separator moves an hour on to the minute; any other
character is ignored. Returns whether the key was the entry's.

members.name: setPeriod
members.description:
DTM-14, DTM-47: `period` (0 before noon, 1 after) becomes the pending period. The hour's number and the minute stay,
the dial's handle stays where it is (the same angle), and neither the unit the dial shows nor the selected selector
changes. A typed entry ends first, keeping what it read.

members.name: periodKey
members.description:
DTM-47: the keys of the period — Up and Down change it (it has two values), and on the period selector Right and
Left too, in every layout direction; Home is before noon, End after; Enter and Space do what Up does; the first
letter of a period's name in the locale (A or P in English) sets that period, and where the two names begin with
the same letter (午前, 午後) it changes the period, as a browser's own time field does. Returns the period the key
asks for, or null for a key that is not the period's (a digit or any other letter is ignored).

members.name: periodByInitial
members.description:
DTM-47: the period whose name in the locale begins with the typed character — compared without case, in the
locale's own casing — or `other` where both names begin with it; null for a character neither begins with, and for
a key that is no character.

members.name: periodHandlers
members.default: { onPointerDown: (event: PointerEvent) => { // DTM-45: a press ends a typed entry, keeping what it read. this.endEntry(true); this.periodPress.onPointerDown(event); }, onClick: () => this.setPeriod(periodOf(this.time.hour) ? 0 : 1), onKeyDown: (event: KeyboardEvent) => { const period = this.periodKey(event, true); if (period === null) return; event.preventDefault(); this.ringPeriod(); if (event.repeat && (event.key === 'Enter' || event.key === ' ')) return; this.periodPress.onKeyDown(event); this.setPeriod(period); }, /** * DTM-47: the period shows its ring for keyboard focus only — what the picker asked for when it moved the focus * (none after a press on the period wheel), otherwise what the browser says of how focus arrived (Tab, or a press). */ onFocus: (event: FocusEvent) => { const control = event.currentTarget as HTMLElement; syncFocusStyle(this, control); const ring = this.nextRing ?? control.matches(':focus-visible'); this.nextRing = null; this.ringed = ring ? 'period' : this.ringed === 'period' ? null : this.ringed; }, onBlur: () => { if (this.ringed === 'period') this.ringed = null; }, }
members.description: DTM-14: the period selector — a press, Enter or Space changes it to the other period; it shows no unit and is never selected.

members.name: ringPeriod
members.description:
DTM-47, as DTM-20 for the other wheels: a key that works the period makes its focus keyboard focus, however focus
first reached it — after a press and then an arrow, the ring says where focus is.

members.name: settlePeriod
members.description: DTM-46: the period wheel's rows settle on `period` over the wheel motion, and the period is taken once they have.

members.name: periodShift
members.description: DTM-46: how far the rows may be moved off their place, in rows: to the first name and to the last, and no further.

members.name: onPeriodScroll
members.description: DTM-46: a scroll moves the rows, to the first and the last name at most; when it stops, the nearer name settles.

members.name: showUnit
members.description: DTM-22: a selector focused or pressed shows its unit on the dial and is drawn as selected.

members.name: targetAngle
members.description: The angle of the pending value of the unit shown, clockwise from the top (0–359).

members.name: innerRing
members.description: On the 24-hour hour dial, 12 to 23 are on the inner ring.

members.name: setFromPoint
members.description: DTM-25: the value under a point — the nearest angle's, on the nearer ring for the 24-hour hour dial, a minute of the step.

members.name: onDialUp
members.description: DTM-25: a press or drag on the hour dial ends — the minute dial, its selector selected, and focus moved there from the hour's.

members.name: atAnchor
members.description: Whether `node` is the anchor or the opener, or inside one.

members.name: onSurfaceKeyDown
members.description: DTM-5: Escape; Tab (the modal keeps focus in, the docked one lets it leave and closes).

members.name: onNativeCancel
members.description: DTM-5: the native dialog's cancel is `escape` when an Escape key caused it, and the platform's `back` otherwise.

members.name: onSurfacePointerDown
members.description: DTM-45: a press elsewhere in the picker — anywhere but the wheel or the selector the entry is on — ends a typed entry, keeping what it read.

members.name: onDialogPointerDown
members.description: DTM-5: a press that starts and ends on a modal picker's scrim.

members.name: onSurfaceMouseDown
members.description: A press on something in the docked surface that takes no focus keeps focus where it is.

members.name: onFocusOut
members.description: DTM-5: focus moving out of a docked picker — anywhere but its anchor and opener — asks to close.

members.name: onOutsidePress
members.description: DTM-5: a press outside a docked picker and its anchor asks to close; the press also reaches what is under it.

members.name: place
members.description: DTM-2, DTM-36: a docked picker below its anchor (flipped, shifted, its height limited to the room), following it.

members.name: follow
members.description:
DTM-2: the docked container follows its anchor while it moves (scrolling, layout, the viewport) — asked by
FollowController when something can have moved, frame by frame only while something does.

members.name: following
members.default: new FollowController(this, { followed: () => [this.anchorElement], sized: () => [this.surface, this.renderRoot?.querySelector('.body')], check: this.follow, })

members.name: onWindow
members.description: DTM-1: above the on-screen keyboard; DTM-9: the layout is decided again when the window changes.

members.name: arrange
members.description:
DTM-9, DTM-34, DTM-36: the layout — vertical or horizontal as `layout` says; for auto, horizontal only when the
vertical one does not fit the window's height and the horizontal one fits its width — the actions in a row or a
column, and the whole surface scrolling as one when the header and the actions leave no room between them.

members.name: present
members.description: DTM-1, DTM-2, DTM-3: the overlay is presented and focus moves in — when it opens, not when its motion ends.

members.name: focusInitial
members.description:
DTM-3: focus to the calendar's active day (or displayed year), the hour wheel, or the selector of `unit`. The ring
shows when the picker was opened from the keyboard — from an element that showed its own keyboard focus — and not
when it was opened by a press or with the page.

members.name: returnFocus
members.description: DTM-4: focus back where it was when the picker opened (the opener, then the anchor, when that is gone).

members.name: inside
members.description: Whether `node` is in the picker, its shadow root, or the shadow root of an element it draws.

members.name: withdraw
members.description: DTM-4, DTM-35: out of the top layer (fading), the page given back, focus back where it was if it was inside.

members.name: syncOpener
members.description: DTM-37: the element that opens a docked picker says it opens a dialog, whether it is open, and which.

members.name: linkPanels
members.description: DTM-13: the entry-mode tabs control their panel (the row sets none of its own: it has no panels).

members.name: heading
members.description: DTM-10, DTM-48: the title's words and the surface's name — `label`, the instance's alone; nothing while it is empty.

members.name: renderValue
members.description:
DTM-10: the pending choice in the header — a date with its weekday, a range joined by an en dash, a date not chosen
yet as `dateLabel`, for a single value and for either end of a range: no word for start or end is drawn. Each part of
a range is an isolated run (`<bdi>`: a date as its locale writes it, or the product's word), and the two stand in
reading order around the dash: in a right-to-left layout the start is at its right.

members.name: renderEntryTabs
members.description:
DTM-13: the entry-mode tabs — two icon-only tabs that hug, the keyboard glyph for the wheels at the start and the
schedule glyph for the dial at the end. No word is drawn: `wheelsLabel` and `dialLabel` are their accessible names.

members.name: renderHeader
members.description: DTM-10: the title row (and in a modal picker with a date, the value and the divider below it).

members.name: renderCalendar
members.description: DTM-11: the calendar, in single or range mode, given the pending dates and the picker's words; no label of its own.

members.name: renderRangeDisplay
members.description:
DTM-15, DTM-42: the range display — the start's range field, an en dash and the end's, in reading order. Each field
is a button that holds its end's pending time as the locale writes it (an isolated run), "next day" after an
overnight end; no word says start or end. The one the time section sets is drawn from the selected selector's
tokens and is the pressed one; assistive technology hears "Start, 9:00 AM" in a group named rangeLabel. The error
line, while it is shown, describes the end's field (DTM-33).

members.name: periodFirst
members.description: DTM-14: whether the locale writes the period before the hour ("午前7:30"); otherwise it stands after the minute.

members.name: periodNames
members.description: The two names of the period, each in the same place: the part is as wide as the wider needs, whichever is shown.

members.name: renderPeriodWheel
members.description:
DTM-46, DTM-47: the period wheel — two rows, the name before noon above the one after, that do not run on; the
pending period on its selection container (its own, or its part of the joined band). Its control is its middle row,
a spin button of two values that takes no text: the period begins no typed entry (a typed letter sets it, DTM-47).

members.name: renderPeriodSelector
members.description:
DTM-14, DTM-47: the period selector — a spin button of two values that shows the pending period's name and changes
to the other on a press. It is drawn from the unselected selector's tokens in every state: it never takes the
selected class, which marks the unit the dial sets.

members.name: renderWheel
members.description:
DTM-18, DTM-20, DTM-43: one wheel — its rows running on past its ends, the pending value on its selection container
— whose control is its middle row: a native input that is a spin button, read-only until a number is typed into it,
showing the digits typed in place of the value.

members.name: renderWheels
members.description:
DTM-18: the hour wheel, the separator and the minute wheel, left to right — each wheel on a selection container of
its own, or, where the system joins them (wheel.selection.span, read from the cascade now), on one band. DTM-46: with
the 12-hour clock the period wheel beside them, after the minute or before the hour as the locale writes a time —
its side follows the layout direction, the digits do not (DTM-39) — on the same band where the span is joined.

members.name: renderMeasure
members.description:
DTM-12: what the other entry mode needs of the section's width, measured and never drawn — the time display beside
or above the dial for the wheels mode, the wheels for the dial mode — so that the section is as wide in the one mode
as in the other and switching does not change the picker's width. Only where the system offers both.

members.name: renderSelector
members.description: DTM-21, DTM-22: a selector — a spin button drawn from its condition.

members.name: dialNumbers
members.description: DTM-23: the numbers of a unit around the dial, clockwise from the top (two rings for the 24-hour hours).

members.name: renderDial
members.description: DTM-23 … DTM-25: the dial, its numbers, the handle over the pending value and the track to it; hidden from assistive technology.

members.name: renderTime
members.description:
DTM-12: the time section, top to bottom — the range display across its whole width, the time display (dial) and the
wheels or the dial; the time display is the row next to the dial. DTM-14: the period of a 12-hour time is a part of
the time display (the period selector) and of the wheels (the period wheel) — after the minute, or before the hour
where the locale writes it first; its side follows the layout direction while the hour, the separator and the minute
stay left to right (DTM-39). There is no row of tabs in the section.

members.name: renderActions
members.description: DTM-34: Cancel and OK, placed as a full-width Button group places a dismissive and a confirming item.

events.name: change
events.description: The person committed a choice that differs from the one before (OK, or choosing a date in a docked picker that sets a date only). `value`, `start` and `end` are already the new ones; `detail` holds them too. Fired before the `close` it causes.

events.name: close
events.description: The picker asks to be closed: `detail.reason` is `escape`, `back`, `outside`, `tab`, `focus-out`, `cancel`, `confirm` or `select`. Set `open` to false.

attributes.name: open
attributes.description: Whether the picker is shown. Open it from your field or button; set it to false when the picker fires `close`.

attributes.name: presentation
attributes.description: `modal`: a dialog over a scrim, committed by OK. `docked`: a surface below `anchor`.

attributes.name: mode
attributes.description: `date`, `time` or `date-time`: what is chosen.

attributes.name: range
attributes.description: Chooses a span (`start` … `end`) instead of one `value`: of dates, of times (the end may fall on the next day) or of both.

attributes.name: value
attributes.description: The chosen value without a range: "2026-09-17" (date), "19:30" (time, 24-hour), "2026-09-17T19:30" (date-time); empty when none.

attributes.name: start
attributes.description: The first value of the chosen span when `range` is true, in the mode's form; empty when none.

attributes.name: end
attributes.description: The last value of the chosen span when `range` is true, in the mode's form; empty while only `start` is chosen.

attributes.name: min
attributes.description: The earliest date that can be chosen (it bounds the calendar only); empty for no limit.

attributes.name: max
attributes.description: The latest date that can be chosen; empty for no limit.

attributes.name: disabled-dates
attributes.description: Dates that cannot be chosen, passed to the calendar. The `disabled-dates` attribute is a space-separated list or a JSON array.

attributes.name: today
attributes.description: The date the calendar draws as today; empty uses the device's current date.

attributes.name: first-day-of-week
attributes.description: The weekday in the calendar's first column (`first-day-of-week`).

attributes.name: locale
attributes.description: A BCP 47 tag ("en-US", "ja-JP") for names, digits, forms, the separator and the clock; empty: the nearest `lang`, then the browser's.

attributes.name: start-view
attributes.description: Whether the calendar opens on the days of a month or on the list of years (`start-view`).

attributes.name: show-adjacent-days
attributes.description: Whether the calendar shows the neighbouring months' days in its spare cells (`show-adjacent-days`).

attributes.name: hour-cycle
attributes.description: `h12` (1–12 with a period), `h23` (00–23) or `locale` (the locale's clock). Values are 24-hour in every cycle (`hour-cycle`).

attributes.name: minute-step
attributes.description: The minutes a person can choose: every minute (1), or every 5, 10, 15 or 30 (`minute-step`).

attributes.name: entry-mode
attributes.description: How the time is set when the picker opens (`entry-mode`): `wheels` or `dial`. Not HTML's `inputmode`.

attributes.name: unit
attributes.description: Dial mode: the unit the dial shows, and the selector that takes focus, when the picker opens.

attributes.name: layout
attributes.description: `vertical`, `horizontal`, or `auto`: horizontal only when the window is too short for vertical and wide enough.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Names the picker: its surface's accessible name and the start of its title row — what is being chosen ("Check-in", "Meeting time"). Required, and this instance's alone: the product's words hold none. Empty, the title row draws no words and keeps its height, and the surface has no name.

attributes.name: date-label
attributes.description: What the header shows for a date not chosen yet: a single value's, and either end's of a range (`date-label`). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ dateLabel })`); Tanrei has none: without them nothing is drawn there, and the place keeps its height.

attributes.name: start-label
attributes.description: Range: the accessible name of the start's range field and the calendar's start day's description; never drawn (`start-label`). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ startLabel })`); Tanrei has none: without them the field and the day say nothing of it.

attributes.name: end-label
attributes.description: Range: the accessible name of the end's range field and the calendar's end day's description; never drawn (`end-label`). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ endLabel })`); Tanrei has none: without them the field and the day say nothing of it.

attributes.name: confirm-label
attributes.description: OK's label (`confirm-label`). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ confirmLabel })`); Tanrei has none: without them an icon-only Button with the check glyph, unnamed.

attributes.name: cancel-label
attributes.description: Cancel's label (`cancel-label`). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ cancelLabel })`); Tanrei has none: without them an icon-only Button with the close glyph, unnamed.

attributes.name: previous-month-label
attributes.description: Passed to the calendar (`previous-month-label`). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ previousMonthLabel })`); Tanrei has none: without them the button is drawn and works, unnamed.

attributes.name: next-month-label
attributes.description: Passed to the calendar (`next-month-label`). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ nextMonthLabel })`); Tanrei has none: without them the button is drawn and works, unnamed.

attributes.name: year-view-label
attributes.description: Passed to the calendar (`year-view-label`). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ yearViewLabel })`); Tanrei has none: without them the view toggle has no description.

attributes.name: today-label
attributes.description: Passed to the calendar (`today-label`). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ todayLabel })`); Tanrei has none: without them the locale's own word for the present day, from the browser.

attributes.name: hour-label
attributes.description: The accessible name of the hour wheel and the hour selector (`hour-label`). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ hourLabel })`); Tanrei has none: without them the locale's own name for the hour, from the browser.

attributes.name: minute-label
attributes.description: The accessible name of the minute wheel and the minute selector (`minute-label`). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ minuteLabel })`); Tanrei has none: without them the locale's own name for the minute, from the browser.

attributes.name: wheels-label
attributes.description: The accessible name of the entry-mode tab that shows the wheels, which draws the keyboard glyph alone (`wheels-label`). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ wheelsLabel })`); Tanrei has none: without them the tab is drawn and works, unnamed.

attributes.name: dial-label
attributes.description: The accessible name of the entry-mode tab that shows the dial, which draws the schedule glyph alone (`dial-label`). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ dialLabel })`); Tanrei has none: without them the tab is drawn and works, unnamed.

attributes.name: entry-mode-label
attributes.description: The accessible name of the row of entry-mode tabs (`entry-mode-label`). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ entryModeLabel })`); Tanrei has none: without them the row of tabs has no name.

attributes.name: period-label
attributes.description: The accessible name of the period — the period wheel or the period selector, a spin button (`period-label`). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ periodLabel })`); Tanrei has none: without them the locale's own name for the day period, from the browser.

attributes.name: range-label
attributes.description: The accessible name of the range display, the group of the two range fields (`range-label`). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ rangeLabel })`); Tanrei has none: without them the group has no name.

attributes.name: next-day-label
attributes.description: Mode time with a range: added after the end's time, in its range field and its accessible name, while it falls on the next day (`next-day-label`). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ nextDayLabel })`); Tanrei has none: without them "+1" in the locale's digits.

attributes.name: range-error-text
attributes.description: Mode date-time with a range: the error line while the end is before the start (`range-error-text`). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ rangeErrorText })`); Tanrei has none: without them the line draws no words and keeps its height; OK is still disabled.

attributes.name: anchor
attributes.description: Docked: the id of the element the surface is placed against (as the menu's `anchor`), in the picker's own document or shadow root.

attributes.name: opener
attributes.description: Docked: the id of the element that opens the picker, when it is not the anchor (a text field's picker button). It gets `aria-haspopup`, `aria-controls` and `aria-expanded`.

attributes.name: inline
attributes.description: For tests and documentation: draws the open surface in place (DTM-1's verify), without the overlay's behaviour.

declarations.description:
Presents what is known about one thing as named facts — a quiet term and the value that answers it — with the terms in one column beside their values, above them, or under a large figure. An order, a file, an account, a component; the few numbers a screen opens with. It is laid out by its own width and is never a control. Contract: specs/description-list.spec.json. The element has **no shadow root**: it is the box around the product's own native `
`, which stays in the document and is never given a role — the description list a screen reader, a crawler and a page without script meet is the browser's own. ```html
Category
Actions
Owners
Aiko Tanaka
Samir Haddad
Status
 ``` A fact is a `
` around one `
` and its `
`s. The term and each value hold text or any view of the product's; a fact may have several values, and a value may be empty. A `
` without groups — `
` and `
` as its children, as some Markdown renderers write it — is drawn in one column, inline or stacked; `columns` and the stat layout need the groups. Everything drawn is `@tanrei/web/description-list.css` — every value a `--tanrei-comp-description-list-*` token — which draws the list before and without this script; the element adds the same sheet to the root it is connected to, so it also works inside another component's shadow root. The script adds the one thing a stylesheet cannot say: an inline list whose values would be left less than `comp.description-list.column.min-width` draws its terms above their values. The element measures the widest term and writes that width as a container query of the list, so the browser itself draws the other form as the list is resized. Without the script such a list wraps its terms instead. The list takes no input and emits no event.
declarations.name: TanreiDescriptionList

slots.description: The native `<dl>`: one `<div>` per fact around a `<dt>` and its `<dd>`s. It is a child in the document, not a slotted node: the element has no shadow root.

members.name: layout
members.description:
How a fact is drawn. `inline`: the term beside its value, every term in one column as wide as the widest term; the
list draws its terms above their values by itself while it is too narrow for that. `stacked`: the term above its
value, for long values or long terms, and for facts in several columns. `stat`: the value first, as a large
figure, with the term under it as its label.

members.name: columns
members.description: The most columns of facts the list draws in the stacked and stat layouts; it draws fewer while it is too narrow for that many, and never more than it has facts. An inline list is one column.

members.name: density
members.description: How close the facts are and how large their text is: regular for facts a person reads, compact for facts a person scans. A design system may add values.

members.name: separation
members.description: How a fact is told from the fact below it: `divider` is one hairline, `gap` empty space and no line; `auto` takes `comp.description-list.separation`, the design system's answer.

members.name: owners
members.description:
One observer of sizes for every list of the page, so that the lists that change size in one frame — every list of
a page when it is first laid out, or when a reader changes the text size — are reported, and measured, together.

members.name: due
members.description: The lists to read in this turn (`read`), and those to read in the next frame (`resized`) with the frame asked for.

members.name: list
members.description: The list the box holds now, and the one the observer of sizes watches.

members.name: watch
members.description: The list whose size is watched: the one the box holds, or none.

members.name: readDensity
members.description:
DSL-23: a density the core does not have was added by a design system — its rules are added to the root, falling
back to the default's tokens — or is unknown to the active one, which a debug build says.

members.name: readColumns
members.description: DSL-7: the columns the list may draw. One for a number that is less than one or not whole, and for an inline list.

members.name: read
members.description:
Reads the list the box holds and writes what follows from it: the separation where the browser cannot query it,
and the width under which an inline list stacks. Called when a property changes, when the list's content does
(DSL-16) and when a face arrives; it writes only what differs, so it settles.

Every list that asks in one turn is read in ONE microtask after it (`readTogether`), still in the task that drew
them and before any frame: a list that measured its widest term in its own update had the page styled and laid
out for itself, twice (fifty lists appended at once: 153 style passes and 103 layouts).

members.name: readTogether
members.description:
`read()` for every box of a turn: each finds its list and is laid out for measuring; then everything is read —
one style pass and one layout for them all; then everything is written.

members.name: check
members.description: What a debug build says about a list it still draws (DSL-7, DSL-11).

members.name: hold
members.description:
DSL-3, DSL-4: for as long as it is held, an inline list is laid out in its two columns with no term wrapped
(`data-measuring`), whatever its width, so that the widest term can be read from the layout itself. Returns
whether this call began it (and `release()` ends it). Nothing is painted in between.

members.name: measure
members.description:
DSL-3, DSL-4: the width under which this list's values would be left less than `column.min-width` — the widest
term set on one line, the space between the columns and that least width — or null where the list is not inline
or is not drawn. Read while the list is held (`hold()`); it writes nothing.

members.name: resized
members.description:
Lists changed size: their text may have (a reader's text size, a design system switched above them, a face), and
with it the widest term. They are measured again here — all held, then all read, one layout for them all — and a
width that differs is written in the next frame: a write inside the observer's own callback would change the size
it observes and be reported as a loop. Resizing a list alone changes no term, so nothing is written and no frame
is asked for.

attributes.name: layout
attributes.description:
How a fact is drawn. `inline`: the term beside its value, every term in one column as wide as the widest term; the
list draws its terms above their values by itself while it is too narrow for that. `stacked`: the term above its
value, for long values or long terms, and for facts in several columns. `stat`: the value first, as a large
figure, with the term under it as its label.

attributes.name: columns
attributes.description: The most columns of facts the list draws in the stacked and stat layouts; it draws fewer while it is too narrow for that many, and never more than it has facts. An inline list is one column.

attributes.name: density
attributes.description: How close the facts are and how large their text is: regular for facts a person reads, compact for facts a person scans. A design system may add values.

attributes.name: separation
attributes.description: How a fact is told from the fact below it: `divider` is one hairline, `gap` empty space and no line; `auto` takes `comp.description-list.separation`, the design system's answer.

declarations.default: css` :host { display: contents; } /* DLG-17: the resolved compact.window-width, which the script matches the window against. */ .probe { position: fixed; inset-block-start: 0; inset-inline-start: 0; inline-size: ${t('compact-window-width')}; block-size: 0; visibility: hidden; pointer-events: none; } /* DLG-1, DLG-7: a native modal <dialog> in the top layer, centred in the window above the keyboard, as wide as its widest part (the actions' row at their own widths among them, --_row) between its bounds and never wider or taller than the window less the margins; its color, elevation and corners (eased by the smoothing). None of the browser's dialog box. */ dialog { box-sizing: border-box; position: fixed; inset: 0 0 var(--_keyboard, 0px) 0; margin: auto; inline-size: fit-content; min-inline-size: min(max(${t('container-min-width')}, calc(var(--_row, 0px) + 2 * ${t('container-padding')})), ${t('container-max-width')}, ${unsafeCSS(INLINE_ROOM)}); max-inline-size: min(${t('container-max-width')}, ${unsafeCSS(INLINE_ROOM)}); block-size: fit-content; max-block-size: ${unsafeCSS(BLOCK_ROOM)}; border: 0; padding: ${t('container-padding')}; overflow: visible; flex-direction: column; background: ${t('container-color')}; box-shadow: ${t('container-elevation')}; ${unsafeCSS(cornerRadius('--tanrei-comp-dialog-container-shape'))} color: ${t('content-color')}; text-align: start; outline: none; /* DLG-13, DLG-18: out, it fades over the exit motion — kept in the top layer and displayed until it has. */ opacity: 0; transition-property: opacity, scale, translate, display, overlay; transition-duration: ${t('motion-exit-duration')}; transition-timing-function: ${t('motion-exit-easing')}; transition-behavior: allow-discrete; } /* DLG-17: a compact window: at the bottom of the safe area, the margin above its bottom edge (or the keyboard) and from its sides, as wide as the window less those margins up to max-width, centred between the sides; all four corners stay the container's. */ dialog.compact { inline-size: min(${t('container-max-width')}, ${unsafeCSS(INLINE_ROOM)}); min-inline-size: 0; margin-block: auto calc(${t('container-margin')} + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)); } /* DLG-18: out at the bottom, it also sinks by enter-offset. */ dialog.compact:not([open]) { translate: 0 ${t('motion-enter-offset')}; } dialog[open] { display: flex; opacity: 1; /* DLG-13: in, centred, it fades in and grows about its centre from enter-scale over the enter motion; DLG-18: at the bottom it rises by enter-offset instead, without growing. */ transition-duration: ${t('motion-enter-duration')}; transition-timing-function: ${t('motion-enter-easing')}; } @starting-style { dialog[open] { opacity: 0; declarations.description:
Stops a person for a decision or a few details that the task cannot go on without, in a surface that dims and blocks
everything behind it and always offers at least one answer, until one is chosen or the dialog is dismissed.

Contract: specs/dialog.spec.json. A native `<dialog>` in the shadow root, opened with `showModal()` while `open` is
true: in the top layer over `::backdrop` (the scrim, `comp.dialog.scrim.color`), with everything else inert and the page
held from scrolling. Focus goes to the slotted element marked `autofocus`, or to the dialog itself, stays inside it
(Tab wraps), and returns where it was when the dialog closes. It is an operated modal overlay.
Centred in the window, or at the bottom of a window narrower than `comp.dialog.compact.window-width` (DLG-17).

While `closedby` is not `none`, Escape, the platform's back and a press on the scrim fire `cancel`, which is
cancelable: the dialog then closes itself unless you call `preventDefault()`, as a native `<dialog>` does. Actions
never close it: close it from their handlers with `open = false`. `close` follows every close.

The actions are `<tanrei-button slot="actions">` children, each marked `confirming` or `dismissive`, placed as a
full-width button group places them: dismissive at the start and confirming at the end of a row, confirming on top of
a column when they do not fit in a row. Focus and assistive technology follow that order. A Button without a
`variant` attribute takes the dialog's (`comp.dialog.actions.variant`, tonal in the default system).

Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-dialog-*` tokens.

declarations.description:
Separates groups of content in a list, a layout or a toolbar with a thin line.

Contract: specs/divider.spec.json. The line's color, thickness, inset and the lengths of its dots, dashes and wave are
`--tanrei-comp-divider-*` tokens; one divider may be given a thickness of its own (`thickness`, DIV-16), which also
scales the pattern lengths it takes from tokens, so a thicker dotted, dashed or wavy line keeps its proportions. The divider has no margin of its own (DIV-2): put the space around it in the layout
that places it. It spans its container's inline size when horizontal (in block flow, a flex column or a grid) and its
container's block size when vertical (in a flex row or a grid, which stretch it; elsewhere give it a block size).

Not an `<hr>`: an hr is horizontal only and always a separator. Decorative (the default), the host is
`aria-hidden="true"`; with `decorative="false"` (or the property set to false) it is `role="separator"` with its
`aria-orientation`. It is never focusable.
declarations.name: TanreiDivider

cssParts.description: The drawn line (the inset stretch is outside it): a bordered box for solid, dotted and dashed, an SVG for wavy.
cssParts.name: line

members.name: orientation
members.description: Horizontal spans the container's width; vertical spans its height.

members.name: inset
members.description: Shortens the line by `insetLength` (else `comp.divider.line.inset`) at its start (`start`) or at both ends (`both`).

members.name: lineStyle
members.description: Solid, dotted, dashed or wavy (`line-style`).

members.name: lineCap
members.description: `butt` ends square at the length; `round` ends in a half-disc inside it (`line-cap`). Shows only on a line thicker than a hairline.

members.name: insetLength
members.description: The inset's length in CSS px while `inset` is `start` or `both` (`inset-length`); null takes `comp.divider.line.inset`.

members.name: thickness
members.description:
How thick this divider's line is, in CSS px; null takes `comp.divider.line.thickness`. It stands in for the token
wherever the line's thickness is read — the line, a dot's side, a dash's width and least length, the wave's stroke,
a round cap's diameter and the divider's own size across its axis — and the pattern lengths that come from tokens
(not from `dash-length`, `gap`, `amplitude` or `wavelength`) are scaled by it over the token, so the pattern keeps
its proportions (DIV-16). The inset is not scaled. 0, a negative number or a value that is not a number takes the token.

members.name: dashLength
members.description: One dash's length in CSS px, round caps included (`dash-length`); null takes `comp.divider.line.dash.length`. Dashed only.

members.name: gap
members.description: The least space between two dots or dashes in CSS px; null takes `comp.divider.line.dot.gap` / `comp.divider.line.dash.gap`. Dotted and dashed only.

members.name: amplitude
members.description: A wave's crest from the midline to the stroke's center in CSS px; null takes `comp.divider.line.wave.amplitude`. Wavy only.

members.name: wavelength
members.description: One wave (a crest and a trough) in CSS px, before it is fitted to the line; null takes `comp.divider.line.wave.wavelength`. Wavy only.

members.name: decorative
members.description: Hidden from assistive technology. Set to false (`decorative="false"`) only when the grouping is meaningful: the divider is then a separator.

members.name: given
members.description:
The lengths this divider was given, as `--_given-*` on the host, after the static styles (DIV-14) — a sheet of its
own, made when a length is first given: a divider given none, which nearly every one is, shares the static styles
and has no sheet.

members.name: resize$
members.description: A pattern is laid out from the line's length, so a patterned divider follows its own size; a solid line follows nothing.

members.name: drawnStyle
members.description: The style drawn: an unknown one is solid (DIV-7).

members.name: draws
members.description: Whether the current style and inset draw a length prop; one that is not drawn is ignored and not reported (DIV-14).

members.name: givenThickness
members.description: The valid thickness this divider was given, or null (DIV-14).

members.name: declarations
members.description: The `--_given-*` declarations of the lengths given, and the scale of the token pattern lengths (DIV-16).

members.name: scale
members.description:
DIV-16: the pattern lengths taken from tokens are scaled by the thickness given over the token's. The quotient of
two lengths is not something CSS can compute in every engine, so it is taken here, from the token as the probe
resolves it, and handed to the styles as a number. A solid line has no pattern (and no probe).

members.name: measure
members.description: The lengths a pattern is laid out from, resolved in CSS px, and the host's length and cross size.

members.name: lay
members.description: Lays the current style's pattern out; a resize calls it again, without a render.

members.name: layDashes
members.description:
DIV-10, DIV-11, DIV-13: the dots or dashes over the drawn stretch, as the line's mask. As many as fit at least the
gap apart, the first at the start and the last at the end, every gap widened alike; one that fits alone is centered
and no longer than the stretch. A round cap is drawn inside each dash's length. The pattern is symmetric, so it
needs nothing for RTL (DIV-4).

members.name: layWave
members.description:
DIV-12, DIV-13: the wave's path, in the host's CSS px, laid out along the logical start (CSS mirrors it in RTL,
DIV-4). Circular arcs of half the fitted wavelength each, alternating sides of the midline and meeting on it; the
first rises toward the top (horizontal) or the left (vertical). A round cap lies inside the length: the arcs are laid
out over the drawn stretch less half the thickness at each end.

attributes.name: orientation
attributes.description: Horizontal spans the container's width; vertical spans its height.

attributes.name: inset
attributes.description: Shortens the line by `insetLength` (else `comp.divider.line.inset`) at its start (`start`) or at both ends (`both`).

attributes.name: line-style
attributes.description: Solid, dotted, dashed or wavy (`line-style`).

attributes.name: line-cap

members.name: label

members.name: description

members.name: placeholder
members.description: A hint drawn while the value is empty. Never the name. A multi-line input is as tall as the placeholder's lines, within `min-rows` and `max-rows`.

members.name: multiline
members.description: False: one line that scrolls sideways inside itself. True: lines that wrap, and a height that follows them between `min-rows` and `max-rows`, changed with a motion.

members.name: minRows
members.description: The fewest lines a multi-line input is tall (`min-rows`). Anything below 1 is 1.

members.name: maxRows
members.description: The most lines a multi-line input is tall (`max-rows`); beyond it the text scrolls inside. 0 is no limit; one below `min-rows` is `min-rows`.

members.name: enterKey
members.description: What Enter does on a hardware keyboard in a multi-line input (`enter-key`). `line-break`: it begins a new line. `action`: it emits `action` and inserts nothing, and Shift+Enter begins a new line. Under both, Ctrl+Enter and Command+Enter emit `action`. A single-line input ignores it: its Enter always emits `action`. A value it does not know behaves as `line-break`.

members.name: required

members.name: disabled
members.description: Not focusable and not editable; the text and the placeholder read as disabled content. The disabled look of the box is its holder's.

members.name: readOnly

members.name: autocomplete

members.name: name

members.name: says

members.name: shownValue
members.description:
The value as the native element holds it: a single-line element keeps no line break and a text area writes every
line break as one character. The element's own value is not changed for it (ETI-25: the line breaks are there
again when `multiline` returns).

members.name: rows
members.description: The number of lines the input shows, or is on its way to show: what the last `rowschange` carried. 1 for a single-line input. Read-only.

members.name: selectionStart
members.description: Where the selection begins, as the native element's `selectionStart`: the caret's place where nothing is selected.

members.name: selectionEnd
members.description: Where the selection ends, as the native element's `selectionEnd`.

members.name: setSelectionRange
members.description: Sets the selection, as the native element's `setSelectionRange()`.

members.name: setRangeText
members.description:
Replaces a range of the text — the selection, where no range is given — as the native element's `setRangeText()`:
what an action of the holder's inserts at the caret. The value is then the product's: no `input` is emitted.

members.name: select
members.description: Selects the whole value, as the native element's `select()`.

members.name: focusAt
members.description:
ETI-12: gives the input focus and places the caret at the point of its text nearest to a point of the window
(`clientX`, `clientY`) — what a holder calls for a press on its own box outside its other controls. Where the
browser cannot say which character stands at a point, the caret goes to the start of the text for a point above
or before it and to its end otherwise. Does nothing while disabled.

members.name: form
members.description: The form it belongs to, if any: none in the shadow root of a holder.

members.name: validity
members.description: The native constraint validity: `valueMissing` while it is required and empty.

members.name: sync
members.description: ETI-19: what it submits and what it is restored from, and a missing value while it is required and empty.

members.name: take
members.description: ETI-2: the person gave the native element this text; it is the value.

members.name: onInput
members.description:
ETI-2: the person changed the value. The native `input` event is composed, so it leaves the shadow root by itself,
after the element has taken the new value. ETI-4: during a composition the value follows the element and nothing
is written back.

members.name: onNativeChange
members.description: The browser's own `change` is not the input's (ETI-3 decides when a value is committed).

members.name: onFocusOut
members.description: ETI-3: focus left with a changed value — `change`, once.

members.name: commit
members.description: ETI-3: `change` when the value differs from the one last committed. Never while disabled or read-only (ETI-15, ETI-16), and never during a composition (ETI-4).

members.name: onCompositionEnd
members.description: ETI-4: where the platform reports the committing Enter only after the composition has ended, it is still the composition's.

members.name: onKey
members.description:
ETI-6, ETI-21: a key pressed in the input, read where it has passed every element around it — at the window, the
last place it reaches — so that whatever holds the input has seen it first; one a holder cancelled is not read.
The input gives a meaning to Enter alone: Tab moves focus as the platform has it, and Escape does nothing.

members.name: act
members.description: ETI-6: the change it causes, then `action` with the value — and nothing else: the value, the selection and the focus stay. Answers whether the action was let through.

members.name: onHostPointerDown
members.description: ETI-9: while a pointer or a touch is held down in the text its height changes at once.

members.name: onHostMouseDown
members.description:
ETI-12: a press in the hit area beyond the lines — whose target is the host itself — is a press on the text: focus,
and the caret at the nearest point. No pressed state and no feedback: a press on a place to type is not an action.
The press would give the native element focus by itself (the shadow root delegates it) and leave the caret where
it last stood: its default is prevented and the caret is placed here.

members.name: adopt
members.description:
ETI-27: the platform's own text element that the product wrote as a child is the control until the element is
defined. Now its text is the first value where `value` was not given, and it is hidden and disabled, so that the
form submits the input alone.

members.name: watch
members.description: ETI-9: a width, a text size or a text style that changed is a height that changes at once; so is being shown again.

declarations.description:
What stands in the place of content that is not there — a search with no results, a list nobody has added to, a page
before its first item: what is missing, why or what to do, and the action that does it. Quiet and flat: no fill, no
edge, no elevation.

Contract: specs/empty-state.spec.json. `<tanrei-empty-state headline="No projects yet">…</tanrei-empty-state>`: the
description is the element's own content (text, with the product's links), the title is the `headline` attribute or
the `title` slot, a glyph of the icon set or a picture of the product's own goes in the `media` slot, and the
product's Buttons or links in the `actions` slot. Every visual value is a `--tanrei-comp-empty-state-*` token.

It is content, read where it stands: no role, no name, no focus, no state. With `live` it is announced once, politely,
when it is shown after its page was presented and when its title or description changes — for an empty place that
answers what the person just did (a search, a filter). It is never an alert.

Every word it draws or exposes is the product's: the element has none of its own.

`title` is the `headline` property and attribute, because HTML's global `title` would show a tooltip over the block.
The element neither shows nor hides itself: the product puts it there and takes it away.

members.name: announce
members.description:
EMP-9: announced once — through the polite region in the shadow root, a frame after it was emptied, so that a text
equal to the last one is announced again. Nothing is announced while it is not live or says nothing. The host has
no live role: its own content is not read a second time.

the title or the description is announced (EMP-9) — what changes inside the media or an action is not one.

declarations.description:
Where the list goes (FBM-13, FBM-22): its bottom edge `offset` above the toggle's top edge, its end edge on the
toggle's end edge (the left one in right-to-left), kept inside the viewport's inline extent. The answer is the fixed
box's insets from the viewport's edges, each measured from the edge the list is held by — its bottom, and the
toggle's end edge (or the viewport's edge the list would cross) — so the list's own size never enters a length: a
list that changes size after it was placed (its label font arriving, a label changing) keeps its bottom and end edges
where they were put, in the same layout, with no frame in between. The size only decides which edge holds it.

Opens a short list of related actions from a floating action button, which turns into the list's close button while
they show.

Contract: specs/fab-menu.spec.json. The toggle is a native `<button>` in the shadow root, drawn as a collapsed main
action button of the variant and size: it says it opens a menu (`aria-haspopup`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`), and while open takes the
variant's open look, round corners and the close glyph. The items are `<tanrei-fab-menu-item>` children, presented as
a column above the toggle in a manual popover — the top layer, so nothing clips them and no content moves — with role
`menu`. The FAB menu is an operated overlay that is not modal: it moves focus to the first item when it
opens (to the last, the one nearest the toggle, when Up Arrow opened it) and back to the toggle when it closes, never
traps focus and draws no scrim. It never opens or closes itself: set `open` from `toggle`, and to false from `close`.

Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-fab-menu-*` tokens: per variant three looks (the closed toggle, the open
toggle, the items), each in every state. How a press is answered and how keyboard focus is drawn are the system's
choices of kind (`--tanrei-sys-behavior-*`), and how far corners ease is its amount.

The element does not position itself (FBM-12): it is inline, at the toggle's size, and the page places it — as a main action button.
The `inline` attribute, for tests and documentation, draws the open items in place above the toggle instead: with
their elevation, without the top layer, open motion, focus on opening or light dismiss (FBM-13).

declarations.description:
Names a set of controls that answer one question — checkboxes, switches, or fields that belong together — with a
label that can say the set is required or optional, a description, and one error for the set, and lays the controls
out in a column or a row. It frames the set and never selects, moves focus or holds a value.

Contract: specs/field-group.spec.json. `<tanrei-field-group label="Notify me by"><tanrei-checkbox label="Email">
</tanrei-checkbox>…</tanrei-field-group>`: the controls are the elements of the default slot. They stay in the
product's light DOM, so each keeps its place in a `<form>`, its `name` and `value` and its events; the group is not
form-associated, holds no value and emits no event. Every visual value is a `--tanrei-comp-field-group-*` token.

The shadow root holds a `<fieldset>` with a `<legend>` around the slot, so the controls are inside the group the
label names. A group has neither a required nor an invalid state: its description is `supporting-text`, then
`error-text` while `error` is true, then the requirement in words (`required-text`, `optional-text`); `error` puts
each checkbox it holds in the checkbox's own error condition and gives it the error text as its description. A
switch, which has no error condition, stays as it is drawn, and a field keeps the error the product gave it.
`disabled` disables every control. The group gives these through the composed `tanrei-field-connect` event a control
asks with (`src/primitives/field.ts`), or as attributes on any other element, and takes back exactly what it gave.

It answers no press and no key and adds no stop to the focus order.

`kind="radio-group"` (FGR-25) makes the same element the radio group of the radio buttons it holds — a set of radio
buttons of one `name`, written by hand, or the radio buttons of the `<tanrei-radio-group>` built around it: the
`<fieldset>` carries the radio group's role with `aria-required` while the set is required, `aria-invalid` while
`error` is true and `aria-orientation`, and `required-text` is left out of its description, because the state says
it. Nothing that is drawn changes, and the group still holds no value, moves no focus and handles no key: selection,
the arrow keys and the one tab stop stay the radio buttons' own group's.

declarations.name: styles
declarations.default: css` /* FLD-1: a block as wide as its layout gives it, as tall as its rows and its control together. */ :host { display: block; } :host([hidden]) { display: none; } /* The positioning container of the announcer, which is drawn nowhere. */ .frame { position: relative; min-inline-size: 0; } /* FLD-8, FLD-13, FLD-14: the current color of every part, from the tokens of the look and the state the field is in. Focused is never set while disabled, so each later rule wins over the ones before it. */ ${frameColors( PREFIX, 'standard', { rest: '.frame', error: '.frame[data-error]', focused: '.frame[data-focused]', focusedError: '.frame[data-focused][data-error]', disabled: '.frame[data-disabled]', disabledError: '.frame[data-disabled][data-error]', }, [...FRAME_PARTS, 'error-text', 'counter', 'value-text'], null, // FLD-31: the error text has one color, whichever look the frame is in — it is drawn only in error. ['error-text'], )} /* FLD-2 … FLD-7, FLD-9, FLD-13, FLD-16, FLD-17, FLD-21: the frame, from the field's tokens. */ ${frameStyles({ prefix: PREFIX, glyph: true, disabled: '.frame[data-disabled]' })} /* FLD-7, FLD-26, FLD-27, FLD-31: the supporting row — its texts from its start, the count at the end of its first line, at least counter.gap apart — supporting-text.gap below the control. The texts are one column that takes the room beside the count: the help, and while the field is in error the error text — in the help's place, which the element then does not render (error-text.placement replace), or error-text.gap below it (append); where there is no help the error text is the column's first line. The row starts and ends where the control says its content does (--_inset-start / --_inset-end, which the element writes from what the control said; a control that says nothing has the row at the field's edges). The texts wrap; the count stays whole on one line, in figures of one width, in the supporting text's style and its own color, and is never announced: the control says its own count. Nothing here moves by itself: the error text comes and goes with the layout, at once (FLD-31). */ .supporting { display: flex; align-items: flex-start; column-gap: var(--tanrei-comp-field-counter-gap); min-inline-size: 0; margin-block-start: var(--tanrei-comp-field-supporting-text-gap); padding-inline: var(--_inset-start, 0px) var(--_inset-end, 0px); } .texts { display: flex; flex: 1 1 auto; flex-direction: column; row-gap: var(--tanrei-comp-field-error-text-gap); min-inline-size: 0; } .texts > .supporting-text { margin-block-start: 0; } /* FLD-31: the error text, in the supporting text's style and the error text's own color, wrapping and never cut. */ .error-text { min-inline-size: 0; overflow-wrap: break-word; font: var(--tanrei-comp-field-supporting-text-typescale-font); letter-spacing: var(--tanrei-comp-field-supporting-text-typescale-letter-spacing); color: var(--_frame-error-text); transition: color var(--tanrei-comp-field-motion-state-duration) var(--tanrei-comp-field-motion-state-easing); } /* FLD-21: the error text is a run of its own, in the direction of its first strong character, as the help is. */ ${productText('.error-text', { align: 'start' })} .counter { flex: none; align-self: flex-start; margin-inline-start: auto; font: var(--tanrei-comp-field-supporting-text-typescale-font); letter-spacing: var(--tanrei-comp-field-supporting-text-typescale-letter-spacing); color: var(--_frame-counter); white-space: nowrap; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; transition: color var(--tanrei-comp-field-motion-state-duration) var(--tanrei-comp-field-motion-state-easing); } /* FLD-21: the count is a run of its own, in the direction of its first strong character, as wide as itself. */ ${productText('.counter')} @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .counter, .error-text { transition: none !important; } } /* FLD-17: under forced colors the count and the error text are in the platform's text color, as the help is: the two texts are then told apart by their words and their order, the help first. */ @media (forced-colors: active) { .counter, .error-text { color: CanvasText; } .frame[data-disabled] :is(.counter, .error-text) { color: GrayText; } } /* FLD-29: the value text at the end edge of the label row, on the baseline of the label's first line, at least value-text.gap from the label with its mark. The row and the text are the two items of a line that wraps: the row takes the room the text leaves and is never given less than half of the line — where the two would not fit so, the text takes a line of its own after the row, from the start edge, and wraps there where it must. label.gap is then below the line, whichever of the two ends it. The row's baseline is the label's, with a glyph before it too. */ .label-line { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: baseline; column-gap: var(--tanrei-comp-field-value-text-gap); min-inline-size: 0; margin-block-end: var(--tanrei-comp-field-label-gap); } .label-line > .label-row { flex: 1 1 0; min-inline-size: 50%; margin-block-end: 0; } .label-line > .label-row > .label { align-self: baseline; } .value-text { flex: 0 1 auto; min-inline-size: 0; overflow-wrap: anywhere; font: var(--tanrei-comp-field-value-text-typescale-font); letter-spacing: var(--tanrei-comp-field-value-text-typescale-letter-spacing); color: var(--_frame-value-text); cursor: default; transition: color var(--tanrei-comp-field-motion-state-duration) var(--tanrei-comp-field-motion-state-easing); } /* FLD-21: the value text is a run of its own — isolated, in the direction of its first strong character (data-own-direction, which the element sets where the text has one) and in the layout's where it has none: a number, or a range's two values, each isolated already, in reading order.
