declarations.description:
Frames one control with what a form gives every field: a label above it that can say the control is required or
optional, a line of help, and the reason a value was refused, each tied to the control for assistive technology. It
is a frame, never a control.

Contract: specs/field.spec.json. `<tanrei-field label="Volume"><tanrei-slider></tanrei-slider></tanrei-field>`: the
control is the one element in the default slot. It stays in the product's light DOM, so it keeps its place in a
`<form>`, its `name` and `value`, its events and its styles; the field is not form-associated, holds no value and
emits no event. Every visual value is a `--tanrei-comp-field-*` token.

The label names the control; the help describes it, with the error text after it while the field is in error and
`optional-text` after that while the control is optional. They are given as values, because an id cannot be referenced across a shadow root: a Tanrei
control asks for them (the composed `tanrei-field-connect` event; `src/primitives/field.ts`) and writes them on the
element that carries its semantics, its own `label` winning; any other element receives `aria-label` (only where it
has no name of its own), `aria-description`, `aria-invalid`, `aria-required` and, where it has the property,
`disabled`. The field takes back exactly what it gave when the element leaves the slot.

`requirement="required"` exposes the control as required and draws the required mark beside the label — a small
filled tag, an asterisk or nothing, as the design system or `required-mark` says; `requirement="optional"` draws the
optional tag. Neither validates: `error` is the product's to set, and `error-text` says what is wrong in words. While
the field is in error the error text takes the help's place, so a form in error is no taller than at rest; a design
system whose `--tanrei-comp-field-error-text-placement` is `append` keeps the help and draws the error text below
it. A disabled field draws its requirement tag as a tag inside something disabled. An error that appears while
focus is inside the field is announced once, politely — the error text alone, never the help again.

A press on the label moves focus to the control and never operates it; a press on the help, the error or the count
does nothing. A control that names itself (a checkbox with its own label) takes a field with an empty `label`, which
then adds help and an error only. A control that is a field already — a composed field such as
`<tanrei-text-field>`, which is this element around `<tanrei-text-input>`, or anything with a `supportingText` of its
own — needs no field.

A control may say of itself what only it knows, through the same connection (`src/primitives/field.ts`): that it
draws the label itself, floating in its own box — the field then draws no label row and gives the control the name,
whether it is hidden, and an asterisk or none for a required one (FLD-25); how far its content is inset — the
supporting row starts and ends there (FLD-26); and that it refused what was entered, with its words — the field is
then in its error condition and shows them as its error text (FLD-28); and that it is drawn focused though focus is elsewhere — a
combobox or a select for as long as its list is open — so that the field's rows are drawn focused with it (FLD-13).
`count-text` is a count about the control's value as it is to
be drawn ("12/40"), at the end of the supporting row: the field draws it, never counts, and keeps it from assistive
technology, which hears the count from the control (FLD-27). `value-text` is the control's present value in words
("40 %"), at the end of the label row, for a control whose value cannot be read from the control itself (a slider):
the field draws it, never reads or formats a value, and keeps it from assistive technology, which hears the value
from the control (FLD-29, FLD-30).

never a heading; an element with `data-part="title"` in the figure is drawn in its place. It is the figure's

members.description: The caption: the text below the frame that says what is shown. A `<figcaption>` written in the figure is drawn in its place. The figure's name where there is no title, and its description where there is one.

members.description: The accessible name of a figure that draws neither a title nor a caption. Never drawn; ignored where a title or a caption is given.

members.name: variant
members.description: How the stage is set apart: `outlined` is the surface inside one hairline, `filled` a quiet tone and no edge, `plain` no fill, no edge, no padding and no line. A design system may add values.

members.description: Whether the stage is padded inside the frame. False (the `flush` attribute) lets a picture, a chart or a map reach the frame's edges, clipped by its corners. The plain look is never padded.

members.description: How the parts inside the frame are told apart: `divider` draws a line under the header and above the attachment, `gap` draws none and stands the attachment inside the frame; `auto` takes `comp.figure.separation`, the design system's answer.

part with `slot` go to that part, everything else is the stage — and children added later go the same way.

members.name: headerPart
members.description: The header's title or actions, written where the frame has none: the title first, the actions after it.

members.name: readText

a title or a caption of the product's own, that one is drawn and the property ignored.

members.name: readName

has no title — written too: a browser does not name a figure by its `<figcaption>` in the tree it gives assistive
technology — unless the product wrote a label on the figure itself, which a labelling element would take the
place of; `label` where it draws neither; and a figure with none of the three has no name, which a debug build
says.

members.name: give
members.description: Writes `wanted` on `element`, leaving alone what the product wrote there itself, and takes off only what `own` says this element wrote.

members.name: watch
members.description: The stage and what stands in it are what the sizes are read from (FIG-5): content can outgrow a stage that stays as it is.

members.name: measure

FIG-6: while the stage scrolls sideways it is one stop in the focus order and a group with the figure's name, and

attributes of the stage alone.

declarations.description:
Shows one file: a glyph that says its format, or a small picture of it; its name; a second line with what the
product says of it — its format, its size, where its sending stands, what went wrong; a bar while it is sent; and
the actions to take it back and to try it again. As a row of a column of files (`form="row"`, the default) or as a
tile of a strip of pictures (`form="tile"`, a box of `width` by `height`). **It never reads, keeps or sends the
file** (FIT-7, FIT-33): what it shows is what its props say.

Contract: specs/file-item.spec.json. `<tanrei-file-item name="brief.pdf" size-text="820 KB"
remove-label="Remove"></tanrei-file-item>`; a tile: `<tanrei-file-item form="tile" preview width="160" height="90"
name="floor-plan.png"></tanrei-file-item>`. `progress` absent is null: the bar is drawn as under way.

The glyph is chosen by the file's format — `media-type`, else the end of `name` — in ten kinds (FIT-5); `glyph`
names another of the icon set, and the `icon` slot holds one the set does not have. With `preview` the picture at
`preview-src` stands in the glyph's place, or — for an image — a picture of `file` (a `File`, a property and never an
attribute), for which the element makes one object URL when it first comes near the viewport and revokes it when it
is taken out of the page, given another file or no longer asked for the picture. Until a picture can be drawn, and
where it cannot, the glyph stands there. A picture that moves is played by the browser's image element: give a still
`preview-src` where a strip must not move.

The body — the glyph or the picture, and the texts — is a button with `interactive` (it emits `click`) and a link
with `href`; the two actions stand beside it, never inside it, and emit `remove` and `retry`. The element
removes nothing and changes no status: whoever holds it does. `readonly` draws no action; `disabled` disables them
and the body and leaves what is shown as it is.

Alone it is a group named by `name`. A component that holds it as an item of a list of its own — a File upload —
says so through an internal channel, and gives it there what every one of its rows shares.

Without script, and until the element is defined, nothing is drawn: the name is an attribute.
declarations.name: TanreiFileItem

cssParts.description: The body: the glyph or the picture, and the texts. The button or the link where the file item is pressable.
cssParts.name: container

cssParts.description: The box of the glyph or the picture: the leading box of a row, the whole box of a tile.
cssParts.name: media

cssParts.description: The box of the format's glyph (hidden from assistive technology).
cssParts.name: icon

cssParts.description: The picture, in the glyph's place.
cssParts.name: preview

cssParts.description: The file's name.
cssParts.name: headline

cssParts.description: The second line: the format, the size, then the status or the error.
cssParts.name: supporting-text

cssParts.description: The mark before the words of a file that is done or failed.
cssParts.name: status-icon

cssParts.description: The bar, while the status is uploading (a `<tanrei-progress-indicator>`).
cssParts.name: progress

cssParts.description: An action: also `retry` or `remove`.
cssParts.name: action

slots.description: A glyph of the product's own in place of the format's glyph, where a name in the icon set (`glyph`) is not enough. Decorative. A glyph the icon set flags is mirrored in right-to-left; `data-mirror="auto | always | never"` on the element decides for one use.
slots.name: icon

members.name: form
members.description: How the file is shown. `row`: one line across the width its layout gives — for a column of files. `tile`: a box of `width` by `height` holding the picture or the glyph, the texts beneath it and the actions at its corner — for a strip of pictures. Anything else is `row`.

members.name: value
members.description: What identifies the file to the product: given back by `click`, `remove` and `retry`.

members.name: name
members.description: The file's name as the person knows it ("report-2026.pdf"). The file item's name for assistive technology in every form, also where it is not drawn. Empty, it is read from `file.name`.

members.name: mediaType
members.description: The file's kind as the browser reports it ("image/png"), from which the glyph is chosen (`media-type`). Empty, it is read from `file.type`, and then from the end of `name`.

members.name: glyph
members.description: The name of a glyph of the icon set, drawn in place of the one the file's format would choose. Empty lets the format choose.

members.name: formatText
members.description: The file's format in the product's words ("PDF"), drawn first on the second line (`format-text`). Empty draws none.

members.name: sizeText
members.description: The file's size as text, formatted by the product for the reader's locale ("1.2 MB"); the `size-text` attribute. Empty draws none.

members.name: status
members.description: Where the file stands: `pending`, `uploading` (the bar is drawn), `done` or `error` (`errorText` says why). Anything else is `pending`.

members.name: statusText
members.description: The status in the product's words ("Waiting", "Uploading", "Uploaded"), drawn last on the second line; the `status-text` attribute.

members.name: progress
members.description: How far the sending has come, from 0 to 1, while the status is uploading. Null (no attribute) draws the bar as under way.

members.name: errorText
members.description: Why the file failed and what to do, in the product's words; drawn in the status's place while the status is error (`error-text`), in every form, and never cut.

members.name: retryable
members.description: Whether a failed file offers the retry action.

members.name: preview
members.description: Whether a picture of the file is drawn in the glyph's place: the one at `preview-src`, or — for an image — a picture of `file`. False draws the glyph, also for an image.

members.name: previewSrc
members.description: The address of a picture of the file (`preview-src`): a small rendition the product's server made. With `preview` it is drawn for a file of any format. Empty, the picture comes from `file`.

members.name: fit
members.description: How the picture fills its box. `cover`: it fills the box and is cut at the edges. `contain`: the whole picture inside the box, on the box's ground. Anything else is `cover`.

members.name: nameHidden
members.description: In a tile: the name is not drawn beneath a tile that draws a picture (`name-hidden`). It stays the file item's name for assistive technology, and is drawn all the same wherever no picture is. Not read in a row.

members.name: width
members.description: In a tile: the width of the box, in CSS pixels. Null (no attribute) makes it as wide as it is high.

members.name: height
members.description: In a tile: the height of the box, in CSS pixels. Null (no attribute) reads the token of a tile's height.

members.name: interactive
members.description: Makes the body — the glyph or the picture, and the texts — one button that emits `click`, for a product that opens the file where it is. The actions stay their own.

members.name: href
members.description: The destination: the address of the file. Not empty, the body is a link to it whether `interactive` is set or not: an `<a href>`, followed by Enter and not by Space.

members.name: target
members.description: Where the destination opens. `same`: where the person is. `new`: a new tab, which a row marks and `target-label` says. Ignored without `href`.

members.name: targetLabel
members.description: What assistive technology reads after the link's name while `target` is `new` ("opens in a new tab"): your words (`target-label`).

members.name: removeLabel
members.description: The accessible name of the remove action (`remove-label`): your sentence with the place `{name}`, which the file item fills with the file's name ("Remove {name}"). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ removeLabel })`).

members.name: retryLabel
members.description: The accessible name of the retry action (`retry-label`), with the place `{name}` filled by the file's name ("Retry {name}"). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ retryLabel })`).

members.name: disabled
members.description: The actions are disabled and the body cannot be pressed. What the file item shows of the file stays as it is and stays readable.

members.name: readOnly
members.description: The file is shown and cannot be taken back: no remove action and no retry action is drawn (`readonly`). The body can still be pressed where `interactive` or `href` says so.

members.name: rel
members.description: Web only: forwarded to the anchor's `rel`. `noopener` is added while `target` is `new`. Ignored without `href`.

members.name: download
members.description: Web only: forwarded to the anchor's `download` (the file name; empty for the address's own), so that the link saves the file in place of opening it. Ignored without `href`.

members.name: file
members.description: The file itself, as the browser's own handle: what a picture is drawn of (with `preview`, for an image), what `name` and `media-type` are read from where they are empty, and what a File upload submits for the item. A property, never an attribute; no byte of it is read.

members.name: address
members.description: FIT-7: the one address made for `file`, while its picture is asked for and the item has come near the viewport.

members.name: pictured
members.description: FIT-6: the address whose picture can be drawn.

members.name: failed

render, in its turn (GlyphDrawnController), and again when the face arrives: looked at after each, never at rest.

events.name: retry
events.description: The person asked to try a failed file again. Bubbles and is composed; `detail.value` is the file item's value.

events.name: remove
events.description: The person asked to take this file back. Bubbles and is composed; `detail.value` is the file item's value. Whoever holds the file item removes it.

The body of a pressable file item was activated. Bubbles and is composed; `detail.value` is the file item's value. A link fires it before the browser follows the address; `preventDefault()` cancels the navigation.
events.name: click

attributes.name: form
attributes.description: How the file is shown. `row`: one line across the width its layout gives — for a column of files. `tile`: a box of `width` by `height` holding the picture or the glyph, the texts beneath it and the actions at its corner — for a strip of pictures. Anything else is `row`.

attributes.name: value
attributes.description: What identifies the file to the product: given back by `click`, `remove` and `retry`.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: The file's name as the person knows it ("report-2026.pdf"). The file item's name for assistive technology in every form, also where it is not drawn. Empty, it is read from `file.name`.

attributes.name: media-type
attributes.description: The file's kind as the browser reports it ("image/png"), from which the glyph is chosen (`media-type`). Empty, it is read from `file.type`, and then from the end of `name`.

attributes.name: glyph
attributes.description: The name of a glyph of the icon set, drawn in place of the one the file's format would choose. Empty lets the format choose.

attributes.name: format-text
attributes.description: The file's format in the product's words ("PDF"), drawn first on the second line (`format-text`). Empty draws none.

attributes.name: size-text
attributes.description: The file's size as text, formatted by the product for the reader's locale ("1.2 MB"); the `size-text` attribute. Empty draws none.

attributes.name: status
attributes.description: Where the file stands: `pending`, `uploading` (the bar is drawn), `done` or `error` (`errorText` says why). Anything else is `pending`.

attributes.name: status-text
attributes.description: The status in the product's words ("Waiting", "Uploading", "Uploaded"), drawn last on the second line; the `status-text` attribute.

attributes.name: progress
attributes.description: How far the sending has come, from 0 to 1, while the status is uploading. Null (no attribute) draws the bar as under way.

attributes.name: error-text
attributes.description: Why the file failed and what to do, in the product's words; drawn in the status's place while the status is error (`error-text`), in every form, and never cut.

attributes.name: retryable
attributes.description: Whether a failed file offers the retry action.

attributes.name: preview
attributes.description: Whether a picture of the file is drawn in the glyph's place: the one at `preview-src`, or — for an image — a picture of `file`. False draws the glyph, also for an image.

attributes.name: preview-src
attributes.description: The address of a picture of the file (`preview-src`): a small rendition the product's server made. With `preview` it is drawn for a file of any format. Empty, the picture comes from `file`.

attributes.name: fit
attributes.description: How the picture fills its box. `cover`: it fills the box and is cut at the edges. `contain`: the whole picture inside the box, on the box's ground. Anything else is `cover`.

attributes.name: name-hidden
attributes.description: In a tile: the name is not drawn beneath a tile that draws a picture (`name-hidden`). It stays the file item's name for assistive technology, and is drawn all the same wherever no picture is. Not read in a row.

attributes.name: width
attributes.description: In a tile: the width of the box, in CSS pixels. Null (no attribute) makes it as wide as it is high.

attributes.name: height
attributes.description: In a tile: the height of the box, in CSS pixels. Null (no attribute) reads the token of a tile's height.

attributes.name: interactive
attributes.description: Makes the body — the glyph or the picture, and the texts — one button that emits `click`, for a product that opens the file where it is. The actions stay their own.

attributes.name: href
attributes.description: The destination: the address of the file. Not empty, the body is a link to it whether `interactive` is set or not: an `<a href>`, followed by Enter and not by Space.

attributes.name: target
attributes.description: Where the destination opens. `same`: where the person is. `new`: a new tab, which a row marks and `target-label` says. Ignored without `href`.

attributes.name: target-label
attributes.description: What assistive technology reads after the link's name while `target` is `new` ("opens in a new tab"): your words (`target-label`).

attributes.name: remove-label
attributes.description: The accessible name of the remove action (`remove-label`): your sentence with the place `{name}`, which the file item fills with the file's name ("Remove {name}"). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ removeLabel })`).

attributes.name: retry-label
attributes.description: The accessible name of the retry action (`retry-label`), with the place `{name}` filled by the file's name ("Retry {name}"). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ retryLabel })`).

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: The actions are disabled and the body cannot be pressed. What the file item shows of the file stays as it is and stays readable.

attributes.name: readonly
attributes.description: The file is shown and cannot be taken back: no remove action and no retry action is drawn (`readonly`). The body can still be pressed where `interactive` or `href` says so.

attributes.name: rel
attributes.description: Web only: forwarded to the anchor's `rel`. `noopener` is added while `target` is `new`. Ignored without `href`.

attributes.name: download
attributes.description: Web only: forwarded to the anchor's `download` (the file name; empty for the address's own), so that the link saves the file in place of opening it. Ignored without `href`.

declarations.description:
Lets people choose files through the browser's own picker — from the product's Button and, where there is room, from
a place files can also be dragged onto — says the limits in words before the choice, judges what was chosen against
them, and hands over what passed and what was refused. **It keeps nothing, lists nothing and takes no part in a
form** (FPK-7): whoever holds the files shows them — a `<tanrei-file-upload>` does, with a list and a form value.

Contract: specs/file-picker.spec.json. `<tanrei-file-picker accept=".json" constraints-text="…"><tanrei-button
slot="trigger" variant="outlined">Choose a file</tanrei-button></tanrei-file-picker>`. `layout="drop-area"` draws a
bounded place around the trigger that takes a drop and opens the picker when pressed. `select` carries the files of
one choice or one drop that passed `accept`, `max-size` and the count of one choice; `reject` the ones that did not,
each with a reason that is a name and not words (`type`, `size`, `count`). `judge(files)` judges files that came
another way — pasted, dropped elsewhere — and emits nothing. A second choice is judged as if it were the first.

`selection-text` stands beside the trigger in the button layout: what is chosen now, written by whoever holds it.
Inside a `<tanrei-field>` it takes the field's label as its group's name, and gives its trigger the field's help,
error, requirement and `disabled`.

Without script, and until the element is defined, the trigger is a button that opens nothing: a page that must take
files where script does not run writes a native `<input type="file">` in its own form.

members.name: layout
members.description: How choosing is offered: `button` is the trigger alone with the line of limits below it; `drop-area` is a bounded place around the trigger that also takes files dragged onto it and opens the picker when pressed. Anything else is `button`.

members.name: multiple
members.description: Whether more than one file can be chosen at a time. False: the picker offers one, and a drop of several is refused whole.

members.name: accept
members.description: The kinds of file that are taken: extensions with their dot (".pdf") and media types ("image/png", a family as "image/*"). The attribute is a comma-separated list, as a native file input's. Empty takes every kind.

members.name: maxSize
members.description: The largest size of one file, in bytes (`max-size`). Null sets no limit. Judged from the size the browser reports; the file is not read.

members.name: maxFiles
members.description: The most files one choice or one drop may bring, while `multiple` is set (`max-files`). Null sets no limit; zero refuses every file — the room a full list has left. Nothing is counted across choices.

members.name: label
members.description: The accessible name of the file picker as a group ("Photo"). Not drawn. Leave it empty inside a Field, whose label names the group; left empty elsewhere, no group is exposed and the trigger stands as the button it is.

members.name: constraintsText
members.description: The limits in the product's words, shown before the choice and given to assistive technology as the trigger's description (`constraints-text`).

members.name: dropText
members.description: The drop area's prompt, in the product's words (`drop-text`). Ignored in the button layout.

members.name: selectionText
members.description: What stands beside the trigger in the button layout (`selection-text`): what is chosen now, in the product's words or the file's own name. Read with the trigger. Never written by the element. Ignored in the drop-area layout.

members.name: disabled
members.description: Nothing can be chosen or dropped: the trigger is disabled and the area answers nothing. Inside a Field, disable the Field.

members.name: error
members.description: Puts the file picker in the error condition: the drop area's edge is drawn in the error role and the trigger is exposed as invalid. A Field sets it with its own error. Never set by the element.

members.name: required
members.description: Exposes the trigger as required; a button has no such state, so it is said by a Field's required text in the trigger's description. Draws nothing and validates nothing.

members.name: drag
members.description: FPK-13: what is dragged over the area can be taken (receiving), cannot (refusing), or nothing is.

members.name: field

name while it has no `label` of its own, the description, the invalid, required and disabled states.

members.description: FPK-27: a layout it does not know is button.

members.name: isDisabled
members.description: Disabled by its own `disabled`, or by a field or a component around it (FPK-19, FPK-21).

members.name: triggers
members.description: The elements in the trigger slot — through a slot that passes them on, too.

members.name: trigger
members.description: FPK-5: the one element in the trigger slot; the first where there are several.

members.name: hasIcon
members.description: FPK-4: the icon slot holds a glyph of the product's.

members.name: groupName
members.description: FPK-17: the group's name — its own label, else the field's.

members.name: shownSelectionText
members.description: FPK-2: selectionText as it is drawn — in the button layout alone.

members.name: given
members.description:
FPK-17: what the trigger is given. Its description is the line of limits, then selectionText while it is drawn,
then what a field or a holder gives; a control whose role has no required state says the requirement in its
description, in the field's words — the file picker has none (FPK-18).

members.name: focus
members.description: FPK-21: moves focus to the trigger — the file picker's one stop — and opens nothing.

members.name: openPicker
members.description: FPK-6: the browser's own picker — one file or any number, the kinds `accept` lists — and never a second while one is open.

members.name: fromTrigger
members.description: Whether the event came from the trigger: a press that begins there is the trigger's alone (FPK-12).

members.name: onClick
members.description:
FPK-5: the trigger was activated, by any input it takes — its click. FPK-12: a press on the area outside the
trigger does what activating the trigger does and moves focus to it. FPK-30: any element in the slot opens the
picker when it is clicked. A trigger that is disabled opens nothing, from either.

members.name: onChange
members.description: FPK-6: the person chose. The value is cleared, so the same file can be chosen again; focus is where it was, on the trigger.

members.name: onCancel
members.description: FPK-6: the person left the picker without choosing: nothing is emitted and nothing changes.

members.name: onPickerInput
members.description:
FPK-7, FPK-9: the input's own `input` event is composed — unlike its `change` — and would leave the element, and a
component that holds it, as the event of a control with a value. The file picker has none: a choice is told by
`select` and `reject` alone.

members.name: take
members.description:
FPK-9: the files of one choice or one drop, judged in the order the browser gave them by what it reports of them —
the name, the size, the kind — and never opened (FPK-7). `select` with those that passed, then `reject` with the
refused and their reasons; nothing is kept.

members.name: judged
members.description: FPK-9: the rule itself — what passed and what was refused, each in the order given.

members.name: judge
members.description:
FPK-31: judges files that came neither through the picker nor onto the area — pasted, dropped on another part of
the page, made by the product — as one arrival, by the rule a choice is judged by. Answers with the files that
passed and the refused files with their reasons, each in the order given. Emits nothing and keeps nothing. Works
while disabled: disabled stops the person, not the product.

members.name: answer
members.description:
FPK-13: what the browser tells before the drop — kinds and a count, never names or sizes. Refusing: it holds no
file, it holds more than one where one is asked, or every file is of a kind `accept` refuses — which can be known
only where `accept` lists media types alone: an extension is the end of a name, and a name is not told yet.

members.name: effect
members.description: Tells the browser what letting go here does: copy, or nothing.

members.name: onDrop
members.description:
FPK-14: the condition ends at once and the drop is taken — also when it is refused and when the file picker is
disabled — so that the browser does not open the file. What was dropped is judged as a choice in the picker is.

members.name: place
members.description: FPK-22: the trigger is told that its label may wrap; one that left the slot is told that it stands alone again.

members.name: onTriggerSlotChange
members.description: FPK-5: the trigger came, left or was replaced: it is given its description, and one that left gets back what it had.

members.name: present
members.description: What a debug build is told about the content is told once it has all been written: a turn after the first render.

members.name: check
members.description: What a debug build is told about the content, once it has all been written: the file picker still renders.

events.name: select
events.description: Files were chosen or dropped and passed. Once per choice; `detail.files` is a `File[]`. Bubbles.

events.name: reject
events.description: Files of one choice or one drop were refused. Once, after `select` where both happen; `detail.files` is `{ file, reason }[]`, the reason `type`, `size` or `count`. Bubbles.

attributes.name: layout
attributes.description: How choosing is offered: `button` is the trigger alone with the line of limits below it; `drop-area` is a bounded place around the trigger that also takes files dragged onto it and opens the picker when pressed. Anything else is `button`.

attributes.name: multiple
attributes.description: Whether more than one file can be chosen at a time. False: the picker offers one, and a drop of several is refused whole.

attributes.name: accept
attributes.description: The kinds of file that are taken: extensions with their dot (".pdf") and media types ("image/png", a family as "image/*"). The attribute is a comma-separated list, as a native file input's. Empty takes every kind.

attributes.name: max-size
attributes.description: The largest size of one file, in bytes (`max-size`). Null sets no limit. Judged from the size the browser reports; the file is not read.

attributes.name: max-files
attributes.description: The most files one choice or one drop may bring, while `multiple` is set (`max-files`). Null sets no limit; zero refuses every file — the room a full list has left. Nothing is counted across choices.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: The accessible name of the file picker as a group ("Photo"). Not drawn. Leave it empty inside a Field, whose label names the group; left empty elsewhere, no group is exposed and the trigger stands as the button it is.

attributes.name: constraints-text
attributes.description: The limits in the product's words, shown before the choice and given to assistive technology as the trigger's description (`constraints-text`).

attributes.name: drop-text
attributes.description: The drop area's prompt, in the product's words (`drop-text`). Ignored in the button layout.

attributes.name: selection-text
attributes.description: What stands beside the trigger in the button layout (`selection-text`): what is chosen now, in the product's words or the file's own name. Read with the trigger. Never written by the element. Ignored in the drop-area layout.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: Nothing can be chosen or dropped: the trigger is disabled and the area answers nothing. Inside a Field, disable the Field.

attributes.name: error
attributes.description: Puts the file picker in the error condition: the drop area's edge is drawn in the error role and the trigger is exposed as invalid. A Field sets it with its own error. Never set by the element.

attributes.name: required
attributes.description: Exposes the trigger as required; a button has no such state, so it is said by a Field's required text in the trigger's description. Draws nothing and validates nothing.

declarations.name: styles
declarations.default: css` /* The positioning container of the live region, which is drawn nowhere. */ .group { position: relative; min-inline-size: 0; } /* FPK-22, as the file picker has it for a trigger of its own: a trigger alone on its line is never wider than that line, and then wraps its label as the Button says. Said again here because the trigger reaches the file picker through a slot that is passed on (W9), and a rule on what is slotted stops at that slot. */ ::slotted([slot='trigger']) { max-inline-size: 100%; min-inline-size: min-content; } /* ── The list (FUP-17) ── the rows, list.gap below the file picker: a column, list.item-gap apart; or, of tiles, a strip from the start edge that wraps, list.item-gap apart along both directions, the tiles of one line aligned at their tops. With no row there is no list and no room for one. Only a file item is drawn: .rows is drawn for nothing and has no font, and a file item makes itself visible, so text or another element among the rows takes no room and is not read (FUP-41). */ .list { margin-block-start: ${t('list-gap')}; } .list[hidden] { display: none; } .rows { visibility: hidden; font-size: 0; line-height: 0; } /* A file item is given a font size again — a length of the root's — and not for its drawing: every text of a file item sets its own role and the row's line height stays nothing. It is for WebKit, which does not follow a change of the root's font size into the shadow tree of an element slotted into a box whose own font size does not change with it (.rows, above; a page of plain elements does the same), unless the slotted element's own font size does: without it a row drawn before a reader enlarges the text keeps every rem length it had. */ ::slotted(tanrei-file-item), .rows > tanrei-file-item { visibility: visible; font-size: var(--tanrei-sys-typescale-body-font-size); } ::slotted(tanrei-file-item:not(:first-of-type)), .rows > tanrei-file-item:not(:first-of-type) { margin-block-start: ${t('list-item-gap')}; } /* The strip's distances are each tile's own margins toward the start and the top, and the strip reaches one distance further those two ways (where nothing scrolls) — not a gap of the strip: a text the product left between two tiles is an item of the strip too, as wide as nothing, and a gap would be counted on both of its sides (FUP-41: it takes no room). The list is a formatting context of its own, so it begins where the first line does. */ .list[data-form='tile']:not([hidden]) { display: flow-root; } .list[data-form='tile'] .rows { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; margin-block-start: calc(-1 * ${t('list-item-gap')}); margin-inline-start: calc(-1 * ${t('list-item-gap')}); } .list[data-form='tile'] ::slotted(tanrei-file-item), .list[data-form='tile'] .rows > tanrei-file-item { margin-block-start: ${t('list-item-gap')}; margin-inline-start: ${t('list-item-gap')}; /* FIT-3: never wider than its layout — the file upload's width, which the strip exceeds by one distance. */ max-inline-size: calc(100% - ${t('list-item-gap')}); } ::slotted(:not(tanrei-file-item, [slot])) { display: none; } .announce {${unsafeCSS(unseen)} } `

declarations.description:
Lets people choose files and shows what was chosen. Built from a File picker (`<tanrei-file-picker>`) — the trigger,
the drop area, the limits in words, the judging of a choice — and File items (`<tanrei-file-item>`), one for each
file, in a column of rows or a strip of tiles; it adds the state that ties them: which files are kept, the room that
is left, one form for all its items, one message for many changes, where focus goes after a removal, and the form's
value. **It never uploads**: it opens no connection and reads no byte of a file (FUP-7).

Contract: specs/file-upload.spec.json. Who holds the rows is `rows`, and the product says which.

`rows="own"`, the default: the element keeps the chosen files and makes a file item for each itself, so a plain form
works by placing it — `<form><tanrei-file-upload name="attachments" multiple remove-label="…"><tanrei-button
slot="trigger" variant="outlined">Choose files</tanrei-button></tanrei-file-upload></form>`. With `multiple` a second
choice adds and `max-files` counts the files kept; without it a file that passes takes the place of the one kept. The
same file (name, size, time of last change) is kept once. A refused file is a failed row with the product's sentence
for its reason (`type-error-text`, `size-error-text`, `count-error-text`, else `setWords`), is not kept, and leaves
when it is removed, when files next arrive or on `clear()`. The remove action removes. `files` reads the kept files,
`add(files)` hands files over and answers with the refused, `clear()` empties, and `formatSize` — a property — writes
a row's size; without it none is drawn. A kept file's row shows no status and no progress: the element sends nothing.

`rows="given"`: the rows are `<tanrei-file-item>` children the product adds on `select` and removes on a row's
`remove`, each with its status, progress and error; the element adds, changes and removes none and keeps no file —
for a product that sends files itself.

Every row is of one form: `item-form` (`row`, `tile`), `item-preview`, `item-fit`, `item-name-hidden`, `item-width`,
`item-height`, with `remove-label`, `retry-label` and `disabled`, are given to every file item it holds — the
product's own included — through an internal channel; a product's item that says one of them otherwise is drawn as
the file upload says. The picture of an image row is made and released by its file item, never by this element.

`select` carries the files that passed `accept`, `max-size` and the count and found room, `reject` the ones that did
not, each with a reason that is a name and not words (`type`, `size`, `count`); while `rows` is `own`, `change` then
carries the files now kept. None is emitted for what the product did itself (`add()`, `clear()`, a reset, a change
of `rows`). The file picker's own two events do not leave the element.

Form-associated: under its `name` it submits the kept files, in order — or, while `rows` is `given`, the `file` of
every row that has one; it is invalid for its form while `required` and there is none. A reset empties the kept
files and changes nothing of the product's rows. Nothing is restored with a page. Inside a `<tanrei-field>` it takes
the field's label, help, error, requirement and `disabled`.

One level down, the same by hand: a `<tanrei-file-picker>` and `<tanrei-file-item>`s the product arranges — for a
list of its own, an order people change (file items in the rows of a List), or files that are only shown.

Without script, and until the element is defined, the trigger is a button that opens nothing and no row is drawn: a
page that must take files where script does not run writes a native `<input type="file">` in its own form.
