slots.description: The product's own Button that opens the picker, with its own label, variant and size. Exactly one.
slots.name: trigger

slots.description: A glyph of the icon set in place of the upload glyph at the top of the drop area; decorative, ignored in the button layout. A glyph the icon set flags is mirrored in right-to-left; `data-mirror="auto | always | never"` on the element decides for one use.
slots.name: icon

slots.description: While `rows` is `given`: the rows, `<tanrei-file-item>` children, in order. Anything else is not drawn, and while `rows` is `own` nothing here is.

members.name: formAssociated
members.description: FUP-31, FUP-49: the one control the form meets. Its members stand in its shadow root, or are the product's own children, and take no part in a form.

members.name: layout
members.description: How choosing is offered: `button` is the trigger alone with the line of limits below it; `drop-area` is a bounded place around the trigger that also takes files dragged onto it and opens the picker when pressed. Anything else is `button`.

members.name: multiple
members.description: Whether more than one file can be chosen at a time. False: the picker offers one, and a drop of several is refused whole.

members.name: accept
members.description: The kinds of file that are taken: extensions with their dot (".pdf") and media types ("image/png", a family as "image/*"). The attribute is a comma-separated list, as a native file input's. Empty takes every kind.

members.name: maxSize
members.description: The largest size of one file, in bytes (`max-size`). Null sets no limit. Judged from the size the browser reports; the file is not read.

members.name: maxFiles
members.description: The most files while `multiple` is set (`max-files`): the files it keeps while `rows` is `own`, the rows the list holds while it is `given`. Files chosen beyond the room that is left are refused. Null sets no limit. It is the file upload's own and is not given to its file picker.

members.name: label
members.description: The accessible name of the group ("Attachments"): the file picker and the list together. Not drawn. Leave it empty inside a Field, whose label names the group.

members.name: constraintsText
members.description: The limits in the product's words, shown before the choice and given to assistive technology as the trigger's description (`constraints-text`).

members.name: dropText
members.description: The drop area's prompt, in the product's words (`drop-text`). Ignored in the button layout.

members.name: emptyText
members.description: What is shown beside the trigger while no file is chosen, in the button layout (`empty-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ noFileText })`); with neither, nothing is drawn. Given to the file picker as its `selectionText` while the list holds no row.

members.name: itemForm
members.description: How the file is shown. `row`: one line across the width its layout gives — for a column of files. `tile`: a box of `width` by `height` holding the picture or the glyph, the texts beneath it and the actions at its corner — for a strip of pictures. Anything else is `row`.

members.name: itemPreview
members.description: Whether a picture of the file is drawn in the glyph's place: the one at `preview-src`, or — for an image — a picture of `file`. False draws the glyph, also for an image.

members.name: itemFit
members.description: How the picture fills its box. `cover`: it fills the box and is cut at the edges. `contain`: the whole picture inside the box, on the box's ground. Anything else is `cover`.

members.name: itemNameHidden
members.description: In a tile: the name is not drawn beneath a tile that draws a picture (`name-hidden`). It stays the file item's name for assistive technology, and is drawn all the same wherever no picture is. Not read in a row.

members.name: itemWidth
members.description: In a tile: the width of the box, in CSS pixels. Null (no attribute) makes it as wide as it is high.

members.name: itemHeight
members.description: In a tile: the height of the box, in CSS pixels. Null (no attribute) reads the token of a tile's height.

members.name: removeLabel
members.description: The accessible name of the remove action (`remove-label`): your sentence with the place `{name}`, which the file item fills with the file's name ("Remove {name}"). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ removeLabel })`).

members.name: retryLabel
members.description: The accessible name of the retry action (`retry-label`), with the place `{name}` filled by the file's name ("Retry {name}"). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ retryLabel })`).

members.name: announcement
members.description: A message assistive technology hears through the one live region when the product sets or changes it ("3 files added"). Not drawn. Set in the same turn as rows change, it is said in their place.

members.name: disabled
members.description: Nothing can be chosen or dropped: the trigger is disabled and the area answers nothing. Inside a Field, disable the Field.

members.name: error
members.description: Puts the file picker in the error condition: the drop area's edge is drawn in the error role and the trigger is exposed as invalid. A Field sets it with its own error. Never set by the element.

members.name: required
members.description: Exposes the trigger as required; a button has no such state, so it is said by a Field's required text in the trigger's description. Draws nothing and validates nothing.

members.name: name
members.description: The name the files are submitted under: the kept files while `rows` is `own`, the files of the product's rows while it is `given`. Web only. A product that sends files itself gives none.

members.name: rows
members.description: Who holds the rows. `own` (the default, and every value it does not know): the file upload keeps the files a person chose and makes a file item for each itself — choose, see the list, remove, submit, with nothing written. `given`: the product gives the rows as `<tanrei-file-item>` children and the file upload keeps no file — for a product that sends files itself and shows each one's status. Never guessed from the children.

members.name: typeErrorText
members.description: While `rows` is `own`: the sentence on the row of a file refused for its kind (`type-error-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ fileTypeErrorText })`); with neither the row is drawn without a sentence.

members.name: sizeErrorText
members.description: While `rows` is `own`: the sentence on the row of a file refused for its size (`size-error-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ fileSizeErrorText })`).

members.name: countErrorText
members.description: While `rows` is `own`: the sentence on the row of a file refused because no more files fit (`count-error-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ fileCountErrorText })`).

members.name: formatSize
members.description: While `rows` is `own`: the product's function from a size in bytes to the text a kept or refused file's row draws ("820 KB"). A property, never an attribute. Null draws no size: the file upload writes none itself.

members.name: count
members.description: FUP-17: how many rows the product gave.

members.name: formDisabled
members.description: Set by an ancestor `<fieldset disabled>`, or by the element's own attribute (the element's `formDisabledCallback`).

members.name: hostNameSentence
members.description:
W8: the sentence a debug build names when the host is given an ARIA name. The host has no role: its name is the
frame's `label`. Empty: nothing is reported.

members.name: words
members.description: FUP-27: the product's words, read where the instance gives none (src/primitives/words.ts).

members.name: field
members.description:
FUP-32: what a field around the file upload gives it (src/primitives/field.ts): the name while it has no `label`
of its own, the description, the invalid, required and disabled states. The file upload is the field's one control.

members.name: provider
members.default: new FieldProviderController(this, { controls: () => (this.picker ? [this.picker] : []), state: () => this.given, plain: () => null, })
members.description:
FUP-24, FUP-32, FPK-21: the file picker inside asks as every control does, and the file upload answers it in a
field's place — the description a field gave and the three states, and no name, so that the file picker exposes no
second group inside this one. The file picker gives its trigger the rest.

members.name: arriving
members.description: FUP-57: what the file picker's two events of one arrival said, until the arrival is over.

members.name: known
members.description: FUP-26: what each row last said; a row not in it is new.

members.name: presented
members.description: FUP-26: the file upload has been presented: a row that comes now was added.

members.name: own
members.description: FUP-26: the product's own sentence, set or changed in this turn.

members.name: kept
members.description: FUP-43: the files it keeps while `rows` is `own`, in order — handles, never read (FUP-51).

members.name: refused
members.description: FUP-45: the files the last arrival refused, in the order they were refused. Not kept.

members.name: arrived
members.description: FUP-50: what the arrivals of this turn say: each newly kept file's name, each refused file's name and sentence.

members.name: hush
members.description: FUP-52: the next message says no row: the rows that are there came by a change of `rows`.

members.name: leavingHeld
members.description: FUP-52: a row that leaves because `rows` changed held focus.

members.name: held
members.description: FUP-30: the row focus is on, as the last `focusin` said, and the rows as they stood.

members.name: children$
members.description: FUP-17, FUP-30: a row that comes or goes is drawn at once; a row that left with focus on it hands focus on.

members.name: picker
members.description: FUP-56: its one file picker, once rendered.

members.name: isDisabled
members.description: Disabled by its own `disabled`, by a field around it, or by its form (FUP-28, FUP-31, FUP-32).

members.name: trigger
members.description: The one element in the trigger slot; the first where there are several (FPK-5).

members.name: control
members.description: W7: the file upload's first stop — the product's own trigger.

members.name: keeps
members.description: FUP-42: it keeps the chosen files and makes their rows itself — `own`, and every value it does not know.

members.name: givenRows
members.description: FUP-17: the rows the product gave, in the order it gave them — and none while `rows` is `own` (FUP-42).

members.name: itemChildren
members.description: The `tanrei-file-item` children the product wrote, whatever `rows` says.

members.name: rowCount
members.description: FUP-17: how many rows the list holds — the product's, or the file upload's own: the kept files, then the refused.

members.name: groupName
members.description: FUP-24: the group's name — its own label, else the field's.

members.name: shownEmptyText
members.description: FUP-2: what the file picker is given as its selectionText — emptyText (the prop, else the product's words) while the list holds no row, and nothing while it holds one.

members.name: shownForm
members.description: FUP-17: the form of every row; one it does not know is a column of rows.

members.name: given
members.description:
FUP-24, FUP-32: what the file picker is given, as a field gives its control: no name; the description a field
gave the file upload, which the file picker puts last in its trigger's description; and the three states.

members.name: gift
members.description: FUP-58, FUP-25, FUP-28: what every file item it holds is given, through the internal channel and through no prop of the item's.

members.name: form
members.description: The form it belongs to, if any.

members.name: validity
members.description: The native constraint validity: `valueMissing` while it is required and no row carries a file.

members.name: formResetCallback
members.description: FUP-31: while `rows` is `given` a reset changes nothing — the rows are the product's to clear. FUP-49: while it is `own` a reset does what `clear()` does, and emits nothing.

members.name: formStateRestoreCallback
members.description: FUP-31, FUP-49: nothing is restored: no state is kept with the form — a handle does not outlast the page.

members.name: syncForm
members.description:
FUP-31: one entry per row that has a file, under the name, in the order of the rows — and nothing while disabled or
unnamed. FUP-49: while `rows` is `own`, one entry per kept file, never a refused one, and no empty entry.

members.name: onPickerSelect
members.description: FUP-57: the file picker's `select` is answered here and does not reach the product as it is.

members.name: onPickerReject
members.description: FUP-57: the file picker's `reject` is answered here and does not reach the product as it is.

members.name: onArrival
members.description: FUP-57: the arrival is over — one choice is told once, by the file upload's own events.

members.name: room
members.description: FUP-9: the room that is left, which the file picker cannot know — `held` is what the list already holds. Answers with the files that found room and the ones that did not.

members.name: handOver
members.description:
FUP-9: while `rows` is `given` nothing is kept: `select` with the files that also found room, then `reject` with
the files the file picker refused, in the order it refused them, and then those refused for want of room. No row
is added: the product adds one for each file it keeps.

members.name: files
members.description:
FUP-48: the files it keeps while `rows` is `own`, in order, as the browser's own `File` handles: a new array on
each read, so changing it changes nothing that is kept. Never a refused file. Empty while `rows` is `given`.

members.name: add
members.description:
FUP-48: hands files over, as a product does that takes them elsewhere — a drop target of its own, a paste. They
are judged by its file picker (FPK-31) and are then an arrival (FUP-43): kept or refused, drawn and announced as a
choice is, with no event. Answers with the refused files and their reasons. Works while disabled. While `rows` is
`given` it does nothing and is reported.

members.name: clear
members.description:
FUP-48: lets go of every file it keeps and removes every row, kept and refused. Emits nothing and announces
nothing; focus that was on a row goes to the trigger. Works while disabled. Does nothing while `rows` is `given`.

members.name: same
members.description: FUP-43: the same file — the same name, size and time of last change, as the browser reports them.

members.name: arrive
members.description:
FUP-43: files arrived while `rows` is `own` — chosen or dropped (`person`), or handed over by `add()` — and were
judged by the file picker. The rows of what an earlier arrival refused leave; a file that passed and that it
already keeps, and a second copy within the arrival, is passed over; the rest is judged for the room that is left.
With `multiple` what found room is kept after the others; without it a file that passed takes the place of them
all, and a refused choice replaces nothing. Then the rows are drawn, and — for what a person did — `select`,
`reject` and `change` are emitted, in that order (FUP-47). One message says it (FUP-50).

members.name: emitChange
members.description: FUP-47: the files it keeps changed by what a person did. Never while disabled (FUP-54).

members.name: sentence
members.description: FUP-53: the product's sentence for a reason — the instance's prop, else the product's words, else nothing.

members.name: sizeOf
members.description: FUP-44: a file's size in the product's words: what its function writes, and nothing where it gave none.

members.name: ownRows
members.description: The file items it made itself, in the order they are drawn.

members.name: redraw
members.description:
Changes the two lists and draws the rows at once, so that what is emitted afterwards is emitted with the rows as
they will be (FUP-47). FUP-30: where a row that leaves held focus, focus goes to the remove action of the row that
followed it, or of the one before where none follows, or to the trigger where no row is left.

members.name: removeOwn
members.description:
FUP-46: the remove action of a row it made itself removes the row, at once. A kept file is let go and `change` is
emitted; a refused one leaves and nothing is emitted. The file item's own `remove` does not leave the shadow root:
it is an event of the product's rows.

members.name: readRows
members.description: The rows were added to, removed from, or changed: drawn at once, said once, submitted as they are now.

members.name: tellRows
members.description: FUP-58, FUP-25, FUP-28: each file item it holds is given the one form of the rows, the two action names, whether it is disabled and that it is an item of a list; one it holds no longer is told so.

members.name: onFocusOut
members.description:
Focus that leaves a row which is still here has gone elsewhere, by the person's doing. An engine that says so
while it removes the focused element says it of a row that is no longer here: that one is the observer's to follow.

members.name: afterLeave
members.description:
FUP-30: a row left while focus was on one of its stops, and focus is now nowhere: it goes to the remove action of
the row that followed, or of the one before where none follows — to its body where it has no remove action and
that is pressable, and on to the next such row otherwise — or to the trigger where no row is left. Where the
product has already put focus somewhere, nothing is done.

members.name: changed
members.description: FUP-26: something that may be said changed in this turn; everything of one turn is one message.

members.name: say
members.description:
FUP-26: the one message of a turn — the product's own sentence alone where it set one, else each row that was
added, finished or failed, in the order of the rows, in the product's words: the name, then the status or the error.
Rows that were there when the file upload was first presented say nothing.

members.name: check
members.description: What a debug build is told about the content, once it has all been written: the file upload still renders.

members.name: ownRow
members.description:
FUP-44, FUP-45: a row it makes itself — a file item, so a row has one drawing. A kept file is a pending file item
given the file's handle, its name and its media type, with the size the product's function writes; a refused one
a failed file item with the product's sentence for its reason, given no handle, never retryable. Neither is
pressable or a link: the file upload opens nothing.

members.name: passing
members.description: W9: the names of the slots it has passed on, and the watch on its own children for them.

members.name: members
members.description: The members it has rendered: the custom elements of its own shadow tree.

members.name: focus
members.description: W7, item 2: focus is the control's.

members.name: blur
members.description: W7, item 2: what has focus inside the control loses it (an engine does not take it from inside a host it blurs).

members.name: pass
members.description:
W9: a slot of a member, passed on — `${this.pass('label-icon')}` among that member's children. Rendered only while
the element has a child for it: a member that draws room for a filled slot would take a passing slot that is
always there for content.

members.name: getUpdateComplete
members.description: The element has updated when its members have: what it gave them, they have taken.

members.name: focusWhenReady
members.description: The control has rendered what takes focus only after its own first update.

events.name: select
events.description: Files were chosen or dropped, passed and found room. Once per choice; `detail.files` is a `File[]` — while `rows` is `own`, the files newly kept. Bubbles.

events.name: reject
events.description: Files of one choice or one drop were refused. Once, after `select` where both happen; `detail.files` is `{ file, reason }[]`, the reason `type`, `size` or `count`. Bubbles.

events.name: change
events.description: While `rows` is `own`: the kept files changed by what a person did — a choice or a drop that kept or replaced a file, or a kept file's row removed. Once, after `select` and `reject`; `detail.files` is the `File[]` now kept. Bubbles. Never for `add()`, `clear()`, a reset or a change of `rows`.

attributes.description: The id of the form the file upload belongs to, where it stands outside it: the platform's own attribute, which then wins over a form around it. The `form` property is read-only and returns the form element.
attributes.name: form
layout
attributes.description: How choosing is offered: `button` is the trigger alone with the line of limits below it; `drop-area` is a bounded place around the trigger that also takes files dragged onto it and opens the picker when pressed. Anything else is `button`.

attributes.name: multiple
attributes.description: Whether more than one file can be chosen at a time. False: the picker offers one, and a drop of several is refused whole.

attributes.name: accept
attributes.description: The kinds of file that are taken: extensions with their dot (".pdf") and media types ("image/png", a family as "image/*"). The attribute is a comma-separated list, as a native file input's. Empty takes every kind.

attributes.name: max-size
attributes.description: The largest size of one file, in bytes (`max-size`). Null sets no limit. Judged from the size the browser reports; the file is not read.

attributes.name: max-files
attributes.description: The most files while `multiple` is set (`max-files`): the files it keeps while `rows` is `own`, the rows the list holds while it is `given`. Files chosen beyond the room that is left are refused. Null sets no limit. It is the file upload's own and is not given to its file picker.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: The accessible name of the group ("Attachments"): the file picker and the list together. Not drawn. Leave it empty inside a Field, whose label names the group.

attributes.name: constraints-text
attributes.description: The limits in the product's words, shown before the choice and given to assistive technology as the trigger's description (`constraints-text`).

attributes.name: drop-text
attributes.description: The drop area's prompt, in the product's words (`drop-text`). Ignored in the button layout.

attributes.name: empty-text
attributes.description: What is shown beside the trigger while no file is chosen, in the button layout (`empty-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ noFileText })`); with neither, nothing is drawn. Given to the file picker as its `selectionText` while the list holds no row.

attributes.name: item-form
attributes.description: How the file is shown. `row`: one line across the width its layout gives — for a column of files. `tile`: a box of `width` by `height` holding the picture or the glyph, the texts beneath it and the actions at its corner — for a strip of pictures. Anything else is `row`.

attributes.name: item-preview
attributes.description: Whether a picture of the file is drawn in the glyph's place: the one at `preview-src`, or — for an image — a picture of `file`. False draws the glyph, also for an image.

attributes.name: item-fit
attributes.description: How the picture fills its box. `cover`: it fills the box and is cut at the edges. `contain`: the whole picture inside the box, on the box's ground. Anything else is `cover`.

attributes.name: item-name-hidden
attributes.description: In a tile: the name is not drawn beneath a tile that draws a picture (`name-hidden`). It stays the file item's name for assistive technology, and is drawn all the same wherever no picture is. Not read in a row.

attributes.name: item-width
attributes.description: In a tile: the width of the box, in CSS pixels. Null (no attribute) makes it as wide as it is high.

attributes.name: item-height
attributes.description: In a tile: the height of the box, in CSS pixels. Null (no attribute) reads the token of a tile's height.

attributes.name: remove-label
attributes.description: The accessible name of the remove action (`remove-label`): your sentence with the place `{name}`, which the file item fills with the file's name ("Remove {name}"). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ removeLabel })`).

attributes.name: retry-label
attributes.description: The accessible name of the retry action (`retry-label`), with the place `{name}` filled by the file's name ("Retry {name}"). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ retryLabel })`).

attributes.name: announcement
attributes.description: A message assistive technology hears through the one live region when the product sets or changes it ("3 files added"). Not drawn. Set in the same turn as rows change, it is said in their place.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: Nothing can be chosen or dropped: the trigger is disabled and the area answers nothing. Inside a Field, disable the Field.

attributes.name: error
attributes.description: Puts the file picker in the error condition: the drop area's edge is drawn in the error role and the trigger is exposed as invalid. A Field sets it with its own error. Never set by the element.

attributes.name: required
attributes.description: Exposes the trigger as required; a button has no such state, so it is said by a Field's required text in the trigger's description. Draws nothing and validates nothing.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: The name the files are submitted under: the kept files while `rows` is `own`, the files of the product's rows while it is `given`. Web only. A product that sends files itself gives none.

attributes.name: rows
attributes.description: Who holds the rows. `own` (the default, and every value it does not know): the file upload keeps the files a person chose and makes a file item for each itself — choose, see the list, remove, submit, with nothing written. `given`: the product gives the rows as `<tanrei-file-item>` children and the file upload keeps no file — for a product that sends files itself and shows each one's status. Never guessed from the children.

attributes.name: type-error-text
attributes.description: While `rows` is `own`: the sentence on the row of a file refused for its kind (`type-error-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ fileTypeErrorText })`); with neither the row is drawn without a sentence.

attributes.name: size-error-text
attributes.description: While `rows` is `own`: the sentence on the row of a file refused for its size (`size-error-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ fileSizeErrorText })`).

attributes.name: count-error-text
attributes.description: While `rows` is `own`: the sentence on the row of a file refused because no more files fit (`count-error-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ fileCountErrorText })`).

declarations.name: styles
declarations.default: css` :host { display: contents; } /* IMP-1: a native modal <dialog> in the top layer, over the whole window, filled with container.color. Nothing of the window is left uncovered, so there is no scrim: ::backdrop is clear. None of the browser's dialog box. The three rows are the bar, the fit area (IMP-11) and the caption (IMP-26). */ dialog { box-sizing: border-box; position: fixed; inset: 0; inline-size: 100%; max-inline-size: none; block-size: 100dvh; max-block-size: none; margin: 0; border: 0; padding: 0; overflow: hidden; grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr); grid-template-rows: auto minmax(0, 1fr) auto; background: transparent; color: ${t('caption-color')}; text-align: start; outline: none; /* IMP-33: out, all of it fades over the exit motion — kept in the top layer and displayed until it has. */ opacity: 0; pointer-events: none; transition-property: opacity, display, overlay; transition-duration: ${t('motion-exit-duration')}; transition-timing-function: ${t('motion-exit-easing')}; transition-behavior: allow-discrete; } dialog[open] { display: grid; opacity: 1; pointer-events: auto; /* IMP-33: in, the container, the bar, the controls and the caption fade in over the enter motion. */ transition-duration: ${t('motion-enter-duration')}; transition-timing-function: ${t('motion-enter-easing')}; } @starting-style { dialog[open] { opacity: 0; } } dialog::backdrop { background: transparent; } /* IMP-1: the fill, behind the image, so that the image's clear parts show it (IMP-11) and so that the downward drag can make the fill clearer and leave the image as it is (IMP-22). */ .surface { position: absolute; inset: 0; background: ${t('container-color')}; pointer-events: none; } /* IMP-11, IMP-32: the image shown and its two neighbours, each on a page as large as the stage; the page of the image after lies one stage and layout.page-gap toward the end — to the left in a right-to-left layout (IMP-35) — and all three follow a drag (IMP-18, IMP-22). The pages take no pointer: the stage above them does. */ .pages { --_direction: 1; position: absolute; inset: 0; pointer-events: none; /* IMP-33: the image grows about the centre of the fit area (which the element measures). */ transform-origin: var(--_fit-x, 50%) var(--_fit-y, 50%); transition: scale ${t('motion-enter-duration')} ${t('motion-enter-easing')}; } .pages:dir(rtl) { --_direction: -1; } @starting-style { dialog[open] .pages { scale: ${t('motion-enter-scale')}; } } .page { position: absolute; inset: 0; translate: calc(var(--_at, 0) * var(--_direction) * (100% + ${t('layout-page-gap')}) + var(--_drag-x, 0px)) var(--_drag-y, 0px); } /* IMP-18, IMP-20, IMP-22: one image replaces another, and a released drag settles, over the page motion. */ .pages.settling .page { transition: translate ${t('motion-page-duration')} ${t('motion-page-easing')}; } /* IMP-11: the image at its fit size, placed and enlarged by a transform the element writes (IMP-12 to IMP-17); never cropped, stretched, mirrored or recolored. */ .image, .thumbnail { position: absolute; inset-block-start: 0; left: 0; display: block; max-inline-size: none; transform-origin: 0 0; user-select: none; -webkit-user-select: none; -webkit-user-drag: none; } /* IMP-13, IMP-14: a step of the zoom moves over the zoom motion; a pinch, a wheel and a drag follow the person. */ .image.stepping { transition: transform ${t('motion-zoom-duration')} ${t('motion-zoom-easing')}; } /* IMP-30: a source that is asked for and not drawn yet has no box of its own. */ .asked { position: absolute; inline-size: 0; block-size: 0; visibility: hidden; } /* IMP-29: the Skeleton's one block, at the size the image will have (written by the element). */ .waiting { position: absolute; inset-block-start: 0; left: 0; } .waiting .tanrei-skeleton-placeholder { inline-size: 100%; block-size: 100%; } tanrei-skeleton { display: block; inline-size: 100%; block-size: 100%; } /* IMP-31: the mark and the product's sentence in the middle of the fit area, error.gap apart, the text centred and wrapping. */ .error { position: absolute; inset-block-start: 0; left: 0; box-sizing: border-box; display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: ${t('error-gap')}; padding-inline: ${t('caption-padding-inline')}; } ${iconGlyph('.glyph', { size: `${PREFIX}-error-icon-size`, selected: ':not(*)' })} .glyph { color: ${t('error-icon-color')}; } /* Nothing in the glyph's place until the icon set can draw it (GlyphDrawnController); the box keeps its size. */ .glyph:not([data-drawn]) { visibility: hidden; } .ink { display: inline-block; vertical-align: top; } .error-text { max-inline-size: 100%; margin: 0; font: ${t('error-text-typescale-font')}; letter-spacing: ${t('error-text-typescale-letter-spacing')}; color: ${t('error-text-color')}; text-align: center; overflow-wrap: break-word; } /* IMP-11, IMP-27: the stage is the whole container: it takes the gestures and the keys and is the one focus stop that is not a Button. It draws nothing (IMP-42), and the browser's own pinch and scroll do not take its gestures. */ .stage { position: absolute; inset: 0; outline: none; touch-action: none; user-select: none; -webkit-user-select: none; -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent; } /* IMP-11: the fit area — inside the safe area, below the bar and above the caption — which the element measures, and inside whose edge the stage's keyboard focus is drawn (IMP-27). */ .fit { position: relative; grid-row: 2; grid-column: 1; margin-left: env(safe-area-inset-left, 0px); margin-right: env(safe-area-inset-right, 0px); min-block-size: 0; pointer-events: none; ${unsafeCSS(cornerRadius('--tanrei-sys-shape-corner-none'))} } dialog:not(.captioned) .fit { margin-block-end: env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px); } ${focusRing((focus) => `.stage${focus} ~ .fit`, { inside: true })} /* IMP-27: focus the stage took as the preview was opened by a press shows no indicator. */ .stage[data-focus-quiet]:focus-visible ~ .fit { outline: none; } .stage[data-focus-quiet]:focus-visible ~ .fit::after { display: none; } /* IMP-8: the bar across the top, inside the safe area, at least bar.height tall, on its own fill: the count at its start, the three controls at its end, bar.gap apart, centred on its height. A zoomed image passes under it. IMP-39: where the three controls leave the count less than half the bar (a narrow window with enlarged text), the count takes a line of its own above them, so that it is never cut. */ .bar { position: relative; grid-row: 1; grid-column: 1; box-sizing: content-box; display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; column-gap: ${t('bar-gap')}; min-block-size: ${t('bar-height')}; padding-block-start: env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px); padding-left: calc(${t('bar-padding-inline')} + env(safe-area-inset-left, 0px)); padding-right: calc(${t('bar-padding-inline')} + env(safe-area-inset-right, 0px)); background: ${t('bar-container-color')}; } .controls { display: flex; flex: none; align-items: center; gap: ${t('bar-gap')}; margin-inline-start: auto; } .controls tanrei-button { flex: none; } /* IMP-9: the count, in its role and color, wrapping — the bar grows — and never cut. It takes the room the controls leave, so they stand at the bar's end with or without it. */ .count { flex: 1 1 50%; box-sizing: border-box; min-inline-size: 0; margin: 0; padding-inline: ${t('count-padding-inline')}; font: ${t('count-typescale-font')}; letter-spacing: ${t('count-typescale-letter-spacing')}; color: ${t('count-color')}; overflow-wrap: break-word; } .count:empty { display: none; } /* IMP-10: the previous control at the inline start of the stage and the next at its inline end, navigation.margin-inline from the safe area's side edge, centred on the height of the fit area. */ .previous, .next { position: relative; grid-row: 2; grid-column: 1; align-self: center; } .previous { justify-self: start; margin-inline-start: ${t('navigation-margin-inline')}; } .next { justify-self: end; margin-inline-end: ${t('navigation-margin-inline')}; } .previous:dir(ltr), .next:dir(rtl) { left: env(safe-area-inset-left, 0px); } .previous:dir(rtl), .next:dir(ltr) { right: env(safe-area-inset-right, 0px); } /* IMP-26: the caption at the bottom, across the container and inside the safe area, on its own fill; no taller than a third of the container, and scrolling inside itself where the text needs more. Its lines begin at the start of a column at most caption.max-width wide, centred in the container. */ .caption { position: relative; grid-row: 3; grid-column: 1; box-sizing: border-box; max-block-size: calc(100dvh / 3); overflow-y: auto; overscroll-behavior: contain; padding-block: ${t('caption-padding-block')} calc(${t('caption-padding-block')} + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)); padding-left: calc(${t('caption-padding-inline')} + env(safe-area-inset-left, 0px)); padding-right: calc(${t('caption-padding-inline')} + env(safe-area-inset-right, 0px)); background: ${t('caption-container-color')}; outline: none; ${unsafeCSS(cornerRadius('--tanrei-sys-shape-corner-none'))} } .caption-text { max-inline-size: ${t('caption-max-width')}; margin: 0 auto; font: ${t('caption-typescale-font')}; letter-spacing: ${t('caption-typescale-letter-spacing')}; color: ${t('caption-color')}; overflow-wrap: break-word; } /* IMP-26: the scrolling region's keyboard focus, inside its edge — drawn by a box in the caption's place in the grid that does not scroll with the text (a box of the caption's own would move away with it). */ .caption-focus { position: relative; grid-row: 3; grid-column: 1; pointer-events: none; ${unsafeCSS(cornerRadius('--tanrei-sys-shape-corner-none'))} } ${focusRing((focus) => `.caption${focus} + .caption-focus`, { inside: true })} /* IMP-38: the count, the caption and the error text are each text of their own direction, isolated; the count and the caption are still placed, and their lines aligned, by the layout. */ ${productText(':is(.count, .caption-text)', { align: 'start' })} ${productText('.error-text')} /* The bar, the two controls at the stage's sides and the caption stand over the stage, which is the whole container; so does the fit area's edge, where the stage's focus is drawn. */ .bar, .previous, .next, .caption, .caption-focus, .fit { z-index: 1; } /* IMP-25: hidden, the bar, the count, the previous and next controls and the caption are only not drawn — they keep their boxes, so the image does not move, stay in the focus order and exposed, and take no press they cannot be seen to take. They fade over the controls motion. */ .bar, .previous, .next, .caption { transition: opacity ${t('motion-controls-duration')} ${t('motion-controls-easing')}; } dialog.controls-hidden :is(.bar, .previous, .next, .caption, .caption-focus) { opacity: 0; pointer-events: none; } /* IMP-22: while a downward drag is followed, the fill, the bar, the controls and the caption are as clear as the drag is long (--_presence, which the element writes); released, they come back over the page motion. */ dialog.clearing :is(.surface, .bar, .previous, .next, .caption) { opacity: var(--_presence, 1); transition: none; } dialog.returning :is(.surface, .bar, .previous, .next, .caption) { transition: opacity ${t('motion-page-duration')} ${t('motion-page-easing')}; } /* IMP-28: what assistive technology is told when the image changes, drawn nowhere. */ .said { position: absolute; inset-block-start: 0; inset-inline-start: 0; inline-size: 1px; block-size: 1px; overflow: hidden; clip-path: inset(50%); white-space: nowrap; pointer-events: none; } /* IMP-34: where motion is reduced it opens and closes by fading without growing; the zoom steps, the change of image, the settle of a released drag and the controls change at once. */ @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .pages, .pages.settling .page, .image.stepping, .bar, .previous, .next, .caption, dialog.returning :is(.surface, .bar, .previous, .next, .caption) { transition: none; } @starting-style { dialog[open] .pages { scale: none; } } } ${shape} /* IMP-41: a person's own colors: the fills are the platform's background, the text and the mark its text color, the focus indicators its own; every image is left exactly as it is. The controls are Buttons and adapt as Buttons do. */ @media (forced-colors: active) { .surface, .bar, .caption { background: Canvas; } .count, .caption-text, .error-text, .glyph { color: CanvasText; } .image, .thumbnail { forced-color-adjust: none; } } `

declarations.name: ITEM_TAG
declarations.default: 'tanrei-image-preview-item'

declarations.description: One picture of an image preview's set: where it is, what it shows in words, and optionally what the product says about it. ``. The element is data for the preview that holds it: it draws nothing, takes no focus and fires no event, and it is not an ``, so the browser asks for no picture the preview has not asked for (IMP-32). The preview reads its children in order and reads them again when an attribute changes. Every property reflects to its attribute, which is what the preview reads.
declarations.name: TanreiImagePreviewItem

members.name: src
members.description: The address of the picture as the preview shows it — usually a larger file than the thumbnail on the page. Required; while it is empty the preview asks for nothing and the image waits. Changed while the image is shown, the new picture replaces the old one in place once it has loaded (IMP-30).

members.name: alt
members.description: What the picture shows, in the product's language: the name assistive technology reads for it. Required for every image (IMP-27). Never drawn.

members.name: caption
members.description: What the product says about the picture, drawn below it and read as its description: a credit, a date, a sentence. Plain text of any length; a long one scrolls in its own region (IMP-26). Empty draws no caption.

members.name: thumbnailSrc
members.description: The address of a smaller picture of the same image that the page has usually loaded already (`thumbnail-src`). Drawn enlarged in the image's place until `src` has loaded, in place of the Skeleton (IMP-29).

members.name: width
members.description: The picture's own width in pixels, where the product knows it. With `height` it lets the preview hold the image's place before the picture has loaded. Null: learned when it loads.

members.name: height
members.description: The picture's own height in pixels; see `width`.

attributes.name: src
attributes.description: The address of the picture as the preview shows it — usually a larger file than the thumbnail on the page. Required; while it is empty the preview asks for nothing and the image waits. Changed while the image is shown, the new picture replaces the old one in place once it has loaded (IMP-30).

attributes.name: alt
attributes.description: What the picture shows, in the product's language: the name assistive technology reads for it. Required for every image (IMP-27). Never drawn.

attributes.name: caption

declarations.description:
Shows one picture of a set over the whole window when the person presses its thumbnail, to be looked at closely —
enlarged and back by a double tap, a pinch, a control or a key, moved about while enlarged — and moved on to the
next picture or back, until it is closed.

Contract: specs/image-preview.spec.json. A feature: its stage — the picture, its zoom and its place —
and its pager are its own; its five controls are real `<tanrei-button>` elements and its placeholder a real
`<tanrei-skeleton>`, each reading its own tokens. The images are `<tanrei-image-preview-item>` children.

The product opens it from its own thumbnail — a `<button type="button" aria-haspopup="dialog">` around its own
picture, named for what it does — by setting `index` and `open`, and closes it in answer to `close` by setting
`open` to false: the preview never closes itself. It is a native `<dialog>` in the shadow root opened with
`showModal()`: in the top layer over the whole window, everything else inert, the page held from scrolling, focus on
the stage and kept inside, and returned where it was when the preview closes. It writes no history entry.

Every gesture has a control and a key: the zoom controls and `+` `−` `0` for a double tap and a pinch; the previous
and next controls, the arrow keys, Page Up, Page Down, Home and End for a sideways drag; the arrow keys for a drag
over an enlarged picture; the close control and Escape for the downward drag by touch. `index`, `zoom` and
`controlsHidden` are plain values the element writes itself on a person's change, before the event.

Only the image shown and the one before and after it are asked for. An item without a `src` is asked for nothing
and waits. Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-image-preview-*` tokens.

members.name: glyphs
members.description: IMP-31: the mark carries `data-drawn` while the icon set can draw its ligature; until then it draws nothing.

members.name: open
members.description: Whether the preview is presented. Open it from your own thumbnail, with `index` set to that image, and close it in answer to `close`. Reflected.

members.name: index
members.description: Which image is shown, counted from 0 in the order the images are given. The person changes it by a drag, the previous and next controls and the keys, and the preview then fires `indexchange`; setting it fires nothing. A number outside the images is taken as the nearest that exists (IMP-20).

members.name: zoom
members.description: How far the image shown is enlarged: 1 is its fit in the window, 2 twice that. The person changes it by a double tap, a pinch, the zoom controls and the keys, and the preview then fires `zoomchange`; it returns to 1 whenever the image shown changes. Kept between 1 and the greatest zoom (IMP-12).

members.name: maxZoom
members.description: The greatest zoom (`max-zoom`). Null takes the greater of 4 and twice the zoom at which the image fills the window's free area, so that a very wide or very tall image can still be read (IMP-12).

members.name: controlsHidden
members.description: Whether the bar, the count, the previous and next controls and the caption are not drawn (`controls-hidden`). The person changes it by one tap on the picture, and the preview then fires `controlshiddenchange`; any key, focus on a control or a moving mouse shows them again (IMP-25). Hidden controls stay in the focus order and exposed to assistive technology. Reflected.

members.name: view
members.description: IMP-12 to IMP-17: where the image shown is.

members.name: stage
members.description: IMP-11: the stage and the fit area in it, as last measured (px, from the stage's top left corner).

members.name: opener
members.description: IMP-4: where focus was when it opened.

members.name: presented
members.description: Presented: in the top layer.

members.name: reportedEmpty
members.description: IMP-43: an opening with nothing to show was reported, until there is something.

members.name: lastTap

type.text: { x: number; y: number; time: number; timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> } | null

members.description: IMP-14: the last single press, which a second one within the interval makes a double tap.

members.name: hiddenAt
members.description: IMP-25: where the pointer was when the controls were hidden by a press: a mouse shows them again once it has moved from there.

members.name: gestureView
members.description: IMP-15: the view when a trackpad pinch that arrives as a gesture event began.

members.name: focusLeaves
members.description: IMP-28: the control that had focus when it became disabled: focus goes to the stage once it is drawn so.

members.name: readImages
members.description: The images, read from its children in order.

members.name: within
members.description: IMP-20: `index` within the images: the nearest that exists.

members.name: syncPictures
members.description: IMP-32: the picture of each of the three images, asked for as its `src` says now; every other is let go.

members.name: ready
members.description: IMP-13, IMP-29, IMP-31: whether the image shown can be enlarged: it has loaded.

members.name: fitSize
members.description: IMP-11: the size an image has at fit: the largest at which the whole of it lies in the fit area, never above its own.

members.name: baseAt
members.description: The size the image at `at` has at fit: from its own size, else its thumbnail's proportions, else the fit area (IMP-29).

members.name: limits
members.description: IMP-12: the greatest zoom of the image shown and its steps.

members.name: held
members.description: IMP-17: `view` within its limits: each edge of the image can reach the matching edge of the fit area and no farther; centred along an axis it does not fill.

members.name: reach
members.description: How far the image shown can be moved from the centre, each way, at its zoom.

members.name: zoomedAbout
members.description: `view` at the zoom `z`, with the point of the image at (`ax`, `ay`) from the centre of the fit area kept there (IMP-13 to IMP-15), within the limits (IMP-17).

members.name: measure
members.description: IMP-11, IMP-40: the stage and the fit area, measured; true when either changed.

members.name: place
members.description: Where everything on the pages is drawn: each image at its fit, the one shown at its zoom and place.

members.name: still
members.description:
Ends a motion of the image shown where it is drawn now (a step of the zoom that a pinch or a drag interrupts): the
view becomes what is drawn, so the person's gesture goes on from what they see.

members.name: stepTo
members.description: IMP-13, IMP-14: the image shown moves to `view` over the zoom motion — at once where motion is reduced (IMP-34).

members.name: commitZoom
members.description: IMP-21: the zoom the person's change ended at becomes `zoom`, and `zoomchange` is fired once for it.

members.name: stepZoom
members.description: IMP-13: one step up or down, or to fit, about the centre of the fit area.

members.name: doubleTap
members.description: IMP-14: fit to the first step with the point under the tap kept there, and any other zoom to fit.

members.name: go
members.description: IMP-20: the person moved to the image at `to`: it slides in as the one shown slides out; `index`, then `indexchange`.

members.name: show
members.description:
IMP-20: the image shown is the one at `index`: the zoom returns to 1 and the image left to its fit, and the new one
is said (IMP-28). True where the zoom was not 1: the caller fires `zoomchange`, after `zoom` is written.

members.name: settle
members.description: The pages move to where they rest over the page motion (IMP-18, IMP-20) — at once where motion is reduced.

members.name: onFaded

members.name: hideControls
members.description: IMP-21: the person hid or showed the controls.

members.name: emit
members.description: Its events bubble and leave the shadow root (the names are the class's `@fires` lines).

members.name: requestClose
members.description: IMP-5: `close` with the reason, once for each asking, while it is presented.

members.name: onControl
members.description: The Buttons' clicks do not leave the preview: it answers them.

members.name: onKeyDownFirst
members.description: IMP-25: any key shows the controls, before the control answers (heard on the way down).

members.name: onNativeCancel
members.description: IMP-5: a close request without a key the preview saw (Android's back) arrives as the native cancel.

members.name: onNativeClose
members.description: The browser closed the dialog itself (a close request it would not let the preview cancel): ask, and stay unless closed.

members.name: onFocusIn
members.description: IMP-25: focus that reaches a control shows the controls. IMP-26, IMP-27: the focus style of the stage and of the caption, where style queries are missing.

members.name: onFocusOut
members.description:
IMP-3, IMP-23: focus stays inside. An engine that gives a button no focus for a press takes focus from where it was
and puts it on nothing: the keys would then reach no part of the preview. Focus that has left for nothing, in a
window that still has it, is on the stage again.

members.name: point
members.description: A point of the window, from the stage's top left corner.

members.name: beginPinch
members.description: IMP-15: two fingers: the zoom follows their distance about the point midway between them, and the image their move.

members.name: begin

type.text: { id: number; x: number; y: number }

members.name: drawnDrag
members.description: How far the pages are drawn from where they rest, sideways (px).

members.name: speed
members.description: The speed of a release along what `samples` hold, px per ms; 0 when the pointer had stopped.

members.name: endDrag
members.description: A drag that is taken over (a second finger) ends where it rests.

members.name: comeBack
members.description: IMP-22: everything back to where it rests, over the page motion.

members.name: fling
members.description: IMP-16: the image goes on as it was flung (`vx`, `vy`, px per ms) and slows, to its limit at most.

members.name: tap
members.description: IMP-14, IMP-24: a press without a drag: the second of two within the interval is a double tap, and one alone hides or shows the controls.

members.name: onWheel
members.description: IMP-15, IMP-16: a wheel with Ctrl or Command — and a trackpad pinch, which arrives as one — zooms about the pointer; without, it moves an enlarged image; at fit it does nothing.

members.name: onGesture
members.description: IMP-15: a trackpad pinch where the browser tells it as a gesture of its own (its `scale` from 1), not as a wheel.

members.name: giveVariants

members.name: present
members.description: IMP-1, IMP-2: in the top layer over the whole window, the page held, focus on the stage.

members.name: withdraw
members.description: IMP-4: out of the top layer (fading), the page given back, focus back where it was.

members.name: say
members.description: IMP-28: what assistive technology is told, politely: each sentence a block of its own, in place of what was said.

members.name: countSentence

members.name: zoomGiven
members.description: IMP-12: the product set `zoom`, and the image shown has not taken it yet (it has not loaded, or is not presented).

members.name: takeZoom
members.description: IMP-12: `zoom` as the product set it, once the image can take it: within 1 and the greatest value, about the centre of the fit area, at once.

members.name: disabledNow
members.description: IMP-10, IMP-13: whether a control is disabled as things are now.

declarations.name: CORE_VARIANTS
declarations.default: ['keycap', 'plain']
declarations.description: The values every design system has. A layer may add more; those get their styles on demand.

declarations.name: CORE_SIZES
declarations.default: ['small', 'medium']

declarations.name: AXES
declarations.default: [ { name: 'size', core: CORE_SIZES, default: DEFAULT_SIZE, rules: (value, selector) => sizeBlock(value, selector, DEFAULT_SIZE), probe: (value) => `${PREFIX}-container-height-${value}` }, { name: 'variant', core: CORE_VARIANTS, default: DEFAULT_VARIANT, rules: (value, selector) => variantBlock(value, selector, DEFAULT_VARIANT), probe: (value) => `${PREFIX}-${value}-label-color` }, ]
declarations.description:
The open axes: a size or variant a layer added gets its block on demand, built by the same functions as the
core blocks and falling back to the default's tokens; a value the active system lacks is reported in debug builds. A
variant a layer adds is drawn in caps; only `plain` draws none (KBS-7).

declarations.name: styles
declarations.default: css` /* KBS-15: inline with the text around it, the legends on its baseline; KBS-16: left to right, isolated from the surrounding direction. */ :host { display: inline-flex; position: relative; align-items: baseline; vertical-align: baseline; max-inline-size: 100%; direction: ltr; unicode-bidi: isolate; } :host([hidden]) { display: none; } ${unsafeCSS(sizeBlock(DEFAULT_SIZE, ':host'))} ${unsafeCSS(CORE_SIZES.filter((size) => size !== DEFAULT_SIZE).map((size) => sizeBlock(size, `:host([size='${size}'])`)).join('\n'))} ${unsafeCSS(variantBlock(DEFAULT_VARIANT, ':host'))} ${unsafeCSS(CORE_VARIANTS.filter((v) => v !== DEFAULT_VARIANT).map((v) => variantBlock(v, `:host([variant='${v}'])`)).join('\n'))} /* KBS-10: the one text read in place of the drawn keys, never drawn. */ .spoken { position: absolute; inline-size: 1px; block-size: 1px; overflow: hidden; clip-path: inset(50%); white-space: nowrap; } /* KBS-8, KBS-15: the chords in order, a sequence gap apart, breaking a line only between chords. */ .sequence { display: inline-flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: baseline; column-gap: var(--_sequence); row-gap: var(--_chord); max-inline-size: 100%; } kbd { font: inherit; } /* KBS-6, KBS-15: the keys of a chord, a chord gap apart (the separator between them where the convention writes one), their legends on one baseline, never broken across lines. */ .chord { display: inline-flex; align-items: baseline; column-gap: var(--_chord); white-space: nowrap; } .key { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; } /* KBS-6: a cap at least its size's height tall and as wide as tall, growing with its legend (KBS-15), the legend centered with the size's padding on each side; its fill, and its edge inside its size — the deeper edge at its bottom — and the size's corners eased by the smoothing. The edge is a border of the tokens' widths and nothing else: a width of 0 (both, in the default system) is no border at all — no least width is applied — and the cap is its fill alone. */ ${unsafeCSS(CAPS)} { box-sizing: border-box; min-block-size: var(--_height); min-inline-size: var(--_height); padding-inline: var(--_pad); background: ${T('container-color')}; border: ${T('outline-width')} solid ${T('outline-color')}; border-block-end-width: ${T('outline-bottom-width')}; ${unsafeCSS(cornerRadius('--_shape'))} } ${shape} /* KBS-6, KBS-7: the legends and the separators in the size's text role and the variant's legend color. */ .label, .separator { font: var(--_font); letter-spacing: var(--_tracking); color: var(--_legend); white-space: nowrap; } /* KBS-7: the plain form writes each chord as one run of text: no cap, fill or edge, and nothing between the keys. */ :host([variant='plain']) .chord { column-gap: 0; } /* KBS-9: disabled fades the legends and separators; the caps stay at rest. */ :host([disabled]) .label, :host([disabled]) .separator { color: var(--_legend-d); } /* KBS-13: hosted in another component's part, the legends take that part's text style and color. */ .sequence.hosted .label, .sequence.hosted .separator { font: inherit; letter-spacing: inherit; color: inherit; } @media (forced-colors: active) { ${unsafeCSS(CAPS)} { border-color: CanvasText; } :host([disabled]) .label, :host([disabled]) .separator { color: GrayText; } } `

declarations.description:
Shows the keys that perform a command, as keys or as text, in the modifier symbols and names of the keyboard the
person is using, read aloud in the product's own words.

Contract: specs/keyboard-shortcut.spec.json. Write the keys once, in neutral names — `<tanrei-keyboard-shortcut
keys="mod+shift+k">` draws ⇧⌘K on Apple platforms and Ctrl+Shift+K elsewhere; `keys="mod+k mod+c"` is a sequence of
two chords. It only shows keys: it takes no focus and no input, and does not make them work (KBS-14). Every visual value
is a `--tanrei-comp-keyboard-shortcut-*` token.

What is drawn is hidden from assistive technology; one visually hidden text is read in its place, where the shortcut
sits: `label`, the shortcut in the product's own words ("Shift Command K", KBS-10) — and without it the notation of
`aria-keyshortcuts` ("Meta+Shift+K", KBS-11), because Tanrei has no names for keys in any language. The convention is `convention`, or under
`auto` the nearest ancestor's `data-tanrei-keyboard-convention` (`apple` or `standard`), else the platform's (KBS-2).
declarations.name: TanreiKeyboardShortcut

members.name: keys
members.description:
The shortcut: one chord per string, pressed in order. A chord is key names joined by + (`mod+shift+k`): the modifiers
mod (Command on Apple platforms, Control elsewhere), ctrl, alt and shift; the named keys enter, escape, tab,
backspace, delete, space, arrow-up, arrow-down, arrow-left, arrow-right, home, end, page-up, page-down, caps-lock,
f1 to f24 and plus; any other single character is that character's key. Names ignore case. The attribute holds the
chords separated by spaces (`keys="mod+k mod+c"`).

members.name: variant
members.description: How the keys are drawn: `keycap` puts each key in its own cap; `plain` writes the shortcut as a line of text.

members.name: size
members.description: `small` (20 caps, 12 text) sits in a line of body text or a menu row; `medium` (24 caps, 14 text) beside larger text.

members.name: convention
members.description: Whose keyboard the keys are written for: `apple`, `standard`, or `auto` — the nearest ancestor's, else the platform's.

members.name: label
members.description: What assistive technology reads in place of the drawn keys: the shortcut in the product's own words ("Shift Command K"). Tanrei has no names for keys: without it the notation of `aria-keyshortcuts` is read ("Meta+Shift+K").

members.name: ariaKeyShortcuts
members.description:
KBS-12: the shortcut in the form `aria-keyshortcuts` takes — each chord's modifiers then its key joined by +, mod as
Meta under the apple convention and Control under the standard one, the chords separated by spaces (`Meta+Shift+K`;
`Control+K Control+C`) — or null without keys. Read-only: a component that hosts the shortcut (a menu item) sets it on
its own element. The shortcut itself sets no `aria-keyshortcuts`: it only shows keys.

declarations.description: One link drawn as a block: the destination's title, a sentence about it, its picture and the site it is on — from values the card is given and never loads. The host under the text is always computed from `href`. Contract: specs/link-card.spec.json. The element has **no shadow root**: it is the box around the product's own anchor, which stays in the document — a link before any script runs, for a crawler, a reader mode and the browser's own menu (LKC-1). ```html Designing with tokens How a handful of dials becomes a whole system. Example Journal example.com ``` That markup is what `linkCardToNodes()` / `linkCardToHtml()` of `@tanrei/web/links/node` write where a site is built; `@tanrei/web/link-card.css` draws all of it before and without this script, so a page of link cards does not move when the script arrives (LKC-36). The script adds what a document cannot hold: the host computed anew from `href` (one written in the document that differs is replaced, and reported), the title as the link's name and the other parts as its description, `data-external` where the page was not marked, a picture that fails taken away, the shared press primitive, and the debug reports. **A card the element builds.** A `` that holds no anchor is given one from its attributes — `href`, `headline`, `description`, `image`, `image-alt`, `site-name`, `site-icon`, `target`, `target-label`, `external`, `external-label` — each value cleaned and written as text, never as markup (LKC-15). That form is drawn when the element is defined, not before. Where the element holds the product's own anchor, an attribute that is given is written over that anchor's part and one that is not leaves the markup as it is. **It requests nothing about the destination** (LKC-14): no address is derived from `href`, and the only requests are the two pictures it was given, each an `` asked for without the page's address.

slots.description: The product's own anchor, holding the parts (`data-part`: `body` around `title`, `description`, `image-alt`, `site` and `words`; then `media`). A child in the document, not a slotted node: the element has no shadow root. Nothing in it is pressed by itself (LKC-35).

members.name: target
members.description: Where the destination opens: `same` (where the person is) or `new` (a new tab or window, marked with open_in_new and said through `targetLabel`). HTML's `_blank` and `_self` are read as the two.

members.name: targetLabel

members.name: image

members.name: read
members.description:
Reads the card and writes what follows from it: the anchor and the parts the properties ask for, then what a
document cannot hold — the host, the marks, the name and the description, the pictures' attributes and failures.
Called when a property changes and when the card's content does (LKC-34); it writes only what differs, so it
settles. It asks the network for nothing (LKC-14): the only addresses it writes are the two pictures it was given.

members.name: speaks

members.name: write

members.name: picture
members.description: LKC-10, LKC-11, LKC-14: a picture the card was given, as an `` and nothing else — asked for without the page's address and only once the card is near what is shown. An address that is no picture's is treated as empty.

members.name: enhance
members.description: What a document cannot hold (LKC-36), written on the product's own anchor and on one this element built alike.

members.name: give
members.description: Writes `wanted` on the anchor, leaving alone what the product wrote there itself, and takes off only what this element wrote.

members.name: readPicture
members.description:
A picture as the document holds it: what the markup left out is written (the build step writes all of it, so the
first request already carries it), an address that is no picture's is taken away, another party's is reported, and
one that has already failed is taken away. Returns the picture where it is still there.

members.name: failed
members.description: LKC-10, LKC-13: a picture that cannot be loaded is taken away — no mark, no text, no box — and not asked for again.

declarations.description:
One row of a list — the spec's item kind `list-item`: a headline with an optional overline, supporting
text, leading icon or media and trailing text, icon or control. Placed as a child of `<tanrei-list>`, which decides
whether it is an option; otherwise it is static, one action with `interactive`, or a link with `href`.

Contract: specs/list.spec.json. Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-list-*` tokens, one set per condition
(unselected, selected) and state. How a press is answered and how keyboard focus is drawn are the system's choices of
kind (`--tanrei-sys-behavior-*`), read from the cascade.

Semantics: the host is a `listitem` — or, in a selectable list, an `option` with its selected state, named by the
headline and described by the overline, supporting text and trailing text, which takes focus itself. An interactive
item draws one element with the button role inside its list item, named and described the same way. The list sets
each item's position and the list's size (`aria-posinset`, `aria-setsize`) and which one is the tab stop.

With `href` (and outside a selectable list) the item is a link item (LST-31): an `<a href>` in place of the
element with the button role, inside the host's list item, in the list's one tab stop and arrow-key order, drawn as an
interactive item is. Enter follows it and Space does not; `click` fires first and cancelling it cancels the
navigation. `target="new"` opens a new tab, safely (`noopener`), draws the icon set's `open_in_new` as the trailing
icon unless `trailing-icon` names one, and reads `target-label` at the end of the item's description.

declarations.description:
Shows a column of related items that people read, open one by one, choose from, or put in another order.

Contract: specs/list.spec.json. The list draws nothing and adds no space around its `<tanrei-list-item>` children;
it carries the semantics — a `list`, or a `listbox` named by `label` while `selection` is `single` or `multiple` — and
moves keyboard focus among the items: one tab stop (a roving tabindex), Up and Down Arrow without wrapping, Home, End
and typeahead. Moving focus never changes the selection; Space or Enter chooses.

The selection is the list's: `value` names the selected option of a single-select list, `values` those
of a multiple-select list, each by the options' `value`. The list sets them before firing `change`, as a native
control does; set them yourself to select from script (a new array for `values`).

With `reorder="buttons"` (and `selection` none) the list is reorderable (LST-36): every item is static and draws two
move buttons — Tanrei Buttons, each a focus stop of its own in reading order, before the item's trailing control —
and the list is not one tab stop and handles no key. A press fires `move` with `from` and `to` and changes nothing:
the order is your data. Reorder your items in answer (move the elements, or let your framework render the new
order) and the list draws the two rows changing place, keeps focus on the same button of the moved item — on its
other button once it is first or last — and says `moved-text` once through its one polite live region, with
`{headline}`, `{position}` (from 1) and `{count}` filled. A move you have not made within
`--tanrei-comp-list-motion-reorder-duration` is taken as refused: nothing is announced. The three words are yours
(`move-up-label`, `move-down-label`, `moved-text`, or once with `setWords()`): without them the buttons work unnamed
and nothing is announced, and a debug build says so. The spec's `reorder="drag"` (a handle a pointer drags) is not
built yet and is read as `buttons`.

slots.description: The items: `<tanrei-list-item>` children.

members.name: selection
members.description: Whether people choose items: `none` shows or opens things; `single` chooses one; `multiple` any number.

members.name: label
members.description: The accessible name of the list: what the items are. Required while `selection` is `single` or `multiple`.

members.name: value
members.description: The value of the selected option while `selection` is `single`; `null` selects none.

members.name: values
members.description: The values of the selected options while `selection` is `multiple`. Assign a new array to change it.

members.name: reorder
members.description:
Whether people can put the items in another order: `none` fixes it; `buttons` draws in every item a button that
moves it up and one that moves it down. The list fires `move` and never changes the order itself: the items are
your data. Read only while `selection` is `none`, and every item of a reorderable list is static (LST-36). The
spec's `drag` is not built yet: it is read as `buttons` and reported in debug builds.

members.name: moveUpLabel
members.description: The accessible name of the button that moves an item up by one place: your sentence with the place `{headline}`, which the list fills with the item's headline ("Move {headline} up"). Empty reads the product's words (`setWords({ moveUpLabel })`); Tanrei has none, and without them the button works unnamed (LST-38).

members.name: moveDownLabel
members.description: The accessible name of the button that moves an item down by one place ("Move {headline} down"). As `moveUpLabel`.

members.name: movedText
members.description:
The sentence assistive technology is told once an item stands in its new place. Write the whole sentence in your
language and mark three places, which the list fills: `{headline}` with the moved item's headline, `{position}`
with the place it now has, counted from 1, and `{count}` with the number of items. Empty reads the product's words
(`setWords({ movedText })`); Tanrei has no sentence, and without one nothing is announced (LST-38).

members.name: lastFocused
members.description: LST-15: the item that had focus last, which stays the tab stop.

members.name: words

members.name: stacked
members.description: LST-51: whether the controls of every item stand below its text.

members.name: pending
members.description: LST-41: the move that was emitted and is not answered yet.

members.name: held
members.description: LST-41, LST-52: where keyboard focus stands among the items' controls.

members.name: returning
members.description: The record `keepFocus()` is returning focus to, until it has: a loss of focus meanwhile does not drop it.

members.name: places

members.description: LST-43: where each item was drawn (its top, from the list's), and the motions that are running.

members.name: raised
members.description: LST-43: the item the last move was asked for, drawn above the one it passes.

members.name: items
members.description: The items, in order: the list's `<tanrei-list-item>` children.

members.name: mode
members.description: LST-7: a selection the list does not define is drawn as `none`.

members.name: reorderable
members.description: LST-36: reorderable while nothing is chosen from it and `reorder` asks for the buttons (`drag` is read as them, until its handle is built).

members.name: announcer
members.description: LST-42: the one live region, while the list is reorderable.

members.name: chosen
members.description: LST-26: which values are selected now.

members.name: sync
members.description: Tells every item what it is now (LST-12, LST-15, LST-26, LST-36) and reports what a debug build should (LST-23, LST-26, LST-38).

members.name: scheduleReports
members.description:
LST-26: an option without a value, a value two options share, and a selected value that names no option — reported a
frame after the list changed, against what it holds then: while the page is still being parsed, or an item is still
upgrading, the list is briefly without items or values it is about to have.

members.name: settle
members.description:
LST-41: whether the product has given the order that was asked for — the moved item stands at `to`, as the element
it was or as a new one for the same content — and, if so, what follows: the announcement and the focus.

members.name: motion
members.description: The reorder motion's time (in milliseconds) and curve as the cascade computes them: a duration token is an expression (LST-41, LST-43).

members.name: announce
members.description:
LST-42: the product's sentence with its places filled, put into the live region in place of what it held. The
headline is a run of its own direction, isolated from the sentence (LST-30); the two numbers are written as the
list's language writes a whole number. LST-38: without the sentence nothing is announced.

members.name: keepFocus
members.description:
LST-41, LST-52: puts keyboard focus back on the control it was on. An element the product moves in the document, or
replaces, loses focus without anything having taken it: the same control of the same item gets it back, or — the
item gone — the control in the same place of the item that now stands where it stood, else of the one before it.
Where that control is absent or disabled, the first control of that item that can take focus; where the list is
empty or the item has none, focus is left to the product. `moved`: a move took effect, so focus goes to the moved
item wherever the browser left it.

members.name: laidOut
members.description: An item's top as it is laid out, from the window's: without what a running motion adds to it.

members.name: recordPlaces
members.description: LST-43: where every item is drawn now. Read when the list's box changes and when a move is asked for, never at rest.

members.name: placesChanged
members.description:
LST-43: the order changed — every item whose place changed moves from where it was drawn to its new place, along
the list's axis, without fading or scaling, the focus ring with the item that holds it. An element the product
gave anew for an item it had is moved as that item; an item that is new or gone appears or leaves at once. Where
motion is reduced the new order is drawn at once.

members.name: measureStacked
members.description:
LST-51: where the controls of any item would leave its text less than half its row, the controls of every item
stand on a line of their own.

members.name: onSlotChange
members.description: The list's children changed: what each item is, where each is drawn, and where focus stands.

members.name: onKeyDown
members.description: LST-15: arrows, Home, End and typeahead move focus among the items that take it, without wrapping.

members.name: onFocusOut
members.description:
Focus left a control of a reorderable item. Where it went somewhere — another control, the page — the list holds
nothing any more, and its live region is at rest (LST-42). Where the item was taken out of its place by the
product, nothing took focus: the record stays, and `keepFocus()` reads it when the children have changed.

declarations.description:
Shows that a short wait of unknown length is under way, inline or over content.

Contract: specs/loading-indicator.spec.json. A quarter arc that turns once per cycle, with no track; `contained` draws
it on a raised circle of its own, for waits over content. Every visual value is a `--tanrei-comp-loading-indicator-*`
token. When the length of the wait can be measured, use `<tanrei-progress-indicator>` instead.

Insert it when the wait starts and remove it when the wait ends. From its insertion it waits `showDelay` (null takes
`motion.show-delay`) with its box kept, drawing nothing and exposing nothing (`aria-hidden="true"`); then it enters
(`entrance`: fade, or grow from its center, over `enterDuration`) and the arc starts turning. Moving it within the
document starts a new delay; hiding it (`hidden`, CSS, scrolling) neither restarts nor pauses it. A change of
`showDelay`, `entrance` or `enterDuration` applies from the next insertion.

Once shown, the host is a progressbar with no value (`role="progressbar"`, `aria-label` from `label`,
`aria-busy="true"`). It is never focusable and never announces itself: mark the region being loaded `aria-busy` and
announce its arrival in the product. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the arc stops turning and the whole circle
pulses, and grow enters as a fade; the delay is kept. Off screen, the turning is paused (the entrance is not).

declarations.description: Performs the single most important action of a screen on a raised container that floats above the content, showing its icon and its written name (extended), or collapsing to its icon alone. Contract: specs/main-action-button.spec.json. Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-main-action-button-*` tokens, one set per variant and state — the container color, the label color (the icon's too) and the elevation: how a state looks is the active design system's decision, not this component's. How a press is answered and how keyboard focus is drawn are the system's choices of kind (`--tanrei-sys-behavior-*`), and how far its corners ease is the system's amount (`--tanrei-sys-shape-corner-smoothing`); all are read from the cascade, so they follow `data-tanrei-system`. `label` is the visible text while extended and the accessible name in either form. The icon is the `icon` slot: a glyph of the system's icon set, given as its ligature text (`edit`), drawn in the label color at the size's icon size, on the side `iconPosition` names. `extended = false` (the `collapsed` attribute) collapses the button to a square holding only the icon, over the resize motion. Without an icon it stays extended; without a label it never extends (both reported in debug builds). It is an action, never a toggle: it has no pressed, selected or expanded state, and collapsing changes no role, name or focus. The element does not position itself (MAB-18): it is inline, at its own size, and the page places it; which edge stays put while it collapses is the layout's decision too (an element anchored at the inline end collapses toward it).
