declarations.description: An item of any kind (MNU-10…22, MNU-27, MNU-37…42): the row, its columns, its texts, its mark and the submenu indicator.

declarations.name: placeMenu

type.text: { anchor: MenuBox; surface: { width: number; height: number }; viewport: { width: number; height: number }; placement: TanreiMenuPlacement; offset: number; margin: number; rtl: boolean }

declarations.description:
Where the surface goes (MNU-2): `offset` from the anchor on the placement's side, flipped to the other side when this
one has less room than the surface needs within `margin` of the viewport's edge and the other has more; aligned by its
start or end edge with the anchor's (mirrored in right-to-left), then shifted along the anchor to stay `margin` inside
the viewport; its height limited to the room left. Coordinates are the viewport's (`left` is physical).

declarations.name: placeSubmenu
declarations.description:
Where a submenu's surface goes (MNU-46, MNU-47): beside the surface that holds its item (`parent`), `offset` from that
surface's inline-end edge — or from the side `prefer` names, the side its parent surface was itself placed on — and on
the other side when this one has less room than the surface needs within `margin` of the viewport's edge and the
other has more. Where the side it is on has room for `minWidth` but not for the surface, the surface is narrowed to
the room. Where neither side has room for `minWidth` it is laid over `parent`: on the side with more room, as far
towards it as the margin allows, as wide as leaves `touch` of the parent uncovered on its other side and never
narrower than `minWidth`. Its first row (`lead` below its own block-start edge) is level with the item's `row`, then
it is shifted along the block axis to stay `margin` inside the viewport, its height limited to the room.
Coordinates are the viewport's (`left` and `side` are physical).

declarations.name: inTriangle
declarations.description: Whether `p` lies in the triangle `a`, `b`, `c` (its edges included). MNU-45: the pointer's path to a submenu.

What every row of a menu is (the spec's `item`, `checkbox-item`, `radio-item` and `submenu` kinds): a label, optional
supporting text, a leading icon and trailing text. The host carries the row's semantics and takes focus — except a
link item (MNU-53), whose row is the browser's own link: the anchor in its shadow root carries them, and the host is
nothing to assistive technology. The menu moves focus among the rows of a surface, tells each its position, the
surface's size and which columns the surface reserves, and answers its activation.
declarations.name: TanreiMenuRowBase

members.name: label
members.description: The item's text and its accessible name. Required.

members.name: supportingText
members.description: A line below the label that says more about the item; it is the item's description.

members.name: leadingIcon
members.description: The name of a glyph of the system's icon set before the label. A glyph the icon set flags as showing a direction (`arrow_forward`, `send`) is drawn mirrored in a right-to-left layout.

members.name: trailingText
members.description:
Text at the end of the row that is not a keyboard shortcut, such as a count or "Beta": it is the item's description,
never its keyboard shortcut. An item's shortcut goes in `shortcut`; an item that has both draws the shortcut.

members.name: disabled
members.description: Prevents activation. The item stays reachable with the arrow keys.

members.name: context
members.default: { position: 0, size: 0, markColumn: false, iconColumn: false, trailingIconColumn: false, radioChecked: false, shortcutVariant: DEFAULT_SHORTCUT_VARIANT, groupMarkIcon: '', }
members.description: What the menu says about this item.

members.name: pointerFocused
members.description: MNU-8: focus the pointer moved here, which draws no focus ring.

members.name: glyphs
members.description:
MNU-30: a glyph the menu draws — the check of a mark, the check in a checked box, a named mark, the submenu
indicator — carries `data-drawn` while the icon set can draw it rather than spell its name in a fallback face. Its
ink — the glyph's name at its own width — is watched for any change of size: the icon face loading or failing, the
family changing with the system, the menu opening.

members.name: mirror
members.description:
MNU-33: the leading and trailing glyphs, the glyph a `mark-icon` names and the submenu indicator are marked when the
icon set mirrors their names in right-to-left (`arrow_right`, `chevron_right`, `undo`), and `iconGlyph()` draws the
mark. The check (MNU-22, MNU-39) is not among them: it is never mirrored.

declarations.description:
An action in a menu — the spec's item kind `item`: it does something and closes the menu.

With `href` it is a link item (MNU-53): the row is an `<a href role="menuitem" tabindex="-1">` in the shadow
root, drawn exactly as an action is and moved to with the same keys, and the browser's own link in everything else —
its context menu, a new tab by a modified or a middle click, its address shown on hover. It is exposed as a menu
item, not as a link: a menu is read by its items. A plain activation — a click, a touch, Enter, and Space too, which
activates every row of a menu — fires the item's `click` (the anchor's own: `preventDefault()` cancels the
navigation, as a router does), then the menu's `close`, and then the browser follows the link (MNU-54). A modified
or a middle click is the browser's: no `close`, and the menu stays open. `target="new"` opens a new tab, safely
(`noopener`), ends the row with the icon set's `open_in_new` in the trailing icon column unless `trailing-icon` names
a glyph, and is said through `targetLabel` (MNU-55). A disabled link item is the anchor without `href` (MNU-56).

declarations.description:
Offers a short set of actions or choices on a temporary surface that opens from the element that asked for it, with
further levels in submenus where the set needs them.

Contract: specs/menu.spec.json. The surface is a manual popover in the top layer, placed against the anchor (the
element whose id is `anchor`) by script: below or above it as `placement` says, flipping and shifting to stay inside
the viewport, scrolling when it is taller than the room, following the anchor while it moves. The menu is an operated
overlay that is not modal: it moves focus to its first enabled item when it opens and back to the anchor
when it closes, never traps focus and draws no scrim. It never closes itself: it fires `close` with a reason — Escape,
a press outside the surface and the anchor, Tab, focus leaving it, an item's activation — and you set `open` to false.

A `<tanrei-submenu>` among the items opens another level beside its row (MNU-42 … MNU-52), by the WAI-ARIA menu
pattern: the arrow key that points to the inline end, Enter, Space, a press or a tap open it and move focus in; the
opposite arrow key and Escape close one level and return focus to its item; a pointer that rests on the item opens it
after `comp.menu.motion.submenu-delay`, and may then cross other items on its way in. Every surface of the tree is
inside the menu: a press in a submenu is not a press outside, and whatever closes the menu closes every level with one
`close`.

A group is told from what is next to it as `separation` names (MNU-35): a divider, or a gap of
`comp.menu.group.gap`; `auto` takes `comp.menu.separation`, which follows the design system's choice.

Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-menu-*` tokens, the items' by condition (unselected, selected,
destructive, expanded) and state. The `inline` attribute, for tests and documentation, draws the open surface in place
instead: at its natural size, with its elevation, without an anchor, placement, open motion, focus on opening or light
dismiss, each open submenu beside its item.

A component that holds a menu in its shadow root may forward its own children into it: a `<slot>` child of the menu
stands for the elements assigned to it, each forwarded child in a slot of its own (the split button, SPB-15).

declarations.name: titleStyles
declarations.description:
A title (MBR-2 … MBR-8, MBR-17, MBR-28, MBR-29) — a menu's, the overflow item's, and the copies the bar measures —
as three boxes:

  .title      the room the title takes in the row and everything of it that answers a pointer: at least the minimum
              target long, and by its `::before` as tall as the target and half the gap further toward each
              neighbour, so that two hit areas meet in the middle of the gap and never overlap (MBR-17)
  .container  what is drawn and what carries the states: the title's height, paddings and corners, centred in .title
  .content    the label, or the overflow item's glyph; a bar item's label and, for a link item that opens a new
              context, the mark after it (MBR-37)

A bar item (MBR-32) is a title in all of this: the same three boxes, the same rules, always unselected. Its link
form is the product's own anchor, slotted into `.label` (`itemStyles` below gives the anchor the title's box).

`focused` names where keyboard focus is read, given the condition: the element that takes the title's focus is the
menu's host, and for the overflow item its own box in the bar's shadow root. Every state selector has the same
specificity, so the order `stateRules()` writes them in is the precedence (MBR-4).

declarations.name: menuStyles
declarations.default: css` :host { position: relative; display: flex; flex: none; /* The ring is drawn around the container, never around the host. */ outline: none; } :host([hidden]) { display: none; } :host([data-tanrei-folded]) { display: contents; } ${titleStyles((focus) => `:host(${focus})`)} /* MBR-9: the menu is a popover in the top layer, placed by script against the container. Drawn in place (the bar's inline, for tests), it stands below the title, comp.menu.surface.offset from it, their start edges together. */ .menu { position: absolute; inset-block-start: 100%; inset-inline-start: 0; } .menu[inline] { margin-block-start: var(--tanrei-comp-menu-surface-offset); } ${shape} `
declarations.description:
A menu of the bar (MBR-2, MBR-9): its title in the row, and — at no size of its own — the Menu it opens. Folded into
the overflow item (MBR-22) it has no box: the submenu item it draws is a row of the overflow item's menu.

declarations.name: itemStyles
declarations.default: css` :host { position: relative; display: flex; flex: none; /* The ring is drawn around the container, never around the host. */ outline: none; } :host([data-tanrei-folded]) { display: contents; } /* MBR-8: keyboard focus is the host's for an action; for a link item it is its anchor's, which the element marks on the host. */ ${titleStyles((focus) => `:host(${focus.replace(':focus-visible', ':is(:focus-visible, [data-tanrei-focus])')})`)} ::slotted(a) { font: inherit; letter-spacing: inherit; color: inherit; text-decoration: none; cursor: inherit; outline: none; -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent; } ::slotted(a)::before { content: ''; position: absolute; z-index: 1; inset-block: calc((100% - ${unsafeCSS(REACH)}) / 2); inset-inline: calc((100% - ${unsafeCSS(REACH)}) / 2 - ${t('bar-gap')} / 2); } /* MBR-43, MBR-45: folded, the product's anchor stays in the document and is not displayed. */ .kept { display: none; } /* MBR-43: a folded link item that names the current page keeps the emphasized weight, in the menu's own text style. */ tanrei-menu-item.current::part(label) { font-weight: var(--tanrei-comp-menu-label-typescale-font-weight-emphasized); } ${shape} `
declarations.description:
A bar item (MBR-32): a title in the row, drawn by the title's rules; folded (MBR-43), a row of the overflow item's
menu that it draws of itself, with no box of its own.

Its link form (MBR-35) is the product's own anchor, in the document, slotted into the label. The anchor is drawn as
the label is — the title's text style and the color of its state, no underline, no look of its own for a link or for
a visited one — and by its `::before` it is given the whole of the title's hit area (MBR-17: the target's height and,
on each side, half the gap beyond the room the title keeps), above the mark, so that every press on the title is a
press on the link and what a browser gives a link it gives anywhere on it. The focus ring is the container's, as for
every title: the anchor draws none. A product's own rule for its anchor wins over these, as over any slotted rule.

declarations.name: barStyles
declarations.default: css` :host { display: block; } :host([hidden]) { display: none; } /* MBR-1: no position, no edge, no elevation. Nothing is clipped: a title's focus ring has room (MBR-5). MBR-21: the row gives the bar no inline size of its own — what the bar could be at most, and must be at least, is the copies' (below), so that a bar in a place sized by its content is as long as its titles and one that folds does not shrink its place with every title it folds. */ .bar { box-sizing: border-box; display: flex; flex-wrap: nowrap; align-items: center; gap: ${t('bar-gap')}; padding-block: ${t('bar-padding-block')}; padding-inline: ${t('bar-padding-inline')}; background: ${t('bar-color')}; contain: inline-size; } /* MBR-2, MBR-21: every title keeps its own size. */ ::slotted(*) { flex: none; } .overflow { position: relative; display: flex; flex: none; outline: none; } ${titleStyles((focus) => `.overflow${focus} >`)} .menu { position: absolute; inset-block-start: 100%; inset-inline-start: 0; } .menu[inline] { margin-block-start: var(--tanrei-comp-menu-surface-offset); } /* MBR-21: what fits is measured from copies of every title, the overflow item and the gap — never drawn, never hit, nothing to assistive technology — laid out as the row would be with nothing folded, on lines of their own so that the bar is at least as long as its longest title and at most as long as all of them. They take no block size and nothing of them shows or scrolls. */ .ruler { box-sizing: border-box; position: relative; display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0 ${t('bar-gap')}; block-size: 0; padding-inline: ${t('bar-padding-inline')}; overflow: hidden; visibility: hidden; pointer-events: none; } .ruler > .apart { position: absolute; inset-block-start: 0; inset-inline-start: 0; } .ruler > .gap { inline-size: ${t('bar-gap')}; block-size: 0; } @media (forced-colors: active) { /* MBR-28: no fill for the bar. */ .bar { background: none; } } ${shape} `
declarations.description:
The bar (MBR-1, MBR-21): one row across the inline size its parent gives it, the bar's fill behind it, the titles
from the start edge a gap apart inside the paddings; the overflow item, a title of the bar's own, at the end of the
row; and the copies the fold is measured from.

One menu of a menubar — the spec's item kind `menu`: its title in the bar's row, and the items that open below it.

It holds the menu's own item elements as its children, exactly as `<tanrei-menu>` holds them, and forwards them — each
in a slot of its own, none of them moved — into a Tanrei Menu in its shadow root, a manual popover in the top layer
placed below its title. The host is the title: `role="menuitem"` with `aria-haspopup="menu"`, `aria-expanded`,
`aria-disabled`, its position among the bar's titles, and the bar's roving `tabindex`; it draws its label in its shadow
root from the `--tanrei-comp-menubar-*` tokens of its condition (unselected, or expanded while its menu is open) and
state. The bar it is in does the rest: the keys, the pointer, which menu is open, and folding it into the overflow
item when the row has no room — it is then drawn as a submenu item of the overflow item's menu, with the same label
and the same items, and `open` and `toggle` mean the same there.

`open` is its own: the bar sets it when the person opens or closes the menu and fires `toggle`; the product may set it
to open or close the menu itself, which fires none. The items' own `click`, `change` and `toggle` bubble through it.

declarations.description: A bar item of a menubar — the spec's item kind `item`: an entry of the row that acts by itself instead of opening a menu. It is drawn exactly as a menu's title is and reached by the same keys; nothing at rest tells them apart but their words, so name an action with a verb ("Run") and a link with its place ("Documentation"). **An action** is written with a `label`: ``. The host is the entry — `role="menuitem"` with neither `aria-haspopup` nor `aria-expanded`, `aria-disabled`, its position among the bar's entries and the bar's roving `tabindex` — and `click` is the host's own: a press, Enter, Space (on key up, as a button) and assistive technology produce it, once, after the menu of the bar that was open has closed. **A link item** is the same element around the product's own anchor, which stays in the document: `Documentation`. The anchor is the entry: the element writes `role="menuitem"`, the roving `tabindex` and the position on it and `role="none"` on the host, and draws the title around it. Everything a link is, is the anchor's — its text is the label, `href`, `target` (`_blank` opens a new context: the element adds `noopener` to `rel` and draws the icon set's `open_in_new` after the label), `aria-current="page"` (drawn at the emphasized weight, with no fill), `rel`, `download` — and the properties `label`, `href`, `target` and `current` of the host read the anchor and write it. `click` is the anchor's own click: `preventDefault()` cancels the navigation, a click with a modifier key or the middle button is the browser's, and so is Enter with a modifier key; Space follows the link as Enter does. The link works before the element is defined and where script does not run (`@tanrei/web/menubar.css` lays it out there). `disabled` on the host is the one statement that the entry is disabled; a disabled link item's anchor is written without `href`. Folded into the overflow item, a bar item is an item of that menu, which it draws of itself; its `click` is the same event of the same element.

declarations.description:
Keeps an application's commands within reach in one persistent row of named menus (File, Edit, View…), each opening
a menu below its title, with the arrow keys moving along the row and into each menu.

Contract: specs/menubar.spec.json. The host is `role="menubar"`, named by `label`; its children are
`<tanrei-menubar-menu>` elements, each of which is its title and holds its menu's items, and — for the one or two
entries that act by themselves — `<tanrei-menubar-item>` elements, an action or the product's own anchor as a link
item, drawn and reached as the titles are (a press, Enter or Space runs or follows one; the block arrow keys do
nothing on it; from a menu the inline arrow keys land on it and open nothing). The bar is one Tab stop: the
inline arrow keys, Home, End and a typed character move along the titles; Enter, Space and the block arrow keys open
a title's menu; from inside a menu the inline arrow keys go on to the neighbouring menu; Escape returns to the title
and Tab leaves the bar. While one menu is open a pointer that moves onto another title opens that one at once. It
shows one menu at a time, sets each menu's `open` and fires its `toggle`.

Titles that the row has no room for are folded whole, from the end, into one overflow item — the icon set's
`more_horiz`, named by `overflow-label` — whose menu holds each folded menu as a submenu. The bar measures what fits
and decides again when its size, its menus, a label, the text size or the direction changes. It draws no position,
edge or elevation of its own: you place it. Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-menubar-*` tokens; the
surfaces the titles open are Menus, drawn from `--tanrei-comp-menu-*`.

The `inline` attribute, for tests and documentation, draws an open menu in place below its title instead of in the
top layer, as the menu's own does: without placement, open motion, focus on opening or light dismiss.

declarations.description:
The bar (NVB-11, NVB-18): the parent's full width, at least container.height above the bottom inset, on its color and
elevation with its top edge — the same whichever destination is selected and while the indicator moves; its width,
less container.padding at its start and at its end, divided into equal cells in reading order (logical, so RTL
mirrors). The color reaches under the bottom and side insets, the destinations stay inside them.

The active indicator while it moves (NVB-15, NVB-27): one layer under the destinations, an item container's size, in
the selected destination's item container color, which the element places between the destinations' item containers —
sliding to a new selection, or where a dragged pointer is. At rest it is not drawn: the selected destination's item
container is the indicator, so it is never painted twice.

NVB-27: a sideways drag on the bar is the indicator's and a vertical one the page's (`touch-action: pan-y`).

declarations.description:
A destination (NVB-4…10, NVB-12…16, NVB-23): the shared destination styles with the icon indicator and the covered
colors as parts of every condition and the filled conditions, its cell the bar's full height and an equal share of its
width, narrower than the touch target when the bar is (NVB-6), its focus indicator held inside the bar (NVB-5: the room
around the item container is container.padding); then the item container that is the whole cell.

One destination of a navigation bar — the spec's item kind `destination`: an icon, a label under it and an
optional badge on the icon, inside the item container. Placed as a child of `<tanrei-navigation-bar>`, in order; the
bar decides whether it is the selected one and answers its activation.

It is a button, or with `href` a link (NVB-30): an `<a href>` in the shadow root, drawn exactly as the button
is, whose context menu, new-tab gestures and address are the browser's own — except that it is not dragged as a link,
because a sideways drag moves the active indicator. A link is not selected by a press (NVB-31): a plain activation
makes the bar fire `change` (or `reselect`) — cancelable, with `detail.href`, before the browser follows the link —
and the page shown next sets the bar's `value`; a modified or a middle click, a link whose `target` is `new` and a
download fire nothing. Without a `value` a link's `href` is its value. `target="new"` opens a new tab, safely
(`noopener`), and draws no mark — a cell has no place for one — so `targetLabel` says it (NVB-32). Space does not
activate a link.

It is named by its label whether or not the label is drawn, the selected one `aria-current="page"`, its badge's
text and then, for a link that opens a new context, `targetLabel` its description; its host is a list item of the
bar's list. Its icon and label are drawn twice: the second copy, in the covered colors and clipped to the active
indicator, is hidden from assistive technology (NVB-23).

Its properties are the shared destination's (`src/primitives/destination.ts`): `value`, `label`, `icon`, `disabled`,
`badge`, `badgeCount` (`badge-count`), `badgeLabel` (`badge-label`), `href`, `target`, `targetLabel`
(`target-label`) and the web-only `rel` and `download`.

declarations.description:
Three to five top-level destinations along the bottom edge of a compact window, one of them the current screen.

Contract: specs/navigation-bar.spec.json. `<tanrei-navigation-bar-item>` children are the destinations, in order. The
bar's `value` is the selected destination's value; the bar sets it when a destination is activated — pointer, Enter,
Space, `item.click()` — and then fires `change`, or `reselect` when the selected destination is activated again. The
host is a navigation landmark named by `label`.

A bar of links (NVB-30…33): a destination with `href` is a link, and the selected destination is the current page
(`aria-current="page"`) — one state, which in a site of separate pages the page says, through `value` (a link without
a `value` takes its `href`). The bar never writes `value` for a link: a plain activation (Enter, not Space) fires
`change` or `reselect` with `detail.href`, cancelable, before the browser follows the link (a router cancels it, goes
to `detail.href` itself and sets `value`), and the active indicator stays on the destination `value` selects until
`value` changes; a modified or a middle click, a link whose `target` is `new` and a download are the browser's and
fire nothing.

The bar is the ground the active indicator moves on: one constant color. Each destination's item container is its
whole equal share of the bar, held in from the bar's edges by `comp.navigation-bar.container.padding` — the same box
for every destination, whatever it holds — and it is where the active indicator, hover, press and the focus indicator
are drawn. When the selection changes, the active indicator — one layer of the bar — slides at its full size from the
previous destination's item container to the new one's, and the covered copy of every destination's icon and label is
clipped to it in the same frame (NVB-15, NVB-23); where nothing was selected it fades in, in place.

A drag across the bar — by touch, a pen or a mouse, past 8 px and further sideways than up or down, while a
destination is selected — carries the indicator with the pointer, its place and the covered colors changing
continuously (NVB-27). Nothing is selected before the release, which chooses the nearer of the two destinations the
indicator lies between (or the one a fling is toward), activates it as a tap would — `value`, one `change` — or
returns the indicator and fires nothing; a release on a link is a plain press on that link (`change` with its
`href`, the link followed, `value` not written), so the indicator returns to the destination `value` selects and goes
on to the chosen one when the product sets `value`; Escape, a cancelled pointer, or `value` set meanwhile returns it
(NVB-28, NVB-29).

Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-navigation-bar-*` tokens: `variant` chooses the conditions the
destinations are drawn from (tonal: unselected and selected; filled: filled-unselected and filled-selected). How a
press is answered and how keyboard focus is drawn are the system's choices of kind (`--tanrei-sys-behavior-*`).
The color reaches under `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` and the side insets; the destinations stay inside them.

members.description:
NVB-15: a new selection moves the active indicator from the destination drawn selected before — or from where the
indicator is, mid-way or where a released drag left it — to the new one. The first selection, and a destination
that arrives already selected, are put in place at once; so is every change of size or place without a new
selection (the styles draw the rest state).

NVB-29: while a drag lasts, a selection the product sets — or a destination under the indicator that it removes or
disables — ends the drag, and the indicator goes to the selected destination from where it is.

members.name: motion
members.description: A motion of the indicator's own, read through real properties of its layer — 0 where motion is reduced.

members.name: clock
members.description: A clock: an effect without keyframes on the indicator's layer (it draws nothing), whose progress follows `easing`.

members.name: slideTo
members.description:
NVB-15, NVB-28, NVB-29: the indicator goes to `to` over the selection motion — from where it is drawn, or from
`from`'s item container, at its full size all the way; with nowhere to come from it fades in on `to`, and with
nowhere to go it fades out where it is. At once where motion is reduced.

members.name: frame
members.description:
One frame of a slide: the indicator at the eased progress between where it started and the new destination's item
container as it is now, and every covered copy clipped to it — the look a drag draws with the indicator at that
place (NVB-27).

members.name: draw
members.description:
Draws the indicator at `box`, in `owner`'s colors (the destination it belongs to), and clips every destination's
covered copy to it in the same frame (NVB-23); `fill` is the destination drawn selected, whose own item container's
fill is not drawn meanwhile.

members.name: stopMoving
members.description: Nothing moves the indicator any longer; what is drawn stays as it is.

members.name: rest
members.description: The indicator at rest: the bar's layer is not drawn, and every destination's styles draw its item container and covered copy.

members.name: takeDrag
members.description:
NVB-27: the bar took the drag. The press activates nothing and the destination under it leaves its pressed state as
when a press ends; the indicator comes from where it is drawn — a running slide stops there — to the pointer's place
over the state motion (not where motion is reduced), following the pointer meanwhile.

members.name: placeAt
members.description:
NVB-27: where the indicator is drawn while the pointer is at `x` — on an enabled destination's item container at its
cell's centre, halfway between two neighbouring enabled ones where their cells meet, at the linear interpolation in
between — and the two destinations it lies between.

members.name: followPointer
members.description:
NVB-27: draws the indicator where the pointer is, in the frame it moves — without a motion of its own, except the
catch-up that brings it from where it rested — in the selected destination's colors.

members.name: releaseDrag
members.description:
NVB-28: a release chooses one enabled destination — the one the indicator is nearer to of the two it lies between
(the one after it from halfway on), or the one of the two a fling is toward. Another than the selected one is
activated as a tap activates it: with its own click, so the bar sets `value` and fires `change` once, and the
indicator settles from where the release left it. A link is pressed the same way and is not selected by it
(NVB-31): `change` with its `href`, the link followed, `value` not written — so the indicator returns to the
destination `value` selects, unless the product set `value` in its listener, and then it goes on to the chosen one
from where it is. The selected one: the indicator returns, and nothing is fired.

members.name: returnIndicator
members.description: NVB-28, NVB-29: the indicator goes back to the selected destination from where it is, over the selection motion.

events.description: The user activated another destination, or released a drag of the active indicator on one: `detail.value` (and, for a button destination, the bar's `value`) is its value. For a link it is fired before the link is followed, only for a plain activation of a link that opens in place, carries `detail.href`, leaves `value` to the page, and is cancelable: `preventDefault()` stops the browser's navigation.
events.name: change

events.description: The user activated the selected destination again: `detail.value` is its value; for a link, as `change`. A drag that returns the indicator to it does not fire it.
events.name: reselect

attributes.name: value
attributes.description: The value of the selected destination; empty selects none. The bar sets it when a button destination is activated, and never for a link (NVB-31): in a site of separate pages each page sets it to its own destination (a link's `href` where it has no `value`).

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description: How the active indicator is filled: `tonal` (a soft container, the default) or `filled` (the strong color, the content inverted on it); anything else is `tonal`. Reflected.

attributes.name: label-visibility
attributes.description: Which destinations draw their label: `always`, `selected` (only the selected one) or `never` (anything else is `always`). No item container changes size with it. Reflected.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Names the navigation landmark ("Main").

declarations.default: ['standard', 'modal']

declarations.default: 'standard'

declarations.description:
The open axis (NVD-26): a variant a layer added gets its block on demand, built by the same function and
falling back to standard's tokens (and presented as a standard drawer); a value the active system lacks is reported.

declarations.description:
The drawer (NVD-11, NVD-12, NVD-18, NVD-19, NVD-22, NVD-25, NVD-30, NVD-35, NVD-38, NVD-40). The panel is its form's
width (container.width expanded, collapsed.container.width collapsed) beside the start inset and the full height of
its parent (standard, or a collapsible modal drawer's column) or of the window (modal), on its variant's color and
elevation, its end corners rounded by its variant's shape and its start corners square, with its variant's end edge.
Inside it: the header, which stays in place, and then the items, which scroll. Logical, so right-to-left puts it at the
right edge, mirrored.

declarations.description:
A cell — a destination's, or a group's row (NVD-4…10, NVD-13, NVD-14, NVD-27, NVD-31…35, NVD-41, NVD-43, NVD-44). The
cell is the native button or link: the drawer's full width (its current width, so its hit area follows the form) and
its height, with half of container.gap above and below it and at least the minimum target. In it, the row — laid out
for the expanded drawer, clipped by the cell: at least item.container.height, the icon on the icon column and the
cell's icon line (the row's centre), the label (wrapping) item.gap after it, the trailing content at its end — and,
placed around the same icon line, the item container (the row expanded; the pill collapsed) and the short label under
the icon.

A group (NVD-44…48): its row is a cell (above), and under it its items, revealed and hidden over the disclosure motion
while it opens and closes (and over the change of form's while the drawer collapses: the collapsed drawer draws none of

declarations.description:
One destination of a navigation drawer — the spec's item kind `destination`: an icon, a label (a short label
while the drawer is collapsed), optional trailing content at the end of its row and an optional badge on its icon. A
child of `<tanrei-navigation-drawer>`, of one of its sections or of one of its groups, in order.

It is a button, or with `href` a link (NVD-59): an `<a href>` in the shadow root, drawn exactly as the button
is, whose context menu, new-tab clicks, drag and address are the browser's own; Enter follows it and Space does not.
A link is not selected by a press (NVD-60): a plain activation makes the drawer fire `change` (or `reselect`) —
cancelable, with `detail.href`, before the browser follows the link — and the page shown next sets the drawer's
`value`; a modified or a middle click, a link whose `target` is `new` and a download fire nothing. Without a `value`
a link's `href` is its value. `target="new"` opens a new tab, safely (`noopener`), ends the expanded row with the icon
set's `open_in_new` unless the row has trailing content, and says `targetLabel` (NVD-63).

Either is named by its label in both forms, the selected one `aria-current="page"`; its badge's description, then its
trailing content and then, for a link that opens a new context, `targetLabel` are its description. Its host is a
list item, its position counted among the items of its level.

members.name: value
members.description:
What identifies the destination: the drawer's `value` selects it by this, and `change` / `reselect` carry it. While
it is given none, a link's `href` stands for it, as written (NVD-59) — so a page sets the drawer's `value` to its
own address and nothing on the items.

members.name: trailingText
members.description: Short text at the end of the expanded row ("24", "New"), quieter than the label; the trailing slot's content wins.

members.name: badge
members.description: Draws a Tanrei badge on the icon, in both forms, from `badgeCount` and `badgeLabel`.

members.name: badgeCount
members.description: The badge's count: null (no attribute) draws the dot, 0 nothing, above 0 the number (999+ above 999).

members.name: badgeLabel
members.description: What assistive technology reads after the destination's name and state ("3 unread"). A dot needs one.

members.name: href
members.description: The address the destination leads to: a URL, a path or a fragment. Not empty, the destination is a link and not a button (NVD-59), and the drawer does not select it by a press (NVD-60). White space is no address; a `javascript:` address or one that cannot be read is refused and reported (NVD-64).

members.name: target
members.description: Where a link opens: `same` (here) or `new` (a new tab or window, with `noopener`), which the expanded row marks with `open_in_new` and says through `targetLabel` (NVD-63). HTML's `_self` and `_blank` are read as those; anything else is `same` and is reported (NVD-64). Ignored without `href`.

members.name: targetLabel
members.description: What assistive technology reads at the end of the link's description while `target` is `new` ("opens in a new tab"): your words, in your language. Required then; ignored otherwise.

members.name: rel
members.description: Web only: the anchor's `rel`. `noopener` is added while `target` is `new`; `noreferrer` is yours to add.

members.name: download
members.description: Web only: the anchor's `download`. A link that asks for a download is the browser's: the drawer fires nothing for it (NVD-60).

members.name: link
members.default: new LinkController(this, { ids: { refused: 'NVD-64', newContext: 'NVD-63' }, disabled: () => this.disabled })
members.description:

debug build is told (src/primitives/link.ts).

members.name: pressKeys
members.description: NVD-1, NVD-59: a link is pressed by Enter alone; Space is the browser's, and shows no pressed state.

members.name: click
members.description: `element.click()` activates the destination as a person would; a disabled one does nothing.

members.name: onTrailingChange
members.description: NVD-15, NVD-43: what the trailing slot holds, and what it says as part of the description.

members.name: glyph
members.description: NVD-42: the glyph, inside the badge when there is one — the badge is drawn above the icon indicator.

members.name: trailingContent
members.description:
NVD-43: the trailing slot's content, or else the trailing text; inert, and part of the description (NVD-15).

members.description: The name of a glyph of the system's icon set: outlined while unselected, filled while selected. Empty draws none. A glyph the icon set flags as showing a direction (`arrow_forward`, `send`) is drawn mirrored in a right-to-left layout.

group's chevron (`expand_more`, NVD-44) is not named here.

declarations.description:
A group of a drawer's destinations — the spec's item kind `group`: a row that opens and closes it (an icon,
a label, a short label for the collapsed drawer, and the icon set's `expand_more` turned half a turn while open), and
under it, indented one level further, its `<tanrei-navigation-drawer-item>` and `<tanrei-navigation-drawer-group>`
children. A collapsed drawer draws it as one cell; activating that cell expands the drawer with the group open.

Its row is a `<button aria-expanded aria-controls>` named by its label, and its items a nested list labelled by it.
Activating the row sets `open` and then fires `toggle`; with focus on the row, the arrow toward the end of the line
opens it and the one toward the start closes it (NVD-45).

declarations.description:
A panel of destinations at the start edge, in two variants — `standard`, a layout region beside the content,
and `modal`, a modal overlay over a scrim that closes itself after a destination is chosen — and, while `collapsible`,
in two forms: expanded, and collapsed to a column of icons, which is the expanded drawer with its labels gone: every
row is the same row cut after its icon, at the same height and with the same corners, and every icon exactly in place
while the drawer moves between the two. A collapsed cell shows its name in a plain tooltip on hover and keyboard focus;
`collapsed-labels` draws short labels under the icons instead, for a product or a system whose column is labelled.

Contract: specs/navigation-drawer.spec.json. `<tanrei-navigation-drawer-item>`, `<tanrei-navigation-drawer-group>` and
`<tanrei-navigation-drawer-section>` children, in order; header buttons (icon-only `<tanrei-button>`s) with
`slot="header-button"`, the main action (`<tanrei-main-action-button>`) with `slot="main-action"`, and the `header`
slot. The drawer's `value` is the selected destination's value; the drawer sets it when a button destination is
activated and fires `change`, or `reselect` for the selected one.

A site's sidebar (NVD-57…64): a destination with `href` is a link, and the selected destination is the current page
(`aria-current="page"`) — one state, which in a site of separate pages the page says, through `value` (a link without
a `value` takes its `href`). The drawer never writes `value` for a link: a plain activation fires `change` or
`reselect` with `detail.href`, cancelable, before the browser follows the link (a router cancels it and goes to
`detail.href` itself), and then closes a modal drawer; a modified or a middle click, a link whose `target` is `new`
and a download fire nothing and close nothing. The row that shows the selection is brought into view when the drawer
first appears and whenever `value` changes — centred if it was not wholly in view, untouched if it was, without motion
and without moving focus — and `reveal-selected` opens the groups that hold it (each fires `toggle`). `scrollOffset`
reads and writes how far the items are scrolled; the scroll does not chain to the page. Nothing is stored: a site keeps
each group's `open` (from `toggle`) and `scrollOffset` (read on `pagehide`) itself and gives them back as attributes.

Forms (NVD-30): not collapsible, always expanded. Collapsible and standard: `expanded` chooses. Collapsible and modal:
collapsed — its column in the layout, drawn as a standard drawer's — while closed, and expanded over the content while
open. The first header button is then the menu button: the drawer sets `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` on its
native button (`ariaExpanded`, `ariaControlsElements`), and its activation asks for the other form: the drawer sets
`expanded` (or `open`) and fires `expandedchange`. The main action's `extended` follows the form. The read-only
`collapsed` attribute reflects the form.

Standard: a `<nav>` named by `label`, taking its form's width in the layout while `open` and none while closed (sliding
while the content beside it resizes). Opening it moves focus in; closing it with focus inside returns focus to where it
was; Tab leaves it without closing it.

Modal: a native `<dialog>` in the shadow root, opened with `showModal()` while `open` — in the top layer over its
`::backdrop` (the scrim), everything else inert, the page held from scrolling, focus kept inside. Escape, the platform's
back, a press on the scrim, a drag toward the start edge past half its width (or a fling), the menu button and a
destination's activation close it: the drawer sets `open` to false itself and fires `close`. Focus returns to where it
was.

Responsive (NVD-53…55): with `responsive`, the window's width chooses what the drawer is, and `variant` is ignored —
a standard drawer, shown whatever `open` says, from `comp.navigation-drawer.breakpoint.expanded` (1024 px at the
default text size); its column, widening over the content while `open`, from `breakpoint.collapsed` (600 px) while
`collapsible`; a modal drawer below that. The read-only `presentation` says which (and the `presentation` attribute, for
styling); `presentationchange` fires when it is first decided and whenever the width changes it. A change of
presentation is drawn at once, is entered closed (an open overlay closes: `open` is false and `close` fires once), and
keeps `expanded`, `value` and every group's `open`. The presentation is derived from the width alone: it is never
written to `variant`, `open` or `expanded`, and the element stores nothing — a product that wants the user's choice of
form remembered keeps what `expandedchange` carries and sets `expanded` from it.

Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-navigation-drawer-*` tokens. The color reaches under
`env(safe-area-inset-*)` at the start, top and bottom.

members.name: responsive
members.description: Lets the window's width choose the drawer's presentation (NVD-53): standard where it is wide, its column where it is narrower (while `collapsible`), modal where it is narrow. Reflected.

members.name: decided
members.description: What the window's width has decided for a responsive drawer; null while it is not responsive, or the width is not known.

members.name: value
members.description:
The value of the selected destination, wherever it stands; empty selects none. The selected destination is the place
being shown, exposed as the current page. The drawer sets it when a button destination is activated; it never sets
it for a link (NVD-60) — in a site of separate pages each page sets it to its own destination (a link's `href`
stands as its value while it has none).

members.name: revealSelected
members.description:
Opens the groups that hold the selected destination when the drawer first appears (in its first frame, without
motion) and whenever `value` changes, whatever their `open` said; each fires `toggle` (NVD-58). The user may close
such a group again: it then stays closed until `value` changes. While false a closed group stays closed and its row
shows the selection (NVD-47).

members.name: givenOffset
members.description:
The offset the product gave, while it still has work to do: until it has been written (`unwritten` — nothing is
laid out yet), and until the first frame is drawn, because the first frame's order may run more than once while the
drawer's children are still arriving (NVD-62).

members.name: lastScroll
members.description: NVD-61: where the items were scrolled when the drawer last looked — before the browser answered a focus by scrolling.

members.name: scrollOffset
members.description:
How far the items are scrolled from their start, in CSS pixels (NVD-61). Reading it gives the present distance;
setting it scrolls there at once, without motion, held inside the scroll range — before the drawer first appears
included, when it is where the first frame is drawn (the `scroll-offset` attribute is read once, for that frame).
No event is fired while the user scrolls, and nothing is stored (NVD-62): a site reads it when the page is left and
gives it back on the next page.

first appears, and when `value` changes to a destination (or `revealSelected` is turned on). A group the user

members.name: viewSelection
members.description:

children were parsed has nothing to scroll yet, and one whose later cells are still to come has a shorter range

members.name: showSelection
members.description:
NVD-57, NVD-62: once every cell is drawn — and, after the first frame, the groups just opened have finished
opening — the items go to the offset the product gave (in the first frame's order) and the row that shows the
selection is brought into view. Before the first frame all of it happens in microtasks, so no frame shows the
items anywhere else; and it reads the layout once for a whole burst of updates, however many cells there are.

members.name: scrollItemsTo
members.description: Writes how far the items are scrolled: at once (the scroller's `scroll-behavior` is auto), held inside the range by the browser.

members.name: onScroll
members.description: NVD-61: the user scrolled, or the range changed under the items. No event is fired for it.

members.name: onFocusIn
members.description:
NVD-61: keyboard focus that moves to a cell which is not wholly in view scrolls it into view by the least distance
that shows it whole. The browsers answer a focus each in its own way — one centres a cell that was out of view,
another leaves one that is partly in view where it is — and some before this event, some after it: so the items
are put back where they were before the focus, and then moved by the least distance; a browser that answers
afterwards finds the cell in view and does nothing. A pointer's focus scrolls nothing.

members.name: showWhole
members.description: Scrolls the items by the least distance that puts `cell`'s row wholly inside the space they scroll in; by nothing if it is.

members.name: applyOffset
members.description: NVD-61: the items go to the offset the product gave; `orStart`: to their start, the default, where it gave none.

members.name: bringSelectionIntoView
members.description:
NVD-57: the row that shows the selection — the selected destination, or the group's row NVD-47 names — is centred
in the space the items scroll in if it is not wholly inside it, as far as the range allows, and left alone if it
is. A write to `scrollTop`: never `scrollIntoView()`, which would scroll the page as well; no focus moves.

members.name: watchWidths

such a group again: it then stays closed until `value` changes. While false a closed group stays closed and its row

declarations.description:
Lets people enter a number as one complete field. Built from a Field (`<tanrei-field>`) and the Number input
(`<tanrei-number-input>`) it frames: the box — the number, its unit and its two steppers — under the Field's label,
or, in the filled and the outlined look, with the label floating in it; with the Field's requirement mark, its help
and its error, tied together for assistive technology and taking part in a form as one control.

Contract: specs/number-field.spec.json. `<tanrei-number-field name="quantity" label="Quantity" min="1" max="99"
requirement="required" supporting-text="Up to 99 per order." increment-label="Increase"
decrement-label="Decrease"></tanrei-number-field>`.

Composed (`src/primitives/composed.ts`): its shadow root holds the two members' own elements and nothing
else, so it draws nothing of its own and has no token — every `--tanrei-comp-field-*`,
`--tanrei-comp-input-box-*`, `--tanrei-comp-number-input-*` and, for the two steppers, `--tanrei-comp-button-*` value reaches the members by
inheritance, and one number field is set apart by setting such a property on this element. Each property is its
member's, set on that member unchanged: `label`, `label-hidden`, `supporting-text`, `error-text`, `error`,
`disabled`, `requirement`, `required-mark`, `required-text` and `optional-text` are the Field's, every other one the
number input's. One level down, the same by hand: `<tanrei-field label="Quantity" requirement="required"
supporting-text="Up to 99 per order."><tanrei-number-input name="quantity" min="1" max="99"
increment-label="Increase" decrement-label="Decrease"></tanrei-number-input></tanrei-field>` — and the box alone,
where a label stands elsewhere (beside a slider, in a cell of a table), is `<tanrei-number-input>` with a `label`
of its own.

It is a block as wide as its place, and its box fills it (NUM-47): give it a narrower place for a narrower box.

`value` is at every moment the number input's — a number, or null while it holds none — and the four events are
that input's own, with this element as their target: `event.target.value` is the new value in every listener of
`change`. It dispatches none itself, and coordinates nothing: the input tells its Field that it floats the label,
where its number's line starts and ends, and its refusal of a text that is not a number, exactly as it does one
level down.

Form-associated (NUM-48): it submits the value under `name` as a plain decimal number ("12.5") whatever the locale
shows — nothing while disabled —, resets to its `value` attribute, is restored on navigation, follows a disabled
`<fieldset>`, and reports what its number input reports: a missing value while `requirement` is `required` and it
holds none, and a bad input while it holds a text that is not a number. Enter presses the default button of this
element's form.

The element is not focusable itself and has no role: `focus()` goes to the input, the field is one stop in the focus
order, and its name is `label` (with `label-hidden` where it is not drawn), never `aria-label`. A press on the label
row, on the box or on a floating label focuses the input; a press on a stepper steps and moves no focus; a press on
the help or the error text does nothing.

members.name: label

members.name: disabled

members.name: requirement
members.description: What the form asks of the control: `required` exposes it as required and draws the required mark; `optional` draws the optional tag; `none` says and draws nothing. It never validates.

members.name: requiredMark
members.description: How this control shows that it is required (`required-mark`): `tag` is a small filled tag with `requiredText`, `asterisk` is "*" after the label, `none` draws nothing and keeps the semantics; `auto` takes the design system's answer (`--tanrei-comp-field-requirement-mark`, which follows `--tanrei-sys-behavior-requirement-mark`).

members.name: requiredText

members.name: optionalText
members.description: The text of the optional tag, also part of the description (`optional-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ optionalText })`). Tanrei has none: without them no tag is drawn and nothing is said.

members.name: variant

members.name: size
members.description: The container's minimum height: `medium` or `large` (48 / 56 in the default system), the text input's two sizes. The hit area always meets the minimum target. Reflected.

members.name: value
members.description: The committed number, or null while the input holds none. It changes when the person commits — focus leaves, Enter, a step — not on every keystroke; `input` carries what is being typed. The `value` attribute is a plain decimal number ("12.5"), and the value a form reset returns to.

members.name: placeholder
members.description: A hint shown while the input is empty and the label is not in the input line. Never a replacement for `label`.

members.name: readOnly
members.description: The number can be focused, selected and copied, and is submitted, but not changed: no key steps it and no stepper is drawn. The attribute is `readonly`.

members.name: min
members.description: The lowest number a commit keeps; a lower one is raised to it. Null for no limit. It is also where the steps are counted from.

members.name: max
members.description: The highest number a commit keeps; a higher one is lowered to it. Null for no limit. A `max` below `min` is no limit.

members.name: step
members.description: How far Up Arrow, Down Arrow and a stepper move the number; Page Up and Page Down move ten times as far. It does not limit what may be typed. 0 or less, or not a number, steps by 1.

members.name: noSteppers
members.description: Draws no steppers (`no-steppers`: the spec's `steppers`, inverted, because a boolean attribute cannot default to true): for an input in a row too narrow for them, or beside a slider that does their work. The keys still step. Reflected.

members.name: incrementLabel
members.description: The accessible name of the stepper that steps up (`increment-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ incrementLabel })`). Tanrei has none: without them the stepper is drawn, works for a pointer and is kept from assistive technology, where the spin button steps by itself.

members.name: decrementLabel
members.description: The accessible name of the stepper that steps down (`decrement-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ decrementLabel })`). Tanrei has none: without them the stepper is drawn, works for a pointer and is kept from assistive technology, where the spin button steps by itself.

members.name: prefixText
members.description: Fixed text before the number, not part of the value (`prefix-text`): a currency sign. Written before the number along the direction of the run the two affixes make — that of their first strong character, the prefix asked first, and left-to-right where they have none — in every layout direction.

members.name: suffixText
members.description: Fixed text after the number, not part of the value (`suffix-text`): the unit. Read to assistive technology with the number. Written after the number along the run's direction: at its right for a unit in Latin letters or signs, at its left for one in a right-to-left script or one that begins with a right-to-left mark (U+200F).

members.name: valueText
members.description: The value as words (`value-text`: "12 pixels"), given to assistive technology in place of the number with its prefix and suffix. The same text a slider beside the field takes.

members.name: align
members.description: Where the number stands in the input: at the `start`, the field's start edge, as the text of every other field; or at the `end` of the number's run — the edge at which the suffix stands or would stand, the right for a number alone or with a unit in Latin letters or signs in every layout direction — for a number against its unit or in a column of numbers. Anything else is `start`. Reflected.

members.name: minFractionDigits

members.name: maxFractionDigits

declarations.name: numberOrNull
declarations.description: A finite number, or null: what `value`, `min` and `max` are whatever they were given (a string of an attribute, undefined, NaN).

declarations.name: NUMBER_OR_NULL
declarations.default: { converter: { fromAttribute: (value: string | null) => numberOrNull(value) } }
declarations.description: An attribute that holds a plain decimal number ("12.5"), or nothing: a property that is a number or null.

The box of a number: lets people enter a number as a number — typed in their locale's form or stepped by a key or a
button, kept within limits, with its unit beside it — and draws no row around it. A `<tanrei-field>` frames it with
a label, a requirement mark, help and an error, or the product names it with `label` where its visible label is
elsewhere: the head of a table's column, a toolbar, the title of a row that also holds a slider.
`<tanrei-number-field>` is the two as one element.

Contract: specs/number-input.spec.json. Every visual value is a token: the box is drawn from
`--tanrei-comp-input-box-*`, the one set every input box is drawn from (NMI-47), and where the steppers stand and how
a hold repeats from `--tanrei-comp-number-input-*`; the steppers are `<tanrei-button>`s, drawn from
Button's own tokens.

```html
<tanrei-number-input label="Scale" value="1.5" min="0.25" max="4" step="0.05" suffix-text="×" value-text="1.5 times" align="end" no-steppers></tanrei-number-input>
```

`value` is a number, or null while the input holds none. It changes on a **commit** — focus leaves, Enter, a step —
and never while the person types: the text is theirs until then, and nothing typed is refused, reformatted, clamped
or rounded. `input` carries what the text reads as meanwhile (what a slider beside the input follows). A commit
raises the number to `min`, lowers it to `max`, rounds it to `maxFractionDigits` and writes it back in the locale's
form — its digits and its decimal separator, no grouping separators. A text that is not a number is kept, marked as
an error, reported with `entryerror` and told to the Field that frames it, which shows `invalidText`.

`step` is how far Up Arrow, Down Arrow and a stepper move the number (Page Up and Page Down ten times as far), to
the next number on the step's grid counted from `min`; it does not limit what may be typed. Home and End stay the
caret's, and the wheel never changes the number.

It is a block as wide as its place, with no width of its own: give it a narrower place for a narrower box. In a
Field it takes the Field's name, description and required, invalid and disabled states, floats the Field's label
in the filled and the outlined look, and tells the Field where its number's line starts and ends. It is a
form-associated element: it takes `name`, submits its value as a plain decimal number ("12.5") whatever the locale
shows, resets to the `value` attribute, is restored on navigation, follows `<fieldset disabled>` and reports
`valueMissing` while its Field says it is required and it holds no value, and `badInput` while it holds a text that
is not a number.

To assistive technology it is a spin button: its value the committed number, its limits `min` and `max`, its value
text `valueText` or the number as shown with its prefix and suffix. The two steppers are named buttons outside the
focus order.

cssParts.name: prefix

cssParts.description: The fixed text after the number.

members.name: variant
members.description: The look, as the text inputs beside it: `stacked` is a filled box whose label is the row of its Field; `filled` and `outlined` float the label inside the box. Use one style per form. A value the number input does not know by name is laid out as stacked. Reflected.

members.name: size
members.description: The container's minimum height: `medium` or `large` (48 / 56 in the default system), the text input's two sizes. The hit area always meets the minimum target. Reflected.

members.name: value
members.description: The committed number, or null while the input holds none. It changes when the person commits — focus leaves, Enter, a step — not on every keystroke; `input` carries what is being typed. The `value` attribute is a plain decimal number ("12.5"), and the value a form reset returns to.

members.name: name
members.description: The name the value is submitted under in a form. Reflected.

members.name: label
members.description: Names the number input where no Field does, or where its visible label is elsewhere: it wins over the Field's label as the accessible name, and is what a filled or an outlined input floats. Never drawn by a stacked input.

members.name: labelHidden
members.description: Does not draw the floating label of a filled or an outlined input, which stays the accessible name (`label-hidden`). The Field that frames it says the same with its own `labelHidden`.

members.name: placeholder
members.description: A hint shown while the input is empty and the label is not in the input line. Never a replacement for `label`.

members.name: error
members.description: Puts the number input in the error condition: every part of its box is drawn from the error parts and it is exposed as invalid. The Field that frames it sets the same through its own `error`. The number input never sets this itself; it enters an error of its own while the text it was left with is not a number.

members.name: disabled
members.description: Prevents focus, editing, stepping and form submission.

members.name: readOnly
members.description: The number can be focused, selected and copied, and is submitted, but not changed: no key steps it and no stepper is drawn. The attribute is `readonly`.

members.name: min
members.description: The lowest number a commit keeps; a lower one is raised to it. Null for no limit. It is also where the steps are counted from.

members.name: max
members.description: The highest number a commit keeps; a higher one is lowered to it. Null for no limit. A `max` below `min` is no limit.

members.name: step
members.description: How far Up Arrow, Down Arrow and a stepper move the number; Page Up and Page Down move ten times as far. It does not limit what may be typed. 0 or less, or not a number, steps by 1.

members.name: noSteppers
members.description: Draws no steppers (`no-steppers`: the spec's `steppers`, inverted, because a boolean attribute cannot default to true): for an input in a row too narrow for them, or beside a slider that does their work. The keys still step. Reflected.

members.name: incrementLabel
members.description: The accessible name of the stepper that steps up (`increment-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ incrementLabel })`). Tanrei has none: without them the stepper is drawn, works for a pointer and is kept from assistive technology, where the spin button steps by itself.

members.name: decrementLabel
members.description: The accessible name of the stepper that steps down (`decrement-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ decrementLabel })`). Tanrei has none: without them the stepper is drawn, works for a pointer and is kept from assistive technology, where the spin button steps by itself.

members.name: prefixText
members.description: Fixed text before the number, not part of the value (`prefix-text`): a currency sign. Written before the number along the direction of the run the two affixes make — that of their first strong character, the prefix asked first, and left-to-right where they have none — in every layout direction.

members.name: suffixText
members.description: Fixed text after the number, not part of the value (`suffix-text`): the unit. Read to assistive technology with the number. Written after the number along the run's direction: at its right for a unit in Latin letters or signs, at its left for one in a right-to-left script or one that begins with a right-to-left mark (U+200F).

members.name: valueText
members.description: The value as words (`value-text`: "12 pixels"), given to assistive technology in place of the number with its prefix and suffix. The same text a slider beside the field takes.

members.name: align
members.description: Where the number stands in the input: at the `start`, the field's start edge, as the text of every other field; or at the `end` of the number's run — the edge at which the suffix stands or would stand, the right for a number alone or with a unit in Latin letters or signs in every layout direction — for a number against its unit or in a column of numbers. Anything else is `start`. Reflected.

members.name: minFractionDigits
members.description: The fewest digits shown after the decimal separator; zeros fill them (`min-fraction-digits`: 2 for an amount of money).

members.name: maxFractionDigits
members.description: The most digits kept after the decimal separator (`max-fraction-digits`): a commit rounds to it. 0 makes the field hold whole numbers and asks for a keyboard without a separator.

members.name: locale
members.description: A BCP 47 language tag ("de-DE", "ar-EG") for how the number is shown and read: its digits and its decimal separator. Empty reads the nearest `lang` attribute, then the browser's language. The value itself is a number in every locale.

members.name: invalidText
members.description: The words of the refusal of a text that is not a number (`invalid-text`: "Enter a number"): what the Field that frames the input shows in its supporting row while the entry error lasts — its own `errorText` while this is empty — and the input's description where no Field frames it.

members.name: text
members.description: The text in the input: the person's while they edit, the committed number in the locale's form otherwise (NMI-16, NMI-17).

members.name: entryError
members.description: NMI-21: the field was committed with a text that is not a number, and holds it still.

members.name: given
members.description: What `value` holds: what the product set last, or what the input made the value since.

members.name: focused
members.description: NMI-15: the input has focus, however it was gained.

members.name: formDisabled
members.description: Set by an ancestor `<fieldset disabled>` (the element's `formDisabledCallback`).

members.name: says
members.description: What it tells its form, said where an element composed around it hears it (src/primitives/form-says.ts).

members.name: ownValue
members.description: The value the number input committed or took from the product last: another `value` is the product's (NMI-31).

members.name: base
members.description: NMI-20: the value last committed — when the product set it, or at the last `change`.

members.name: edited
members.description: NMI-16: the person changed the text since it was last written.

members.name: awaited
members.description: NMI-31: the product set a value while an input method was composing: its text is written when the composition ends, and is not the person's.

members.name: reveal
members.description: NMI-22: a step wrote the text: the caret goes to its end and all of it is kept in view, once it is drawn.

members.name: hold

type.text: { direction: 1 | -1; timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined; repeats: number; interval: number; fast: number } | null

members.description: NMI-27: the stepper that is held down, and its next step.

members.name: pressed
members.description: NMI-26: a press of a pointer stepped already; the `click` that ends it is not another step.

members.name: pressing
members.description:
NMI-26: the stepper whose press has begun and whose `mousedown` is still to come (0: none). The step is taken at
`pointerdown`; a step that reaches the limit does not disable that stepper before the `mousedown` of the same
press has been heard — at once for a mouse, at the release for a touch — because that event is where the field
keeps focus where it is (`onContainerPress`), and a control disabled in between is not sent it: focus left the
input, or the control it was on, for the page.

members.name: axes
members.default: new OpenAxesController(this, { component: 'number-input', behavior: 'NMI-43', axes: AXES })
members.description: NMI-43: sizes and variants a design system adds, and a value the active system does not have (src/primitives/axes.ts).

members.name: frame
members.default: new FieldControlController(this, { errorCondition: true, named: () => !!this.label.trim(), says: () => this.saysToField, changed: () => (this.frameChanged = true), })
members.description:
NMI-45: the input's side of the exchange with the Field that frames it (src/primitives/field.ts). It takes the
Field's name, description and states, whether the label is hidden and whether an asterisk follows it; and it says
what only it knows — that it draws the label, how far its number's line is inset, its own refusal of an entry. It
has an error condition of its own (NMI-10). No Field: it is drawn as a bare input (NMI-46).

members.name: frameChanged
members.description: The Field's answer changed since the last update: the floating label may have other lines (NMI-8).

members.name: native

the length the pair takes is what a floating label must end before (`--_steppers`).

members.description: NMI-32: disabled by its own `disabled`, a fieldset's, or the Field or the field group that frames it.

members.name: labelled

members.name: wrong

members.name: saysToField
members.description:
NMI-45: what the input says to the Field that frames it. That it draws the label while its look floats one — the
Field draws no label row either way (FLD-25). How far the line of its number stands from its start edge and from
its end edge: its inline padding at each, with and without steppers (`INSET`, in the styles; FLD-26). And an
entry error, with its words (FLD-28).

members.name: described
members.description:
NMI-12, NMI-21: what the input is described by — `invalidText` while an entry error lasts and no Field frames it
(a Field shows the words and gives them back as its own description, FLD-28), then the description its Field gives.
