members.description: NMI-30: the limits as decimals; a `max` below `min` is no limit.

members.name: digits
members.description: NMI-30: the digits after the separator: the most a commit keeps, and the fewest shown — never more than the most.

members.name: stepNow
members.description: NMI-22: the step as a decimal; 0 or less, or not a number, is 1.

members.name: form_
members.description: NMI-17, NMI-43: the locale's form — `locale`, or where it is empty or no tag the browser knows, the nearest `lang` attribute, then the browser's language.

members.name: shown
members.description: NMI-17: a number as the input shows it; an empty value is an empty input.

members.name: reading
members.description: NMI-18: what a text reads as, by the locale's form, without the prefix and the suffix where they were typed with it.

members.name: form
members.description: The form it belongs to, if any.

members.name: validity
members.description: The native constraint validity: `valueMissing` while its Field says it is required and it holds no value, `badInput` while it holds a text that is not a number.

members.name: focus
members.description: Moves focus to the input: the number input's one stop in the focus order.

members.name: select
members.description: Selects the text in the input.

members.name: syncForm
members.description:
NMI-35: the form's view — the committed value as a plain decimal number, whatever the locale shows, or an empty
string; left out while disabled. A missing value while its Field says it is required, and a bad input while an entry
error lasts (NMI-12, NMI-21). Said through `FormSays`, where an element composed around it hears it. Said when the number input is drawn, and at once when it commits: a listener of `change`
or `action`, and the form Enter submits, already see the new value.

members.name: took
members.description: NMI-31: the product gave a value: it is written into the input, whatever was typed, an entry error ends, and nothing is said.

members.name: keep
members.description: The number input makes `value` the value itself.

members.name: changed
members.description: NMI-20: `change`, once, while the value differs from the one last committed. `value` is already the new one.

members.name: typed
members.description:
NMI-16, NMI-19, NMI-21: the person changed the text. Nothing is rewritten: the text is theirs. `input` carries the
number it reads as, or null; `value` stays the committed number. A text that became a number, or empty, ends an
entry error.

members.name: commit
members.description:
NMI-20, NMI-21: commits the text. A number is raised to `min`, lowered to `max`, rounded to `maxFractionDigits`,
made the value and written back in the locale's form; an empty text makes the value empty; a text that is not a
number is kept, makes the value empty and enters the entry error (`entryerror`). Then `change`, once, while the
value differs from the one last committed. A text the person did not change commits nothing.

members.name: stepBy
members.description:
NMI-22: steps `direction` by `factor` steps. From the number the text reads as — or from the value where the
person did not change the text, or changed it into what is not a number — to the `factor`th number that is `min`
(or zero) plus a whole multiple of the step (NMI-23: a page key's ten steps stay on the step's grid), held within the limits and computed in decimal; a field that holds no
value takes the number nearest to zero the limits allow, and nothing more. The result is a commit's: rounded to
`maxFractionDigits`, made the value and written into the input. `input`, then `change` — or, while a stepper is
held, `change` when the hold ends. A step that would not change the value says nothing. Returns whether it stepped.

members.name: atLimit
members.description: NMI-25: the stepper of `direction` has nowhere to go: the value is at or past that limit, or the field is disabled.

members.name: holdTimes
members.description: NMI-27: the three waiting times of a hold, in milliseconds: before the first repeat, between repeats, and between them after the tenth.

members.name: onStepperDown
members.description:
NMI-26, NMI-27: a press on a stepper steps once when it begins, and takes no focus (the container's `mousedown`
keeps it where it is). Held, it steps again after `motion.repeat-delay`, then once every `motion.repeat-interval`,
and after its tenth repeated step once every `motion.repeat-interval-fast`, until the press ends, the pointer
leaves the stepper, or the value reaches the limit. Every step is one step; `change` follows once, when it ends.

members.name: release
members.description: NMI-27: the hold ends: no more steps, and `change` once while the value differs from the one last committed.

members.name: onStepperClick
members.description: NMI-26: a stepper activated through assistive technology — a `click` no press of a pointer began — steps once.

members.name: onKeyDown
members.description:
NMI-20, NMI-23: the input's keys. Up Arrow and Down Arrow step by `step`, Page Up and Page Down by ten times it —
once for each repeat of a held key; Enter commits, fires `action` after any `change`, and asks the form to submit
unless `action` was cancelled. Home, End, Left Arrow and Right Arrow, and every arrow or page key with a modifier,
are the text's. While an input method composes, every key is its own.

members.name: onBlur
members.description: NMI-20: the input lost focus: the text is committed.

members.name: onContainerPress
members.description:
NMI-14: a press on the container's padding, on a floating label, on the prefix or on the suffix moves focus to the input and does
nothing else. A press in the input places the caret. NMI-26: a press on a stepper moves no focus: a field that was
not focused stays unfocused, and a focused input keeps its focus and its caret.

members.name: measureSteppers
members.description:
NMI-8: the length the steppers take, for a floating label to end before. Read now; what is returned writes it
(nothing where it is what the field has): the fields of a page are all read before any of them is written
(src/primitives/kept-length.ts).

members.name: readWrap
watchWrap
members.description: NMI-37: the container and the input's line are watched while the number input is on the page.

members.name: reports
members.description: What a debug build tells the developer; the number input still renders.

events.name: change
events.description: A commit changed the value: focus left the input, Enter was pressed, a key stepped it, or a pressed stepper was released; `value` is already the new one. Composed and bubbling. Never fired when the product sets `value`.

events.name: input
events.description: The person changed the text, or a step changed the value. `detail.value` is the number the text reads as — not clamped, not rounded — or null while it reads as no value or as not a number. Composed and bubbling. Never fired when the product sets `value`.

events.name: entryerror
events.description: The person committed a text that is not a number. `detail.reason` is `invalid`, `detail.text` the input's `invalidText` (empty where none was given). Composed and bubbling.

events.name: action
events.description: The person pressed Enter; after any `change` it caused. Cancelable: unless it is cancelled, the form the number input stands in is then asked to submit.

attributes.description: The id of the form the number input belongs to, where it stands outside it: the platform's own attribute, which then wins over a form around it. The `form` property is read-only and returns the form element.
attributes.name: form
variant
attributes.description: The look, as the text inputs beside it: `stacked` is a filled box whose label is the row of its Field; `filled` and `outlined` float the label inside the box. Use one style per form. A value the number input does not know by name is laid out as stacked. Reflected.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: The container's minimum height: `medium` or `large` (48 / 56 in the default system), the text input's two sizes. The hit area always meets the minimum target. Reflected.

attributes.name: value
attributes.description: The committed number, or null while the input holds none. It changes when the person commits — focus leaves, Enter, a step — not on every keystroke; `input` carries what is being typed. The `value` attribute is a plain decimal number ("12.5"), and the value a form reset returns to.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: The name the value is submitted under in a form. Reflected.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Names the number input where no Field does, or where its visible label is elsewhere: it wins over the Field's label as the accessible name, and is what a filled or an outlined input floats. Never drawn by a stacked input.

attributes.name: label-hidden
attributes.description: Does not draw the floating label of a filled or an outlined input, which stays the accessible name (`label-hidden`). The Field that frames it says the same with its own `labelHidden`.

attributes.name: placeholder
attributes.description: A hint shown while the input is empty and the label is not in the input line. Never a replacement for `label`.

attributes.name: error
attributes.description: Puts the number input in the error condition: every part of its box is drawn from the error parts and it is exposed as invalid. The Field that frames it sets the same through its own `error`. The number input never sets this itself; it enters an error of its own while the text it was left with is not a number.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: Prevents focus, editing, stepping and form submission.

attributes.name: readonly
attributes.description: The number can be focused, selected and copied, and is submitted, but not changed: no key steps it and no stepper is drawn. The attribute is `readonly`.

attributes.name: min
attributes.description: The lowest number a commit keeps; a lower one is raised to it. Null for no limit. It is also where the steps are counted from.

attributes.name: max
attributes.description: The highest number a commit keeps; a higher one is lowered to it. Null for no limit. A `max` below `min` is no limit.

attributes.name: step
attributes.description: How far Up Arrow, Down Arrow and a stepper move the number; Page Up and Page Down move ten times as far. It does not limit what may be typed. 0 or less, or not a number, steps by 1.

attributes.name: no-steppers
attributes.description: Draws no steppers (`no-steppers`: the spec's `steppers`, inverted, because a boolean attribute cannot default to true): for an input in a row too narrow for them, or beside a slider that does their work. The keys still step. Reflected.

attributes.name: increment-label
attributes.description: The accessible name of the stepper that steps up (`increment-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ incrementLabel })`). Tanrei has none: without them the stepper is drawn, works for a pointer and is kept from assistive technology, where the spin button steps by itself.

attributes.name: decrement-label
attributes.description: The accessible name of the stepper that steps down (`decrement-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ decrementLabel })`). Tanrei has none: without them the stepper is drawn, works for a pointer and is kept from assistive technology, where the spin button steps by itself.

attributes.name: prefix-text
attributes.description: Fixed text before the number, not part of the value (`prefix-text`): a currency sign. Written before the number along the direction of the run the two affixes make — that of their first strong character, the prefix asked first, and left-to-right where they have none — in every layout direction.

attributes.name: suffix-text
attributes.description: Fixed text after the number, not part of the value (`suffix-text`): the unit. Read to assistive technology with the number. Written after the number along the run's direction: at its right for a unit in Latin letters or signs, at its left for one in a right-to-left script or one that begins with a right-to-left mark (U+200F).

attributes.name: value-text
attributes.description: The value as words (`value-text`: "12 pixels"), given to assistive technology in place of the number with its prefix and suffix. The same text a slider beside the field takes.

attributes.name: align
attributes.description: Where the number stands in the input: at the `start`, the field's start edge, as the text of every other field; or at the `end` of the number's run — the edge at which the suffix stands or would stand, the right for a number alone or with a unit in Latin letters or signs in every layout direction — for a number against its unit or in a column of numbers. Anything else is `start`. Reflected.

attributes.name: min-fraction-digits
attributes.description: The fewest digits shown after the decimal separator; zeros fill them (`min-fraction-digits`: 2 for an amount of money).

attributes.name: max-fraction-digits
attributes.description: The most digits kept after the decimal separator (`max-fraction-digits`): a commit rounds to it. 0 makes the field hold whole numbers and asks for a keyboard without a separator.

attributes.name: locale
attributes.description: A BCP 47 language tag ("de-DE", "ar-EG") for how the number is shown and read: its digits and its decimal separator. Empty reads the nearest `lang` attribute, then the browser's language. The value itself is a number in every locale.

attributes.name: invalid-text
attributes.description: The words of the refusal of a text that is not a number (`invalid-text`: "Enter a number"): what the Field that frames the input shows in its supporting row while the entry error lasts — its own `errorText` while this is empty — and the input's description where no Field frames it.

declarations.name: ZERO
declarations.default: { int: 0n, scale: 0 }

declarations.name: decimalFromString
declarations.description:
A plain decimal string — ASCII digits, a period, an optional sign and exponent ("12.5", "-0.25", "1e-7") — as a
decimal; null for anything else. The form of the `value` attribute, of a form's value, and of a number as JavaScript
writes it.

declarations.name: decimalOf
declarations.description: A number as the decimal its shortest text names (0.1 is one tenth, not the binary fraction nearest to it); null for what is not a finite number.

declarations.name: canonical
declarations.description: The plain decimal string of a decimal: ASCII digits and a period, never an exponent, never the locale's form ("12.5").

declarations.name: numberOf
declarations.description: The number a decimal is (the nearest one a JavaScript number can hold).

declarations.name: clamp
declarations.description: NMI-20: held within the limits — raised to `min`, lowered to `max` — where each is given.

declarations.name: round
declarations.description: NMI-20: rounded to `digits` digits after the separator, a half away from zero.

declarations.name: stepped
declarations.description:
NMI-22: the `count`th number from `from`, in `direction`, that is `base` plus a whole multiple of `amount` (which is
above zero) — so a number between two such numbers goes to the nearer one in that direction, and not past it, and
each further count is one more `amount` (NMI-23: a page key's ten steps stay on the step's grid, 42 → 62 by 2).

declarations.name: numberForm
declarations.description: The form of a locale `Intl` knows (a tag `supportedLocale()` of src/primitives/locale-date.ts returned).

declarations.name: format
declarations.description:
NMI-17: the number in the locale's form — its digits and its decimal separator, its minus sign before a negative
number, at least `minDigits` and at most `maxDigits` digits after the separator with no other trailing zeros, no
exponent and no grouping separators: what is shown can be typed back.

declarations.name: read
declarations.description:
NMI-18: reads a text as a number, leniently, by the locale's form.

- Spaces, around the number and inside it, and marks of direction are ignored.
- A hyphen-minus or a minus sign before the digits, or a plus sign, is its sign — before or after a prefix.
- `prefix` before the number and `suffix` after it are ignored where they were typed or pasted with it.
- ASCII digits, the locale's own, full-width digits and the decimal digits of other scripts are digits.
- The locale's decimal separator, once, is the separator. So is a period, the separator of a plain decimal number,
  wherever the locale does not group with it: a period in a locale that groups with periods is a grouping separator
  ("1.500" is 1500 in German), and never a guess.
- The locale's grouping separator is ignored wherever it stands between two digits before the separator.
- An empty text, or one of spaces only, is no value. Anything else is not a number.

Asks for a short code sent to the person as one complete field. Built from a Field (`<tanrei-field>`) and the
One-time-code input (`<tanrei-one-time-code-input>`) it frames: the input under the Field's label, with the Field's
help and its error, tied together for assistive technology and taking part in a form as one control.

Contract: specs/one-time-code-field.spec.json. `<tanrei-one-time-code-field name="code" label="Verification code"
supporting-text="Enter the 6-digit code we sent to your phone." group-size="3"></tanrei-one-time-code-field>`.

Composed (`src/primitives/composed.ts`): its shadow root holds the two members' own elements and nothing
else, so it draws nothing of its own and has no token — every `--tanrei-comp-field-*` and
`--tanrei-comp-one-time-code-input-*` value reaches the members by inheritance, and one instance is set apart by
setting such a property on this element. Each property is its member's, set on that member unchanged. One level
down, the same by hand: `<tanrei-field label="Verification code"><tanrei-one-time-code-input name="code"
group-size="3"></tanrei-one-time-code-input></tanrei-field>` — for something of the product's own inside the frame.

`value` is at every moment the One-time-code input's, and the four events are that input's own, with this element
as their target: `event.target.value` is the code in every listener. It dispatches none itself.

Form-associated: it submits the code under `name` — nothing while disabled —, resets to its `value` attribute, is
restored on navigation, follows a disabled `<fieldset>`, and reports a missing value while `requirement` is
`required` and it is empty. Enter in the cells presses the default button of this element's form.

The element is not focusable itself and has no role: `focus()` goes to the cells, and its name is `label` (with
`label-hidden` where it is not drawn), never `aria-label`.

members.name: formAssociated
members.description: OTF-4: the one control the form meets. Its members stand in its shadow root, outside every form.

members.name: label
members.description: Names the control, visibly and to assistive technology. Required, unless the control names itself (a checkbox or a switch with its own label): then leave it empty and the field adds only help and an error.

members.name: labelHidden
members.description: Does not draw the label, which stays the accessible name (`label-hidden`). For a control whose visible label is elsewhere.

members.name: supportingText
members.description: Help shown below the control and given to assistive technology as the control's description (`supporting-text`). While the field is in error it gives way to `errorText`, unless the design system keeps both (`--tanrei-comp-field-error-text-placement: append`).

members.name: errorText
members.description: Shown while `error` is true, in `supportingText`'s place (below it, which stays, where the design system says `append`): what is wrong with this answer and how to put it right, in words (`error-text`).

members.name: error
members.description: Puts the field in the error condition: the error text is drawn, the control is exposed as invalid and, where it has an error condition of its own, drawn in it. The field never sets this itself.

members.name: disabled
members.description: Disables the control and draws the frame as disabled. Disable a framed control here, not on the control, so that its label follows.

members.name: requirement
members.description: What the form asks of the control: `required` exposes it as required and draws the required mark; `optional` draws the optional tag; `none` says and draws nothing. It never validates.

members.name: requiredMark
members.description: How this control shows that it is required (`required-mark`): `tag` is a small filled tag with `requiredText`, `asterisk` is "*" after the label, `none` draws nothing and keeps the semantics; `auto` takes the design system's answer (`--tanrei-comp-field-requirement-mark`, which follows `--tanrei-sys-behavior-requirement-mark`).

members.name: requiredText
members.description: The text of the required tag (`required-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ requiredText })`). Tanrei has none: without them the asterisk is drawn in the tag's place and the required state is kept.

members.name: optionalText
members.description: The text of the optional tag, also part of the description (`optional-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ optionalText })`). Tanrei has none: without them no tag is drawn and nothing is said.

members.name: value
members.description: The code entered so far: at most `length` characters, digits or — for `alphanumeric` — digits and upper-case letters, with no separator. The `value` attribute is what a form reset returns to.

members.name: length
members.description: How many characters the code has, and so how many cells are drawn. A whole number of 1 or more; anything else draws 6.

members.name: type
members.description: What a cell takes: `numeric` (the default; a numeric keypad) or `alphanumeric` (digits and A to Z, held in upper case; a general keyboard). Anything else behaves as numeric.

members.name: groupSize
members.description: Draws the cells in groups of this many, with a mark between two groups (`group-size`; 3 for a code written "123 456"). 0 draws one group. The value has no separator.

members.name: mask
members.description: Draws the browser's password mark in each filled cell in place of its character, and exposes the field as a password field. Paste and autofill still work.

members.name: readOnly
members.description: Keeps the field focusable and its value readable, and lets nothing change it (`readonly`): for the moment a complete code is being checked.

members.name: hostNameSentence
members.description:
W8: the sentence a debug build names when the host is given an ARIA name. The host has no role: its name is the
frame's `label`. Empty: nothing is reported.

members.name: valueMember
members.description: W5: the member that holds the value, once rendered.

members.name: name
members.description: Web only: the name the value is submitted under.

members.name: formDisabled
members.description: W6, item 6: a disabled `<fieldset>` around the element, or its own `disabled` attribute, as the platform says it.

members.name: control
members.description: W7: the member focus goes to, once rendered.

members.name: given
members.description: W5: the value last set on the element, while the member has not taken it.

members.name: memberValue
members.description: W5: what `value` returns — `initial` is the member's own default, for an element that has not rendered and was given nothing.

members.name: giveValue
members.description: W5: what `value` is set with. The member takes it at the element's next render; what the member holds already changes nothing.

members.name: firstValue
members.description: W6, item 4: the value a form's reset returns to — the `value` attribute, where the first value is written.

members.name: form
members.description: The form it belongs to, if any.

members.name: validity
members.description: The element's validity: its value member's (W6, item 3).

members.name: repeat
members.description: W6, items 2 and 3: the same value and state, the same flags and message, and the member's own anchor.

members.name: memberUpdated
members.description:
W14 (`fills`): called after each word the value member tells its form — when the element first hears it, and after
each of the member's updates, which is when a member speaks. An element whose spec names a member's prop it fills
itself from state the value member holds (a text field: its Field's count text, from its input's count) sets it
here; it reads the member and writes the other member's property, and computes nothing of its own. Does nothing
otherwise.

members.name: passing
members.description: W9: the names of the slots it has passed on, and the watch on its own children for them.

members.name: members
members.description: The members it has rendered: the custom elements of its own shadow tree.

members.name: focus
members.description: W7, item 2: focus is the control's.

members.name: blur
members.description: W7, item 2: what has focus inside the control loses it (an engine does not take it from inside a host it blurs).

members.name: pass
members.description:
W9: a slot of a member, passed on — `${this.pass('label-icon')}` among that member's children. Rendered only while
the element has a child for it: a member that draws room for a filled slot would take a passing slot that is
always there for content.

members.name: getUpdateComplete
members.description: The element has updated when its members have: what it gave them, they have taken.

members.name: focusWhenReady
members.description: The control has rendered what takes focus only after its own first update.

events.description: The person committed a changed value: focus left the field, or Enter was pressed.
events.name: change

events.description: A change by the person left the value `length` characters long. After that change's input, once.

events.description: The person pressed Enter. Cancel it to keep the enclosing form from being submitted.

attributes.description: The id of the form the one-time-code field belongs to, where it stands outside it: the platform's own attribute, which then wins over a form around it. The `form` property is read-only and returns the form element.
attributes.name: form
label
attributes.description: Names the control, visibly and to assistive technology. Required, unless the control names itself (a checkbox or a switch with its own label): then leave it empty and the field adds only help and an error.

attributes.name: label-hidden
attributes.description: Does not draw the label, which stays the accessible name (`label-hidden`). For a control whose visible label is elsewhere.

attributes.name: supporting-text
attributes.description: Help shown below the control and given to assistive technology as the control's description (`supporting-text`). While the field is in error it gives way to `errorText`, unless the design system keeps both (`--tanrei-comp-field-error-text-placement: append`).

attributes.name: error-text
attributes.description: Shown while `error` is true, in `supportingText`'s place (below it, which stays, where the design system says `append`): what is wrong with this answer and how to put it right, in words (`error-text`).

attributes.name: error
attributes.description: Puts the field in the error condition: the error text is drawn, the control is exposed as invalid and, where it has an error condition of its own, drawn in it. The field never sets this itself.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: Disables the control and draws the frame as disabled. Disable a framed control here, not on the control, so that its label follows.

attributes.name: requirement
attributes.description: What the form asks of the control: `required` exposes it as required and draws the required mark; `optional` draws the optional tag; `none` says and draws nothing. It never validates.

attributes.name: required-mark
attributes.description: How this control shows that it is required (`required-mark`): `tag` is a small filled tag with `requiredText`, `asterisk` is "*" after the label, `none` draws nothing and keeps the semantics; `auto` takes the design system's answer (`--tanrei-comp-field-requirement-mark`, which follows `--tanrei-sys-behavior-requirement-mark`).

attributes.name: required-text
attributes.description: The text of the required tag (`required-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ requiredText })`). Tanrei has none: without them the asterisk is drawn in the tag's place and the required state is kept.

attributes.name: optional-text
attributes.description: The text of the optional tag, also part of the description (`optional-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ optionalText })`). Tanrei has none: without them no tag is drawn and nothing is said.

attributes.name: value
attributes.description: The code entered so far: at most `length` characters, digits or — for `alphanumeric` — digits and upper-case letters, with no separator. The `value` attribute is what a form reset returns to.

attributes.name: length
attributes.description: How many characters the code has, and so how many cells are drawn. A whole number of 1 or more; anything else draws 6.

attributes.name: type
attributes.description: What a cell takes: `numeric` (the default; a numeric keypad) or `alphanumeric` (digits and A to Z, held in upper case; a general keyboard). Anything else behaves as numeric.

attributes.name: group-size
attributes.description: Draws the cells in groups of this many, with a mark between two groups (`group-size`; 3 for a code written "123 456"). 0 draws one group. The value has no separator.

attributes.name: mask
attributes.description: Draws the browser's password mark in each filled cell in place of its character, and exposes the field as a password field. Paste and autofill still work.

attributes.name: readonly
attributes.description: Keeps the field focusable and its value readable, and lets nothing change it (`readonly`): for the moment a complete code is being checked.

attributes.name: name

declarations.name: readCharacter
declarations.description:
OTC-4: one character as the field reads it — a decimal digit of any script and a full-width digit or letter as its
ASCII form, a lower-case letter as its upper-case form — or `null` where the type does not permit it.

declarations.name: readPermitted
declarations.description: The permitted characters of `text`, each read by OTC-4, in order; what is not permitted is dropped.

declarations.name: readValue
declarations.description: OTC-18, OTC-19: a value the product set as the field holds it, and whether anything of it was dropped.

declarations.name: readCode
declarations.description:
OTC-11: a whole text — pasted, dropped, dictated or given by autofill — read as one code, or `null` where it holds
none. White space, hyphens and dashes go; if every remaining character is permitted (and there is one) the code is
the first `length` of them. Otherwise, for digits only, the text is searched: exactly one run of exactly `length`
digits that no other digit adjoins is the code ("Your code is 123456."). Anything else is no code.

declarations.name: furthest
declarations.description: OTC-5: the furthest cell that can be active — the first empty cell, or the last cell while all are filled.

declarations.name: settle
declarations.description: The state with its active cell brought inside what the value allows.

declarations.name: typeCharacter
declarations.description:
OTC-6, OTC-10: one permitted character typed — it stands in the active cell, in place of what the cell holds, and the
active cell moves on (it stays on the last); typed over a selected value it replaces the whole value.

declarations.name: typeText
declarations.description: Characters typed one after another (OTC-6: text an input method commits is read character by character).

declarations.name: removeBackward
declarations.description:
OTC-9, OTC-10: Backspace — a filled active cell loses its character and stays active; an empty one loses the
character before it and the active cell moves there; a selected value is emptied. The rest closes the gap.

declarations.name: removeForward
declarations.description: OTC-9, OTC-10: Delete — the active cell loses its character; a selected value is emptied.

declarations.name: removeRun
declarations.description: The platform's removal of a word or a line: everything before the active cell, or everything from it on.

declarations.name: replaceAll
declarations.description: OTC-11, OTC-18: a whole value taken at once; the active cell is the first empty cell, or the last.

declarations.name: PREFIX
declarations.default: '--tanrei-comp-one-time-code-input'

declarations.name: CARET_BLINK_MS
declarations.description:
OTC-7: how long the caret the element draws is shown and hidden for, in milliseconds. The platform's own caret rate
is not exposed to the web; this is the rate browsers' text carets use where the system gives them none. A behaviour
of the platform, not a design value.

declarations.description:
Takes a short code sent to the person — a sign-in or verification code — as one text value drawn in separate cells,
so that its length and what is still missing can be seen, and the browser can fill it in one step.

Contract: specs/one-time-code-input.spec.json. Every visual value is a `--tanrei-comp-one-time-code-input-*` token.

One field, not one input per character: in the shadow root there is exactly one native `<input>`, laid over the row,
whose own text and caret are not drawn; the cells, the caret and the group marks under it are a drawing of its value
and are hidden from assistive technology. So it is one Tab stop and one text box whose value is the whole code, and
an input method, the browser's autofill (`autocomplete="one-time-code"`), the clipboard and dictation meet one text
input. It has no `maxlength` and no `pattern`: a code pasted as "123 456" would be cut before it could be read.

It has no label, help or error text of its own: put it in a `<tanrei-field>`, which names it, describes it, marks it
required and puts it in its error condition; where the visible label is elsewhere (a dialog's headline), give
`label`, which is never drawn. `<tanrei-field label="Verification code"><tanrei-one-time-code-input name="code"
group-size="3"></tanrei-one-time-code-input></tanrei-field>`.

A permitted character fills the active cell — replacing what it holds — and moves on; other characters are dropped.
Text that is pasted, dropped or filled is read whole as one code ("123 456", "123-456", "Your code is 123456.").
`input` fires on every change by the person, `complete` once after the `input` that leaves the value `length` long,
`change` when a changed value is committed (focus leaves, or Enter), `action` on Enter. Nothing else happens when the
code is complete: checking it is the product's.

Form-associated: it submits the code under `name`, resets to its `value` attribute, is restored on navigation,
follows a disabled `<fieldset>`, and reports a missing value while its Field says it is required and it is empty.

members.name: focused
members.description: OTC-7: the native input has focus, however it was gained.

members.name: state
members.description: OTC-5, OTC-10: the active cell and whether the whole value is selected. Its `value` follows the element's.

members.name: composingText
members.description: OTC-6: the text an input method is composing, as the method gave it; empty while none is.

members.name: formDisabled
members.description: Set by an ancestor `<fieldset disabled>`.

members.name: says
members.description: What it tells its form, said where an element composed around it hears it (src/primitives/form-says.ts).

members.name: field
members.description:
What a Field around it gives it (src/primitives/field.ts): the name while it has no `label` of its own, the
description, the invalid, required and disabled states (OTC-17, OTC-20, OTC-22).

members.name: held
members.description: The value the element last held by its own doing: a `value` that differs was set by the product (OTC-18).

members.name: committed
members.description: OTC-13: the value at the last commit.

members.name: composing
members.description: OTC-6: an input method is composing; the native element is its own until it ends.

members.name: settling
members.description: A composition has just ended: what the engine still sends for it (an input, the key that committed it) is not the person's edit or the action key.

members.name: pressing
members.description: OTC-5: focus arrives by a press on a cell, which has chosen the active cell.

members.name: fresh
members.description: Focus has arrived and the person has done nothing yet: a selection of the whole text is the browser's own (it selects a text input it tabs into), not the person's select all.

members.name: form
members.description: The form it belongs to, if any.

members.name: validity
members.description: The element's validity: a missing value while its Field says it is required and it is empty (OTC-29).

members.name: cells
members.description: OTC-19: the number of cells — `length`, or 6 where it is not a whole number of 1 or more.

members.name: kind
members.description: OTC-19: `type`, or numeric for a value it does not know.

members.name: groups
members.description: OTC-15, OTC-19: the cells of each group — one group unless `groupSize` is a whole number from 1 to length minus 1.

members.name: locked
members.description: OTC-20, OTC-21: nothing the person does changes the value.

members.name: syncForm
members.description: The value a form submits — the code alone, or an empty string — and what its validation is told.

members.name: markRows
members.description:
OTC-23: the mark of a group that begins a row is not drawn. The one thing read from the layout: whether a group
stands on the row of the group before it. The mark is positioned, so hiding it moves nothing.

members.name: show
members.description:
OTC-2, OTC-5: the native element holds the value and its insertion point stands at the active cell — before its
character while it is filled, at the end of the value while it is empty — or the whole value is selected (OTC-10).
Never written into a composition: the text is the input method's until it ends.

members.name: take
members.description:
Takes a state an edit produced. When it changes the value the element holds it before anyone hears of it, as a
native control does: `input`, then `complete` when the value is `length` long — once for the change.

members.name: commit
members.description: OTC-13: a changed value is committed — `change`, when it differs from the value at the last commit.

members.name: insert
members.description:
Text that arrives in the field. One character from the keyboard is typed (OTC-4, OTC-6): a permitted one fills the
active cell, any other is dropped. A whole text — pasted, dropped, dictated, filled — is read as one code wherever
the active cell is (OTC-11), and changes nothing where it holds none.

members.name: onInput
members.description:
The native element's own `input`: it is stopped here (the element's `input` is the composed event `take()` fires).
What reaches this without having been read in `beforeinput` — autofill, and input a browser does not announce or
does not let be stopped — is read from the element: a removal as the browser made it, one character as typed, and
anything else as a whole text (OTC-11).

members.name: onNativeChange
members.description: The browser's own `change` is not the field's (OTC-13 decides when a value is committed).

members.name: onCompositionEnd
members.description:
The composition ended: what it committed is read character by character, as typed text is; a cancelled one leaves
nothing. The engines differ in what follows — an `input` that is no longer composing (Firefox), nothing (Chromium),
and the `keydown` of the key that committed it, which no longer says that it composes (WebKit) — so for the rest of
this turn nothing the native element sends is read as an edit or as the action key.

members.name: act
members.description: OTC-13: the action key — the commit, then `action`, then the form's submission unless `action` was cancelled.

members.name: cellAt
members.description: The cell at a point of the window, or -1: the native element lies over the cells and takes the press.

members.name: onMouseDown
members.description:
OTC-25: a press takes focus and makes the pressed cell active while it is filled, and otherwise the first empty
cell. It is not an action and draws no answer. The native element's own answer to a press — its caret where the
unseen text is, a selection by dragging or by a second press — is not wanted (OTC-10), so the press is the
element's: it focuses the native element itself.

members.name: onSelect
members.description:
OTC-10: a selection of the native text. The whole value selected by the person — the browser's menu, a touch
keyboard's "select all" — is select all; any other selection (a part of the text, or the one a browser makes when
it focuses an input) is undone: the field has no selection of some cells only.

members.name: onCopy
members.description: OTC-10: copy takes the whole value, without group marks, whichever cell is active; nothing while mask is set.

members.name: onCut
members.description: OTC-10: cut takes the whole value and empties the field; while mask is set it gives nothing and changes nothing.

members.name: onPaste
members.description: OTC-11: pasted text is read whole as one code. Never blocked, masked or not.

members.name: onDrop
members.description: OTC-11: dropped text is read whole as one code, and the field takes focus as a native input does.

members.name: drawn
members.description:
What the cells draw: the value, or — while an input method composes — the value as it would be if the composing
text were committed now, with the cells that text fills marked (OTC-6). The value itself does not change.

declarations.description:
One choice of a select or a combobox: a label, the value it stands for, and optionally a supporting line and a
glyph. `<tanrei-option value="jp">Japan</tanrei-option>`: the label is the `label` attribute or, without one, the
element's text, as a native `<option>`'s.

The element is data for the field that holds it: it draws nothing itself, takes no focus and fires no event. Its
field reads it, renders the option's row in its own list and reads it again when an attribute or the text changes.
Every property reflects to its attribute, which is what the field reads.

A run of related options of a select or a combobox, optionally titled:
`<tanrei-option-group label="Asia">…</tanrei-option-group>`. The title is the `label` attribute, as a native
`<optgroup>`'s — a `title` attribute would also draw the browser's tooltip. The field separates a group from what is

declarations.description:
The head of a page's content: the page's title as its heading, with a sentence that says what the page is, a line of facts about it, the actions for the whole page and the way back up above it — in the content, scrolling with it, laid out by its own width, and never a control. Contract: specs/page-header.spec.json. The element has **no shadow root**: it is the box around the page's own elements, which stay in the document. The title is the page's own heading — the `h1` a crawler, a reader mode, a page without script and a screen reader all find — and is never hidden, repeated or given another level. ```html …

Announcements

Tokens are derived, and design systems are layers

One value changes in one place, and everything built on it follows.

20 September 2026 The Tanrei team 4 min read
EditShare
 ``` Parts are found by what they are, among the element's children, and are written in the order they are read (PGH-11): `tanrei-breadcrumbs` or `[data-part="breadcrumbs"]`; `[data-part="eyebrow"]`; the title — the heading (`h1` to `h6`), or `[data-part="title"]` for one that is not a heading; the description — the first `p` without a `data-part`, or `[data-part="description"]`; `[data-part="meta"]`, each of whose element children is one item; and `[data-part="actions"]`. Everything drawn is `@tanrei/web/page-header.css` — every value a `--tanrei-comp-page-header-*` token — which draws the head before and without this script; the element adds the same sheet to the root it is connected to, so it also works inside another component's shadow root. Nothing is shown differently before the element is defined. The script adds two things a reader does not see on a content page: the parts of a head **built by script** — `headline`, `description` and `eyebrow` each write their element where the children have none, the heading at `level` — and the debug reports of PGH-23 and PGH-24. The head takes no input and emits no event.
declarations.name: TanreiPageHeader

slots.description: The page's own elements, in reading order: the breadcrumbs, `[data-part="eyebrow"]`, the heading, the description's `p`, `[data-part="meta"]` and `[data-part="actions"]`. They are children in the document, not slotted nodes: the element has no shadow root.

declarations.description:
Shows content a person can read and operate on a small surface that opens beside the control they pressed and stays
with it, without dimming or blocking the rest of the page.

Contract: specs/popover.spec.json. The product owns the control: `anchor` is the id of the element the popover stands
beside, in the popover's own tree (`anchorElement` for an element an id cannot reach), and that element is also the
opener — the one that carries `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` and takes focus back —
unless `opener` / `openerElement` names another (a field that anchors the surface, with a button inside it that
opens it). The product sets `open` when the opener is pressed, and to false when the popover fires `close`: the
popover never opens or closes by itself, on hover, on focus or after a time.

The drawn popover is a `popover="manual"` element in the shadow root, in the top layer (above an open modal
`<dialog>` the element stands in), holding a `role="dialog"` container that is not modal: no scrim, no focus trap,
nothing behind it inert. It is placed against the anchor by script — the side and the alignment `placement` names,
`offset` away and moved along the side by `crossOffset`; flipped to the opposite side, limited to the room where
neither side has enough (its content then scrolls between the header and the actions), shifted along the side and,
in a window smaller than its least size, moved back over the anchor — and follows the anchor while open. When
nothing of the anchor can be seen it fires `close` with the reason `anchor-hidden`.

Focus: opening moves focus to the slotted element marked `autofocus`, else to the container (`initialFocus="anchor"`
leaves it where it is). The popover stands in the focus order directly after its opener wherever it is in the
document: Tab on the opener enters it, Shift+Tab from its first element returns to the opener, Tab from its last
element moves on to what follows the opener. Escape, a press outside, focus leaving, the close button and the
anchor going out of sight each fire `close` once, with the reason; an action never does. An overlay opened from an
element inside it (a menu, a tooltip, another popover, a dialog) is its own: a press or focus in it is not outside,
Escape closes it first, and it closes with the popover. Closing returns focus to the opener if it was inside.

The actions are `<tanrei-button slot="actions">` children, each marked `confirming` or `dismissive` where it is one,
placed as a Button group places them; a Button without a `variant` attribute takes the popover's
(`comp.popover.actions.variant`). `arrow` draws a triangle that points at the anchor, one shape with the container
(unset, the system's `comp.popover.arrow.visible` decides).

Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-popover-*` tokens.

members.name: words

members.name: open
members.description: Whether the popover is shown. Controlled: set it when the opener is pressed, and to false in answer to `close`. Reflected.

members.name: placement
members.description:
Where it prefers to stand: a side of the anchor and how it lines up along it, or `auto`. It flips to the opposite
side when that one has no room, keeping the alignment. Anything else is placed as `bottom-start` (POP-37). Reflected.

members.name: offset
members.description: The distance from the anchor's edge, in CSS pixels; 0 lets them touch. Null takes `offset`, the token.

members.name: crossOffset
members.description:
How far it moves along the side it stands on, in CSS pixels: positive towards the end above or below the anchor,
towards the bottom beside it. It never moves the popover off the anchor's side. The attribute is `cross-offset`.

members.name: arrow
members.description:
Whether it draws an arrow that points at the anchor. Null, the default, takes the system's choice
(`arrow.visible`, off in the default system). The attribute: absent is null, `arrow` is true, `arrow="false"` is false.

members.name: width
members.description: `content`: as wide as its content, between its least and greatest width. `anchor`: as wide as the anchor. Anything else is `content` (POP-37). Reflected.

members.name: inset
members.description: Insets the content by the container's paddings. False — the attribute `no-inset` — lets content that pads itself reach the edges.

members.name: initialFocus
members.description:
`popover`: focus moves into it when it opens. `anchor`: focus stays where it is (a surface under a field the person
is typing in). Anything else is `popover` (POP-37). The attribute is `initial-focus`.

members.name: headline
members.description: What the popover is about, drawn in its header and used as its accessible name. Empty draws none; the popover is then named by `label`.

members.name: label
members.description: Names the popover for assistive technology where it draws no headline. Never drawn; ignored while `headline` is given.

members.name: closable
members.description: Draws the close button at the end of the header. Reflected.

members.name: closeLabel
members.description: The close button's accessible name ("Close filters"). Required while `closable` (POP-13). The attribute is `close-label`.

members.name: anchor
members.description: The id of the anchor — the element the popover stands beside — in the popover's own tree (its document or shadow root).

members.name: anchorElement
members.description: The anchor as an element, for one an id cannot reach (another shadow root). It wins over `anchor`.

members.name: opener
members.description: The id of the opener, where it is not the anchor: the element that is pressed, carries the open state and takes focus back.

members.name: openerElement
members.description: The opener as an element, for one an id cannot reach. It wins over `opener`.

members.name: inline
members.description: For tests: draws the open container in place — inside its positioned ancestor, which stands for the window — not in the top layer; it then answers no dismissal and moves no focus.

members.name: hasActions

members.name: content
members.description: POP-14: the content children, assigned to the default slot.

members.name: presented

members.name: lastReason

events.name: close
events.description: The popover asks to be closed: `detail.reason` is `escape`, `outside`, `focus-out`, `close` (its close button) or `anchor-hidden`. Set `open` to false.

attributes.name: open
attributes.description: Whether the popover is shown. Controlled: set it when the opener is pressed, and to false in answer to `close`. Reflected.

attributes.name: placement
attributes.description:
Where it prefers to stand: a side of the anchor and how it lines up along it, or `auto`. It flips to the opposite
side when that one has no room, keeping the alignment. Anything else is placed as `bottom-start` (POP-37). Reflected.

attributes.name: offset
attributes.description: The distance from the anchor's edge, in CSS pixels; 0 lets them touch. Null takes `offset`, the token.

attributes.name: cross-offset
attributes.description:
How far it moves along the side it stands on, in CSS pixels: positive towards the end above or below the anchor,
towards the bottom beside it. It never moves the popover off the anchor's side. The attribute is `cross-offset`.

attributes.name: arrow
attributes.description:
Whether it draws an arrow that points at the anchor. Null, the default, takes the system's choice
(`arrow.visible`, off in the default system). The attribute: absent is null, `arrow` is true, `arrow="false"` is false.

attributes.name: width
attributes.description: `content`: as wide as its content, between its least and greatest width. `anchor`: as wide as the anchor. Anything else is `content` (POP-37). Reflected.

attributes.name: no-inset
attributes.description: Insets the content by the container's paddings. False — the attribute `no-inset` — lets content that pads itself reach the edges.

attributes.name: initial-focus
attributes.description:
`popover`: focus moves into it when it opens. `anchor`: focus stays where it is (a surface under a field the person
is typing in). Anything else is `popover` (POP-37). The attribute is `initial-focus`.

attributes.name: headline
attributes.description: What the popover is about, drawn in its header and used as its accessible name. Empty draws none; the popover is then named by `label`.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Names the popover for assistive technology where it draws no headline. Never drawn; ignored while `headline` is given.

attributes.name: closable
attributes.description: Draws the close button at the end of the header. Reflected.

attributes.name: close-label
attributes.description: The close button's accessible name ("Close filters"). Required while `closable` (POP-13). The attribute is `close-label`.

attributes.name: anchor
attributes.description: The id of the anchor — the element the popover stands beside — in the popover's own tree (its document or shadow root).

attributes.name: opener
attributes.description: The id of the opener, where it is not the anchor: the element that is pressed, carries the open state and takes focus back.

attributes.name: inline
attributes.description: For tests: draws the open container in place — inside its positioned ancestor, which stands for the window — not in the top layer; it then answers no dismissal and moves no focus.

declarations.description:
Shows how far a task has come, or that it is under way when how far is unknown, as a bar or a ring.

Contract: specs/progress-indicator.spec.json. As a native `<progress>`: no `value` attribute (or removing it, or
`value = null`) is indeterminate. Every visual value is a `--tanrei-comp-progress-indicator-*` token — the bar's
thickness and the ring's size and stroke per size, the track and indicator colors, the ends' shape, the gap after the
indicator, the stop indicator, and the motion of a value change and of the indeterminate cycle. Whether the gap is
drawn at all is `separation` (PRG-17): `auto` follows `comp.progress-indicator.track.separation`, and so the design
system's `sys.behavior.separation`. Whether the stop indicator is drawn is its size alone, under either (PRG-5).

The host is the progressbar (`role="progressbar"`, `aria-label` from `label`, `aria-valuemin` / `-max` / `-now` and
`aria-valuetext` from `value-text` while determinate; `aria-busy="true"` and no value while indeterminate). It is
never focusable and never announces a change by itself. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` a value change shows
at once and the indeterminate form pulses in place; off screen, its animation is paused.

declarations.description:
Lets people choose exactly one option from a small group shown all at once.

Contract: specs/radio-button.spec.json. Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-radio-button-*` tokens, one set
per condition (unselected, selected) and state: how a state looks is the active design system's decision.

A group is the options with one `name` in the same form — or, outside any form, in the same document or shadow root —
as for a native radio. The options keep it themselves: selecting one clears the others (RAD-3), the arrow keys move
through the enabled ones and select as they go (RAD-4), and the group has one tab stop (RAD-5). Put the options in an
element with `role="radiogroup"` and a name (`aria-labelledby`), or in a `<fieldset>` with a `<legend>` (RAD-16).

Form-associated: while selected it submits `value` under `name`, resets to its `checked` attribute and follows a
disabled `<fieldset>`. It selects itself before it fires `input` and `change`; the option it replaced fires nothing.

declarations.description:
Asks one question that has exactly one answer among a few options shown all at once. Built from a field group
(`<tanrei-field-group>`) and radio buttons (`<tanrei-radio-button>`): the field group itself, in its radio-group
kind — its label, requirement, description and one error — around the product's own radio buttons, whose chosen
value the group holds under one name.

Contract: specs/radio-group.spec.json. `<tanrei-radio-group label="Delivery" name="delivery" value="express">
<tanrei-radio-button value="standard" label="Standard"></tanrei-radio-button>…</tanrei-radio-group>`: the radio
buttons are the element's children and stay in the product's light DOM; inside the group they need no `name`
(RAD-25).

Composed (`src/primitives/composed.ts`): its shadow root holds the field group's own element, with
`kind="radio-group"` and `spacing="controls"`, around a slot, so it draws nothing of its own and has no token — every
`--tanrei-comp-field-group-*` and `--tanrei-comp-radio-button-*` value reaches the members by inheritance, and one
instance is set apart by setting such a property on this element. Each of the eleven props of the frame is the field
group's, set on it unchanged. One level down, the same by hand: `<tanrei-field-group kind="radio-group"
label="Delivery"><tanrei-radio-button name="delivery" value="standard" label="Standard"></tanrei-radio-button>…
</tanrei-field-group>` — the same picture and the same radio group, without the one value, the one `change` and the
place in a form as one control.

It holds one value. `value` decides which radio button is selected; a person's selection sets `value` and fires
`input` and one `change`, and the radio buttons inside it fire nothing of their own. The arrow keys move through the
enabled radio buttons, wrapping, and select as they go; the group is one stop in the focus order — the selected
radio button, or the first enabled one.

Form-associated: it submits `value` under `name` — also while the radio button of that value is one the product
disabled by itself — returns to its `value` attribute when the form is reset, is restored on navigation, follows
`<fieldset disabled>`, and reports `valueMissing` while `requirement="required"` and `value` is empty, in the
browser's own words for an unanswered set of radio buttons. It never sets `error` itself.

The element is not focusable itself and has no role: `focus()` goes to the radio button that is the stop, and the
radio group that assistive technology is told of — its name, its description and its required, invalid and disabled
states and its orientation — is the field group's own element (`label`, never `aria-label` on this one).

A result group (SRC-44): its heading — a quiet title, or a result's row while it has a destination — then its
results, group.gap from what stands above and below it in the view; under a linked heading they step in by
group.indent, hit areas and highlights with them.

A suggestion the search offers while the person types — the spec's item kind `suggestion`: a query they searched
before, or a completion. Choosing it fires `select` and the product sets the value; a thing the product opens is a
`<tanrei-search-result>`. It is data, as an `<option>` in a `<datalist>`: the search draws the row, names it and
answers it; the element itself draws nothing.

declarations.description:
A thing the search found that the person can go to — the spec's item kind `result`: a page, a section of a page, a
message, a file. It is a link, never an option: with `href` its row is an `<a>` in its shadow root, which the browser
follows as it follows any link; without one it is a `<button>`, and `select` is all that happens.

The excerpt is its child content — text with `<mark>` elements around the matches, which is what search engines hand
back (`<tanrei-search-result headline="Layers" href="/tokens/#layers">A layer changes a <mark>token</mark>.</tanrei-search-result>`)
— or, while it has no child content, the `excerpt` runs. Putting an engine's HTML there is the product's act: the
element never parses a string as markup.

Place it in a `<tanrei-search>` or a `<tanrei-search-result-group>`: the search answers its press and its keys (Down
and Up Arrow move through the results; typing returns to the input) and fires `select` when it is activated in place.

Results that belong together, under one heading — the spec's item kind `result-group`: the sections found in one

declarations.description:
Lets people search the product from a bar or a compact trigger, and offers suggestions and results while they type in
a view under the bar, in a dialog or over the whole screen.

Contract: specs/search.spec.json. The value is edited in a native `<input type="search" enterkeyhint="search">` in the
shadow root, as the text field's, with the browser's own cancel button hidden: the search draws its own
clear button. Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-search-*` tokens, its one condition's parts by state.

Opening and closing: a press on the bar, typing or Down Arrow opens the view (focus alone never does); Escape, a
chosen suggestion, submitting, the back button, and — docked — a press outside, Tab and focus leaving close it. The
element sets its own `expanded` and then fires `toggle`, whose `detail` holds `expanded` and, when closing, `reason`.
Set `expanded` yourself to open or close it without an event.

`docked` (the default) opens a view under the bar: a manual popover in the top layer, placed by script (flipped above
the bar when there is more room there), following the bar. Focus stays in the input — the WAI-ARIA combobox pattern:
the input controls the suggestions' listbox and names the active suggestion as its active descendant. A press outside
closes it AND reaches the element under it. `full-screen` opens a modal `<dialog>` over the whole window with its own
header (a back button, the input, the clear button); it takes focus, keeps it, and gives it back to the bar's input.

A site search. `bar="button"` draws a trigger shaped like the bar — the search glyph, the placeholder
and the shortcut hint — and `bar="icon"` an icon-only Button; a trigger opens a modal view, where the input is
(`presentation="dialog"`: a `<dialog>` hung from the top of the window over a scrim, a press on which closes it,
its header starting with the same back button as the full-screen view's, so it can be left by Tab and Enter alone;
`docked` with a trigger opens as `dialog`). `shortcut` (chords separated by spaces, as the keyboard shortcut's `keys`)
is written as a hint — a line of text, no keycaps — and exposed as `aria-keyshortcuts`; it makes the keys work only with `bind-shortcut`, which adds one
`keydown` listener on the window while the element is connected and enabled. The results are
`<tanrei-search-result>` and `<tanrei-search-result-group>` children: links, never options, reached from the input
with Down Arrow (real focus), left with Up Arrow or by typing. `status` and `status-text` draw the status row — a
`role="status"` element that exists from the first render (`role="alert"` while `status="error"`). The search never
runs a query: listen to `input`, then set the results, `status` and `status-text`.

Form-associated: with a `name` it submits `value`, and Enter (with no suggestion active) requests its form's
submission after `submit`, unless `submit` was cancelled. The `inline` attribute, for tests and documentation, draws
the open view in place: the docked view under the bar, the full-screen view filling the element.

members.name: kept

members.name: mirror
members.description:
SRC-32: a suggestion's leading glyph is marked when the icon set mirrors its name in right-to-left
(src/primitives/glyph-mirror.ts); `iconGlyph()` draws the mark. The search glyph (SRC-2) is not named here, and the
back and clear Buttons mark their own glyphs (BTN-19: `arrow_back` is flagged, `close` is not).

members.name: system
members.description: SRC-32: a switch of the design system changes the icon set; the results' glyphs are marked again (`updated()`).

members.name: presentation
members.description:
Where the view opens: `docked` under the bar, without taking focus from it; `dialog`, a modal surface near the top
of the window with its own header (a large screen, opened from a trigger); or `full-screen`, over the whole window
with its own header (a small screen).

members.name: bar
members.description:
What stands where the search is placed. `field`: the bar with its input. `button`: a trigger shaped like the bar
that holds no input — the search glyph, the placeholder and the shortcut hint — for an app bar with room. `icon`: an
icon-only Button showing the search glyph, for an app bar without. A trigger opens a modal view (`dialog` or
`full-screen`), where the input is; `docked` with a trigger opens as `dialog`.

members.name: value
members.description: The query. Setting it shows it and fires nothing. The `value` attribute is what a form reset returns to.

members.name: label
members.description: Names the search field, the trigger, the view, the suggestions and the results for assistive technology ("Search mail"). Drawn only as a button trigger's text while `placeholder` is empty. Required.

members.name: placeholder
members.description: A hint shown while the value is empty, and the text of a button trigger. Never a replacement for `label`.

members.name: expanded
members.description: Whether the view is open. The search sets it itself (and fires `toggle`); set it to open or close the view yourself.

members.name: disabled
members.description: Prevents focus, editing and opening the view.

members.name: clearLabel
members.description: The clear button's accessible name, in the product's language ("Clear search"; `clear-label`).

members.name: backLabel
members.description: The accessible name of the back button in a modal view's header — dialog or full-screen ("Back"; `back-label`).

members.name: shortcut
members.description:
The keyboard shortcut that opens the search, in the keyboard shortcut component's key names: one chord per string
(`["mod+k"]`, `["/"]`; the attribute holds the chords separated by spaces, `shortcut="mod+k"`). The search writes it
as a hint, a line of text with no keycaps — at the end of a button trigger, and in the bar while the value is empty and the input is not focused —
and exposes it as `aria-keyshortcuts` of its trigger or its input. It makes the keys work only with `bindShortcut`;
otherwise the product binds them and sets `expanded`.

members.name: bindShortcut
members.description:
Makes the search itself listen for `shortcut`, anywhere in the window, while it is connected and enabled: the keys
open it, and close it again while it is open (`bind-shortcut`). One chord; a press something else cancelled, a key
repeating while held, an input-method composition and — for a chord without mod, ctrl or alt — a press while focus
is in an element that takes text are left alone. Off by default.

members.name: status
members.description:
What the product's search is doing, which the product sets: `idle` (results, or none, are final), `loading` (a
query is running: the status row shows a loading indicator after its delay, and the results are marked busy) or
`error` (the query failed: `statusText` is drawn as an error and announced at once). The search never runs a query.

members.name: statusText
members.description:
The status row's text, in the product's language, announced to assistive technology when it changes
(`status-text`): the count ("12 results for tokens"), that nothing was found, the failure; while loading, the
loading indicator's name ("Searching"). Empty draws no status row unless `status` is `loading`.

members.name: inline
members.description: For tests and documentation: draws the open view in place, without the overlay's behaviour.

members.name: name
members.description: Web only: the name it is submitted under.

members.name: entries
members.description: The results and result groups (children), in the product's order.

members.name: iconColumn
members.description: SRC-16, SRC-42: any suggestion or result has a leading icon, so every row keeps the column.

members.name: active
members.description: The active suggestion's index (the input's active descendant), or -1.

members.name: hasContent
members.description: The default slot holds the product's own content (anything but the suggestions).

members.name: formDisabled
members.description: Set by an ancestor `<fieldset disabled>`.

members.default: new NativeTextController({ input: () => this.barInput, value: () => this.value, setValue: (value) => (this.value = value) })
members.description: SRC-4: the bar's input and the header's, each kept in step with `value` around an input method (TXF-1, TXF-4).

members.name: headerText
members.default: new NativeTextController({ input: () => this.headerInput, value: () => this.value, setValue: (value) => (this.value = value) })

members.description:

button trigger is pressed as the bar is, and by Enter and Space as a button.

members.name: binding

members.name: barForm

members.name: triggered
