Where the view opens now. SRC-27: a presentation the search does not define is drawn as docked. SRC-36: a trigger
opens a modal view — a docked view has no input of its own — so docked with a trigger is the dialog.

members.name: modal
members.description: SRC-9, SRC-40: the view is a modal one, with a header of its own.

members.name: statusNow
members.description: SRC-27: a status the search does not define is idle.

members.name: statusShown
members.description: SRC-47: the status row is drawn.

members.name: viewHasContent
members.description: The view has content: a suggestion, a status row, a result, a result group, or something in the default slot (SRC-7).

members.name: rows
members.description: SRC-49: the results in view order, across groups — a linked group heading counts as one, a title does not.

members.name: currentInput
members.description: The input focus belongs to now: the header's while a modal view is open, else the bar's.

members.name: focus
members.description:
Sends focus to the input it belongs to now: the header's while a modal view (dialog or full-screen) is open, the
bar's while the view is docked or closed — and, while the bar is a button or an icon and the view is closed, to
that trigger, as the platform's own delegation does. It opens and closes nothing (SRC-5), and a disabled search
takes no focus (SRC-25). This is how the product's own content in the view (SRC-46) gives focus back when it
removes the element that held it, as the search's own clear button does (SRC-10): behind an open modal view the
platform's delegation alone would land on the dialog, where nothing can be typed.

members.name: form
members.description: The form it belongs to, if any.

members.name: readChildren
members.description: The suggestions, the results and the result groups (children), and whether anything else is the view's content.

members.name: checkResults
members.description: SRC-27: what a debug build reports about the results and the result groups.

members.name: checkSuggestions
members.description: SRC-27: what a debug build reports about the suggestions.

members.name: expand
members.description: SRC-5: the search opens its view — its own `expanded`, then `toggle` — once.

members.name: collapse
members.description: SRC-6: the search closes its view with a reason, once; the value stays as it is.

members.name: choose
members.description: SRC-15: a suggestion was chosen: `select` with its value, then the view closes. The value is the product's to set.

members.name: submit
members.description:
SRC-13: the action key: `submit`, then the view closes — unless it shows a result, a result group or a status row:
what the person asked for is already in front of them — then, in a form, unless cancelled, the form is submitted.

members.name: clearValue
members.description: SRC-10, SRC-12: the value emptied by the person (the clear button, Escape): `input` once, never a toggle.

members.name: setActive
members.description: SRC-14: the active suggestion, scrolled into view inside the view's scrolling box, and its ring's focus style (SRC-21).

members.name: onInput
members.description:
SRC-4 (TXF-1): the person changed the value. The native `input` is composed, so it leaves the shadow root by itself —
after the element has taken the new value. SRC-5: typing opens the view; SRC-14: it leaves no suggestion active.

members.name: onInputKeyDown
members.description: SRC-5, SRC-12, SRC-13, SRC-14: the keys the input answers. Escape while open and Tab are the host's (below).

members.name: onHostKeyDown
members.description: SRC-6, SRC-9: Escape anywhere in the search closes an open view; Tab closes the docked one and stays in the full-screen one.

members.name: onResultKeyDown
members.description:
SRC-49: the keys a focused result answers. Down and Up Arrow move real focus through the results in view order,
across groups, staying on the last and going from the first back to the input (the last suggestion active, where
there is one). Typing, deleting or pasting moves focus to the input, so that the key edits the value there. Enter is
the browser's own activation of the link; the row only shows its press (SRC-19). Returns whether the key was taken.

members.name: focusResult
members.description: SRC-49: real focus on the result at `index` in view order (the browser scrolls it into view); none is active meanwhile.

members.name: resultFocused
members.description: Whether focus is in a result's row now.

members.name: onFocusIn
members.description: SRC-42, SRC-51: the result that takes focus — its ring's focus style (SRC-21), and which one to miss when it is removed.

members.name: onResultClick
members.description:
SRC-45: a result was activated. In place — a primary press, a touch or Enter, without a modifier key, in the same
window — `select` with its value, then the browser follows the link unless `select` was cancelled (a router took
it), then the view closes. Any other way (a modifier key, `target: new`; the middle button fires no click) nothing
is emitted and the view stays, so that a person can open several results from one search. Never Space on a link.

members.name: onResultPointerDown
members.description: SRC-42, SRC-19: a result's row shows its press, from the point of contact.

members.name: onResultPointerOut
members.description: The pointer left the pressed result (its row fills it), as a row's own `pointerleave`.

members.name: onFocusOut
members.description: SRC-6: focus moving out of the search closes the docked view.

members.name: onOutsidePress
members.description: SRC-6: a press outside the bar and the view closes the docked view; the press also reaches what is under it.

members.name: onInputPointerDown
members.description: SRC-14: a press in the input moves the caret, which leaves no suggestion active.

members.name: fromBar
members.description: Whether an event came from the bar's own elements rather than a slot's icon button or the clear button.

members.name: onBarMouseDown
members.description: A press on the bar outside the input focuses the input without leaving it first (as the text field's TXF-8).

members.name: onBarClick
members.description: SRC-5: a press on the bar — outside its slots and the clear button — focuses the input and opens the view.

members.name: onClear
members.description: SRC-10: the clear button empties the value and gives focus back to the input it belongs to; nothing opens or closes.

members.name: onBack
members.description: SRC-11, SRC-40: the back button closes the modal view it stands in — full-screen or dialog.

members.name: onTriggerClick
members.description: SRC-36: the trigger was activated (by pointer, touch, Enter or Space — a button's own click): the modal view opens.

members.name: onTriggerFocus
members.description: SRC-36: where style queries are missing, the trigger's focus style is read when focus arrives (the glow).

members.name: outsideDialog
members.description: SRC-40, SRC-6: a press on the dialog view's scrim — outside its container, begun and ended there — closes it.

members.name: onScrimClick
members.description: The scrim of a dialog view drawn in place (tests and documentation) answers as the backdrop does.

members.name: onNativeCancel
members.description: SRC-6: the browser's own close request without a key (Android's back) arrives as the dialog's cancel.

members.name: pressRow
members.description: The row that is pressed now; a new press ends the last one's at once.

members.name: onViewMouseDown
members.description:
SRC-8: a press on a suggestion, on the status row or on the docked view's surface never takes focus from the input.
SRC-9, SRC-40: in a modal view a press on anything that takes no focus of its own keeps focus inside (on the header,
it goes to the input).

members.name: place
members.description: SRC-7: the docked view, placed under the bar (or above it when there is more room there), as wide as it.

members.name: follow
members.description: SRC-7: follows the bar while it moves (scrolling, layout, the viewport, the keyboard) — asked by FollowController, frame by frame only while something moves.

members.name: following
members.default: new FollowController(this, { followed: () => [this.barElement], sized: () => [this.view, this.view?.querySelector('.scroll')], check: this.follow, })

members.name: syncView
members.description: SRC-7, SRC-23: the docked view is drawn while expanded, docked and holding content; it grows in and fades out.

members.name: onViewport
members.description: SRC-9: the full-screen view above the on-screen keyboard.

members.name: presentFull
members.description: SRC-9: modal over the whole window, the page held, focus to the header's input with the caret at the end.

members.name: withdrawFull
members.description: SRC-9: out of the top layer (fading), the page given back, focus back to the bar's input — which does not reopen it.

members.name: convention
members.description:
SRC-38, KBS-2: whose keyboard the chord is read for — the one the hint is written for: the nearest ancestor's
`data-tanrei-keyboard-convention` (the search's own included), else the platform's.

members.name: onWindowKeyDown
members.description:
SRC-38: the bound chord, pressed anywhere in the window, opens the search — as its trigger does, or by focusing its
input — and closes it again with the reason shortcut, and does nothing else. Left alone: a press something else has
taken, a key repeating while held, an input-method composition, and a chord without mod, ctrl or alt while focus is
in an element that takes text (the search's own input included), so that such a key types there.

members.name: expose
members.description:
SRC-36, SRC-37: what the trigger or the bar's input carries for assistive technology besides its name — the
shortcut as `aria-keyshortcuts`, in the form the keyboard shortcut it draws gives (KBS-12), and for a trigger that
it opens a dialog and whether that is open. An icon trigger is a Tanrei Button: they go on its native button.

members.name: keepActions
members.description: SRC-34: the bar's action buttons in reading order — the clear button while it is shown, then the trailing slot's elements.

members.name: renderInput
members.description: SRC-24: the input's semantics — a search field named by label; a combobox while its view shows the suggestions.

members.name: renderClear
members.description: SRC-10: an icon-only text Button showing close, small in the bar and medium in the header.

members.name: renderBody
members.description:
SRC-7, SRC-9, SRC-16, SRC-24, SRC-29, SRC-46: what a view holds, from top to bottom — the suggestions' listbox, the
status row, the results and result groups, then the product's content; a part that is absent takes no room.

SRC-47, SRC-48: the status row's two live regions exist from the moment the view opens — the polite one holds
statusText while idle, the assertive one while the query failed; while loading both are empty, so nothing is
announced, and the loading indicator, named by statusText, stands in the text's place. SRC-50: the results are links
in one list named by label, outside the listbox, marked busy while loading.

members.name: renderHint
members.description: SRC-37: the hint — the keyboard shortcut, hosted (KBS-13): its plain form (a line of text, no cap), small, the ambient convention, faded with the search.

members.name: renderTrigger
members.description:
SRC-35, SRC-36: what stands in the bar's place while bar is button or icon — one button that opens a modal view.
As a button: the bar's container at the trigger's height, holding the search glyph, the placeholder (or the label)
and the hint. As an icon: an icon-only text Button showing the search glyph, from the Button's own tokens, and no
drawn hint (its keys are still exposed).

events.name: toggle
events.description: The search opened or closed its view: `detail.expanded` (and the element's `expanded`) is the new value, and `detail.reason` says why it closed (`escape`, `back`, `select`, `submit`, `outside`, `tab`, `focus-out`, `shortcut`), or `null` when it opened.

events.name: select
events.description: The person chose a suggestion, or activated a result in place (without a modifier key, in the same window): `detail.value` is its value. The search does not change `value`; set the value you want. For a result it is fired before the browser follows the link and is cancelable: cancelling it keeps the link from being followed, so that a router can take it. A result opened in a new tab (a modifier key, the middle button, `target="new"`) fires nothing.

events.name: submit
events.description: The action key (Enter, Search) was pressed with no suggestion active: `detail.value`. Cancelable: cancelling it keeps an enclosing form from being submitted.

events.name: input
events.description: The person changed the value (typing, deleting, pasting, dictating, the clear button, Escape); `value` is already the new one. Never fired when the product sets `value`.

attributes.description: The id of the form the search belongs to, where it stands outside it: the platform's own attribute, which then wins over a form around it. The `form` property is read-only and returns the form element.
attributes.name: form
presentation
attributes.description:
Where the view opens: `docked` under the bar, without taking focus from it; `dialog`, a modal surface near the top
of the window with its own header (a large screen, opened from a trigger); or `full-screen`, over the whole window
with its own header (a small screen).

attributes.name: bar
attributes.description:
What stands where the search is placed. `field`: the bar with its input. `button`: a trigger shaped like the bar
that holds no input — the search glyph, the placeholder and the shortcut hint — for an app bar with room. `icon`: an
icon-only Button showing the search glyph, for an app bar without. A trigger opens a modal view (`dialog` or
`full-screen`), where the input is; `docked` with a trigger opens as `dialog`.

attributes.name: value
attributes.description: The query. Setting it shows it and fires nothing. The `value` attribute is what a form reset returns to.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Names the search field, the trigger, the view, the suggestions and the results for assistive technology ("Search mail"). Drawn only as a button trigger's text while `placeholder` is empty. Required.

attributes.name: placeholder
attributes.description: A hint shown while the value is empty, and the text of a button trigger. Never a replacement for `label`.

attributes.name: expanded
attributes.description: Whether the view is open. The search sets it itself (and fires `toggle`); set it to open or close the view yourself.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: Prevents focus, editing and opening the view.

attributes.name: clear-label
attributes.description: The clear button's accessible name, in the product's language ("Clear search"; `clear-label`).

attributes.name: back-label
attributes.description: The accessible name of the back button in a modal view's header — dialog or full-screen ("Back"; `back-label`).

attributes.name: shortcut
attributes.description:
The keyboard shortcut that opens the search, in the keyboard shortcut component's key names: one chord per string
(`["mod+k"]`, `["/"]`; the attribute holds the chords separated by spaces, `shortcut="mod+k"`). The search writes it
as a hint, a line of text with no keycaps — at the end of a button trigger, and in the bar while the value is empty and the input is not focused —
and exposes it as `aria-keyshortcuts` of its trigger or its input. It makes the keys work only with `bindShortcut`;
otherwise the product binds them and sets `expanded`.

attributes.name: bind-shortcut
attributes.description:
Makes the search itself listen for `shortcut`, anywhere in the window, while it is connected and enabled: the keys
open it, and close it again while it is open (`bind-shortcut`). One chord; a press something else cancelled, a key
repeating while held, an input-method composition and — for a chord without mod, ctrl or alt — a press while focus
is in an element that takes text are left alone. Off by default.

attributes.name: status
attributes.description:
What the product's search is doing, which the product sets: `idle` (results, or none, are final), `loading` (a
query is running: the status row shows a loading indicator after its delay, and the results are marked busy) or
`error` (the query failed: `statusText` is drawn as an error and announced at once). The search never runs a query.

attributes.name: status-text
attributes.description:
The status row's text, in the product's language, announced to assistive technology when it changes
(`status-text`): the count ("12 results for tokens"), that nothing was found, the failure; while loading, the
loading indicator's name ("Searching"). Empty draws no status row unless `status` is `loading`.

attributes.name: inline
attributes.description: For tests and documentation: draws the open view in place, without the overlay's behaviour.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Web only: the name it is submitted under.

declarations.description:
One segment (SEG-4…7, SEG-9…11, SEG-13…17, SEG-21, SEG-23, SEG-24): its native button — the container that answers
the states, clips its fill and ripple to its corners and draws the ring inside itself — the content centred in it
(the leading glyph, then the label), and the divider in the gap before it.

One option of a segmented button — the spec's item kind `segment`: a label, an optional icon, and the value
that selects it. Placed as a child of `<tanrei-segmented-button>`, as `<option>` in a `<select>`; the set decides
whether it is selected and which segment is the Tab stop, and answers its activation.

Its native `<button>` carries its semantics: a radio with `aria-checked` in a single-choice set, a toggle button with
`aria-pressed` in a multiple-choice one, named by its label whether or not the label is drawn.

declarations.description:
Lets people choose one option, or several, from two to five related options drawn side by side as the joined
segments of one control.

Contract: specs/segmented-button.spec.json. `<tanrei-segment>` children are the segments, in order. The selection is
the set's: `value` names the selected segment while `selection` is `single` (`null` selects none), and
`values` the selected segments while it is `multiple`. The set sets them itself when a segment is activated — by
pointer, touch, Enter, Space, or (single) the arrow keys, which select the segment they reach — and then fires
`change`, as a native control does.

Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-segmented-button-*` tokens: the set's fill, outline, corners and
padding, the dividers, per size the segments' height, paddings, gap, label style, icon and check sizes, and per
condition (unselected, selected) and state each segment's colors and elevation. How a press is answered and how
keyboard focus is drawn are the system's choices of kind (`--tanrei-sys-behavior-*`), read from the cascade.

declarations.description:
Lets people choose one value from a closed list as one complete field of a form. Built from a Field
(`<tanrei-field>`) and the Select (`<tanrei-select>`) it frames: the trigger and its list under the Field's label —
or, in the filled and the outlined look, with the label floating in the box — with the Field's help and its error,
tied together for assistive technology and taking part in a form as one control.

Contract: specs/select-field.spec.json.

```html
<tanrei-select-field name="country" label="Country" requirement="required" supporting-text="Where your invoices are addressed.">
  <tanrei-option value="jp">Japan</tanrei-option>
  <tanrei-option value="ke">Kenya</tanrei-option>
</tanrei-select-field>
```

Composed (`src/primitives/composed.ts`): its shadow root holds the two members' own elements and nothing
else, so it draws nothing of its own and has no token — every `--tanrei-comp-field-*`,
`--tanrei-comp-input-box-*` and `--tanrei-comp-select-*` value reaches the members by inheritance, and one select field is set apart by setting such a property on this
element. Each property is its member's, set on that member unchanged: `label`, `label-hidden`, `supporting-text`,
`error-text`, `error`, `disabled`, `requirement`, `required-mark`, `required-text` and `optional-text` are the
Field's, every other one the select's. One level down, the same by hand: `<tanrei-field label="Country"
requirement="required"><tanrei-select name="country">…options…</tanrei-select></tanrei-field>` — and the box alone,
where a label stands elsewhere (a bar, a toolbar, a column of a table), is `<tanrei-select>` with a `label` of its
own.

The options are its `<tanrei-option>` and `<tanrei-option-group>` children, exactly as a select's: they stay the
product's, are never moved or copied, and reach the select inside through the default slot, which the select reads.
Replacing them by hand works as on a select.

It is a block as wide as its place, and its box fills it (SEF-1): give it a narrower place for a narrower box.

`value` and `open` are at every moment the select's, read through to it and never copied, and the two events are
that select's own, with this element as their target: `event.target.value` and `event.target.open` are new in every
listener. It dispatches none itself. `toggle` is composed and does not bubble: it is heard on this element and by no
ancestor.

Form-associated: it submits the value under `name` — nothing while disabled —, resets to its `value` attribute, is
restored on navigation, follows a disabled `<fieldset>`, and reports a missing value while `requirement` is
`required` and the value is empty.

The element is not focusable itself and has no role: `focus()` goes to the select's trigger, and its name is `label`
(with `label-hidden` where it is not drawn), never `aria-label`. A press on the label row focuses the trigger and
opens nothing; a press on the trigger opens the list; a press on the help or the error text does nothing.

SEL-63, FLD-26: how far the value stands from the container's start edge — the inline padding or, beside a leading
icon, the padding beside a glyph, the icon and its gap — and the padding the container keeps at its end edge (the
padding beside a glyph while the chevron is drawn), as lengths of the box's tokens for `size`: the same sums

declarations.description:
Lets people choose one value from a closed list: a trigger that looks and measures like a text input's box and
shows the chosen option, and a list of options, optionally grouped, that opens from it. The bare control: it draws
no label row, no requirement mark, no help and no error text.

Contract: specs/select.spec.json. The options are `<tanrei-option>` children, optionally in
`<tanrei-option-group>` elements (the pair a combobox holds too); the select reads them — and reads them again when
they change — and renders the rows itself. Every visual value is a token: the trigger is drawn from
`--tanrei-comp-input-box-*`, the one set every input box is drawn from (SEL-65), and the list from
`--tanrei-comp-select-*`, which hold the menu's values in every shipped design system.

```html
<tanrei-select size="small" label="Theme" value="auto">
  <tanrei-option value="auto">Follow the device</tanrei-option>
  <tanrei-option value="light">Light</tanrei-option>
</tanrei-select>
```

Alone it is for a place where its label stands elsewhere or is plain from where it stands — a theme or a language
in a bar, a toolbar, a column of a table — and `label` names it for assistive technology; a filled or an outlined
select also draws that name, floating in its box. In a form it stands in a `<tanrei-field>`, which names it,
describes it and marks it: that pair as one element is `<tanrei-select-field>`. The select says to its Field what
only it knows (`src/primitives/field.ts`): that it draws the label while its look floats one, where its value
starts and ends, and that it is drawn focused while its list is open.

Bare and given no width it is an inline box as wide as its widest option; in a Field it is a block that fills the
Field's width.

It is a form-associated element: it takes `name`, submits `value`, resets to the `value` attribute, is restored on
navigation, follows `<fieldset disabled>` and reports `valueMissing` while the Field that frames it says it is
required and `value` is empty. It never validates beyond that: `error` is the product's to set.

The options may also reach it through a `<slot>` among its children: the elements assigned to that slot stand in
the slot's place. That is how a select field's options reach the select inside it, and how a product's own element
passes options on (`<tanrei-select label="Plan"><slot></slot></tanrei-select>` in its shadow root).

The pattern is the select-only combobox. Focus stays on the trigger while the list is open and one option is the
active one: Enter, Space, Down or Up Arrow, or a printable character open the list; the arrow keys, Home, End, Page
Down and Page Up and typing move the active option; Enter or Space choose it; Escape, Tab, a press outside or on the
trigger close the list without choosing. The value changes only when the person confirms an option.

An option is a value, never a destination: a list of places to go is a menu or links.

members.name: stop
members.description: Disabled under the focus it holds, its stop keeps its `tabindex` for one frame, as the platform's own control keeps focus (src/primitives/disabled-while-focused.ts).

members.name: variant
members.description: The look, as the text inputs beside it: `stacked` is a filled box whose label is the row of the Field that frames it; `filled` and `outlined` float the label inside the box. Use one style per form. A value the select does not know by name is laid out as stacked. Reflected.

members.name: size
members.description: The container's minimum height: `small`, `medium` or `large` (40 / 48 / 56 in the default system). The hit area always meets the minimum target. Reflected.

members.name: value
members.description: The value of the chosen option. The select shows that option's label; while `value` names no option it shows the placeholder. An option whose value is the empty string is a choice like any other. The `value` attribute is the value a form reset returns to.

members.name: name
members.description: The name the value is submitted under in a form. Reflected.

members.name: label
members.description: Names the select for assistive technology, where no Field frames it or its visible label is elsewhere; it then wins over the Field's label. A filled or an outlined select also draws it, floating in its box; a stacked select draws no label. A select no Field frames needs one.

members.name: labelHidden
members.description: Does not draw the floating label of a filled or an outlined select, which stays the accessible name (`label-hidden`). It changes nothing on a stacked select, which draws no label.

members.name: placeholder
members.description: A hint shown while nothing is chosen and the label is not in the line. Never a replacement for `label`, and never a choice.

members.name: error
members.description: Puts the select in the error condition: it is exposed as invalid and drawn in its error parts. The select never sets this itself and shows no error text: the words are the `errorText` of the Field that frames it, which puts its select in this condition too.

members.name: disabled
members.description: Disables the select: it takes no focus, does not open and is left out of form submission. Disable a framed select on its Field, so that the label follows.

members.name: readOnly
members.description: The value is shown, can be focused and is submitted, but cannot be changed: the list does not open and no chevron is drawn. The attribute is `readonly`.

members.name: open
members.description: Whether the list is shown. The select opens and closes itself and emits `toggle`; the product may also set it. Ignored while the select is disabled or read-only or holds no option. Reflected.

members.name: separation
members.description: How a group of options is told from what is next to it: `divider`, `gap`, or `auto` for the design system's answer (`--tanrei-comp-select-separation`).

members.name: inline
members.description: For tests and fixtures: draws the open list in place below the trigger — inside its positioned ancestor, which stands for the window — not in the top layer; it then answers no dismissal.

members.name: hasLeading
members.description: Whether the leading-icon slot has content.

members.name: focused
members.description: SEL-20: the container has focus, however it was gained.

members.name: formDisabled
members.description: Set by an ancestor `<fieldset disabled>` (the element's `formDisabledCallback`).

members.name: says
members.description: What it tells its form, said where an element composed around it hears it (src/primitives/form-says.ts).

members.name: presented
members.description: Whether the list is presented: open, usable, and beside a container in the page.

members.name: byKeyboard
members.description: What opened the list last: a key shows the active option's focus indicator, a press does not (SEL-32).

members.name: pressed
members.description: A mouse press on the container was answered as it went down: the click that follows it is not a second press.

members.name: reportedLeft
members.description: SEL-64: what left the element with the frame has been reported for this element.

members.name: axes
members.default: new OpenAxesController(this, { component: 'select', behavior: 'SEL-60', axes: AXES })
members.description: SEL-60: sizes and variants a design system adds, and a value the active system does not have (src/primitives/axes.ts).

members.name: system
members.description: SEL-45: where style queries are missing, what parts two groups is read by script, again when the system is switched.

members.name: frame
members.default: new FieldControlController(this, { errorCondition: true, named: () => !!this.label.trim(), says: () => this.saysToField, changed: () => this.framedChanged(), })
members.description:
SEL-63: the select's side of the exchange with the Field that frames it (src/primitives/field.ts). It takes the
Field's name, description and states, whether the label is hidden and whether an asterisk follows it; and it says
what only it knows — that it draws the label, where its value starts and ends, that it is drawn focused while its
list is open. It has an error condition of its own (SEL-9). No Field: it is drawn as a bare select.

members.name: frameChanged
members.description: The Field's answer changed since the last update: the floating label may have other lines (SEL-15).

members.name: options$
members.description: SEL-17, SEL-36: the options, read from the children and read again when they change (src/primitives/option-list.ts).

members.name: list
members.default: new OptionListController(this, { model: () => this.options$.model, chosen: () => this.chosen, choose: (option, event) => this.choose(option, event), widens: true, })
members.description: SEL-26, SEL-31 … SEL-35, SEL-41, SEL-42: the active option, the keys that move it, the press and the choice.

members.name: anchored
members.description: SEL-24, SEL-25, SEL-30: where the list is — the anchored surface a popover is drawn on, at least as wide as the container.

members.name: dismiss
members.default: new DismissController(this, { related: () => [this], request: (reason: DismissReason) => this.closeList(reason), tab: (event) => { if (!event.ctrlKey && !event.metaKey) this.closeList('tab'); }, })
members.description: SEL-27, SEL-28: Escape, a press outside and focus leaving (src/primitives/dismiss.ts); Tab closes at once.

members.name: floating
members.description: SEL-15: a floating label that does not fit on one line is given the room its lines take (src/primitives/field-trigger.ts).

members.name: mirror
members.description: SEL-57: the glyph of the slot, the chosen option's own and the options' are marked when the icon set mirrors them.

members.name: glyphs
members.description: SEL-19: a glyph the select draws by name is drawn once the icon set can draw it; until then nothing stands in its place.

members.name: framedChanged
members.description:
SEL-49: a select a Field frames is a block that fills the Field's width; a bare one is an inline box as wide as its
widest option. Said on the element as a state (`:state(framed)`), at the moment the Field answers or lets go, so
that the Field reads the control's display as it is.

members.name: name_
members.description: SEL-11: the accessible name — its own label, else the label of the Field that frames it.

members.name: invalid
members.description: SEL-9: in the error condition — its own `error`, or its Field's.

members.name: labelled
members.description: SEL-15: the label floats in the box — a filled or an outlined select with a name, unless its own `labelHidden` or its Field's says to draw none.

members.name: leading
members.description: SEL-18: what stands at the start of the container — the slot's glyph, else the chosen option's own, else nothing.

members.name: saysToField
members.description:
SEL-63: what the select says to the Field that frames it. That it draws the label while its look floats one — its
name, or nothing while the label is hidden; the Field draws no label row either way. How far its value stands from
its start edge and the padding it keeps at its end edge, as lengths of the box's tokens (`INSET`, in the styles).
And that it is drawn focused for as long as its list is open, whether or not it has focus (SEL-20).

members.name: inert_
members.description: Disabled by its own `disabled`, a fieldset's, its Field's or a field group's.

members.name: layout
members.description: How the variant is laid out: filled and outlined by name, every other value as stacked (SEL-60).

members.name: chosen
members.description: SEL-17: the chosen option — the first, in order and across groups, whose value equals `value`; a disabled one and one whose value is empty included.

type.text: { model: OptionModel; placeholder: string; text: string; said: { label: string; lang: string }[] } | null

members.name: sizerLines
members.description:
SEL-49: what the select's own width is measured from — every option's label and the placeholder, one to a line of
one hidden text, each as it would be drawn in the line (spaces collapsed). One element whatever the number of
options; made again only when the options or the placeholder change.

SEL-59: an option that says a language is shown, once chosen, in that language, and a browser may draw it in
another face than the field's: its label is measured in a line of its own that says the same language — an
element for each such option only, so a list that says none stays one text.

members.name: usable
members.description: SEL-23, SEL-46, SEL-47, SEL-61: whether the list can be shown at all.

members.name: form
members.description: The form it belongs to, if any.

members.name: validity
members.description: The native constraint validity: `valueMissing` while the Field that frames the select says it is required and its value is empty.

members.name: focus
members.description: Moves focus to the container: the select's one stop in the focus order.

members.name: openList
members.description: SEL-23: the person opens the list. `open` is true before `toggle` is fired; the list is presented by the render that follows.

members.name: closeList
members.description: SEL-27: the person closes the list, for `reason`. `open` is false, and the list no longer takes input, before `toggle` is fired.

members.name: choose
members.description: SEL-34: the person confirmed `option`. `value` is the new one before `change`; the list then closes, so `toggle` follows.

members.name: present
members.description: SEL-24, SEL-26: into the overlay layer beside the container. Focus stays where it is.

members.name: withdraw
members.description: SEL-27, SEL-29, SEL-30: out of it, fading; closed or closing it takes no pointer input.

members.name: toggleByPress
members.description: A press on the container opens the list with the press, or closes an open one (`press`). Never while disabled or read-only.

members.name: onClick
members.description: A touch, a pen and assistive technology press with a click; a mouse press was answered as it went down.

members.name: reports
members.description: What a debug build tells the developer; the select still renders.

events.name: toggle
events.description: The list was opened or closed by the person; `open` is already the new one. `detail.open`, and for a close `detail.reason`: `select`, `escape`, `outside`, `focus-out`, `anchor-hidden`, `press` or `tab`. After a choice it follows `change`. Composed and not bubbling: heard on the element — and on an element composed around it — and by no ancestor. Never fired when the product sets `open`.

events.name: change
events.description: The person chose an option whose value differs from the select's; `value` is already the new one. A composed, bubbling Event, as a native select's. Never fired when the product sets `value`, when the chosen option is chosen again, or while the person only moves through the list.

attributes.description: The id of the form the select belongs to, where it stands outside it: the platform's own attribute, which then wins over a form around it. The `form` property is read-only and returns the form element.
attributes.name: form
variant
attributes.description: The look, as the text inputs beside it: `stacked` is a filled box whose label is the row of the Field that frames it; `filled` and `outlined` float the label inside the box. Use one style per form. A value the select does not know by name is laid out as stacked. Reflected.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: The container's minimum height: `small`, `medium` or `large` (40 / 48 / 56 in the default system). The hit area always meets the minimum target. Reflected.

attributes.name: value
attributes.description: The value of the chosen option. The select shows that option's label; while `value` names no option it shows the placeholder. An option whose value is the empty string is a choice like any other. The `value` attribute is the value a form reset returns to.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: The name the value is submitted under in a form. Reflected.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Names the select for assistive technology, where no Field frames it or its visible label is elsewhere; it then wins over the Field's label. A filled or an outlined select also draws it, floating in its box; a stacked select draws no label. A select no Field frames needs one.

attributes.name: label-hidden
attributes.description: Does not draw the floating label of a filled or an outlined select, which stays the accessible name (`label-hidden`). It changes nothing on a stacked select, which draws no label.

attributes.name: placeholder
attributes.description: A hint shown while nothing is chosen and the label is not in the line. Never a replacement for `label`, and never a choice.

attributes.name: error
attributes.description: Puts the select in the error condition: it is exposed as invalid and drawn in its error parts. The select never sets this itself and shows no error text: the words are the `errorText` of the Field that frames it, which puts its select in this condition too.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: Disables the select: it takes no focus, does not open and is left out of form submission. Disable a framed select on its Field, so that the label follows.

attributes.name: readonly
attributes.description: The value is shown, can be focused and is submitted, but cannot be changed: the list does not open and no chevron is drawn. The attribute is `readonly`.

attributes.name: open
attributes.description: Whether the list is shown. The select opens and closes itself and emits `toggle`; the product may also set it. Ignored while the select is disabled or read-only or holds no option. Reflected.

attributes.name: separation
attributes.description: How a group of options is told from what is next to it: `divider`, `gap`, or `auto` for the design system's answer (`--tanrei-comp-select-separation`).

attributes.name: inline
attributes.description: For tests and fixtures: draws the open list in place below the trigger — inside its positioned ancestor, which stands for the window — not in the top layer; it then answers no dismissal.

declarations.name: sideSheetRelease
declarations.description:
SSH-4: whether a released drag asks to close — past half the sheet's width toward its end edge, or flung that way.
`distance` is how far the sheet is drawn from where it rests, toward the end edge; `velocity` the pointer's speed that
way at the release, in px per ms.

Shows supplementary content or a secondary task in a panel at the end edge, with a headline, an optional close button
and actions: `standard`, beside the content in the layout (a layout region), where actions are optional, or
`modal`, over the content with a scrim, holding focus until it closes (a modal overlay), with at least one
action (SSH-16).

Contract: specs/side-sheet.spec.json. The content is the default slot. The header holds `headline` (the sheet's
accessible name, a heading) and, while `closable`, an icon-only `<tanrei-button>` of the medium size showing the close
glyph, named by `close-label`, in the variant `comp.side-sheet.close-button.variant` names (tonal in the default
system).

The actions are `<tanrei-button slot="actions">` children, each marked `confirming` or `dismissive`, placed below a
divider as a full-width Button group places them: dismissive at the start and confirming at the end of a row the
actions share equally, confirming on top of a column when a label does not fit its share (or, where the system's
`actions.arrangement` is `start`, at their own widths from the start edge). Focus and assistive technology follow that
order. A Button without a `variant` attribute takes the sheet's (`comp.side-sheet.actions.variant`, tonal in the
default system). Actions never close the sheet: close it from their handlers.

Controlled: the sheet never closes itself. It fires `close` with a reason — its close button in either variant, and for
a modal sheet a press on the scrim, Escape, the platform's back or a drag toward its end edge — and you set `open` to
false. A product that does not close it after a drag sees it slide back.

Standard: an `<aside>` (a complementary landmark) named by the headline; place it as the last item of a flex row (the
full height of that row). Its width animates while open changes, the content beside it resizing. Opening it moves focus
in, closing it with focus inside gives focus back, Tab leaves it open, and Escape and drags do nothing.

Modal: a native `<dialog>` in the shadow root opened with `showModal()`, at the window's end edge in the top layer over
`::backdrop` (the scrim), everything else inert, the page held from scrolling and focus kept inside. Focus goes to the
slotted element marked `autofocus`, else the sheet (also when it is mounted open), and returns where it was when it
closes.

The content scrolls between the header and the actions; a divider appears below the header while it is scrolled from
its top. While the on-screen keyboard covers the bottom of the sheet, the actions sit directly above it (the
`visualViewport`).

Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-side-sheet-*` tokens. The color reaches under
`env(safe-area-inset-*)` at the end, top and bottom.

declarations.description:
Stands where content will be while it loads: quiet placeholders in the shape of what is coming — lines of text, a block, a circle — that keep the box the content will take, in a region that says once that it is busy. Contract: specs/skeleton.spec.json. The element has **no shadow root**: it is the box around the product's own layout, and a placeholder is the product's own empty element with the class `tanrei-skeleton-placeholder`. ```html

``` A placeholder: `data-shape` (`text`, the default and what an unknown value draws; `block`; `circle`), `data-lines` (text: how many lines) and the CSS properties `inline-size` and `block-size` for its sizes. A text placeholder takes the text style of where it stands — the inherited `font` — so it goes where the text will be, and is exactly its lines high. Placeholders that are the skeleton's own children are stacked, `container.gap` apart; anything else is the product's own layout inside the skeleton. Everything drawn is `@tanrei/web/skeleton.css` — every value a `--tanrei-comp-skeleton-*` token — which draws the skeleton before and without this script: the shapes, the show delay (the skeleton is hidden for its length, with its box kept), the pulse, stillness under reduced motion, outlines in forced colors. The element adds the same sheet to the root it is connected to, and what a stylesheet cannot say: once the delay has passed it is a progressbar with no value (`role="progressbar"`, `aria-busy="true"`, `aria-label` from `label`, else from the product's words, `loadingLabel`) — unless `decorative`, or inside another skeleton, when it is kept from assistive technology (`aria-hidden="true"`); what it holds is `inert`; its animation is held while it cannot be seen; a wave, which has to be measured, is drawn (before the element is defined a wave is a pulse); and a debug build reports what it ignored. A page that must be right before its script runs writes `role`, `aria-busy` and `aria-label` itself, and the element leaves what it finds. Insert it when the wait starts and remove it when the wait ends. It takes no input and emits no event.

slots.description: The placeholders — empty elements with `class="tanrei-skeleton-placeholder"` — alone or inside a layout of the product's own. They are children in the document, not slotted nodes: the element has no shadow root.

members.name: label
members.description:
What is loading, in the product's language ("Loading projects"): the name assistive technology is given for the
whole skeleton, once. Never drawn. Left empty, it reads the product's words (`loadingLabel`). Not read while
`decorative` is true.

members.name: decorative
members.description:
Whether something else already says this wait: a loading indicator beside it, a status text, a region the product
itself exposes as busy and names. True keeps the whole skeleton from assistive technology; it changes nothing that
is drawn.

members.name: showDelay
members.description:
How long, in milliseconds, it waits from its insertion before it is drawn and exposed; 0 shows it as it is
inserted. Null takes `motion.show-delay`, as does a negative or non-finite value (reported). A page that is drawn
before its script runs writes `show-delay="0"`, which the stylesheet reads; any other number is the element's.

members.name: visibility
members.description: SKL-14: the placeholders stir only while the skeleton can be seen.

members.name: system
members.description: SKL-12: the manner is read again when the document's root switches the design system.

members.name: shown
members.description: SKL-7, SKL-8: false during the show delay.

members.name: authored
members.description: The attributes of `EXPOSURE` the page wrote itself: found at the first insertion, and never touched.

members.name: exposed
members.description: The attributes of `EXPOSURE` the element wrote.

members.name: inerted
members.description: The children the element made inert (SKL-19).

members.name: sizes
members.description: A wave is measured again when the skeleton or a placeholder changes size.

members.name: beginning
members.description: The skeletons inserted in this turn (`beginTogether`), and those whose manner is read after their update (`stirTogether`).

members.name: together
members.description:
Every skeleton of one turn in ONE microtask after it: what each asks of the cascade is read for them all, and only
then does each write what follows. A skeleton that read in its own insertion and in its own update — its delay,
the stylesheet's wait, the manner — after the attributes the one before it had just written had the page styled
for itself, twice (fifty inserted at once: about a hundred style passes).

members.name: begin
members.description:
SKL-7, SKL-9, SKL-11: every insertion waits its whole delay, with the value of that moment. The element counts it
(`data-clocked`), so that it is also counted where the skeleton is not rendered (SKL-10) and ends at the same
moment for what is drawn and for what is exposed. A skeleton that was in the page before the element was defined
has been waiting by the stylesheet's animation: what is left of that wait is counted on, and a skeleton the
stylesheet has already shown stays as it is — nothing it draws changes when the element is defined.

members.name: beginning

type.text: { token: number; elapsed: number | null; drawn: boolean; manner: Manner }

members.description:
The reading half of `begin()`: the delay the tokens name, how long the stylesheet's wait has run (null: there is
none, or the element counts already), whether a skeleton that has no wait is drawn, and the manner. It writes nothing.

members.name: show
members.description: SKL-8: shown — drawn at once, exposed, and stirring from the beginning of a pulse.

members.name: nested
members.description: Whether this skeleton stands inside another (SKL-17), through shadow roots.

members.name: expose
members.description:
SKL-15, SKL-17, SKL-18: once shown, one busy progressbar with no value, named by `label` or by the product's
words; kept from assistive technology while decorative or nested; and nothing while it waits, when it is hidden,
or while it holds no placeholder (SKL-26).
An attribute the page wrote itself is left as it was found.

members.name: manner
members.description: SKL-12, SKL-25: the manner the tokens name now, read from the cascade; a name the skeleton does not know is a pulse.

members.name: stir
members.description: What the stylesheet cannot read or measure of the manner: its name where there are no style queries, and the wave.

members.name: wave
members.description: SKL-12, wave: the placeholders are measured against the skeleton, and measured again when a size changes.

members.name: measure
members.description:
The skeleton's inline size, and each placeholder's distance from the skeleton's left edge: where the one mask of
the wave stands in each of them. Written only where it differs, so it settles; nothing is asked for at rest.

members.name: placeholders
members.description: The placeholders this skeleton draws: every one in it, those of a skeleton inside it too (it is silent, SKL-17).

members.name: step
read
members.description:
Reads what the skeleton holds and writes what follows from it: `inert` on each of its children (SKL-19), the rule
of a `data-lines` the stylesheet does not read (SKL-3), and in a debug build what it ignored (SKL-25, SKL-26).
Called when it is inserted and when what it holds changes; it writes only what differs, so it settles.

members.name: check
members.description: What a debug build says about a skeleton it still draws (SKL-25, SKL-26).

declarations.description:
Lets people choose a value, or a range of values, on a scale as one complete field. Built from a Field
(`<tanrei-field>`) and the Slider (`<tanrei-slider>`) it frames: the track under the Field's label, with the value
in words at the end of the label row, the Field's help and its error, tied together for assistive technology and
taking part in a form as one control.

Contract: specs/slider-field.spec.json. `<tanrei-slider-field name="text-size" label="Text size"
supporting-text="Applies to every page." min="50" max="200" step="10" value="120"></tanrei-slider-field>`.

Composed (`src/primitives/composed.ts`): its shadow root holds the two members' own elements and nothing
else, so it draws nothing of its own and has no token — every `--tanrei-comp-field-*` and `--tanrei-comp-slider-*`
value reaches the members by inheritance, and one slider field is set apart by setting such a property on this
element. Each property is its member's, set on that member unchanged: `label`, `label-hidden`, `supporting-text`,
`error-text`, `error`, `disabled`, `requirement`, `required-mark`, `required-text` and `optional-text` are the
Field's, every other one the Slider's — `end-label` is the Slider's `label`, the name of a range's end handle,
because `label` is the visible name here. It has no orientation: the track runs along the line. One level down, the
same by hand: `<tanrei-field label="Text size" value-text="120"><tanrei-slider name="text-size" min="50" max="200"
step="10" value="120"></tanrei-slider></tanrei-field>`, with the product writing the Field's `value-text` at each
`input` (`field.valueText = slider.shownValueText`).

That is the one thing it does that the pair by hand does not: unless `value-hidden` is set it gives its Field, as
the value text at the end of the label row, the words its Slider gives each handle — `value-text` (and
`start-value-text`), or what `formatValue` writes, or the number in the page's locale — at every change, a range's
two in reading order with an en dash between. `formatValue` is a property, never an attribute: a function the
product gives once, from a value to its words (`field.formatValue = (value) => percent.format(value / 100)`). It
writes no number, unit or word itself.

It is a block as wide as its place, and its track fills it: give it a narrower place for a shorter track.

`value` and `startValue` are at every moment the Slider's, and the two events are that Slider's own, with this
element as their target: `event.target.value` is the new value in every listener. It dispatches none itself.

Form-associated: it submits the value under `name` — a range the start value and then the value, under the one name;
nothing while disabled —, resets to its `value` and `start-value` attributes, is restored on navigation and follows a
disabled `<fieldset>`.

The element is not focusable itself and has no role: `focus()` goes to the handle — a range's start handle — and its
name is `label` (with `label-hidden` where it is not drawn), never `aria-label`. A range's two handles are named by
`start-label` and `end-label`. A press on the label row focuses the handle and changes no value; a press on the
help or the error text does nothing.

members.name: formAssociated
members.description: SLF-6: the one control the form meets. Its members stand in its shadow root, outside every form.

members.name: label
members.description: Names the control, visibly and to assistive technology. Required, unless the control names itself (a checkbox or a switch with its own label): then leave it empty and the field adds only help and an error.

members.name: labelHidden
members.description: Does not draw the label, which stays the accessible name (`label-hidden`). For a control whose visible label is elsewhere.

members.name: supportingText
members.description: Help shown below the control and given to assistive technology as the control's description (`supporting-text`). While the field is in error it gives way to `errorText`, unless the design system keeps both (`--tanrei-comp-field-error-text-placement: append`).

members.name: errorText
members.description: Shown while `error` is true, in `supportingText`'s place (below it, which stays, where the design system says `append`): what is wrong with this answer and how to put it right, in words (`error-text`).

members.name: error
members.description: Puts the field in the error condition: the error text is drawn, the control is exposed as invalid and, where it has an error condition of its own, drawn in it. The field never sets this itself.

members.name: disabled
members.description: Disables the control and draws the frame as disabled. Disable a framed control here, not on the control, so that its label follows.

members.name: requirement
members.description: What the form asks of the control: `required` exposes it as required and draws the required mark; `optional` draws the optional tag; `none` says and draws nothing. It never validates.

members.name: requiredMark
members.description: How this control shows that it is required (`required-mark`): `tag` is a small filled tag with `requiredText`, `asterisk` is "*" after the label, `none` draws nothing and keeps the semantics; `auto` takes the design system's answer (`--tanrei-comp-field-requirement-mark`, which follows `--tanrei-sys-behavior-requirement-mark`).

members.name: requiredText
members.description: The text of the required tag (`required-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ requiredText })`). Tanrei has none: without them the asterisk is drawn in the tag's place and the required state is kept.

members.name: optionalText
members.description: The text of the optional tag, also part of the description (`optional-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ optionalText })`). Tanrei has none: without them no tag is drawn and nothing is said.

members.name: value
members.description: The value of the only handle, or of a range's end handle. The `value` attribute is what a form reset returns to.

members.name: startValue
members.description: The value of a range's start handle (the `start-value` attribute). Ignored while `range` is false.

members.name: range
members.description: Two handles, choosing the range from `startValue` to `value`.

members.name: min
members.description: The lowest value, at the track's start.

members.name: max
members.description: The highest value, at the track's end.

members.name: step
members.description: 0 is continuous; above 0 the values are `min` plus whole multiples of `step`, up to `max`.

members.name: origin
members.description: Where the active track starts: null (no attribute) starts it at `min`; a value inside the range makes a centered slider. Ignored for a range.

members.name: stops
members.description: A stop dot at every value a discrete slider can take. Ignored while `step` is 0.

members.name: size
members.description: The track's weight: small (the default), medium or large, or a size the design system adds. Anything else draws small (SLD-23).

members.name: valueIndicator
members.description: `none` (the default), `active` (while a handle is pressed or has keyboard focus) or `always` (the `value-indicator` attribute).

members.name: valueText
members.description: The value as words ("40 %"), spoken and shown by the value indicator in place of the number (the `value-text` attribute). For a range, the end handle's.

members.name: startValueText
members.description: The start handle's value text, for a range (the `start-value-text` attribute).

members.name: startLabel
members.description: Names a range's start handle ("Minimum price"; the `start-label` attribute). Required while `range` is true.

members.name: endLabel
members.description: Names the slider (a range's end handle) for assistive technology. Never drawn: put your visible label beside it, in the same words. Required.

members.name: formatValue
members.description: The product's function from a value to its words (`(value) => percent.format(value / 100)`), asked for each handle at every change of a value and when it is set. A property, never an attribute. `valueText` and `startValueText` win over it; an empty answer is no answer, and the value is then written as a number in the page's locale.

members.name: valueHidden
members.description: Does not draw the value at the end of the label row (`value-hidden`). For a slider set by feel, whose number means nothing to the person (a volume, a brightness). The handle still says its value to assistive technology, and `value-indicator` still shows it.

members.name: hostNameSentence
members.description:
W8: the sentence a debug build names when the host is given an ARIA name. The host has no role: its name is the
frame's `label`. Empty: nothing is reported.

members.name: startGiven
members.description: W5, for the second value of a range: the start value last set on the element, while the Slider has not taken it.

members.name: valueMember
members.description: W5: the member that holds the value, once rendered.

members.name: firstValue
members.description: W6, item 4: the value a form's reset returns to — the `value` attribute, as a number; 0 without one, as the Slider's.

members.name: formResetCallback
members.description: W6, item 4: a range resets its start value too, to the `start-value` attribute.

members.name: formStateRestoreCallback
members.description: W6, item 5: the Slider restores both values; both are then the Slider's.

members.name: fill
members.description:
SLF-3, SLF-4 (`fills`: `field.valueText`): the Field is given the words the Slider gives each handle, as the Slider
writes them — after each of the Slider's updates, and after each of this element's own. A range's two are each a
run of its own direction (`isolated()`), in reading order, with an en dash between. Nothing while `valueHidden` is
set. No number, unit or word is written here.

members.name: memberUpdated
members.description:
W14 (`fills`): called after each word the value member tells its form — when the element first hears it, and after
each of the member's updates, which is when a member speaks. An element whose spec names a member's prop it fills
itself from state the value member holds (a text field: its Field's count text, from its input's count) sets it
here; it reads the member and writes the other member's property, and computes nothing of its own. Does nothing
otherwise.

members.name: name
members.description: Web only: the name the value is submitted under.

members.name: formDisabled
members.description: W6, item 6: a disabled `<fieldset>` around the element, or its own `disabled` attribute, as the platform says it.

members.name: control
members.description: W7: the member focus goes to, once rendered.

members.name: given
members.description: W5: the value last set on the element, while the member has not taken it.

members.name: memberValue
members.description: W5: what `value` returns — `initial` is the member's own default, for an element that has not rendered and was given nothing.

members.name: giveValue
members.description: W5: what `value` is set with. The member takes it at the element's next render; what the member holds already changes nothing.

members.name: form
members.description: The form it belongs to, if any.

members.name: validity
members.description: The element's validity: its value member's (W6, item 3).

members.name: repeat
members.description: W6, items 2 and 3: the same value and state, the same flags and message, and the member's own anchor.

members.name: passing
members.description: W9: the names of the slots it has passed on, and the watch on its own children for them.

members.name: members
members.description: The members it has rendered: the custom elements of its own shadow tree.

members.name: focus
members.description: W7, item 2: focus is the control's.

members.name: blur
members.description: W7, item 2: what has focus inside the control loses it (an engine does not take it from inside a host it blurs).

members.name: pass
members.description:
W9: a slot of a member, passed on — `${this.pass('label-icon')}` among that member's children. Rendered only while
the element has a child for it: a member that draws room for a filled slot would take a passing slot that is
always there for content.

members.name: getUpdateComplete
members.description: The element has updated when its members have: what it gave them, they have taken.

members.name: focusWhenReady
members.description: The control has rendered what takes focus only after its own first update.

declarations.name: TOUCH_SLOP
declarations.description:
How far a touch travels along the track before it is a drag, or across it before it is left to the page's scroll
(SLD-2: "the platform's touch slop"). The web does not expose the platform's value; this is Android's
`ViewConfiguration` default, as React Native's slider uses. A behaviour of the platform, not a design value.

declarations.name: sliderScale
declarations.description:
The slider's numbers (SLD-1, SLD-3, SLD-22): the range, the keyboard step, and the snap of a value — clamped between
`low` and `high` (min and max by default), and while step is above 0 on min plus a whole multiple of step, the nearest.

Lets people choose a value, or a range of values, from a continuous or stepped scale by dragging a handle along a
track.

Contract: specs/slider.spec.json. Every visual value is a `--tanrei-comp-slider-*` token: per size the track's
thickness and corners, the handle's height and the stop dots' size; the round state layer, the handle's width, fill,
outline color and elevation, the track, active track and stop-dot colors in each state; the outline's width, the gap,
the value indicator and the motion. The handle is its fill with its outline drawn over it, inside its edge (SLD-24).

Each handle is an element with `role="slider"` in the shadow root (its own Tab stop, the start handle first), named by
`label` (a range's start handle by `start-label`), with `aria-valuemin` / `-max` (bounded by the other handle in a
range), `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuetext` (`value-text`, or what `formatValue` writes, or the value in the page's
locale) and `aria-orientation`. `formatValue` is a function the product gives once, as a property, from a value to
its words (`slider.formatValue = (value) => percent.format(value / 100)`): it is asked for each handle at every
change of a value. `shownValueText` (and `shownStartValueText`) is the value text of a handle as it is spoken now,
read-only: what a product that frames the slider by hand gives its Field's `value-text` at each `input`.
The whole slider is the hit area: a press moves the nearer handle there and a drag follows it; the arrow keys, Page
Up / Down, Home and End move the focused handle. It sets its own `value` (and `startValue`) before it fires `input`
(every change) and `change` (a finished change). A value the product sets fires neither and moves over the value
motion.

Form-associated: it submits `value` under `name` (a range submits `start-value`, then `value`, under the same name),
resets to its attributes and follows a disabled `<fieldset>`.

members.name: stop
members.description: Disabled under the focus it holds, its stop keeps its `tabindex` for one frame, as the platform's own control keeps focus (src/primitives/disabled-while-focused.ts).

members.name: size
members.description: The track's weight: small (the default), medium or large, or a size the design system adds. Anything else draws small (SLD-23).

members.name: orientation
members.description: `horizontal` (the default) or `vertical`. Anything else draws horizontal (SLD-23).

members.name: value
members.description: The value of the only handle, or of a range's end handle. The `value` attribute is what a form reset returns to.

members.name: startValue
members.description: The value of a range's start handle (the `start-value` attribute). Ignored while `range` is false.

members.name: range
members.description: Two handles, choosing the range from `startValue` to `value`.

members.name: min
members.description: The lowest value, at the track's start.

members.name: max
members.description: The highest value, at the track's end.

members.name: step
members.description: 0 is continuous; above 0 the values are `min` plus whole multiples of `step`, up to `max`.

members.name: origin
members.description: Where the active track starts: null (no attribute) starts it at `min`; a value inside the range makes a centered slider. Ignored for a range.

members.name: stops
members.description: A stop dot at every value a discrete slider can take. Ignored while `step` is 0.

members.name: valueIndicator
members.description: `none` (the default), `active` (while a handle is pressed or has keyboard focus) or `always` (the `value-indicator` attribute).

members.name: disabled
members.description: Prevents interaction and removes the handles from the focus order.

members.name: label
members.description: Names the slider (a range's end handle) for assistive technology. Never drawn: put your visible label beside it, in the same words. Required.

members.name: startLabel
members.description: Names a range's start handle ("Minimum price"; the `start-label` attribute). Required while `range` is true.

members.name: valueText
members.description: The value as words ("40 %"), spoken and shown by the value indicator in place of the number (the `value-text` attribute). For a range, the end handle's.

members.name: startValueText
members.description: The start handle's value text, for a range (the `start-value-text` attribute).

members.name: formatValue
members.description: The product's function from a value to its words (`(value) => percent.format(value / 100)`), asked for each handle at every change of a value and when it is set. A property, never an attribute. `valueText` and `startValueText` win over it; an empty answer is no answer, and the value is then written as a number in the page's locale.

members.name: name
members.description: Web only: the name it is submitted under.

members.name: hovered
members.description: The handle a fine pointer over the slider would move (SLD-11).

members.name: dragging
members.description: A press is dragging a handle: it follows without the value motion (SLD-16).

members.name: formDisabled
members.description: Set by an ancestor `<fieldset disabled>`.

members.name: says
members.description: What it tells its form, said where an element composed around it hears it (src/primitives/form-says.ts).

members.name: axes
members.default: new OpenAxesController(this, { component: 'slider', behavior: 'SLD-23', axes: AXES })
members.description: SLD-23: sizes a design system adds, and a size the active system does not have (src/primitives/axes.ts).

members.name: presses
members.description: SLD-13 / SLD-14: each handle's pressed state, press-hold and ripple — grown from the handle's center, where the press moves it.

members.name: gesture

type.text: { pointer: number; handle: HandleId; touch: boolean; x: number; y: number; dragging: boolean; before: Values } | null

members.description: The press being answered: the pointer, the handle it moves, where it began and whether it has become a drag.

members.name: direction
members.default: new DirectionController(this, () => { for (const part of this.renderRoot.querySelectorAll('.piece, .dots, .thumb')) { // The state motion (a color) is not the direction's and runs on. for (const motion of part.getAnimations()) if (!(motion instanceof CSSTransition) || motion.transitionProperty !== 'background-color') motion.finish(); } this.placeIndicators(); })
members.description:
SLD-17, SLD-21, SLD-25: a change of the direction it inherits moves the handles and the tracks to the other side. It
is no change of value, so it is drawn at once: the value motion the new insets started (a piece's two ends are
physical lengths the browser can interpolate) is ended in the frame it began, before it is painted, and the value
indicators are placed again.

members.name: field
members.default: new FieldControlController(this, { requiredState: false, // A range's `label` names its end handle, not the pair: under a field's label the pair is the field's to name. named: () => !!this.label.trim() && !(this.range && !!this.field.label), })
members.description:
What a field around the slider gives it (src/primitives/field.ts): the name while it has no `label` of its own, the
description, the invalid state and `disabled` (FLD-8, FLD-10, FLD-11, FLD-14). The slider's role has no required
state, so a required slider says so in its description.

members.name: form
members.description: The form it belongs to, if any.

members.name: validity
members.description: The element's validity. A slider always has a value on its scale, so it is always valid: the platform's own members of a form control, as an element composed around it has them.

members.name: interactive
members.description: SLD-20, SLD-22: a disabled slider, or one whose max is not above its min, takes no input.

members.name: values
members.description: SLD-1, SLD-22: the values as drawn and exposed — clamped, snapped, and a range's start never past its end.

members.name: bounds
members.description: SLD-5: in a range each handle stops at the other's value.

members.name: reportValues
members.description: SLD-22: what a value outside the scale is drawn and exposed as, named in debug builds.

members.name: move
members.description: Sets one handle to `target`, snapped within its bounds, and emits input when that changes it. True when it did.

members.name: valueAt
members.description: A position in the viewport → the value under it along the travel (null before layout).

members.name: nearer
members.description: SLD-2: the handle a press at `target` moves — the nearer one; where the two meet, the one that can move toward it.

members.name: focusHandle
members.description: Focus that a press gives a handle is not keyboard focus: no ring, no focused state (SLD-11, SLD-12).

members.name: endGesture
members.description: The press is over: press-hold runs out, the value motion is back, and a change is emitted when the values moved.

members.name: hover
members.description: SLD-11: a fine pointer over the slider hovers the handle a press there would move.

members.name: onMouseDown
members.description: A mouse press never focuses on its own (the pointer's press has already been handled).

members.name: onKeyDown
members.description: SLD-3, SLD-4 (assistive technology on the web adjusts a slider with these keys): one change, input then change.

members.name: onFocus
members.description: SLD-15: where style queries are missing, the focus style is read when focus arrives.

members.name: placeIndicators
members.description: Shifts each value indicator along the axis so it stays inside the window, from its handle's settled place.

members.name: shownValueText
members.description:
SLD-18: the value text of the only handle, or of a range's end handle, as it is spoken and shown now — `valueText`,
else what `formatValue` writes, else the value as a number in the page's locale. Read-only, and new with every
change of the value: a product that frames the slider by hand gives it to its Field's `valueText` in its own
`input` listener, and `<tanrei-slider-field>` does so by itself.

members.name: shownStartValueText
members.description: SLD-18: the value text of a range's start handle, as `shownValueText` is the end handle's; empty while `range` is false.

members.name: language
members.description: The language of the place the slider stands in: the nearest `lang`, through the shadow roots it is inside.

members.name: words
members.description: SLD-18: a handle's value text — the product's words, or what its function writes, or the value in the page's locale.

members.name: pieces
members.description: SLD-6, SLD-8: the three pieces of the tracks — the track, the active track, the track — between their ends.

members.name: dots
members.description:
SLD-9: the dots each kind of piece holds, as fractions of the travel. The track holds the travel's two ends; with
`stops` every piece holds every value. A dot is drawn only where its piece is — so not where it lies on the active
track (an end), and not in a handle's gap; while the gap is 0 a dot under a handle lies under its fill (SLD-24).

members.name: renderPiece
members.description: A piece of the tracks, and its stop dots: a layer the travel's size, clipped to the piece.

declarations.description: The host: the two live regions (SNK-10), drawn nowhere; its snackbars are in the top layer.

Tells a person briefly, at the bottom edge of the screen, what the app just did or what happened (neutrally, or as
information, a warning, an error or a success), with at most one action, without taking focus or interrupting their
work.

Contract: specs/snackbar.spec.json. Shown by a `<tanrei-snackbar-host>` (`host.show({ message, action })`), which
queues, places, times, announces and closes it. Drawn outside a host (a documentation page, a test) it is drawn in
place, at rest: no timeout, queue, entrance or announcement (SNK-19); it still fires `action`, `dismiss` and
`expandedchange`.

It is drawn on a raised surface of the scheme or, `inverse`, as a bar of the opposite scheme; left unset, the system
chooses (`--tanrei-comp-snackbar-container-inverse`, off in the default system). That and its `status` make its form,
one of ten, and the form changes colors only (SNK-30).

The action, the expand button and the close button are the snackbar's own controls, drawn from
`--tanrei-comp-snackbar-action-*` and `-close-*` tokens per state and form; the bar from
`--tanrei-comp-snackbar-container-*`, or its form's `-<status>-*`, `-inverse-*` or `-inverse-<status>-*`. The keyboard
focus indicator's outer stroke is the form's `-focus-ring-color` (SNK-3). The content is aligned to the top of the bar
(SNK-29).

`title` is the `headline` property and attribute, because HTML's global `title` would show a tooltip over the bar.

declarations.description:
Shows snackbars, one at a time, in the order they were asked for (SNK-12), at the bottom of the window (SNK-13).
Place it once, as the last element of the page: its place in the focus order is where a snackbar's controls are
(SNK-11). It holds the two live regions their messages are announced in (SNK-10) — polite (`role="status"`) for the
default, info and success forms, assertive (`role="alert"`) for warning and error — so it must be in the document
before the first one.

`show(options)` resolves once that snackbar has closed: `{ result: 'action' }` or `{ result: 'dismiss', reason }`.
`dismissCurrent()` closes the showing one (reason `host`); `clear()` also drops every waiting one.

declarations.description:
Turns one setting on or off, taking effect at once, with a handle that follows a finger dragged along the track.

Contract: specs/switch.spec.json. Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-switch-*` tokens, one set per condition
(unselected, selected) and state — the handle's color, size and elevation included: how a state looks is the active
design system's decision. The handle travels to the inline end when on (the left in right-to-left layouts).

A tap switches it. A drag along the track (touch, pen or mouse; from the track, the handle or the target around them,
not from the label) carries the handle with the pointer, and every part that differs between off and on is drawn at
the handle's progress between the two, with no threshold. `selected`, the form value and the exposed state change
when the pointer is released — to the nearer side, or the side a fling is toward — with one `input` and one `change`;
Escape, a cancelled pointer, `disabled` or a `selected` set meanwhile return the handle and fire nothing.

Form-associated: while selected it submits `value` (default "on") under `name`, resets to its `selected` attribute and
follows a disabled `<fieldset>`, as a native checkbox does. It switches its own `selected` before it fires `input` and
`change`. The semantics are a native checkbox with the role switch in the shadow root, named by `label`; a click on
the visible label toggles it.

SWT-20: the click that follows a drag the switch took is not an activation — it never reaches the label.
