members.description:

until it is there: `data-between` on `.root`, under which the two layers of a color are added (switch.styles.ts).
Marked before the style pass that starts the travel, with the label's change of condition, and taken away when the
thumb's travel ends — or two frames later where none began (motion is reduced, or the handle is where it goes).

members.name: drag
members.description: The pointer that may become, or is, a drag (SWT-19); null when none is down on the control.

members.description: The handle's progress while a drag holds it: what `PROGRESS` on `.root` was last written to.

members.description: Where the pointer is along the track, as a progress, at its last move.

members.name: lag
members.description: How far the handle was from the pointer when the drag was taken; the catch-up closes it.

members.name: catchUp
members.description: The catch-up's clock: an effect-less animation over the state motion, whose progress is the eased time.

members.name: swallowClick
members.description: The click after a drag the switch took is not an activation (SWT-20); cleared by that click or the next press.

members.name: drawnProgress
members.description:
SWT-19: where the handle is drawn now — at rest, or on its way after a tap — as a progress: how far its `translate`
has carried it along its travel (the property the progress is drawn by, in the track's own pixels).

members.name: progressAt
members.description: SWT-19: where a pointer is along the track, as the handle's progress — 0 at its unselected position, 1 at its selected one (mirrored in RTL, SWT-11).

members.name: onControlPointerDown
members.description: SWT-19: a press on the track, the handle or the target around them may become a drag; the label is not part of the control.

members.name: takeDrag
members.description:
SWT-19: the drag is the switch's. The pointer is captured, the switch stays pressed, and the handle goes to the
pointer: over the state motion when it was away from it (the catch-up), then in the frame the pointer moves.

members.name: drawDrag
members.description: SWT-19: the handle at the pointer's place — less what is left of the catch-up — and every part at that progress.

members.name: onPointerUp
members.description:
SWT-20: a release chooses the side a fling is toward, else the side the handle is nearer to — the other condition
from the middle on. A change switches `selected` with one `input` and one `change`, as an activation does; either
way the progress leaves the pointer's place for the condition's over the selection motion.

members.name: onDragKeyDown
members.description: SWT-21: Escape cancels a drag in progress, and is spent on it: nothing behind the switch hears it.

members.name: onLostPointerCapture
members.description: SWT-21: a capture taken away (a system gesture) cancels the drag; after a release there is none left to cancel.

members.name: cancelDrag
members.description:
SWT-21: the drag is over without a choice. The handle and the look return to the condition `selected` holds, over
the selection motion; nothing is emitted, and a click the pointer still produces is not an activation.

members.name: endDrag
members.description: Lets go of the pointer and of the progress: the stylesheet's value (0 or 1) is its target again.

members.name: onRootPointerDown
members.description: A new press: whatever click a drag left unanswered is not coming any more. Presses on the control arrive here after `onControlPointerDown`.

members.name: onPointerLeave

declarations.description:
The view (TBV-11) is a column: its own row (TBV-16), slotted at the top across its whole width at the row's own
height, and the container directly below it with no space between them. The row is outside the container, so no
switch moves, fades, blurs or clips it (TBV-5), and the container's touch-action does not reach it (TBV-3).

The container (TBV-5, TBV-11): every panel in the same grid cell, so the view is as tall as its row plus the panel it
shows — and the taller of two while a switch draws both — or, when the product sizes the view, the container fills
what the row leaves and each panel scrolls inside it. It clips the panels to its corners (comp.tab-view.container.shape), so neither the travel nor the blur is
drawn outside it. While a swipe is possible its touch-action leaves only vertical panning (and zoom) to the browser,
so a sideways drag reaches the view's pointer events (TBV-3).

The probe draws nothing: the view reads the switch's look and timing through its real properties when a switch or a
drag starts (TBV-4…7) — the travel's distance as a width, the blur as a height, the share of the width as a flex
factor, the opacity as itself, the motion as a transition that names no property — so a token is never parsed, and
a bare `0` a layer writes for a dimension reads as 0. Where motion is reduced the distance, its share and the blur are
0 and the motion is the fade's (TBV-7). The fade's own motion is read through the probe's animation, which names no
animation: it is what a view whose transition is fade switches over (TBV-22).

Shows the view of the selected tab under its own row of tabs, or linked to a row of `<tanrei-tabs>` placed elsewhere,
and lets a person swipe from view to view with the tabs' indicator following the finger.

Contract: specs/tab-view.spec.json. The view's `<tanrei-tab-panel>` children are its panels. By default (`tabs` empty)
the view draws its own row (TBV-16): a `<tanrei-tabs>` it places as its first light-DOM child, in its `tabs` slot above
the panels, with one `<tanrei-tab>` per panel made from the panel's `value`, `label`, `icon`, `label-hidden` and
`disabled`; the row's `variant`, `size`, `track`, `full-width` and `label` are the view's. The product does not edit that row. Linked
(TBV-17): `tabs` is the id of a `<tanrei-tabs>` in the same tree (as `popovertarget` is), and the `tabsElement` property
sets the element itself; either one set means the view draws no row, even while that element is missing. Either way
the panels are matched to the tabs by `value` and take the place of the row's own panels (TAB-13), and the selected
panel is the view's `value`, kept equal to the tabs' `value` in both directions without an event.

Every selection is announced once. With its own row the view fires `change` for a tab and for a swipe; the row's own
`change` never fires (TBV-18). Linked, a selection on the tabs is announced by the tabs' `change`, and a swipe by the
view's. The view sets its `value` (and the tabs') before `change` fires, as a native control does.

A switch — from the tabs, the product, or the rest of a released swipe — runs over `motion.switch-duration`: the old
panel moves `transition.distance` (plus `transition.distance-fraction` of the width) toward the edge it leaves by,
fading toward `transition.opacity` and blurring toward `transition.blur`, while the new one arrives from the other side.
Where motion is reduced only the fade is left, over `motion.fade-duration`. A drag by touch or pen that goes further
sideways than up or down holds the switch under the finger and sets the tabs' `indicatorOffset` in every frame; it
commits past half the width or on a fling toward the tab. Mouse, trackpad and wheel never swipe: the tabs are the way.

`transition` names the form of a switch: `slide` as above, `fade` — the two panels crossfade in place, over
`motion.fade-duration` — and `none`, which shows the new panel whole in the frame the selection is made and gives the
row the view draws the tabs' `transition="none"`, so that its indicator is on the new tab in that frame too; a swipe
is still taken, the panel staying at rest under it while the indicator follows the finger. `auto`, the default, is
the design system's answer (`--tanrei-comp-tab-view-motion-transition`).

A drag across the row — the view's own, or the linked one — is the tabs' (TAB-28): their indicator follows the pointer
and the view takes no drag meanwhile. The shown panel stays at rest for its whole length, because no tab is selected
before the release; the release switches to the chosen tab's panel as any selection does, and with its own row the
view announces it, once.

slots.description: `<tanrei-tab-panel>` children: the panels, one per tab, each with the value of its tab.
The view's own row, which it places there itself (a `<tanrei-tabs>`); not for the product.
slots.name: tabs

members.name: value
members.description:
The value of the selected tab, whose panel is shown — kept equal to the linked tabs' `value`: setting either sets the
other, without an event. `null` shows the panel of the tab the tabs select while theirs is `null` (the first enabled
tab). A swipe sets it (and the tabs') before `change` fires.

members.name: variant
members.description:
The variant of the row the view draws itself, with the tabs' meaning (TBV-16): primary for the main views of a screen,
secondary for views within one of them, tonal for the quiet row of a sample or a setting, or a value the system
adds to the tabs. Unused while linked (TBV-17).

members.name: size
members.description: The size of the row the view draws itself, with the tabs' meaning (TBV-16): `medium`, or `small` for a row in a header. Unused while linked (TBV-17).

members.name: track
members.description:
Whether the row the view draws itself draws its track, with the tabs' meaning (TBV-16): false draws none, true
draws it, and null, the default, takes the system's choice. The attribute: absent is null, `track` is true,
`track="false"` is false. Unused while linked (TBV-17).

members.name: fullWidth
members.description:
How the view's own row lays out its tabs, with the tabs' meaning: false (hug) sizes each tab to its label and scrolls
the row; true (fill) shares the row's width. Unused while linked (TBV-17).

members.name: label
members.description: The accessible name of the view's own row: what the views are views of. Unused while linked (TBV-17).

members.name: tabs
members.description:
Empty (the default): the view draws its own row of tabs from its panels (TBV-16). Set: the id of the `<tanrei-tabs>`
this view is linked to, in the same tree, which names its panels and moves between them; the view draws no row, even
while that element is missing (TBV-17).

members.name: noSwipe
members.description:
The spec's `swipeable`, inverted (an HTML boolean attribute defaults to false): turns the swipe off, leaving the
switch to the tabs alone, for panels whose content is itself dragged sideways (a map, a drawing surface).

members.name: transition
members.description:
The form in which the shown panel gives way to the next. `slide`: the panels travel, fading and blurring on the
way as the system's transition values say, and follow a swipe. `fade`: the two crossfade in place. `none`: the new
panel is shown whole in one frame, and the row the view draws puts its indicator on the new tab in that frame.
`auto` (the default, and what any other value is taken as) takes the design system's answer (`motion.transition`,
slide in the default system). Where motion is reduced slide is drawn as fade, and nothing is added to fade or none.
A row the view is linked to keeps its own `transition`.

members.name: group
members.description:
The group of the row the view draws itself, with the tabs' meaning (TBV-16): Tab views and rows of tabs in the
document that name the same group show the same choice, and a view that has no panel of that value keeps its own. A
view that follows shows its panel at once, without a switch, and fires nothing. Empty (the default): the view's
choice is its own. Unused while linked (TBV-17): the linked row names its own group.

members.name: rememberAs
members.description:
The key of the origin's `localStorage` under which the row the view draws itself keeps a person's choice and from
which it restores it before the view is first drawn, with the tabs' meaning. Empty (the default): nothing is read
or written. Unused while linked (TBV-17): the linked row names its own key.

members.name: swipes
members.description: Whether a drag can be taken now: linked, swipeable (TBV-8, TBV-14).

members.name: explicitTabs
members.description: The tabs set through `tabsElement`, which win over `tabs`.

members.name: link
members.description: The tabs this view is linked to now: its own row, or the row `tabs` names (TBV-14: null while that is missing).

members.name: ownRow
members.description: TBV-16: the row the view draws itself, kept while the view is linked elsewhere so that it can be drawn again.

members.name: rowTabs
members.description: TBV-16: the tab of the own row that each panel makes, kept while the panel is (TBV-12: nothing is recreated).

members.name: synced
members.description: The panels and their values at the last sync: a change of either shows the selected panel at once (TBV-6).

members.name: shown
members.description: The panel exposed as the selected tab's (TBV-9), which is drawn at rest once a switch ends.

members.name: appeared
members.description: Whether the view has shown a panel since it appeared or was linked: the first one is shown at once (TBV-6).

members.name: switching

type.text: { switch: Switch; animation: Animation | null; from: number; to: number; offset: number } | null

members.description: The switch drawn now, from a selection or the rest of a released drag (TBV-4, TBV-6).

members.name: tree$
members.description: While `tabs` names nothing in the tree, the tree is watched for it to appear.

members.name: tabsElement
members.description:
The `<tanrei-tabs>` this view is linked to — the row `tabs` names, or the view's own row; setting it links that
element instead (TBV-17), and `null` gives the view its own row back while `tabs` is empty.

members.name: linkedElsewhere
members.description: TBV-17: whether the view is linked to a row placed elsewhere (it then draws none), rather than drawing its own.

members.name: panels
members.description: The view's panels, in order.

members.name: linked
members.description: The linked tabs, while they are connected.

members.name: resolve
members.description:
Links the view to its tabs (TBV-1, TBV-14, TBV-16, TBV-17): the row `tabsElement` or `tabs` names — drawing none of
its own, even while that row is missing — or, while neither is set, the row it draws itself. A new link takes the
view's `value` over to the tabs — or, while it is null, takes theirs — and shows its panel at once (TBV-6).

members.name: placeOwnRow
members.description:
TBV-16: places the view's own row — created the first time — as its first light-DOM child in its `tabs` slot, drawn
from its panels, and returns it.

members.name: drawRow
members.description:
TBV-16: the own row as the panels and the view say now — its variant, fullWidth and label the view's, and one tab for
each panel TBV-15 shows (the first with each non-empty value), in the panels' order, whose value, label, icon,
labelHidden and disabled are the panel's. A panel keeps its tab; a tab is moved only when the order changed, so a
focused tab keeps its focus.

members.name: namedForm
members.description: TBV-22: the form `transition` names itself, or null while it is auto (or a value the view does not define).

members.name: form
members.description:
TBV-22: the form a switch is drawn in right now: the one `transition` names, else the system's choice as the
cascade gives it at this moment — never cached, and an unknown name is the first value (slide).

members.name: giveRowTransition
members.description:
TBV-23: gives the view's own row the tabs' transition none while the view's form is none, and auto — the tabs' own
answer — otherwise. Written as the attribute, so that the row has it in this task. A linked row is never set.

members.name: panelsChanged
members.description:
TBV-6, TBV-16: panels added, removed or given other values redraw the own row and show the selected tab's panel at
once; a panel's other tab props (label, icon, labelHidden, disabled) redraw the row only, in the same frame.

members.name: target
members.description:
The panel to show (TBV-1, TBV-14, TBV-15): linked, the panel of the tabs' selected tab — the first panel with its
value — or none when it has none; without tabs, the first panel with `value`, or the first panel while it is null.

members.name: sync
members.description:
Brings what the view shows in line with the selection (TBV-1, TBV-2, TBV-6): `switch` draws a switch to a newly
selected panel once the view has appeared; `instant` ends any switch and shows the panel at once. Then exposes the
panels (TBV-9) and reports what it should (TBV-14, TBV-15).

members.name: expose
members.description:
TBV-9, TBV-14: the shown panel is the tab panel, named by its tab (the tab controls it, TAB-13), a Tab stop itself
while it holds nothing focusable; a panel a switch or a drag still draws is inert and hidden from assistive
technology; every other panel is `hidden` and `inert`. Without tabs no panel has the tab panel role.

members.name: releaseFocus
members.description: TBV-10: a switch that hides the panel holding keyboard focus moves focus to the tabs' selected tab.

members.name: reports
members.description: TBV-14, TBV-15, TBV-17: what a debug build tells the developer, once the tree has had a frame to link the tabs.

members.name: look
members.description:
TBV-4…7: the switch's look and timing, read now through the probe's real properties (never cached, so a change of
system or of reduced motion applies to the next switch). TBV-22: under fade the distance, its share, the blur and
the opacity's end are 0 and the motion is the fade's, so the two panels crossfade in place; under none there is no
motion at all.

members.name: startSign
members.description: The physical direction a panel leaves by when the tab it gives way to comes after its own (TBV-5, TBV-13): the start edge.

members.name: tabPosition
members.description: The index among the linked tabs of the tab of a panel's value.

members.name: paint
members.description:
TBV-5: draws both panels of a switch at progress `p` in the same place, B over A, over a travel D of
transition.distance plus transition.distance-fraction of the width: A moved p × D toward the edge it leaves by, faded
to 1 − p × (1 − opacity) and blurred by p × blur; B moved (1 − p) × D from the other side, faded and blurred by
(1 − p). The travel follows p as eased (an overshoot included); the fade and the blur follow it clamped.

members.name: rest
members.description: A panel at rest: nothing of a switch is left on it.

members.name: makeSwitch
members.description: A switch from `from` to `to`: A leaves by the start edge when B's tab comes after A's among the tabs (TBV-5, TBV-13).

members.name: startSwitch
members.description: TBV-2, TBV-6: a selection on the tabs (or by the product) runs a switch from 0 to 1 over the switch's motion.

members.name: run
members.description:
Runs a switch from progress `from` to `to` over the look's motion, and the tabs' indicatorOffset from `offset` to 0
with it (TBV-4, TBV-6, TBV-7). The progress of the motion's easing is read from an effect without keyframes on the
container (it draws nothing), the view's own animation `tanrei-tab-view-switch` on the document's timeline; every
frame draws both panels from it.

members.name: endSwitch
members.description:
TBV-6: ends the running switch at once, as if it had finished — the panel it goes to at rest, the other hidden, the
tabs' indicator on the selected tab.

members.name: neighbour
members.description: The next (1) or previous (−1) enabled tab of the linked tabs from the selected one, in reading order, or null.

members.name: handlesSideways
members.description:
TBV-8: a drag that starts on content that handles sideways drags itself — a region that scrolls sideways, a slider,
a carousel, a text field, a control that sets its own touch-action, selected text — is not the view's.

members.name: onPointerDown
members.description: TBV-3, TBV-8: a touch or pen may start a swipe on the shown panel; a mouse, a trackpad or a wheel never does.

members.name: onPointerMove
members.description:
TBV-3: past the touch slop, further sideways than up or down, the view takes the drag (a running switch ends at once,
TBV-6) and draws the switch toward the tab the drag goes to at p, setting the tabs' indicatorOffset to ±p, in every
move. A drag that went up or down first is the browser's scrolling, for its whole length.

members.name: follow
members.description: TBV-3, TBV-13: the drag's distance `dx` (px, rightward) as a progress toward the next or previous enabled tab.

members.name: onPointerUp
members.description:
TBV-4: a release commits past half the width or on a fling toward the tab, and cancels otherwise (a fling away always
cancels). A commit sets the view's and the tabs' value, re-expresses the offset from the new tab and fires `change`
once, in the same frame; the rest of the switch and the offset then run over the switch's motion from where the
release left them — the offset back at once where motion is reduced (TBV-7). A cancel runs both back to 0.

members.name: onPointerCancel
members.description: A drag the browser took back (or that lost its pointer) goes back to rest.

members.name: endDrag
members.description: Drops a drag in progress: its panels back at rest, the indicator on the selected tab.

events.description: The user selected another panel — by a tab of the view's own row, or by a swipe: `detail.value` (and the view's and the tabs' `value`) is its value.

declarations.name: styles
declarations.default: css` /* TOC-1: as wide as its layout; no fill, no edge, no padding and no place of its own. */ :host { display: block; box-sizing: border-box; min-inline-size: 0; } /* TOC-32: no items — nothing is drawn, no space is taken, nothing is exposed. */ :host([hidden]), :host([data-empty]) { display: none; } nav { display: block; min-inline-size: 0; } /* TOC-2: the title above the list — the label's text, or the product's own heading in its place, in one style. */ .title { display: block; margin: 0; margin-block-end: ${t('container-gap')}; font: ${t('title-typescale-font')}; letter-spacing: ${t('title-typescale-letter-spacing')}; color: ${t('title-color')}; overflow-wrap: anywhere; } ${productText('.title', { align: 'start' })} /* (A rule on a slotted element reads that element's own cascade: only what it inherits and the tokens are named.) */ ::slotted([slot='title']) { margin: 0; padding: 0; font: inherit; letter-spacing: inherit; color: inherit; } /* ── The compact presentation (TOC-25 to TOC-27): one block with a fill, the row, and the list under it ────── */ /* The block is never taller than its layout gives the element (a maximum height of the element's own, or the height a flex or grid layout holds it to): the list then scrolls inside, under the row. */ :host([presentation='compact']) { display: flex; flex-direction: column; } .compact { position: relative; display: flex; flex-direction: column; flex: 0 1 auto; min-block-size: 0; overflow: clip; ${unsafeCSS(cornerRadius(`${PREFIX}-compact-container-shape`))} background-color: ${t('compact-container-color')}; } /* The disclosure row: a button — the title, the current section's name on one line, the chevron. */ .row { all: unset; box-sizing: border-box; position: relative; /* Its own stacking context, so the ripple can sit above the container color and below the row's parts. */ isolation: isolate; display: flex; flex: none; align-items: center; gap: ${t('compact-row-gap')}; inline-size: 100%; min-block-size: max(${t('compact-row-height')}, var(--tanrei-sys-target-pointer)); padding-inline: ${t('compact-row-padding-inline')}; ${unsafeCSS(cornerRadius(`${PREFIX}-row-shape`))} ${unsafeCSS(paint(''))} cursor: pointer; -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent; transition-property: background-color, color, opacity; transition-duration: ${t('motion-state-duration')}; transition-timing-function: ${t('motion-state-easing')}; } @media (pointer: coarse) { .row { min-block-size: max(${t('compact-row-height')}, var(--tanrei-sys-target-touch)); } } /* The title is never cut before the current section's name has been cut to nothing: the name has no size of its own and takes the room that is left; the title gives way — and wraps — only when the name has none. */ .row-title { flex: 0 1 auto; min-inline-size: 0; font: ${t('title-typescale-font')}; letter-spacing: ${t('title-typescale-letter-spacing')}; overflow-wrap: anywhere; } /* (The current section's name too: without a letter it has no dir, and is left to right as every such text.) */ ${productText(':is(.row-title, .row-current)')} .row-current { flex: 1 1 0%; min-inline-size: 0; overflow: hidden; font: ${t('compact-supporting-text-typescale-font')}; letter-spacing: ${t('compact-supporting-text-typescale-letter-spacing')}; color: ${t('compact-supporting-text-color')}; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; /* TOC-37: the name is text of its own direction (the element gives the box dir="auto", so that every engine cuts it at its own end), and its line still begins at the layout's start: the host's direction. */ text-align: left; } :host(:dir(rtl)) .row-current { text-align: right; } /* TOC-25, TOC-35, TOC-38: expand_more in its box, turned half a turn while the list is shown — never mirrored, and nothing in its place until the icon set can draw it (GlyphDrawnController sets data-drawn); declarations.description:
Lists the headings of the page being read as links to them and marks the one whose section is being read. Sub-headings are set in under their heading; where there is no room beside the text, the compact presentation is one row that names the current section and opens the same list. Contract: specs/table-of-contents.spec.json. The items are the product's own nested list of anchors, which stay in the document (TOC-6): before the element is defined, and with scripting off, the page holds a plain list of links that work. ```html
  • Install
    • npm
  • Configure
 ``` An item is an `
  • ` whose first child is its anchor — `href` is the anchor's own attribute and the label its text — and the item's own items are a list after the anchor, inside the same `
  • `. Everything drawn on the list is `@tanrei/web/table-of-contents.css` (every value a `--tanrei-comp-table-of-contents-*` token), which draws it before and without this script; the element adds the same sheet to the root it is connected to. The shadow root holds only what the product did not write: a `
    ` named by `label`, the title, and the compact presentation's block and row. Which item is current (`tracking="auto"`, TOC-9 to TOC-16): the last item, in the page's order, whose target has reached the line — where the browser itself rests a target it is sent to: the top of the view that scrolls the targets, plus that view's `scroll-padding-block-start`, plus the target's own `scroll-margin-block-start`. So a fixed header and the space a heading keeps above itself are declared once, in CSS, and never passed to the element. It reads the view on `scroll` (one passive listener, coalesced to a frame), on `resize` and when what it holds changes size; at rest it runs nothing. It never scrolls the view that holds the targets, never writes the address and never focuses anything in the content.
declarations.name: TanreiTableOfContents

cssParts.description: The navigation landmark; in the compact presentation the filled block.
cssParts.name: nav

cssParts.description: The title above the list (list presentation).
cssParts.name: title

cssParts.description: The compact presentation's row: a button that shows and hides the list.
cssParts.name: disclosure-row

cssParts.description: The row's chevron (hidden from assistive technology).
cssParts.name: icon

cssParts.description: The box that holds the list; in the compact presentation the part that scrolls where the block is held to less than the list needs.
cssParts.name: list

slots.description: The items: the product's own nested list (`<ul>` of `<li>`, each with its `<a href>` first). It stays in the document.

The product's own title in place of the label's text: a heading of the level the page's outline needs. Drawn in the title's text style whatever its level; `label` still names the landmark and the compact row.
slots.name: title

members.name: label
members.description: The title, in the product's language ("On this page"): drawn above the list and in the compact row, and the accessible name of the navigation landmark. Required.

members.name: labelHidden
members.description: Draws no title above the list and keeps `label` as the landmark's name. The compact row always shows the title.

members.name: presentation
members.description: How it stands: `list` is the title and the whole list; `compact` is one row that names the current section and opens the list below it. Which one a window gets is the layout's that places it.

members.name: density
members.description: How tall a row of the list is: `regular` holds the pointer target; `compact` is lower, for a long list beside the text of a product read with a pointer. For touch a row is the touch target in both. A design system may add values.

members.name: open
members.description: In the compact presentation, whether the list is shown below the row. The element sets it when the user opens, closes or chooses. Ignored in the list presentation.

members.name: current
members.description: The `href` of the item whose section the person is in; empty while none is. Set by the element while `tracking` is `auto`, by the product while it is `manual`.

members.name: tracking
members.description: Who decides which item is current: `auto` — the element, from where the items' targets are in the view that scrolls them; `manual` — the product, through `current`.

declarations.description:
Presents data that has rows and columns, with named columns, optional row headers, a caption and footer rows. A price list, a comparison, a list of settings, a status of many things. It scrolls in its own box when it does not fit. A column's header can ask for the rows in its order (`sort`); the table itself never sorts, filters, fetches or pages: it draws the rows it is given, in the order it is given them. Contract: specs/table.spec.json. The element has **no shadow root**: it is the scroll box around the product's own native table, which stays in the document and is never given another `display` — its semantics, a crawler's reading, copy and paste as a table and a screen reader's table navigation are the browser's own. ```html
Visits by region
RegionJanuary
Islands212
All regions6,846
``` A column is a `` of the `` row: its text is the header, `data-align="start | center | end"` says where the column's cells sit and `data-wrap="false"` keeps them on one line. A row is a ``; a footer row is a `` in ``. A cell is a ``, or a `` for the header of its row, and holds text, any view of the product's, or nothing. A cell may name its own `data-align` and `data-wrap`; a Markdown renderer's `align` is read as well (left and right as start and end). Everything drawn is `@tanrei/web/table.css` — every value a `--tanrei-comp-table-*` token — which draws the table before and without this script; the element adds the same sheet to the root it is connected to, so it also works inside another component's shadow root. The script adds what a stylesheet cannot: while the box scrolls it is a focus stop and a region with the table's name (`tabindex`, `role`, `aria-labelledby` or `aria-label`), and the arrow keys, Page Up, Page Down, Home and End scroll it as the browser scrolls a region; a hairline along an inline edge of the box says that columns lie beyond it; a column's alignment reaches its cells; a first column that is kept in view lets go where it would take more than half of the box. A column that can be sorted: its header cell says the order the rows are in — `aria-sort="none"`, `"ascending"` or `"descending"` — and holds the product's own ` ``` No rows: `…`, holding the product's Empty state (or its sentence, in an element). The status line: `

1–20 of 132

…
` after the table, inside the element, holding the product's sentence and its pagination; the `status` attribute is a convenience that writes the paragraph. Rows that can be chosen: `selection="multiple"`, and a first cell `` in every row — in the header row holding the checkbox for every row, in a body row that has a `data-value` holding that row's checkbox (``, or a native ``), and empty in a footer row, a placeholder row and a row that cannot be chosen. A chosen row carries `data-selected`. The table holds the selection: a change of a checkbox writes `data-selected` on its row and emits `selectionchange` with the values of the chosen rows; the product writes `data-selected` to choose a row itself, and nothing is emitted for it. The header's checkbox is kept checked, mixed or unchecked, disabled with no row to choose, and named by `select-all-label` or the product's words (`selectAllLabel`). A row's checkbox that has no name of its own is named by the row's header cell. The table stays a table: no grid, no selected state on a row. ```html
Name
Kettle
``` Loading: `loading` says that the product is fetching rows. The table is exposed as busy (`aria-busy` on the table) and draws what it is given — the rows it had, or rows `` whose cells are empty or hold a Skeleton's placeholder (``). Nothing is dimmed or disabled. Without a sortable column and with `selection` none the table takes no input and emits no event. A table inside a cell is the product's content and is not drawn by this one. Cells that span (`colspan`, `rowspan`) and a second header row work as HTML does and take the same cell styles.

members.name: read
members.description:
Reads the table the box holds and writes what follows from it: the caption and the name, the columns' alignment,
the row headers of a table of plain cells, the separation where the browser cannot query it — then asks for a
measure, which every table of the task shares (`measureSoon`). Called when a property changes and when the
table's content does (TBL-25); it writes only what differs, so it settles, its cost is the header row's, not the
rows', and it reads nothing of the layout: everything it writes is styled once, with what the other tables wrote.

members.name: readStatus

that a change of its text is told politely. A paragraph the product wrote is the one that is read, and is left as
it is. Emptied, this element's paragraph stays, empty and with no room (table.css): a status that is there before
its text is one whose text is told.

A tab panel (TAB-13, TBV-9, TBV-10): shown only while its tab is selected; a Tab stop itself when it holds nothing
focusable. A panel of a `<tanrei-tab-view>` (`.inside`) draws its ring inside its edge — the view clips what is drawn
outside it — with its corners following comp.tab-view.container.shape; the tabs' own panel draws it around its edge.

One tab of a row — the spec's item kind `tab`: a label, an optional icon, and the value that selects it.
Placed as a child of `<tanrei-tabs>`, as `<option>` in a `<select>`; the row decides whether it is selected, which tab
is the Tab stop, and answers its activation.

The host carries the tab's semantics — the tab role, its selected state, its position, the number of tabs and its
name, its label whether or not the label is drawn — and takes focus itself.

A label that does not fit its tab (a row that fills) is truncated with an ellipsis and shown whole in a plain tooltip on
hover and keyboard focus; it stays the tab's whole accessible name, and the tooltip is not exposed a second time.

declarations.description:
Switches between views of the same subject with a row of labelled tabs, one of them selected, above the view it shows.

Contract: specs/tabs.spec.json. `<tanrei-tab>` children are the tabs, in order; `<tanrei-tab-panel>` children after
them are the panels, matched to tabs by `value` — or, where a `<tanrei-tab-view tabs="<this row's id>">` is linked to
the row, the view's panels take their place (TAB-13), and the view draws the indicator between two tabs while it is
swiped (`indicatorOffset`, TAB-26). The row's selected tab is its `value`, as a `<select>`'s: `null`
selects the first enabled tab. The row sets it when a tab is activated — by pointer, touch, Enter, Space, or the arrow
keys, which select the tab they reach (automatic activation) — and then fires `change`.

Three variants say how much the selection weighs — `primary`, `secondary`, and `tonal`, the quiet row whose indicator
is a soft layer under a darker label — and are one control in everything else. `size` is the row's height (`medium`,
the default, and `small`, which stands in a header beside small controls: it stays as low as it is, and a press just
above or below it, on nothing that would answer the press itself, still selects the tab in line with it).

The row sits on a track: one constant color per variant, the same whichever tab is selected (a capsule in the
default system); `track="false"` fills none and changes nothing else, `track` draws it whatever the design system
says, and without the attribute the system decides (`--tanrei-comp-tabs-track-visible`). The tabs hug their content and scroll sideways inside the track (the default), or share the row's
width (`full-width`), truncating a label that does not fit. The selected tab's active indicator — the thumb on the
track: as tall as the row less the track's padding on every tab, a capsule as wide as the tab's content plus its
padding or a circle where that content is not wider than it is tall, and the tab's whole share in a row that fills —
slides to a newly selected tab with the underline, and each label and icon it passes over takes its covered colors
where it is covered.

A drag across the row — by touch, a pen or a mouse, past 8 px and further sideways than up or down — carries the
indicator with the pointer, its place, its width and the covered colors changing continuously. Nothing is selected
before the release, which chooses the nearer of the two tabs the indicator lies between (or the one a fling is
toward), sets `value` and fires `change` once; Escape, a cancelled pointer, or `value` set meanwhile returns it.

`transition` says how a new selection is drawn: `slide` as above, `none` whole in one frame — nothing travels and no
color fades between selected and not, a tab out of view is brought in at once, and a drag still carries the indicator
and lands at once on release — and `auto`, the default, as the design system says
(`--tanrei-comp-tabs-motion-transition`). Hover, focus and press are answered the same under each.

Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-tabs-*` tokens, per variant, look (selected or not) and state. How a
press is answered and how keyboard focus is drawn are the system's choices of kind (`--tanrei-sys-behavior-*`),
read from the cascade.
declarations.name: TanreiTabs

cssParts.description: The row that holds the tabs: the tab list.
cssParts.name: tablist

cssParts.description: The box that lays the tabs out and scrolls them sideways when they do not fit; it is also the track.
cssParts.name: scroller

cssParts.description: The constant background of the whole row (the same element as `scroller`): its color and its corners.
cssParts.name: track

cssParts.description: The line along the bottom of the whole row.
cssParts.name: divider

slots.description: `<tanrei-tab>` children (the tabs) and `<tanrei-tab-panel>` children (the panels).

members.name: variant
members.description:
How much the selection weighs. Primary tabs switch the main views of a screen, at the top of its content; secondary
tabs switch within one of them; tonal tabs are the quiet row, for a choice that should not compete with what it
changes — the language of a code sample, a contrast, a unit, a period. The three are the same control otherwise.

members.name: size
members.description:
The row's height (small 32 / medium 48) and what shrinks with it: a tab's padding, the active indicator's margins
and the icon. A small row puts a tab's icon before its label in every variant, and its tabs still answer a press
within the minimum target.

members.name: track
members.description:
Whether the row draws its track, the background behind all its tabs. False draws none and changes nothing else.
Null, the default, takes the system's choice (`track.visible`, on in the default system). The attribute: absent is
null, `track` is true, `track="false"` is false.

members.name: fullWidth
members.description:
False (hug, the default) sizes each tab to its content, never truncating its label, and scrolls the row sideways when
the tabs do not fit; true (fill) divides the row's width equally among the tabs and truncates a label that does not
fit its share, showing it whole in a tooltip (for two to five short labels).

members.name: value
members.description:
The value of the selected tab; `null` selects the first enabled tab. The row sets it when a tab is activated. While
the row is a member of a group (`group`), the group's choice selects the tab of that value wherever the row has one.

members.name: transition
members.description:
How the row draws a new selection. `slide`: the active indicator and the underline slide and resize to the newly
selected tab, the labels' colors changing under them. `none`: the new selection is drawn whole in one frame.
`auto` (the default, and what any other value is taken as) takes the design system's answer
(`motion.transition`, slide in the default system). A drag across the row carries the indicator under each, and
hover, focus and press are answered the same; where motion is reduced a selection is drawn as `none` does.

members.name: label
members.description:
The accessible name of the row: what the views are views of — or, for a row without panels, what is chosen
("Contrast", "Units"). Needed when a screen has more than one row of tabs, and for every row without panels.

members.name: group
members.description:
Names a choice this row shares with the other rows of tabs in the document — placed by the product or drawn by a
`<tanrei-tab-view>` — that name the same group, compared exactly. Selecting a tab in one selects the tab of the same
value in every other row that has an enabled one, at once and without moving focus or the page; a row that has no
such tab keeps its own. Only the row the person used fires `change`. Empty (the default): the row's choice is its own.

members.name: rememberAs
members.description:
The key of the origin's `localStorage` under which a person's choice on this row is kept across pages and visits,
and from which it is restored before the row is first drawn. The key is the product's own and is used exactly as
given; only the chosen tab's value is stored. Empty (the default): the row neither reads nor writes any storage. It
needs no group, and a group needs no key.

members.name: joined
members.description: TAB-36: the group the row is a member of now (null: none, or the row is out of the document).

members.name: known
members.description: TAB-37: the `value` the row last saw as its own; another one, once the row is drawn, is one the product set.

members.name: restored
members.description: TAB-39: whether the row has looked for a remembered choice, which it does once, before it is first drawn.

members.name: restoring
members.description: TAB-39: the remembered value a row without a group selects as soon as it has an enabled tab of it.

members.name: atOnce
members.description: TAB-38: the selection changed because the row follows (its group, or the storage): the next sync draws it at once.

members.name: following
members.description: TAB-41: the rows that follow one choice together; the row adds itself instead of measuring alone.

members.name: followed
members.description: TAB-41: the `value` the row has already drawn as a follower, so that the update its change asks for draws nothing again.

members.name: offset
members.description: TAB-26: the offset the indicator is drawn at now (0: on the selected tab).

members.name: indicatorOffset
members.description:
Where the active indicator and the underline are drawn while a linked Tab view is swiped, relative to the selected
tab: 0 on it, 1 on the next enabled tab and −1 on the previous one in reading order, and in between for values
between (TAB-26). They follow it in the frame it is set, without a motion of their own; beyond 1 they stay on the
neighbour, and where there is no enabled tab in its direction they stay on the selected tab. The Tab view sets it;
a product leaves it at 0 unless it drives the indicator itself. A property only, with no attribute.

members.name: linked
members.description: TAB-13, TBV-9: the Tab view linked to this row, whose panels take the place of the row's own.

members.name: owner
members.description: TBV-16, TBV-18: the Tab view that draws this row as its own, which announces the row's selections itself.

members.name: axes
members.default: new OpenAxesController(this, { component: 'tabs', behavior: 'TAB-7', axes: AXES })
members.description: TAB-7: a variant or a size a design system adds, and a value the active system does not have (src/primitives/axes.ts).

members.name: watched
members.description:
TAB-15, TAB-17: a change of size or place (a font arriving, the text size, the row resizing) puts things back at
once. One observer for every row (TAB-41): the rows that changed in a frame are told together, so that they are
all measured and then all written.

members.name: observed
members.description:
What the observer watches for this row now, each with the tab it is a part of (null: the row's own). Emptied when
the row leaves the document, and of a tab's parts when the tab leaves the row.

members.name: awaitsObserver
members.description: The row's first placement is the observer's, and has not been reported yet (`sync`).

members.name: shownTab
members.description: The tab drawn selected at the last sync (TAB-17 slides the indicator from it).

members.name: rest
members.description: Where the indicator and the underline are written to rest, in the track's coordinates (null: nowhere).

members.name: sliding

type.text: { clock: Animation; parts: Animation[]; stops: Mark[]; tabs: (TanreiTab | null)[] } | null

members.description:
TAB-17: the slide running now. `clock` is the row's own animation on the strip (it draws nothing; its progress is
the slide's), `parts` every tab's pieces, which the browser moves; `stops` are the indicator's places along the
slide, at equal parts of it — where it was, the enabled tabs it passes, where it goes — and `tabs` the tab each
stop is measured on (null: a place between tabs, where a slide, an offset or a drag had left it).

members.name: mark
members.description:
Where the indicator and the underline are drawn now, in the track's coordinates (null: nowhere): where they rest,
or the place a running slide has reached — worked out from its clock when it is asked for, never frame by frame.

members.name: drag
members.description: TAB-28…30: the drag across the row, from its press to its release.

members.name: swallowClick
members.description: TAB-28, TAB-29: the click that follows a drag the row took is not a tap.

members.name: tabs
members.description: The row's tabs, in order.

members.name: strip
members.description: The box the tabs are laid out in: it scrolls with them, so positions in it do not change while the row scrolls.

members.name: selectedTab
members.description:
TAB-11: the tab `value` selects — the first tab with that value — or, while `value` is null, the first enabled tab;
`null` when `value` names no tab.

members.name: tabOf
members.description: The tab an event came from.

members.name: select
members.description:
TAB-1, TAB-12: selects `tab`, and fires `change` once, when it is enabled and not already selected — or, on the row a
Tab view draws itself, has the view announce it instead (TBV-18), so that the row's `change` never reaches the product.

members.name: choose
members.description:
TAB-37 to TAB-41: a person chose the tab of `value` on this row. The row takes it (`now`: and draws it in this
task); it becomes the group's choice, so every other member that has an enabled tab of it follows at once, in the
same frame, and fires nothing; it is stored once under each key that this row or a member whose tab changed names;
and `hold` — the row, or a Tab view's container for a swipe — stays where it is in the window while the members
before it change height (TAB-40, TBV-21), measured once before anything is written and once after.

members.name: wouldFollow
members.description: TAB-36: whether the group's choice `value` would give this row another selected tab: it has an enabled tab of it.

members.name: enroll
members.description:
TAB-36, TAB-39, TAB-41: brings the row's membership in line with `group` and the document — out of the group it
was in, into the one it names — and, once, before the row is first drawn, looks for the choice remembered under
its key: a group that holds no choice takes it (whether or not this row has a tab of it), and a row without a
group selects its tab of it.

members.name: adopt
members.description:
TAB-36, TAB-39: takes the group's choice — or, without a group, the remembered value — while the row has an
enabled tab of it: `value` is set, nothing is fired, and the next sync draws it at once (TAB-38). Says whether
`value` changed. A row that has no such tab keeps its own, and follows again as soon as it has one.

members.name: followNow
members.description: TAB-38: this member follows the choice now, to be measured and drawn with the others that do (`together`).

members.name: followTogether
members.description:
TAB-38, TAB-41: every row of `rows` takes the choice in this task — its selection, its tabs' exposure and its panels —
and, once their tabs have drawn what they are now, all of them are measured and then all of them written, so that
sixty rows that follow cost one layout and not sixty. `keep` (TAB-40) is run where everything is read, after the
rows' own sizes are written and before their indicators are.

members.name: stilled
members.description: TAB-23, TAB-38: the tabs whose colors change at once now, and the frame that lets them move again.

members.name: still
members.description:
TAB-23, TAB-38: `tabs` change their colors without the state motion — for the frame that draws the change; two
frames on, when it has been drawn, they answer a pointer with their motion again. One frame for every row.

members.name: placing
members.description:
TAB-38: what `place()` and `reveal()` do for a row that follows, in two halves — everything is read now, and the
function returned writes it — so that many rows are read together and then written together. The indicator and the
underline go on `selected` at once (at the current offset), and the tab is brought into view inside the track at
once.

members.name: onClick
members.description: TAB-1: a tab's activation — its click, from a pointer, Enter, Space or `element.click()` — selects it.

members.name: onKeyDown
members.description:
TAB-12: Right and Left Arrow move to the next and previous enabled tab, wrapping (mirrored in right-to-left), Home and
End to the first and last; each move selects the tab it reaches. Disabled tabs are skipped (TAB-2).

members.name: onFocusIn
members.description: TAB-15: a tab that receives keyboard focus is brought into view.

members.name: sync
members.description:
Tells every tab what it is now and every panel whether it shows (TAB-2, TAB-11, TAB-13), assigns the slots, slides
the indicator when the selected tab changed (TAB-17), and reports what it should.

members.name: observe
members.description: Watches what moves the indicator when its size or place changes (TAB-17).

members.name: observeTab
members.description: Watches a tab's parts: what the indicator is measured from.

members.name: unobserve
members.description: Stops watching what `gone` says is no longer the row's: everything when it leaves, a tab's parts when the tab does.

members.name: placeTogether
members.description:
TAB-15, TAB-17, TAB-41: `rows` changed size or place in one frame. Each puts its indicator back on its selected tab
and that tab in view, at once — one row as `place()` and `reveal()` do, several as they do but all read first and
then all written, so that a page of rows costs one layout and not one for each row. A row that slides or follows a
drag keeps its own way.

members.name: settleTogether
members.description:
TAB-41: puts the indicator of every row of `rows` on its `selected` tab, and that tab in view, at once: every row's
tabs are read, then written (`sized`); then every row's place is read — and `keep` run — then written.

members.name: motion
members.description: The indicator's timing (TAB-15, TAB-17): the tokens, read through real properties — 0 where motion is reduced.

members.name: boxes
members.description:
TAB-14, TAB-16, TAB-18: every tab sizes its container — the indicator's box on it — from the row's height and its own
content: all read first, then all written. Also says whether the tabs scroll inside the track (TAB-28).

members.name: readBoxes
members.description: The reading half of `boxes()`: what every tab says of its container now, or null while the row is drawn flat.

members.name: writeBoxes
members.description:
The writing half of `boxes()`: every tab's container as `sizes` say, and how far the end tabs reach into the track's
inset. Says whether a tab changed its own width by it, so that the tabs are read once more.

members.name: scale
members.description:
TAB-16, TAB-24: how much larger the row is drawn than laid out now — not 1 while an ancestor scales it (a picker's
or a dialog's surface growing in over its open motion, which is when a row inside it is first measured). Nothing
reports the end of a transform, so the row never keeps a box measured in the page's pixels.

members.name: scaleSeen
members.description: The scale the row was last measured at, the frame that looks at it again, and for how many frames it has not changed.

members.name: watchScale
members.description:
TAB-16: a row measured at a scale is measured through it — to the page's precision divided by the scale, so the
smaller it is drawn the less exact its boxes are — and nothing reports a transform changing or ending. So while the
row is drawn at a scale that changes, it measures again in every frame the scale changed, and what it has drawn when
the motion ends was measured at the motion's end. It stops looking once the scale is 1, or has not changed for
`SCALE_STILL_FRAMES` frames (a row kept at a scale); a row drawn flat is looked at until it is not, since nothing of
it has been measured yet.

members.name: flat
members.description:
TAB-16: whether the row is drawn flat now — scaled to nothing on an axis, as on the first frame of a surface that
grows from its anchor's edge. Nothing of it can be measured then (every box on the page is empty) and nothing of it
is seen, so nothing is written; `watchScale()` places the indicator once it is not flat.

members.name: scrolls
members.description: TAB-14, TAB-28: whether the tabs do not fit and scroll inside the track.

members.name: measure
members.description:
TAB-16: where the indicator and the underline go on `tab`, in the strip's coordinates. The indicator is the tab's
container (its box): as tall as the row less track.padding above and below and, in a row that hugs, as wide as the
content plus active-indicator.padding-inline on each side — a circle where the content is not wider than it is tall
— or, in a row that fills, as wide as the tab. The underline spans the content (primary) or the tab (secondary).

members.name: draw
members.description:
TAB-16, TAB-24: draws the indicator and the underline at `mark` on every tab at once — each tab its piece, clipped to
it, and the covered copy of its content within it — so the indicator and every inversion move in the same frame.
Everything is read first, then written.

members.name: drawing
members.description: `draw()` in two halves: every tab's box is read now, and the function returned writes every tab's piece.

members.name: frames

type.text: { read: ({ tab: TanreiTab; x: number; y: number } & TabFrame)[]; radius: number }

members.description: Every tab's box and its content's box, in the strip's coordinates and the row's own pixels, and the indicator's corner.

members.name: markTab
members.description: The tab the indicator was last put on at rest (no offset, no slide, no drag), or null.

members.name: at
members.description:
TAB-16, TAB-26: where the indicator and the underline go for `selected` at the current offset — on it at 0, and
otherwise each edge interpolated toward the next (above 0) or previous (below 0) enabled tab in reading order by the
offset's magnitude, clamped to 1; on `selected` where there is no enabled tab in that direction.

members.name: place
members.description:
TAB-17, TAB-26: puts the indicator on the selected tab (at the current offset) at once — or, while it slides, sends
the slide there; while a drag carries it (TAB-28), it stays where the pointer is.

members.name: stopSliding
members.description: Ends a slide where it is: its pieces leave, and what is written under them shows until the caller draws.

members.name: stops

type.text: { tab: TanreiTab; left: number; right: number }[]

members.description: The enabled tabs in the order they are drawn along the row, left to right, with each one's box on the page.

members.name: placeAt
members.description:
TAB-28: where the indicator is drawn while the pointer is at `x` (clientX): on an enabled tab at that tab's centre,
halfway between two neighbouring enabled tabs where they meet (the middle of any disabled tabs between them), each
edge at the linear interpolation in between, and on the first or last enabled tab before or beyond its centre.
Nothing changes at the place where two tabs meet: it is only where `p` passes one half.

members.name: slide
members.description:
TAB-17, TAB-21, TAB-24: the indicator and the underline slide and resize from where they are drawn — on `old`, or
wherever a running slide, an offset or a released drag has left them — to `tab` over the indicator's motion, as one
box measured on the page, so the slide mirrors in right-to-left. The old tab is measured afresh: it may have moved
without changing size (the layout direction flipping), which nothing reports. At once where motion is reduced.

The browser runs it. The row writes once — the end of the slide, where everything rests — and gives every tab the
indicator passes its pieces as animations between the slide's stops (`slideIndicator`), all on the document's
timeline from the same moment as the row's own animation `tanrei-tabs-slide` on the strip, an effect without
keyframes that draws nothing and is the slide's clock. No script runs while it slides; where the indicator has got
to is worked out from the clock when something asks (`mark`): a choice made meanwhile, a drag, an offset.

Every frame is a look a drag draws (TAB-28): from a tab at rest the indicator passes over the enabled tabs between
the two as a drag does, taking each one's box on the way, so its width is always between two neighbouring tabs'.
From anywhere else it goes straight to the tab, each edge interpolated.

members.name: slideThrough
members.description:
TAB-17: writes the slide's end and has the browser move every tab's pieces through `stops` — a new slide, or
(`clock`) the one that is running, which goes on from the moment it began.

members.name: stateMotion
members.description: The state motion (TAB-28's catch-up), read through real properties of the strip — 0 where motion is reduced.

members.name: onPointerDown
members.description:
TAB-28: a press on the row with touch, a pen or a mouse may become a drag. Not while indicatorOffset is not 0 (the
swipe that sets it has the indicator, TAB-26), not without a selected tab to carry the indicator from, and, while the
tabs scroll inside the track, only from the selected tab: every other sideways drag scrolls them.

members.name: watchPointer
members.description:
From the press to the release the pointer is followed on the window: before the drag is taken nothing captures it,
and it may leave the row (a mouse) and be released anywhere.

members.name: onPointerMove
members.description:
TAB-28: past the touch slop, further sideways than up or down, the row takes the drag: the pointer is captured, the
pressed tab leaves its pressed state, and the indicator comes to the pointer over the state motion and then follows
it in every move. A drag that went up or down first is the page's, for its whole length.

members.name: follow
members.description:
TAB-28: draws the indicator and the underline where the pointer is — in the frame it moves, without a motion of their
own, except the catch-up that brings them from where they rested — and scrolls the tabs to keep the indicator in view
while the drag carries it toward an end of the track.

members.name: onPointerUp
members.description:
TAB-29: a release chooses one enabled tab — the one the indicator is nearer to of the two it lies between (the one
after it from halfway on), or the one of the two a fling is toward — and selects it (one `change`, the indicator
settling from where the release left it), or returns the indicator when it is the selected tab. It becomes the Tab
stop; the click that follows is not a tap.

members.name: onPointerCancel
members.description: TAB-30: the platform took the pointer back.

members.name: onLostCapture
members.description: TAB-30: a capture lost while the drag lasts (not by its own release) cancels it.

members.name: onDragKey
members.description: TAB-30: Escape while a drag lasts cancels it, and nothing else hears that key.

members.name: cancelDrag
members.description:
TAB-30: ends a drag the row has taken without a selection — the indicator returns to the selected tab over the
indicator's motion (`settle`), or is left to the caller's own placing — and the pointer, still down, is ignored until
it is released.

members.name: unwatch
members.description: Nothing of the drag is watched any longer.

members.name: endDrag
members.description: The pointer is up (or gone): the drag is over, and the click that may follow it is let through no longer than this task.

members.name: dropDrag
members.description: The row is leaving: nothing of a drag is kept.

members.name: settle
members.description:
TAB-29, TAB-30: after a drag, the indicator and the underline go from where they are to `chosen` — selecting it, with
one `change`, when it is not the selected tab — or back to the selected tab (`null`), over the indicator's motion and
at once where motion is reduced.

members.name: onClickCapture
members.description: TAB-28, TAB-29: the click a taken drag ends with is not a tap — it activates nothing.

members.name: reveal
members.description:
TAB-15: scrolls the tabs inside the track until the whole of `tab` is visible — over the indicator's motion when `animate`, at
once when the row first appears (or is resized) and where motion is reduced. The progress of the motion's easing is
read from an effect without keyframes on the scroller (it draws nothing), so the scroll follows the token's curve and
the motion is the scroller's own animation, `tanrei-tabs-reveal`, on the document's timeline: read, paused or finished
like the indicator's slide.

members.name: revealing
members.description: The reading half of `reveal()`: where the tabs must scroll to for the whole of `tab` to be visible, or null where it is.

members.name: hasNoTransition
members.description:
TAB-43: whether the row draws a new selection at once right now: its `transition` when it names one, else the
system's choice as the cascade gives it at this moment — never cached, and an unknown name is the first value (slide).

members.name: syncChoices
members.description:
TAB-49, TAB-43: where the browser answers no style query, the two choices' names are read from the cascade and
written on the row for the same rules (`whenChosen()`); where it does, nothing is written — an attribute could
only go stale.

members.name: rows
members.description: TAB-5: every row in the page, for the one listener that hears a press beside them.

members.name: listenBeside
members.description: TAB-5: `row` enters or leaves the document; the window is listened to while there is a row.

members.name: onPressBeside
members.description:
TAB-5: a press that no tab took, and that nothing has answered by the time it reaches the window. Where it lies just
above or below a row that is lower than the minimum target, in line with one of its tabs, it is that tab's: the
row's hit area reaches as far beyond its top and bottom edges as it takes to make the target, without the row
being any taller. It yields to whatever would answer the press itself — a control, a link, a field, a Tab stop,
anything that shows the pointer of a link — to a press that ends a selection of text, and to a surface in the top
layer that the row is not inside. No element is laid over the page for it: the tabs scroll inside a box that clips
them, so nothing of a tab can reach beyond the row, and an element laid beside the row would lie over the controls
next to it.

members.name: tabBeside
members.description:
TAB-5, TAB-34: the enabled tab of this row that a press at the event's point belongs to though it missed the row: the
point is in line with the tab — or beyond the track's end beside an end tab that ends there, by no more than that
tab lacks to the target's width — and no further above the row's top edge or below its bottom edge than half of
what the row lacks to the minimum target (sys.target.touch for touch and a pen, and where the input cannot be told on a
device whose pointer is coarse; sys.target.pointer for a mouse), and the tab is not covered where the point is
nearest to it. Null for a row as tall as the target.

events.name: change
events.description: The user selected another tab: `detail.value` (and the row's `value`) is its value.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description:
How much the selection weighs. Primary tabs switch the main views of a screen, at the top of its content; secondary
tabs switch within one of them; tonal tabs are the quiet row, for a choice that should not compete with what it
changes — the language of a code sample, a contrast, a unit, a period. The three are the same control otherwise.

attributes.description:
The row's height (small 32 / medium 48) and what shrinks with it: a tab's padding, the active indicator's margins
and the icon. A small row puts a tab's icon before its label in every variant, and its tabs still answer a press
within the minimum target.

attributes.description:

Null, the default, takes the system's choice (`track.visible`, on in the default system). The attribute: absent is
null, `track` is true, `track="false"` is false.

attributes.name: full-width
attributes.description:
False (hug, the default) sizes each tab to its content, never truncating its label, and scrolls the row sideways when
the tabs do not fit; true (fill) divides the row's width equally among the tabs and truncates a label that does not
fit its share, showing it whole in a tooltip (for two to five short labels).

attributes.name: value
attributes.description:
The value of the selected tab; `null` selects the first enabled tab. The row sets it when a tab is activated. While
the row is a member of a group (`group`), the group's choice selects the tab of that value wherever the row has one.

attributes.name: transition
attributes.description:
How the row draws a new selection. `slide`: the active indicator and the underline slide and resize to the newly
selected tab, the labels' colors changing under them. `none`: the new selection is drawn whole in one frame.
`auto` (the default, and what any other value is taken as) takes the design system's answer
(`motion.transition`, slide in the default system). A drag across the row carries the indicator under each, and

attributes.name: label
attributes.description:
The accessible name of the row: what the views are views of — or, for a row without panels, what is chosen
("Contrast", "Units"). Needed when a screen has more than one row of tabs, and for every row without panels.

attributes.name: group
attributes.description:
Names a choice this row shares with the other rows of tabs in the document — placed by the product or drawn by a
`<tanrei-tab-view>` — that name the same group, compared exactly. Selecting a tab in one selects the tab of the same
value in every other row that has an enabled one, at once and without moving focus or the page; a row that has no
such tab keeps its own. Only the row the person used fires `change`. Empty (the default): the row's choice is its own.

attributes.name: remember-as
attributes.description:
The key of the origin's `localStorage` under which a person's choice on this row is kept across pages and visits,
and from which it is restored before the row is first drawn. The key is the product's own and is used exactly as
given; only the chosen tab's value is stored. Empty (the default): the row neither reads nor writes any storage. It
needs no group, and a group needs no key.

declarations.description:
Lays out a set of tags or chips in lines that wrap, spaced for what it holds, and exposes the set as one named list.

Contract: specs/tag-group.spec.json. It reads four tokens (`--tanrei-comp-tag-group-gap-*` and `-row-gap-*`, one pair
per `spacing`) and draws nothing of its own: no container, no fill, no edge, no padding, and not its `label`. Its
members are `<tanrei-tag>` and `<tanrei-chip>` children, which stay in your DOM where you wrote them, drawn from
their own tokens at their own size, with their own states, events, names and Tab stops (TGR-6). The group takes no
focus, handles no key, keeps no selection, does not make filter chips exclusive and fires no event.

It is a list (TGR-7): the shadow root holds one element with the list role, named by `label`, around the slot, and
each member is given `role="listitem"` while it is in the group — the attribute is written on your element where it
has no `role` of its own, and taken back when it leaves. A chip's button or link, with its state, is inside its item.

`spacing` says what the set holds. Lines of tags stand as close as the tags along a line; lines of chips stand far
enough apart that each chip keeps its whole touch target, and a chip in a group ends its hit area at the middle of
the gap to its neighbour — along a line, and between two lines while the set wraps (TGR-5). A set of chips wants
`spacing="chips"`.

When a member leaves while focus is on it — on a chip or on its remove action — focus goes to the chip that followed
it, or to the one before where none follows (TGR-9). The group removes nothing itself: on a chip's `remove` you take
the element out. When the last member that takes focus has gone the group has nowhere to put it; move it yourself to
the control the set belongs to. A group with no member draws nothing, takes no space and exposes nothing (TGR-8).

It supplies no words: the name of the set is yours, in `label`.

declarations.description: Names a category or a status with a short static label, quietly, outlined or filled, in the colors of a status where it has one. It is text, never a control. Contract: specs/tag.spec.json. ``, with a glyph of the icon set in the `icon` slot (`sell`) or a `dot` before the label. Every visual value is a `--tanrei-comp-tag-*` token, one set per variant and status; how far its corners ease is the system's amount (`--tanrei-sys-shape-corner-smoothing`). A tag has no role, no name, no state and no event: its label is read where it sits, as text. It takes no input and no focus, and input over it reaches the element that holds it — a link, a button, a list item — which draws its own states. A label that must be pressed, switched or removed is a chip; one that leads somewhere is a link; a dot or a count on another element is a badge. Inside something disabled — a disabled field's label, a disabled row — `disabled` draws it in its look's disabled colors, so that it fades with what holds it; it changes nothing else. A status changes colors only, and color alone never says it: the label does ("Failed"), or `statusLabel` adds it in words for assistive technology ("Error", read as "Error, 3 builds") without drawing it. An outlined tag with a status always draws the dot, because nothing else in that look shows the status. The glyph and the dot are decorative. The label is one line. It is cut with an ellipsis when the layout gives the tag less room than it needs, and is still read in full; the tag has no hover to show the rest, so give it room. A tag with no label draws nothing.

declarations.description:
Lets people enter and edit text as one complete field. Built from a Field (`<tanrei-field>`) and the Text input
(`<tanrei-text-input>`) it frames: the box under the Field's label — or, in the filled and the outlined look, with
the label floating in it — with the Field's help, its error and the count, tied together for assistive technology
and taking part in a form as one control.

Contract: specs/text-field.spec.json. `<tanrei-text-field name="email" label="Email" type="email"
autocomplete="email" requirement="required" supporting-text="We never share your address."></tanrei-text-field>`.

Composed (`src/primitives/composed.ts`): its shadow root holds the two members' own elements and nothing
else, so it draws nothing of its own and has no token — every `--tanrei-comp-field-*`,
`--tanrei-comp-input-box-*` and `--tanrei-comp-text-input-*` value reaches the members by inheritance, and one text field is set apart by setting
such a property on this element. Each property is its member's, set on that member unchanged: `label`,
`label-hidden`, `supporting-text`, `error-text`, `error`, `disabled`, `requirement`, `required-mark`,
`required-text` and `optional-text` are the Field's, every other one the text input's. One level down, the same by
hand: `<tanrei-field label="Email" requirement="required" supporting-text="We never share your address.">
<tanrei-text-input name="email" type="email" autocomplete="email"></tanrei-text-input></tanrei-field>` — and the box
alone, where a label stands elsewhere, is `<tanrei-text-input>` with a `label` of its own.

It is a block as wide as its place, and its box fills it (TXF-62): give it a narrower place for a narrower box.

`value` is at every moment the text input's, and the five events are that input's own, with this element as their
target: `event.target.value` is the new value in every listener. It dispatches none itself. The one thing it does
that the pair by hand does not: while `counter` is set it gives its Field the count its text input keeps, at every
change (TXF-67) — by hand a product writes `field.countText = input.countText` in its `input` listener.

Form-associated: it submits the value under `name` — nothing while disabled —, resets to its `value` attribute, is
restored on navigation, follows a disabled `<fieldset>`, and reports what its text input reports: a missing value
while `requirement` is `required` and it is empty, and a date's or a time's entry error. Enter in a single-line
field presses the default button of this element's form.

The element is not focusable itself and has no role: `focus()` goes to the input, and its name is `label` (with
`label-hidden` where it is not drawn), never `aria-label`. A press on the label row, on the box or on a floating
label focuses the input; a press on the help, the error text, the count or the gap between a row and the box does
nothing.
