declarations.name: DISABLED_DATES
declarations.default: { fromAttribute: parseValues, toAttribute: (value: string[]) => value.join(' ') }
declarations.description: `disabled-dates`: a space-separated list or a JSON array (src/primitives/values.ts). An element composed around the input declares the same converter.

The box people type in, and everything typed in it — one line, or several that follow the text or are resized by
hand, or a date or a time entered unit by unit in the locale's form — with optional icons, a prefix and a suffix, a
picker button, and, in the two looks that have one, the label that floats inside the box. It has no label row, no
help and no error text of its own: put it in a `<tanrei-field>`, which names it, describes it and marks it — or use
`<tanrei-text-field>`, which is the two as one element. Bare, it is for a place whose label stands elsewhere: a
filter in a toolbar, a cell of a table, a row with its label beside it; give it `label` there.

Contract: specs/text-input.spec.json. `<tanrei-field label="Email"><tanrei-text-input name="email" type="email">
</tanrei-text-input></tanrei-field>`, or bare: `<tanrei-text-input name="q" type="search" label="Filter tokens">
</tanrei-text-input>`. The box is drawn from `--tanrei-comp-input-box-*`, the one set of
tokens every input box is drawn from (TXI-68), one set per variant, look (plain or error) and state — how a state
looks is the active design system's decision — and what a text input alone draws (the resize grip, a segment, the
code face, the entries place) from `--tanrei-comp-text-input-*`. The text is edited in a native
`<input>` — a `<textarea>` while `multiline` — in the shadow root, so input methods, autofill,
selection and the clipboard work as the browser does. The name (its own `label`, else its Field's), the description
(the prefix and the suffix while shown, the count, then what its Field gives) and the invalid, required, read-only
and disabled states are set on that element.

It is a block as wide as its place, framed and bare alike (TXI-63): it has no width of its own. A narrower box is a
narrower place.

It tells the Field around it what only it knows, through the Field's own connection (`src/primitives/field.ts`):
that it draws the label itself while its look floats one, how far its text stands from its edges — the Field's
supporting row starts and ends there — and its own refusal of a date or a time, with its words (TXI-62). It takes
from that Field its name, its description, the required, invalid and disabled states, whether the label is hidden,
and whether an asterisk or the optional word follows a floating label. `countText` is the count it keeps while `counter` is set, as text
("12/40"): it describes and announces the count and draws none — a Field draws it, given it as `count-text`.

`stacked` (the default) draws no label — the label above it is its Field's row — and marks focus and error with a
line inside the container's edge; `filled` and `outlined` float the label inside the box. A design system may leave some out
: they still work, and a debug build says so.

`multiline` with `resize="auto"` (the default) follows its lines between `min-rows` and `max-rows` with an animated
height; `resize="manual"` draws a grip in the bottom end corner that is dragged, moved with the arrow keys, or
activated to fit the text (`resize-axis="both"` resizes the width too); `resize="fixed"` stays at `min-rows`.

`type="code"` is a field whose value is written for a machine — a pattern, a key, a snippet of configuration — on one
line or, with `multiline`, on many: the input line (prefix, value, placeholder, suffix) is one left-to-right row in
the code face that begins at the left in every layout direction, while the label, the icons, the messages and the
grip follow the page; the browser is asked not to correct, capitalise, spell-check, translate or complete it; a paste
is plain text, character for character; Tab still moves focus. `no-wrap` keeps each line of a multi-line code field
on one row and scrolls it sideways inside the container. It is a field, not an editor: no syntax colors, no line
numbers, no Tab that indents.

`date`, `time` and `date-time` are the stated exception to the native element: a row of segments — one spin button
per unit, in the locale's order — that are focused, stepped, typed into and cleared on their own, held as ISO 8601
(`2026-09-27`, `14:30`, `2026-09-27T14:30`) or empty while a segment is empty or the value is not available. A whole
date can be pasted. With `picker`, the field shows a picker button that asks the product to present a picker
(`pickerrequest`); the field presents none itself.

Form-associated: with a `name` it submits `value`, resets to its `value` attribute, restores on navigation, joins
constraint validation (a missing value while its Field says it is required; a date or time field's entry error as badInput,
rangeUnderflow, rangeOverflow or a custom error) and is left out while disabled — its own or a `<fieldset>`'s.
declarations.name: TanreiTextInput

cssParts.description: The box around the input: its fill, corners and hover state layer.
cssParts.name: container

cssParts.description: The outlined variant's border (with the gap for the floated label); a stacked field's inner line.
cssParts.name: outline

cssParts.description: The filled variant's bottom line.
cssParts.name: active-indicator

cssParts.description: The label that floats in a filled or an outlined box.
cssParts.name: label

cssParts.description: The required asterisk, or the optional word, after a floating label.
cssParts.name: requirement-label

cssParts.description: The native `<input>` or `<textarea>`; a date, time or date-time field's row of segments.
cssParts.name: input

cssParts.description: What was entered already, before the typing part: the content of the `entries` slot. The text input lays it out and draws none of it, so the part has no box of its own.
cssParts.name: entries

cssParts.description: One unit of a date or a time: a spin button in the row.
cssParts.name: segment

cssParts.description: The fixed text before the value.
cssParts.name: prefix

cssParts.description: The fixed text after the value.
cssParts.name: suffix

cssParts.description: The box of the leading icon.
cssParts.name: leading-icon

cssParts.description: The box of the trailing icon.
cssParts.name: trailing-icon

cssParts.description: The picker button, a `<tanrei-button>` (TXI-32).
cssParts.name: picker-button

cssParts.description: The grip of a multi-line field resized by hand (TXI-39).
cssParts.name: resize-grip

slots.description: An icon at the start of the field: a glyph name of the system's icon set, an ``. A glyph the icon set flags as showing a direction (`arrow_forward`, `send`) is drawn mirrored in a right-to-left layout. `data-mirror="auto | always | never"` on the element decides for one use.
slots.name: leading-icon

slots.description: An icon at the end of the field, or the product's own icon-only Button (clear, reveal password). A date or time field's picker button comes after it. A glyph is mirrored in right-to-left as in `leading-icon`.
slots.name: trailing-icon

slots.description: What was entered already — the product's own elements, or the chips of a component that holds the input (a chip field): laid out inside the box before the typing part, in lines that wrap (TXI-64). The text input gives them no role, no focus order and no key (TXI-66).
slots.name: entries

members.name: mirror
members.description:
TXI-35: the glyphs in the leading-icon and trailing-icon slots are marked when the icon set mirrors
their names in right-to-left, or the product's `data-mirror` says so (src/primitives/glyph-mirror.ts);
`iconGlyph()` draws the mark. The picker button's glyph is its Button's (TXI-32) and is not one the icon set flags,
and the resize grip's glyphs are never marked.

members.name: gripGlyph
members.description:
TXI-22, TXI-39: the resize grip's glyph is drawn once the icon set can draw it; until then nothing stands in its
place — not its name spelled out in a text face (src/primitives/glyph.ts).

members.name: frame
members.default: new FieldControlController(this, { errorCondition: true, named: () => !!this.label.trim(), says: () => this.saysToField, changed: () => (this.frameChanged = true), })
members.description:
TXI-62: the input's side of the exchange with the Field that frames it (src/primitives/field.ts). It takes the
Field's name, description and states, whether the label is hidden and whether an asterisk follows it; and it says
what only it knows — that it draws the label, how far its text is inset, its own refusal of an entry. It has an
error condition of its own (TXI-11). No Field: it is drawn as a bare input.

members.name: frameChanged
members.description: The Field's answer changed since the last update: the floating label may have other lines (TXI-13).

members.name: variant
members.description:
Stacked is a filled box that shows focus and error with a line inside its edge, under the label its Field draws
above it; filled and outlined float the label inside the box, marked by a tinted box and a bottom line, or by a
border. Use one style
per form. A design system may leave some out (the default system ships stacked only) or add values.

members.name: size
members.description: Minimum height of a single-line field's container (48 / 56 in the default system). The hit area always meets the minimum target.

members.name: type
members.description:
What the value is: chooses the keyboard, autocorrection, obscured entry and semantics. `code` is text written for
a machine rather than for a reader — a snippet of configuration, a pattern, an identifier, a query, a key: a
left-to-right run in the code face that the browser does not correct, capitalise, check for spelling or complete,
on one line or, with `multiline`, on many. `date`, `time` and `date-time` are entered segment by segment in the
locale's numeric form. The value is always a string.

members.name: value
members.description:
The text in the field; for date, time and date-time, the ISO 8601 form of what its segments give (2026-09-27, 14:30,
2026-09-27T14:30), or empty while a segment is empty or the value is not available. Setting it shows it and fires
nothing. The `value` attribute is what a form reset returns to.

members.name: held
members.description: The value the element holds: what the product set, or the person's last edit as the element took it.

members.name: nativeInput
members.description: The native text element, once drawn (none for a row of segments), and what it held when the element last wrote to it or took from it.

members.name: afterEdit
members.description: TXI-18: what an edit that left `text` in the native element becomes — itself, or what of it fits under maxLength. A composition is the platform's (TXI-4).

members.name: label
members.description: The input's own accessible name, for an input no Field frames or one whose visible label is elsewhere; a filled or an outlined input draws it floating. Inside a Field leave it empty: the Field's label names the input, and its own would win.

members.name: labelHidden
members.description: Does not draw the floating label of a filled or an outlined input, which stays the accessible name (the `label-hidden` attribute). Inside a Field, hide the label on the Field.

members.name: placeholder
members.description:
A hint shown while the value is empty and the label is not in the input line (above, floated or hidden). Never a
replacement for `label`. In a code field it is an example of the code and is drawn as code; a hint in words
belongs in its Field's `supportingText`. Ignored by a date, time or date-time field, whose empty segments each show their own.

members.name: error
disabled
members.description: Prevents focus, editing and form submission. Inside a Field, disable the Field, so that its label follows.

members.name: readOnly
members.description: The value can be focused, selected and copied, but not changed (the `readonly` attribute).

members.name: multiline
members.description: Accepts line breaks and shows several lines, sized as `resize` says. Ignored for password, date, time and date-time.

members.name: minRows
members.description:
The fewest lines a multi-line field shows (`min-rows`): the height of an empty auto-resized field, the starting and
smallest height of a manually resized one, and the height of a fixed one.

members.name: maxRows
members.description:
The most lines an auto-resized field grows to before it scrolls, and the tallest a manually resized one can be made
(`max-rows`); 0 is no limit. Ignored while `resize` is fixed.

members.name: resize
members.description:
How a multi-line field gets its height. `auto`: it follows the number of lines between `minRows` and `maxRows`, with
an animated change, and has no grip. `manual`: it starts at `minRows` lines and the person resizes it with the grip
in its bottom end corner. `fixed`: it stays at `minRows` lines, with no grip.

members.name: resizeAxis
members.description: What the person can resize by hand (`resize-axis`): the height only, or the height and the width. Ignored unless `resize` is manual.

members.name: resizeLabel
members.description: The accessible name of the resize grip (`resize-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ resizeLabel })`). Tanrei has none: without them the grip is drawn and works, and has no name.

members.name: noWrap
members.description:
Keeps every line of a multi-line code field on one row (`no-wrap`; the spec's `wrap: false`): a line wider than the
input scrolls sideways inside the container, and widens nothing. Without it a line that does not fit continues on
following rows; the value is the same either way. Read only while `type` is `code` and `multiline` is set: prose
always wraps, and a single line always scrolls in its line (reported in debug builds).

members.name: maxLength
members.description: The most user-perceived characters the user can enter; 0 is no limit (the `maxlength` attribute). Ignored for date, time and date-time.

members.name: counter
members.description: Keeps a character count (with `maxLength`, when set: "12/40"): part of the description, announced when typing pauses, and readable as `countText`. The input draws none: a Field draws it at the end of its supporting row, given it as `count-text` — which `<tanrei-text-field>` does by itself.

members.name: counterText
members.description:
The count said to assistive technology while `counter` is set and `maxLength` is above 0 (`counter-text`): your
sentence with the places `{count}`, `{limit}` and `{remaining}` ("{remaining} characters left"). Empty reads the
product's words (`setWords({ characterCountText })`); with neither the count is said as its digits ("12/40"). It is
drawn as digits whatever is said: `countText` stays "12/40".

members.name: counterNoLimitText
members.description: The count said while `counter` is set and there is no `maxLength` (`counter-no-limit-text`): your sentence with the place `{count}` ("{count} characters"). Empty reads the product's words (`setWords({ characterCountNoLimitText })`); with neither, the digits.

members.name: prefixText
members.description: Fixed text before the value, not part of it (`prefix-text`). Beside one line of email, url, tel, number or password it is written before the value along the direction of the run the two affixes make — that of their first strong character, left-to-right where they have none — in every layout direction; beside any other value it stands at the field's start edge. In a code field it is code: in the code face, at the left of the value in every layout direction. Ignored for date, time and date-time.

members.name: suffixText
members.description: Fixed text after the value, not part of it (`suffix-text`). Beside one line of email, url, tel, number or password it is written after the value along the run's direction (see `prefixText`); beside any other value it stands at the field's end edge. In a code field it is code: in the code face, at the right of the value in every layout direction. Ignored for date, time and date-time.

members.name: autocomplete
members.description: The autofill hint, as an HTML autofill field name (email, current-password, one-time-code…). A code field left without one asks the browser to offer no remembered entry.

members.name: locale
members.description:
A BCP 47 tag ("en-US", "ja-JP") for how a date, time or date-time field shows and reads its value: the order of its
segments, the separators, the clock, the digits and the names of the units. Empty uses the nearest `lang`
attribute, then the browser's language. The calendar is the Gregorian calendar in every locale.

members.name: min
members.description: The earliest value a date, time or date-time field accepts from the person, ISO 8601; empty for no limit.

members.name: max
members.description: The latest value a date, time or date-time field accepts from the person, ISO 8601; empty for no limit.

members.name: disabledDates
members.description:
Dates inside `min` and `max` that a date or date-time field does not accept from the person, as ISO 8601 calendar
dates — the same list the product gives its date-time picker. The `disabled-dates` attribute is a space-separated
list or a JSON array. Ignored by a time field.

members.name: invalidText
members.description: The words of the refusal of a date, time or date-time input committed with some segments filled and others empty (`invalid-text`): shown by the Field that frames it as its error text, and part of a bare input's description.

members.name: unavailableText
members.description: The words of the refusal of a date, time or date-time input committed with a value before `min`, after `max` or listed in `disabledDates` (`unavailable-text`): shown and described as `invalidText` is.

members.name: segmentEmptyText
members.description: What assistive technology reads as the value of a date or time segment that holds nothing yet (`segment-empty-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ segmentEmptyText })`). Tanrei has none: without them an empty segment has no value text.

members.name: picker
members.description:
Shows the picker button in a date, time or date-time field. The field presents no picker itself: it fires
`pickerrequest`, and the product presents one and sets `value` to what was picked.

members.name: pickerLabel
members.description: The accessible name of the picker button ("Choose date", `picker-label`). Required while the button is shown.

members.name: name
members.description: Web only: the name it is submitted under.

members.name: hasEntries
members.description: TXI-64, TXI-65: whether the entries slot holds content.

members.name: formDisabled
members.description: Set by an ancestor `<fieldset disabled>` (the element's `formDisabledCallback`).

members.name: segments
members.description: What a date or time field's segments hold (TXI-42 … TXI-46).

members.name: entryError
members.description: A date or time field's entry error, while it lasts (TXI-30).

members.name: says
members.description: What it tells its form, said where an element composed around it hears it (src/primitives/form-says.ts).

members.name: axes
members.default: new OpenAxesController(this, { component: 'text-input', behavior: 'TXI-9', axes: AXES })
members.description: TXI-9: sizes and variants a design system adds, and a value the active system does not have (src/primitives/axes.ts).

members.name: native
members.default: new NativeTextController({ input: () => this.input, value: () => this.value, setValue: (text) => this.takeText(text), commit: (input, from) => { if (this.maxLength <= 0 || graphemes(input.value).length <= this.maxLength) return; const allowed = fit(from, input.value, this.maxLength); input.value = allowed.value; this.place(input, allowed.caret); }, settled: () => { this.fitHeight(true); this.scheduleCount(); }, })
members.description:
TXI-1, TXI-4: the value and the native element kept in step around an input method (src/primitives/native-text.ts).
A committed composition is cut to maxLength (TXI-18) from the value it began with. A date or time field has no
native element: its segments take what an input method commits (TXI-45).

members.name: committed
members.description: TXI-2: the value last committed (when focus arrived, at the last change, or as the product last set it).

members.name: userValue
members.description: The value the person's last edit gave the field: a `value` that differs from it was set by the product.

members.name: typedDigits
members.description: TXI-45: the digits typed since the focused segment took focus.

members.name: composing
members.description: TXI-45: an input method is composing on a segment; nothing is taken until it commits.

members.name: within
members.description: TXI-43: focus is on one of the field's segments or on its picker button.

members.name: pickerAsked
members.description: TXI-33: the picker was asked for; focus leaving for it raises no entry error.

members.name: manualLines
members.description: TXI-39: the lines the person gave a manually resized field; null is minRows.

members.name: lines
members.description: The lines the input shows (the grip's value, TXI-41).

members.name: sized
members.description: The textarea whose height was last written: a new one is sized without motion (TXI-38).

members.name: manualWidth
members.description: TXI-39: a width the person gave the field is on the host's inline style; what it replaced is put back.

type.text: { id: number; x: number; y: number; lines: number; width: number; line: number; rtl: boolean; moved: boolean } | null

members.name: bar
members.description: TXI-58: the room a sideways scrollbar takes of the input's height, which an auto-resized field adds to its lines.

members.name: dateKind
members.description: The kind of a date, time or date-time field, or null for every other type.

members.name: row
members.description: TXI-42: the row of segments of a date, time or date-time field in its locale, or null for every other type.

members.name: isCode
members.description: TXI-53: the field holds code — its input line is one left-to-right row in the code face.

members.name: unwrapped
members.description: TXI-57, TXI-58: the lines of the code are not wrapped — read only by a multi-line code field.

members.name: layout
members.description: How the variant is laid out: filled and outlined by name, every other value as stacked (TXI-9).

members.name: resizeMode
members.description: TXI-17: how a multi-line field gets its height; a value the field does not know is auto.

members.name: axis
members.description: TXI-17: what the grip resizes; a value the field does not know is vertical.

members.name: gripShown
members.description: TXI-39: a multi-line field resized by hand draws the grip, read-only too — not while disabled.

members.name: minLines
members.description: TXI-17: the fewest lines; a minRows below 1 is 1.

members.name: maxLines
members.description: TXI-37, TXI-39: the most lines, or 0 for no limit; never fewer than minRows, and minRows itself while fixed.

members.name: words
members.description: TXI-52: the product's words, read where the instance gives none (src/primitives/words.ts).

members.name: gripName
members.description: TXI-41, TXI-52: the grip's name — the instance's, else the product's words, else nothing.

members.name: missingMessage
members.description: TXI-23: the validity message of a date or a time its Field says is required, left empty — the browser's, else the Field's words.

members.name: name_
members.description: TXI-23: the accessible name — its own label, else the label of the Field that frames it.

members.name: required_
members.description: TXI-23: its Field says it is required. It has no requirement of its own.

members.name: labelled
members.description: TXI-13: the label floats in the box — a filled or an outlined input with a name, unless its own `labelHidden` or its Field's says to draw none.

members.name: asterisked
members.description: TXI-50: an asterisk follows the floating label — the Field's answer (FLD-25); never outside a Field.

members.name: optionalWord
members.description: TXI-50: the optional word after the floating label — the Field's (FLD-25); never outside a Field.

members.name: saysToField
members.description:
TXI-62: what the input says to the Field that frames it. That it draws the label while its look floats one — its
name, or nothing while the label is hidden; the Field draws no label row either way. How far its text stands from
its start edge and the padding it keeps at its end edge, as lengths of its own tokens (`INSET`, in the styles).
And an entry error, with its words.

members.name: refusalText
members.description: TXI-30: the words of an entry error while it lasts — invalidText or unavailableText; empty where the product gave none.

members.name: described
members.description:
TXI-23, TXI-30: what the input adds to its own description (the prefix, the suffix and the count are named by id):
the words of an entry error while no Field frames it — a Field shows them and gives them back as its own
description (FLD-28) — and then the description its Field gives.

members.name: shownValue
members.description: What the field shows as text: a date or time field's row as drawn, every other field's value.

members.name: resolvedLocale
members.description: The locale a date or time field reads and writes in (TXI-28): `locale`, else the nearest `lang`, else the browser's.

members.name: limit
members.description: `min` and `max` as ISO values of the kind, or empty (TXI-31: anything else is treated as empty).

members.name: listedDates
members.description: TXI-31: the entries of `disabledDates` that are ISO 8601 calendar dates; a time field has none.

members.name: unavailable
members.description: TXI-46: why an ISO value the row gives is not available — before min, after max, a listed date — or null when it is.

members.name: form
members.description: The form it belongs to, if any.

members.name: validity
members.description: The native constraint validity (a required field's missing value; a date or time field's entry error), as a form sees it.

members.name: validationMessage
members.description: The message of an invalid input, as a form shows it.

members.name: willValidate
members.description: Whether the input is validated with its form: not while disabled.

members.name: focus
members.description: TXI-8, TXI-43: focus given to the element goes to what takes the typing — the native element, or the segment a press would focus.

members.name: select
members.description: Selects the whole value, as a native input's `select()` does. A date or time field has nothing to select: its first segment takes focus.

members.name: showValue
members.description: TXI-28, TXI-31: the value as the product set it fills every segment (an empty one empties them); any entry error ends.

members.name: takeText
members.description: TXI-1: the person gave the native element this text; it is the value.

members.name: edit
members.description:
TXI-45, TXI-46: an edit of a segment. The entry error ends with it (TXI-30); the value is the ISO form of what the
row now gives while every segment is filled and that is available, and empty otherwise; `input` is emitted once
when — and only when — the value changed.

members.name: commitEntry
members.description:
TXI-30: a committed date or time field. A row with some segments filled and others empty, or a whole one whose
value is not available, keeps its segments and begins an entry error; an empty row, and a row that gives an
available value, begin none. Returns the entry error that began, if one did (a commit of the same row again begins none).

members.name: activeSegment
members.description: The segment that has focus, if one has.

members.name: moveFocus
members.description: TXI-43: focus moves to the segment `by` places along the row, stopping at its ends; returns the segment it moved to.

members.name: paintSegments
members.description:
TXI-42: each segment's text is written by the field alone — never by a template the browser's editing could
disagree with, and never into a composition (TXI-45).

members.name: placeCaret
members.description: The (invisible) caret at the end of the focused segment's text, so a touch keyboard's Backspace has something to delete.

members.name: takeWhole
members.description: TXI-29: text handed to the field whole — pasted, dictated, autofilled — fills every segment when it reads as a value of the type.

members.name: typeCharacter
members.description:
TXI-45: one character on a segment (the focused one). A digit is the next digit of its number, and focus moves on
once no further digit could extend it; a separator's character moves on from a segment that is not empty; a or p, or
the first letter of the locale's names, set a day period. Every other character is ignored. Returns the segment the
next character goes to.

members.name: characters
members.description: The characters of text as typed: full-width and the locale's digits as ASCII ones.

members.name: onBeforeInput
members.description:
TXI-45: the browser is about to edit a segment. Nothing it would write is kept — the segment's text is the field's
— and what it carries is read instead: a character is typed, several at once are a whole text (TXI-29: dictation,
autofill, a paste the clipboard event did not bring), a deletion removes a digit. A composition cannot be cancelled
and is left to the input method until it commits.

members.name: eraseOn
members.description: TXI-45: Backspace or Delete removes the focused segment's last digit; Backspace on an empty one moves to the previous segment.

members.name: onSegmentKeyDown
members.description:
TXI-43, TXI-44, TXI-45: the keys of a segment. Left and Right Arrow move to the segment drawn on that side — the
same in a right-to-left layout, where the row runs left to right too; Up and Down Arrow step by one, Page Up and
Page Down by more, Home and End go to the ends of the range; Backspace and Delete remove a digit; Enter is the
action key (TXI-3). Digits and letters arrive as `beforeinput`.

members.name: onSegmentCompositionEnd
members.description:
TXI-45: an input method committed text on a segment. Its digits are taken one by one, as typed (full-width ones
too); any other text is read whole (TXI-29). What the composition drew in the segment is replaced by the field's own text.

members.name: onSegmentInput
members.description: The browser's own `input` on a segment (a composition's) is not the field's: the value's change is (TXI-46).

members.name: onCopy
members.description: TXI-29: copy puts the whole row on the clipboard as drawn, whichever segment has focus.

members.name: onCut
members.description: TXI-29: cut copies the whole row and then empties every segment, unless the field is read-only.

members.name: onPaste
members.description: TXI-29: pasted text is read whole, whichever segment has focus; text that reads as nothing changes nothing.

members.name: keepsEntry
members.description: A node of the field's own that focus may move between without committing (TXI-43): a segment, or the picker button.

members.name: onEntryFocusIn
members.description: TXI-43: focus arrived on a segment or on the picker button of a date or time field.

members.name: onEntryFocusOut
members.description:
TXI-43: focus left a segment or the picker button. Moving between them commits nothing; leaving them for anything
else commits the field (TXI-2, TXI-30) — without the entry error when it leaves for the picker it asked for (TXI-33).

members.name: onInput
members.description:
TXI-1, TXI-18: the user changed the value. The native `input` event is composed, so it leaves the shadow root by
itself — after the element has taken the new value. An edit past maxLength is cut to fit; one that changes nothing
then (a keystroke at the limit) is refused and heard by no one.

members.name: onBlur
members.description: TXI-2: focus left with a changed value — `change`, once.

members.name: commit
members.description:
TXI-2, TXI-30: a commit — `change` when the value differs from the one last committed, then, for a date or time
field left half-filled or with a value that is not available, `entryerror` (not when `quiet`: TXI-33).

members.name: onNativeChange
members.description: The browser's own `change` is not the field's (TXI-2 decides when a value is committed).

members.name: onKeyDown
members.description:
TXI-2, TXI-3: Enter in a single-line field commits the value and fires `action`; then, inside a form and unless
`action` was cancelled, it requests the form's submission as a native input does. Not while composing: there Enter
commits the composition. In a multi-line field Enter is a line break.

members.name: act
members.description: TXI-3: the action key — the commit, then `action`, then the form's submission unless `action` was cancelled.

members.name: onPickerClick
members.description:
TXI-33: the picker button asks the product for a picker and changes nothing itself: no value, no focus, nothing
presented, nothing committed — the value it carries is empty while the row is half-filled or not available, and no
entry error is raised for that, because the picker is about to give a whole value.

members.name: onPickerPress
members.description:
TXI-33: a press on the picker button is already the request, as far as the entry error goes: where a press on a
button moves focus to nothing (Safari), focus leaves the segments before the click arrives.

members.name: entryTarget
members.description: TXI-8, TXI-43: what a press on the field focuses: the input; in a date or time field the first empty segment, or the last while none is empty.

members.name: onFieldMouseDown
members.description:
TXI-8: a press anywhere on the box — its padding, a floating label, the prefix, the suffix, a decorative icon, the
text between two segments — focuses the input (TXI-43: a segment). An
interactive element in a slot, a segment, the picker button and the resize grip keep their own press.

members.name: announce
members.description: Something to be read once, politely, by assistive technology (a live region drawn nowhere).

members.name: scheduleCount
members.description: TXI-19: the count is announced once typing has paused for a second, never on every keystroke.

members.name: spokenCount
members.description:
TXI-19: the count as it is said — in the description and the announcement: the product's sentence with its places
filled, every number in the locale's digits (`counter-text` while there is a limit, `counter-no-limit-text` while
there is none); the digits of `countText` where there is no sentence, or while the value is longer than the limit
(a value the product set), which a sentence of how many are left cannot say.

members.name: countText
members.description:
TXI-19: the count the input keeps, as text — the user-perceived characters of the value, then a slash and
`maxLength` while there is one ("12/40") — and empty while `counter` is not set. Read-only, and new with every
change of the value or of `maxLength`: a product that frames the input by hand gives it to its Field's
`countText` in its own `input` listener, and `<tanrei-text-field>` does so by itself.

members.name: inError
members.description: The input is in the error condition: its own `error`, its Field's (FLD-8), or a date or time input's entry error (TXI-11, TXI-30).

members.name: lineOf
members.description: One line of the input's text style, in px (a duration or a length token is an expression: the element resolves it).

members.name: shownLines
members.description:
The lines the input shows now — during a motion, the height then shown (TXI-38): the room it takes in the
container, which is its box and, while a change of height is moving, what its bottom margin still adds or takes back.

members.name: textLines
members.description: The lines the text needs in the width the input has — a line the text wraps onto counts as one.

members.name: showLines
members.description:
TXI-38: the input shows `target` lines. With `animate` — a change that follows the value, the grip's keys or its
activation — the height moves there from the one shown over motion.resize-* (the styles; at once where motion is
reduced), continuing from wherever a running change had brought it; otherwise it changes at once.

TXI-51: what moves is the room the input takes, never its text. The native element is `target` lines high at once —
a box as tall as its text has nothing to scroll, so the browser cannot scroll the first line away to show the caret
on a line the box does not hold yet (which is what shook) — and `--_lag`, the lines the room shown still differs by,
goes to 0 over the motion: as a bottom margin that takes the new lines back or still holds the removed ones, and as
a clip that uncovers a new line from its top as the container's bottom edge passes it.

members.name: fitHeight
members.description:
TXI-17, TXI-37: the height `resize` names. Auto: exactly the lines of the text, between minRows and maxRows, and it
scrolls only beyond maxRows. Manual: the lines the person gave it, from minRows. Fixed: minRows.

members.name: resizeTo
members.description: TXI-39, TXI-41: the person gives a manually resized field `lines` lines, within minRows and maxRows.

members.name: fitToText
members.description:
TXI-41: the grip activated without a drag — the input becomes as tall as its text needs, within minRows and
maxRows, and returns to minRows when it is already that tall; where it resizes both ways its width alternates too.

members.name: toggleWidth
members.description:
TXI-41: where the field resizes both ways, an activation of the grip also makes it as wide as its layout allows —
its own max-inline-size, or its containing block where it has none — and gives back the width it had before the
person resized it when it already is that wide: the width, too, never depends on a drag (WCAG 2.5.7). At once,
as a drag is.

members.name: resizeWidth
members.description:
TXI-39: the field's own width, as the person gives it — written as the host's inline size, never narrower than its
inline paddings, its icons and sys.target.touch, and no wider than its layout allows (its own max-inline-size, or
its containing block where it has none).

members.name: releaseSize
members.description: TXI-39: the size the person gave the field is kept until resize, resizeAxis, minRows or maxRows changes.

members.name: onGripPointerDown
members.description:
TXI-39, TXI-40: a press that begins on the grip's hit area belongs to the grip — it does not place the caret,
select text or take focus from the input — and a drag follows the pointer without motion.

members.name: onGripClick
members.description: TXI-41: an activation that came with no pointer (a click assistive technology makes) fits the height to the text too.

members.name: onGripKeyDown
members.description:
TXI-41: Down Arrow makes the input one line taller and Up Arrow one line shorter, Home returns it to minRows and
End takes it to maxRows (without one, to the height that shows every line); where the field resizes both ways the
horizontal arrow that points to its end edge widens it by one line height and the other narrows it; Enter and
Space fit the height to the text. Each change moves as TXI-38 says.

members.name: observeSize
members.description:
TXI-37, TXI-38: the height follows a changed width and enlarged text too — at once, without the motion. The
textarea's own box says both: its width, and (its height being a number of lines) the line of its text style.

members.name: syncValidity
members.description:
The form's view of the input: a missing value while its Field says it is required; a date or time field's entry error as badInput
(a half-filled row), rangeUnderflow or rangeOverflow (a value before min or after max) or a custom error (a listed
date) while it lasts (TXI-30). A requirement never validates beyond that (TXI-23).

members.name: iconBoxes
members.description: The measured length of each icon box while what it holds is wider than an icon; empty while it is an icon's.

members.name: observeIcons
members.description: Watches the two icon boxes: an element the product slotted there keeps its own size (TXI-22).

members.name: measureIcons
members.description:
TXI-13, TXI-62: the text starts after the leading box and ends before the trailing one as they are laid out; the
label, its copies and the Field's supporting row are placed by a sum of lengths, which takes the icon's size for
the box's. While a box is wider than that — the product's icon button — its measured length is written into the
sum (`--_lead`, `--_trail`) and said to the Field; a glyph, an icon wide, writes nothing and the field is laid out
from its tokens alone.

members.name: labelObserver
members.description: Watches the two copies of the label that are never drawn, one in each position, for a change in their lines.

members.name: observeLabel
members.description: Returns whether copies are watched from now on that were not before: the observer reports each of them once, after the next layout.

members.name: measureLabel
members.description:
TXI-13: how many lines a floating label takes resting and floated, in the width it is given in each position, and
the width of the widest floated line. The copies are laid out as the drawn label is in each position and never
drawn. While both take one line nothing is set and the field is laid out as it always was; once either wraps, the
field marks it (`data-label-wraps`) and the styles give the lines their room: a taller container, a filled field's
taller band, an outlined field's room above its container, and a gap as wide as the widest line. A stacked label
stands above the container in the flow and wraps there by itself (TXI-25).

members.name: drawn
members.description: Whether the first update has drawn (the first height is shown without motion, TXI-38).

members.name: reportMisuse
members.description: What a debug build reports (TXI-9, TXI-17, TXI-23, TXI-28, TXI-32, TXI-41, TXI-57).

members.name: pickerShown
members.description: TXI-32: a date, time or date-time field with `picker`, not read-only, draws the picker button.

members.name: pickerSize
members.description: TXI-32: the Button size with the field's size name, or Button's default for a size Button does not have.

members.name: renderRow
members.description:
TXI-42, TXI-47: the row of segments — a group named by the label, in one left-to-right run; each segment a spin
button named by its unit and the label, with its range, its value and its value text (segmentEmptyText while it is
empty); the text between them, their placeholders and the copies that give each its width kept from assistive
technology. The shown supporting or error text describes the first segment, and every segment while the field is
in error. A segment's own text is written by `paintSegments()`.

members.name: renderGrip
members.description: TXI-39, TXI-41: the resize grip — a focusable separator whose value is the lines the input shows (`showLines()` writes it).

events.name: input
events.description: The user changed the value (typing, deleting, pasting, dictation, autofill, an input method); `value` is already the new one. A date or time field fires it when its value changes — its last segment is filled, a filled row is edited, or it is emptied — not for a segment that leaves the value empty. Never fired when the product sets `value`.

events.name: change
events.description: The user committed a changed value: focus left the field (a date or time field's segments and picker button), or the action key was pressed in a single-line field.

events.name: entryerror
events.description: The user committed a date, time or date-time field that is half-filled (`invalid`) or whose value is not available (`unavailable`: before `min`, after `max` or listed in `disabledDates`), with the row's text as drawn.

events.name: pickerrequest
events.description: The user activated the picker button of a date, time or date-time field. The product presents the picker and sets `value` to the picked value.
The action key (Enter) was pressed in a single-line field. Cancelable: cancelling it keeps an enclosing form from being submitted.
events.name: action

attributes.description: The id of the form the text input belongs to, where it stands outside it: the platform's own attribute, which then wins over a form around it. The `form` property is read-only and returns the form element.
attributes.name: form
variant
attributes.description:
Stacked is a filled box that shows focus and error with a line inside its edge, under the label its Field draws
above it; filled and outlined float the label inside the box, marked by a tinted box and a bottom line, or by a
border. Use one style
per form. A design system may leave some out (the default system ships stacked only) or add values.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: Minimum height of a single-line field's container (48 / 56 in the default system). The hit area always meets the minimum target.

attributes.name: type
attributes.description:
What the value is: chooses the keyboard, autocorrection, obscured entry and semantics. `code` is text written for
a machine rather than for a reader — a snippet of configuration, a pattern, an identifier, a query, a key: a
left-to-right run in the code face that the browser does not correct, capitalise, check for spelling or complete,
on one line or, with `multiline`, on many. `date`, `time` and `date-time` are entered segment by segment in the
locale's numeric form. The value is always a string.

attributes.name: value
attributes.description:
The text in the field; for date, time and date-time, the ISO 8601 form of what its segments give (2026-09-27, 14:30,
2026-09-27T14:30), or empty while a segment is empty or the value is not available. Setting it shows it and fires
nothing. The `value` attribute is what a form reset returns to.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: The input's own accessible name, for an input no Field frames or one whose visible label is elsewhere; a filled or an outlined input draws it floating. Inside a Field leave it empty: the Field's label names the input, and its own would win.

attributes.name: label-hidden
attributes.description: Does not draw the floating label of a filled or an outlined input, which stays the accessible name (the `label-hidden` attribute). Inside a Field, hide the label on the Field.

attributes.name: placeholder
attributes.description:
A hint shown while the value is empty and the label is not in the input line (above, floated or hidden). Never a
replacement for `label`. In a code field it is an example of the code and is drawn as code; a hint in words
belongs in its Field's `supportingText`. Ignored by a date, time or date-time field, whose empty segments each show their own.

attributes.name: error
disabled
attributes.description: Prevents focus, editing and form submission. Inside a Field, disable the Field, so that its label follows.

attributes.name: readonly
attributes.description: The value can be focused, selected and copied, but not changed (the `readonly` attribute).

attributes.name: multiline
attributes.description: Accepts line breaks and shows several lines, sized as `resize` says. Ignored for password, date, time and date-time.

attributes.name: min-rows
attributes.description:
The fewest lines a multi-line field shows (`min-rows`): the height of an empty auto-resized field, the starting and
smallest height of a manually resized one, and the height of a fixed one.

attributes.name: max-rows
attributes.description:
The most lines an auto-resized field grows to before it scrolls, and the tallest a manually resized one can be made
(`max-rows`); 0 is no limit. Ignored while `resize` is fixed.

attributes.name: resize
attributes.description:
How a multi-line field gets its height. `auto`: it follows the number of lines between `minRows` and `maxRows`, with
an animated change, and has no grip. `manual`: it starts at `minRows` lines and the person resizes it with the grip
in its bottom end corner. `fixed`: it stays at `minRows` lines, with no grip.

attributes.name: resize-axis
attributes.description: What the person can resize by hand (`resize-axis`): the height only, or the height and the width. Ignored unless `resize` is manual.

attributes.name: resize-label
attributes.description: The accessible name of the resize grip (`resize-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ resizeLabel })`). Tanrei has none: without them the grip is drawn and works, and has no name.

attributes.name: counter-text
attributes.description:
The count said to assistive technology while `counter` is set and `maxLength` is above 0 (`counter-text`): your
sentence with the places `{count}`, `{limit}` and `{remaining}` ("{remaining} characters left"). Empty reads the
product's words (`setWords({ characterCountText })`); with neither the count is said as its digits ("12/40"). It is
drawn as digits whatever is said: `countText` stays "12/40".

attributes.name: counter-no-limit-text
attributes.description: The count said while `counter` is set and there is no `maxLength` (`counter-no-limit-text`): your sentence with the place `{count}` ("{count} characters"). Empty reads the product's words (`setWords({ characterCountNoLimitText })`); with neither, the digits.

attributes.name: no-wrap
attributes.description:
Keeps every line of a multi-line code field on one row (`no-wrap`; the spec's `wrap: false`): a line wider than the
input scrolls sideways inside the container, and widens nothing. Without it a line that does not fit continues on
following rows; the value is the same either way. Read only while `type` is `code` and `multiline` is set: prose
always wraps, and a single line always scrolls in its line (reported in debug builds).

attributes.name: maxlength
attributes.description: The most user-perceived characters the user can enter; 0 is no limit (the `maxlength` attribute). Ignored for date, time and date-time.

attributes.name: counter
attributes.description: Keeps a character count (with `maxLength`, when set: "12/40"): part of the description, announced when typing pauses, and readable as `countText`. The input draws none: a Field draws it at the end of its supporting row, given it as `count-text` — which `<tanrei-text-field>` does by itself.

attributes.name: prefix-text
attributes.description: Fixed text before the value, not part of it (`prefix-text`). Beside one line of email, url, tel, number or password it is written before the value along the direction of the run the two affixes make — that of their first strong character, left-to-right where they have none — in every layout direction; beside any other value it stands at the field's start edge. In a code field it is code: in the code face, at the left of the value in every layout direction. Ignored for date, time and date-time.

attributes.name: suffix-text
attributes.description: Fixed text after the value, not part of it (`suffix-text`). Beside one line of email, url, tel, number or password it is written after the value along the run's direction (see `prefixText`); beside any other value it stands at the field's end edge. In a code field it is code: in the code face, at the right of the value in every layout direction. Ignored for date, time and date-time.

attributes.name: autocomplete
attributes.description: The autofill hint, as an HTML autofill field name (email, current-password, one-time-code…). A code field left without one asks the browser to offer no remembered entry.

attributes.name: locale
attributes.description:
A BCP 47 tag ("en-US", "ja-JP") for how a date, time or date-time field shows and reads its value: the order of its
segments, the separators, the clock, the digits and the names of the units. Empty uses the nearest `lang`
attribute, then the browser's language. The calendar is the Gregorian calendar in every locale.

attributes.name: min
attributes.description: The earliest value a date, time or date-time field accepts from the person, ISO 8601; empty for no limit.

attributes.name: max
attributes.description: The latest value a date, time or date-time field accepts from the person, ISO 8601; empty for no limit.

attributes.name: disabled-dates
attributes.description:
Dates inside `min` and `max` that a date or date-time field does not accept from the person, as ISO 8601 calendar
dates — the same list the product gives its date-time picker. The `disabled-dates` attribute is a space-separated
list or a JSON array. Ignored by a time field.

attributes.name: invalid-text
attributes.description: The words of the refusal of a date, time or date-time input committed with some segments filled and others empty (`invalid-text`): shown by the Field that frames it as its error text, and part of a bare input's description.

attributes.name: unavailable-text
attributes.description: The words of the refusal of a date, time or date-time input committed with a value before `min`, after `max` or listed in `disabledDates` (`unavailable-text`): shown and described as `invalidText` is.

attributes.name: segment-empty-text
attributes.description: What assistive technology reads as the value of a date or time segment that holds nothing yet (`segment-empty-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ segmentEmptyText })`). Tanrei has none: without them an empty segment has no value text.

attributes.name: picker
attributes.description:
Shows the picker button in a date, time or date-time field. The field presents no picker itself: it fires
`pickerrequest`, and the product presents one and sets `value` to what was picked.

attributes.name: picker-label
attributes.description: The accessible name of the picker button ("Choose date", `picker-label`). Required while the button is shown.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Web only: the name it is submitted under.

declarations.name: CORE_VARIANTS
declarations.default: ['docked', 'floating']

declarations.name: DEFAULT_VARIANT
declarations.default: 'docked'

declarations.name: AXES
declarations.default: [ { name: 'variant', core: CORE_VARIANTS, default: DEFAULT_VARIANT, rules: (value, selector) => variantBlock(value, selector, DEFAULT_VARIANT), probe: (value) => `${PREFIX}-container-color-${value}` }, ]
declarations.description:
The open axis (TBR-13): a variant a layer added gets its values on demand, built by the same function and
falling back to docked's tokens, and takes the docked structure (the structure is not a value: only `floating` is
drawn as a floating toolbar); a value the active system lacks is reported.

declarations.name: styles
declarations.default: css` /* TBR-1, TBR-3, TBR-13: the docked structure — every variant but floating. The parent's full width; the container at least container.size high above the bottom inset, its color reaching under the bottom and side insets while the items stay inside them. */ :host { display: flex; --_inset-bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px); --_inset-left: env(safe-area-inset-left, 0px); --_inset-right: env(safe-area-inset-right, 0px); } ${unsafeCSS(variantBlock(DEFAULT_VARIANT, ':host'))} ${unsafeCSS(CORE_VARIANTS.filter((v) => v !== DEFAULT_VARIANT).map((v) => variantBlock(v, `:host([variant='${v}'])`)).join('\n'))} :host([hidden]) { display: none; } /* TBR-1, TBR-2: one row in reading order (logical: right-to-left starts at the right, TBR-7), padding-inline at each end, the items spread with equal space between them and never less than the gap, each centred across the row. The edge is the container's top inset line; the fill, elevation and corners are the variant's. */ .container { box-sizing: border-box; flex: 1 1 auto; min-inline-size: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: row; flex-wrap: nowrap; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: var(--_gap); min-block-size: calc(var(--_size) + var(--_inset-bottom)); padding-block-end: var(--_inset-bottom); padding-left: calc(var(--_inset-left) + var(--_pad)); padding-right: calc(var(--_inset-right) + var(--_pad)); background: var(--_bg); box-shadow: var(--_elevation), inset 0 ${t('outline-width')} 0 0 var(--_edge); --tanrei-corner-radius: var(--_shape); --tanrei-corner-pill: var(--_shape-pill); } /* TBR-8, TBR-9: every item keeps its own size (it never shrinks, and a Button's label stays on one line); TBR-2: one item is centred. */ ::slotted(*) { flex: none; } ::slotted(:only-child) { margin-inline: auto; } /* TBR-8: items that need more length than the toolbar has scroll along its axis (the gap at its minimum: space-between starts at the start edge when there is no free space). Only then is the container a scroll container, so at rest nothing of an item — its target, its ring, an elevated Button's shadow — is clipped. */ .container.scrolls { overflow-x: auto; overflow-y: hidden; overscroll-behavior: contain; scrollbar-width: none; } .container.scrolls::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none; } /* TBR-4, TBR-5: floating — at its own size where the layout places it, never wider than its container; the items packed from the start, padding-inline at each end and the gap between them (TBR-16, below), at least container.size across, every item centred; the edge around the whole shape, rounded by the variant's corners eased by corner smoothing. No inset is read. */ ${unsafeCSS(FLOATING)} { display: inline-flex; vertical-align: middle; max-inline-size: 100%; } ${unsafeCSS(FLOATING)} .container { justify-content: flex-start; gap: 0; min-block-size: var(--_size); padding-block-end: 0; padding-left: var(--_pad); padding-right: var(--_pad); box-shadow: var(--_elevation), inset 0 0 0 ${t('outline-width')} var(--_edge); } /* TBR-6: vertical (floating only) — the items stacked top to bottom in the order given, whatever the direction (TBR-7), the paddings and gap along the block axis, at least container.size wide, never taller than its container. */ ${unsafeCSS(VERTICAL)} { flex-direction: column; max-inline-size: none; max-block-size: 100%; } ${unsafeCSS(VERTICAL)} .container { flex-direction: column; min-inline-size: var(--_size); min-block-size: 0; padding-block: var(--_pad); padding-left: 0; padding-right: 0; } /* TBR-16: a floating toolbar's items stand container.gap.floating apart between their visible bounds — 0 in the default system — and two neighbours further only as far as each needs to keep sys.target.touch of length along the axis, centred on itself, that its neighbour's does not reach into: an item at least that long touches its neighbour, a shorter one stands half of what it lacks away (src/primitives/kept-length.ts; the element measures the items' lengths). Nothing of an item is widened or restyled (TBR-9), and the space is the same for every pointer. Along the row, or the column of a vertical toolbar. A docked toolbar spreads its items and keeps its gap (TBR-2). */ ${keptLength(":host([variant='floating']:not([orientation='vertical'])) ::slotted(*)", { gap: FLOATING_GAP })} ${keptLength(`${VERTICAL} ::slotted(*)`, { gap: FLOATING_GAP, axis: 'block' })} ${unsafeCSS(VERTICAL)} .container.scrolls { overflow-x: hidden; overflow-y: auto; } /* TBR-4: corner smoothing, the shared rule, on the container (data-tanrei-shape). */ ${shape} @media (forced-colors: active) { .container { border-block-start: ${t('outline-width')} solid CanvasText; } ${unsafeCSS(FLOATING)} .container { border: ${t('outline-width')} solid CanvasText; } } `

declarations.description:
Holds a short row of actions for the current screen or selection, docked across the bottom edge or floating over the
content.

Contract: specs/toolbar.spec.json. Every value it reads is a `--tanrei-comp-toolbar-*` token of its variant: the
container's color, elevation, corners, cross-axis size, end padding and minimum gap, and the edge's color and width.
It draws no text, glyph or state of its own. Its items are the product's `<tanrei-button>` children,
icon-only or labelled, drawn from their own tokens with their own states, events and semantics (TBR-9); the toolbar lays them out,
scrolls them when they do not fit (TBR-8) and makes them one Tab stop moved through with the arrow keys (TBR-10).

The roving Tab stop is the items' `tabindex` (0 on the stop, -1 on the other enabled items; none on a disabled one):
both items delegate focus to the native button in their shadow root, which a host whose tabindex is -1 takes out of the
Tab order. Between two items each item's hit area stops at the middle of the gap, which the toolbar measures and gives
its items through an internal channel (src/primitives/group-item.ts) — not a styling API.

A floating toolbar lays its items `container.gap.floating` apart — 0 in the default system — and keeps for each a
length of `sys.target.touch` along its axis that its neighbour's does not reach into (TBR-16): two medium Buttons (40)
stand 8 apart, two large ones (56) touch. It measures its items for that and writes each one's length on it as
`--tanrei-kept-*` custom properties (src/primitives/kept-length.ts), which are not a styling API either.
declarations.name: TanreiToolbar

cssParts.description: The surface: the variant's fill, elevation, corners and edge, holding the items (it scrolls them along its axis when they do not fit).
cssParts.name: container

slots.description: The items, in reading order: `<tanrei-button>` elements — an icon-only one for an action (a toggle such as Bold is one with `toggle`), a labelled one for a text action. Anything else is still laid out, and reported in debug builds (TBR-12).

members.name: variant
members.description:
`docked` spans the bottom edge of the screen, flush with it, its color reaching under the bottom inset; `floating` is a
rounded, raised surface over the content, as long as its items, placed by the layout that holds it. A value a design
system adds is drawn with the docked structure and its own values; a value the active system does not have is drawn
as `docked` (reported in debug builds, TBR-13).

members.name: orientation
members.description:
The direction the items run. `vertical` is for a floating toolbar beside the content on a large screen; a docked
toolbar is always horizontal (reported in debug builds, TBR-6). Anything else is horizontal (TBR-13).

members.name: label
members.description: The toolbar's accessible name ("Formatting", "Message actions"). Never drawn. Required (TBR-12).

members.name: scrolls
members.description: TBR-8: the items need more length than the toolbar has, so the container scrolls them.

members.name: axes
members.default: new OpenAxesController(this, { component: 'toolbar', behavior: 'TBR-13', axes: AXES })
members.description: TBR-13: variants a design system adds, and a value the active system does not have (src/primitives/axes.ts).

members.name: keys
members.description: TBR-10: the next and previous enabled item, wrapping, and the first and last (no typeahead is passed to it).

members.name: last
members.description: TBR-10: the item that had focus last — the Tab stop while it is here and enabled.

members.name: roved
members.description: The items whose `tabindex` the toolbar set, so that it can take it back when one leaves.

members.name: places
members.description: TBR-9: where each item was placed last, with its reach toward its neighbours.

members.name: kept
members.description: TBR-16: the lengths a floating toolbar's items keep along its axis; what follows from them is measured again.

members.name: floating
members.description: The structure it draws: only `floating` floats; every other value is docked (TBR-13).

members.name: axis
members.description: The axis its items run along: a column only for a vertical floating toolbar (TBR-6).

members.name: enabled
members.description: TBR-10: an item a key can reach — not disabled by itself, nor by a disabled fieldset around it (BTN-32).

members.name: observe
members.description: The container and every child are observed: a gap, an item's size or the room the toolbar has may change.

members.name: keep
members.description: TBR-16: only a floating toolbar keeps a target's length for each item; a docked one spreads them (TBR-2).

members.name: rove
members.description:
TBR-10: one Tab stop — the item focused last while it is here and enabled, else the first enabled item — at tabindex
0, every other enabled item at -1, a disabled one untouched (it takes no focus, BTN-2 / BTN-2). An item that left the
toolbar gets its tabindex back.

members.name: itemOf
members.description: The toolbar's item an event came from (the child whose shadow root holds the native button), or null.

members.name: onKeyDown
members.description:
TBR-10: Right / Left Arrow (mirrored in right-to-left) in a row, Down / Up Arrow in a column, move to the next and
previous enabled item, wrapping; Home and End to the first and last. Moving focus never activates: Enter and Space
are the focused item's own. Other keys, and keys with a modifier, are left alone.

members.name: reveal
members.description: TBR-8: an item that takes focus is brought fully into view, inside the container's padding, at once (no motion).

members.name: measure
members.description:
TBR-9: each item's hit area reaches toward a neighbour no further than the middle of the gap between their visible
bounds (measured: a docked toolbar spreads its items), and as far as its target where it has none. TBR-8: whether the
items need more length than the toolbar has — their own sizes, the minimum gap and the paddings.

members.name: checkContent
members.description: TBR-12: a toolbar with no item, or with content that is not an icon button or a Button, still lays it out, and says so.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description:
`docked` spans the bottom edge of the screen, flush with it, its color reaching under the bottom inset; `floating` is a
rounded, raised surface over the content, as long as its items, placed by the layout that holds it. A value a design
system adds is drawn with the docked structure and its own values; a value the active system does not have is drawn
as `docked` (reported in debug builds, TBR-13).

attributes.name: orientation
attributes.description:
The direction the items run. `vertical` is for a floating toolbar beside the content on a large screen; a docked
toolbar is always horizontal (reported in debug builds, TBR-6). Anything else is horizontal (TBR-13).

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: The toolbar's accessible name ("Formatting", "Message actions"). Never drawn. Required (TBR-12).

declarations.description:
Describes an element in a few words when a person points at it, focuses it with the keyboard or long-presses it,
without taking focus or blocking anything.

Contract: specs/tooltip.spec.json. Wraps its anchor (the default slot). The drawn tooltip is a `popover="manual"`
element in the shadow root, in the top layer — above an open modal `<dialog>` — placed against the anchor by script:
on the side and with the alignment `placement` names, `offset` away and moved along the side by `crossOffset`, flipped
to the opposite side, shifted along it and, in a window smaller than itself, held inside it; it keeps the side it is on
while that side has room, follows the anchor while open and closes when nothing of the anchor can be seen. It is a
read overlay: it never takes focus and holds nothing focusable.

It opens after a fine pointer rests on the anchor for the show delay (at once while tooltips are warm: another is open
or fading, or one closed a moment ago), at once on keyboard focus, and on a touch long-press; it stays while the pointer
is over the anchor, the gap between the anchor and the tooltip, or the tooltip, or the anchor has keyboard focus, and
closes on Escape, an activation of the anchor, a press on it, the hide delay after the pointer left, or the touch
timeout after the finger lifted. The show delay, hide delay and touch timeout are `showDelay`, `hideDelay` and
`touchTimeout` in milliseconds (0 is at once), or the tokens `motion.show-delay`, `motion.hide-delay` and
`timeout.touch` while unset. Opening and closing by itself fires `toggle`; setting `open` does not.

It comes out of the anchor's side: it fades in while it grows from `motion.enter-scale` and travels
`motion.enter-offset`, the growth fixed where an arrow points or would point, and goes back the same way; a motion that
is interrupted turns round from where it is, a warm tooltip appears whole at once, and where motion is reduced it
fades alone. Its place is never animated.

`arrow` draws a triangle that points at the anchor, one shape with the container; `inverse` draws it in the opposite
scheme's colors (true) or on a surface of the scheme (false). Left unset, each takes the system's choice:
`--tanrei-comp-tooltip-arrow-visible` (off in the default system) and its form's `-plain-container-inverse` (on) or
`-rich-container-inverse` (off). `shortcut` writes the keys of the anchor's command after a plain tooltip's text and
gives them to the anchor as `aria-keyshortcuts`.

While `describes` is true (the default; the attribute `no-describe` turns it off) the text — after the title, for a
rich tooltip — is the anchor's `aria-description`, set on the first focusable element slotted in (a Tanrei component
forwards it from its host to its native element), whether or not the tooltip is open.

Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-tooltip-*` tokens.

members.description:
A heading for a rich tooltip; a plain one ignores it. The attribute is read once and removed from the element, so the
browser does not also draw its own `title` tooltip over the anchor.

members.name: shortcut
members.description:
The keyboard shortcut of the anchor's command, in the keyboard shortcut's key names: one chord per string, pressed
in order (`["mod+b"]`); the attribute holds the chords separated by spaces. A plain tooltip writes it after its text
for the keyboard the person uses and gives it to the anchor as `aria-keyshortcuts`; a rich one ignores it. It does

members.name: placement
members.description:
Where it prefers to stand: a side of the anchor (`top`, `bottom`, `start`, `end`), alone to centre it there or with
the edge it lines up with (`top-start`, `end-bottom`), or `auto` for the first side with room. It flips to the
opposite side when that one has no room, keeping the alignment.

members.name: offset
members.description: The distance from the anchor's edge, in CSS pixels; 0 lets them touch. Null takes `offset`, the token.

members.name: crossOffset
members.description:
How far it moves along the side it stands on, in CSS pixels: positive towards the end above or below the anchor,
towards the bottom beside it. It never moves the tooltip off the anchor's side. The attribute is `cross-offset`.

members.name: arrow
members.description:
Whether it draws an arrow that points at the anchor. Null, the default, takes the system's choice
(`arrow.visible`, off in the default system). The attribute: absent is null, `arrow` is true, `arrow="false"` is false.

members.name: inverse
members.description:
Whether it is drawn inverse — in the opposite scheme's colors. False draws it on a surface of the scheme; null, the
default, takes its form's choice (`plain.container.inverse`, on in the default system, or `rich.container.inverse`,
off). The attribute: absent is null, `inverse` is true, `inverse="false"` is false. Colors and elevation only.

members.name: describes
members.description: Whether the text is the anchor's accessible description. Set `no-describe` when the text repeats the anchor's name.

members.name: open
members.description: Whether the tooltip is showing. It opens and closes itself and fires `toggle`; set it to show a tooltip on your own.

members.name: showDelay
members.description:
How long, in ms, a fine pointer rests on the anchor before it opens; 0 opens it at once. Null takes
`motion.show-delay`. Hover alone: keyboard focus still opens it at once. Not scaled by the motion dial.

members.name: hideDelay
members.description:
How long, in ms, it waits after the pointer has left the anchor, the gap and the tooltip; 0 closes it at once. Null
takes `motion.hide-delay`. It stays hoverable at 0, because the gap counts as hover.

members.name: touchTimeout
members.description:

takes `timeout.touch`.

members.name: dismissed
members.description: TIP-4, TIP-6: closed by Escape, an activation or a press on it: it stays closed until the pointer comes back or focus does.

members.name: left
members.description: TIP-28: it is closing because the pointer or the focus left its anchor, which keeps tooltips warm.

members.name: tookOver
members.description: TIP-28: it opened by itself while tooltips were warm, so it appears whole — noted as it opens, before the other one goes.

members.name: side
members.description: TIP-9: the side it stands on, kept while that side has room; and the placement and direction it was taken for.

members.name: surface
members.description: The placed box: the popover in the top layer. It is never transformed, so its box is the tooltip's at rest (TIP-15).

members.name: anchor

members.name: keys

    • index.ts
  • node_modules
 ``` An item is an `
  • ` whose FIRST child element is its row and whose `
      ` holds its items. In the row, a `.tanrei-icon` is the icon, an element with `data-trailing` the trailing content, one with `data-trailing-text` the trailing text, and the rest is the label: the row's own text, or ONE element around it (a ``: text with inline content, a name whose direction is not the layout's). An element with `data-supporting-text` is the supporting text, inside the label's element or directly in the row. On the `
    • `: `data-value` (what identifies it; without one it cannot be chosen), `data-open`, `data-expandable` (it will hold items: give them at `toggle`), `data-loading`, `data-disabled`. The element sets and removes `data-open` itself when the user opens or closes a parent. Everything drawn is `@tanrei/web/tree-view.css` — every value a `--tanrei-comp-tree-view-*` token — which draws the whole look before this script runs; the element adds the same sheet to the root it is connected to. The script adds what a stylesheet cannot: the tree's roles and states, the single tab stop and the keys, the selection, `change` and `toggle`, the answer to a press, the motion of a list that is revealed or hidden, the loading row, opening for the browser's find-in-page, and the debug reports. Only the rows that are shown are read: a closed parent's items are read when it first opens, so a tree costs what it shows. The ROW is the tree item (`role="treeitem"`, `aria-selected`, `aria-expanded`, the tab stop and the focus); its `
    • ` has no role and a nested list is a `group`, so the level comes from the nesting. An `
    • ` holds every row under it, so what changes while the tree is used is said on the row: one row's change styles that row alone. A server that draws the selection in the first frame writes `aria-selected="true"` on the row.

declarations.description:
The base of a composed element (W1, W7, W8, W9). A subclass renders its members' own elements —
`<tanrei-field part="field" exportparts=${FIELD_PARTS.attribute} ${forward(this, FIELD)}>` — and says which of them
focus goes to (`control`).

never focusable; `focus()` and `blur()` are the control's, a click that arrives on the host itself — a page's own
`<label for>` — moves focus to the control, and `autofocus` on the host reaches the control when the element first
renders.

declarations.description:
A composed element with a value member (W5, W6). The subclass names the member (`valueMember`) and writes the
`value` accessor in place, on these two:

    get value(): string { return this.memberValue(''); }
    set value(value: string) { this.giveValue(value); }

**The value is the member's at every moment** (W5): what was last set on the element until the member has taken it
— the element's next render — and from then on what the member holds. So in every listener of a member's event,
capturing or bubbling, `event.target.value` is the new value, and a value the member changed is read back changed.

**The element is the form's control** (W6): its class says `static formAssociated = true`; it takes `name` and `form`, and repeats on its own
internals what its value member tells its own through `FormSays` (src/primitives/form-says.ts) — the value and the
state as they are, the validity flags, the message and the member's own anchor. It resets to its `value` attribute
(`firstValue()`), passes a restore on to the member, and joins a disabled `<fieldset>` with its own `disabled` for
its frame (`formDisabled`). Enter is the member's: it asks for the element's form (`formOf`).
